title: Quarto inline output Fix/Explain names stale lines and code after the document is edited
description: Fix and Explain on a Quarto inline output error send the assistant the cell's location and code as they were when the output arrived, not when the button is pressed. After editing the document, the prompt points the assistant at the wrong lines ("Fix the error from the python code chunk at lines 8-9 of report.qmd ... fix only this error") and attaches code that may no longer be there. This has been the case since the Quarto quick fix landed (#14735). A similar issue affects plot attribution. Steps to reproduce: 1. In a `.qmd` file, run a Python cell that raises an error, e.g. `raise ValueError("boom")`. 2. Insert a few lines of markdown above that cell. 3. Click Fix on the inline error output.The prompt names the cell's original line range rather than its current one. Captured prompt: ``` Fix the error from the python code chunk at lines 8-8 of report.qmd. The failing code and its error output are attached; fix only this error. ``` ### Acceptance Criteria 1. After lines are inserted or removed above a cell, Fix and Explain name the cell's current line range and code. 2. When the cell that raised the error can no longer be identified, Fix and Explain send the error without naming a location.

title: Support custom (BYO) coding agents with a version-independent kcserver MCP bridge path
description:
_Originally posted by @richgawler in https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/discussions/16280#discussioncomment-19045299_:

Hi Team, 

One of our top 10 customers wants to roll out kiro-cli, a coding agent that is not in Positron's Add to Coding Agent picker, to all Positron users on their Workbench server. They got it working using Positron's "kcserver mcp-stdio" bridge as a stdio MCP entry. It connects to the live Python session, resolves the workspace from the folder, and needs no URL or token environment variables.

The gap is that the entry's "command" must be the full path to the kcserver binary, which sits in a versioned directory (for example /usr/lib/rstudio-server/bin/positron-server/2026.10.0-297/extensions/positron-supervisor/resources/kallichore/kcserver). There is no version-independent path, symlink, wrapper or environment variable for it. Every Positron upgrade leaves the entry pointing at a stale path.

In source (positron 2026.10.0-297), Positron rewrites a stale entry itself, but only for the agents it records (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini). An agent outside the picker is never recorded, so it is never refreshed.

WORKAROUND?

Today the customer would have to re-edit kiro-cli's mcp.json for every user after each Positron upgrade, or script that. The options we can offer are all unsupported:

  - A wrapper script installed once at a fixed path that finds the kcserver at launch and runs it. The risk is picking the wrong version, because Workbench keeps several Positron versions side by side. Using a bridge from a different version than the running supervisor is untested.
  - Reading the command out of Gemini CLI's config, which Positron keeps current. This needs every user to have run Add to Coding Agent for Gemini first, and relies on undocumented behaviour of an experimental feature.

Either way the customer owns the upkeep, and nothing guarantees it keeps working across releases. Rollout size has not been stated in the ticket.

Two potential directions, not mutually exclusive. One is a stable launcher path that Workbench keeps pointed at the active build (or an equivalent environment variable), so third-party entries survive upgrades. The other is a custom or BYO agent entry in the Add to Coding Agent picker, so Positron records it and refreshes it the way it does for the three supported agents. Discussion #16280 already covers this ask.

This is a suggestion based on support observations and will likely need deeper investigation by engineering before scoping.

CUSTOMER SUGGESTIONS

Customer asked whether there is a stable, version-independent path, symlink, wrapper or environment variable for kcserver. They also asked whether there is an equivalent of Add to Coding Agent that can be scripted for a BYO agent, so they would not have to re-run it by hand after each upgrade.

Please reach out if you would like the details of the customer and the ticket

title: New Folder from Git / New Folder from Template defaults to an unwritable parent directory, causing silent failure
description:
**Summary**

"New Folder from Git..." and "New Folder from Template..." both default their parent-folder field to the *parent directory* of the currently open workspace root, rather than the workspace root itself. On Posit Workbench/Posit Cloud deployments where the session's project lives at a fixed path (e.g. `/cloud/project`) and its parent (`/cloud`) is not writable by the session user, this causes folder/project creation to silently fail with no error shown to the user.

**Root cause**

`IFileDialogService.defaultFolderPath()` (`src/vs/workbench/services/dialogs/browser/abstractFileDialogService.ts:92-121`) resolves a default parent folder in this order:
1. Last active workspace root (`historyService.getLastActiveWorkspaceRoot`)
2. Else, parent directory of the last active file
3. Else, `preferredHome()` (reads the `files.dialog.defaultPath` setting, else falls back to the user's home directory)

Critically, when a workspace root **is** found (step 1), the method returns `resources.dirname(candidate)` (line 120) — the *parent* of the workspace root, not the workspace root itself:

```ts
async defaultFolderPath(...): Promise<URI> {
    let candidate = this.historyService.getLastActiveWorkspaceRoot(schemeFilter, authorityFilter);
    ...
    if (!candidate) {
        ...
    }
    return resources.dirname(candidate);
}
```

Both `newFolderFromGitModalDialog.tsx` (`showNewFolderFromGitModalDialog`, ~line 272) and `newFolderFlowModalDialog.tsx` (~line 29) call this same method with no arguments to pre-fill their "parent folder" field:

```ts
parentFolder={await renderer.services.fileDialogService.defaultFolderPath()}
```

So on a session with an open workspace at `/cloud/project`, both dialogs default to `/cloud` as the suggested parent — not `/cloud/project`.

**Impact**

On deployments (e.g. Posit Workbench, Posit Cloud) where:
- every session opens a single fixed project directory (e.g. `/cloud/project`) as its workspace root, and
- the parent of that directory (`/cloud`) is intentionally not writable by the session user (owned by root / a different UID),

clicking through "New Folder from Template..." (or "New Folder from Git...") and accepting the default parent folder results in a silent failure — no folder is created, no error is surfaced, and the user is left in the same directory with no indication of what went wrong.

Reported downstream at rstudio/lucid-server#5721.

**Suggested fix**

When a workspace root is already open, default the parent-folder field to the workspace root itself (not its `dirname`) for these two "create a new folder alongside/inside my project" flows — or introduce a dedicated default-parent-folder resolution for `newFolderFromGitModalDialog.tsx` / `newFolderFlowModalDialog.tsx` that doesn't strip to the parent directory of the open workspace. At minimum, a write-permission check before/at folder creation that surfaces an error to the user (instead of failing silently) would resolve the confusing UX even if the default path itself is unchanged.

**Where this was investigated**

- `src/vs/workbench/services/dialogs/browser/abstractFileDialogService.ts:92-121` (`defaultFolderPath`, `preferredHome`)
- `src/vs/workbench/browser/positronModalDialogs/newFolderFromGitModalDialog.tsx` (~line 272)
- `src/vs/workbench/browser/positronNewFolderFlow/newFolderFlowModalDialog.tsx` (~line 29)
- `extensions/git/src/cloneManager.ts` (confirms `git.defaultCloneDirectory` is unrelated/bypassed for this flow, since Positron always passes an explicit `parentFolder`)

title: python: `python.analysis.completeFunctionParens` can cause duplicate completions
description:
Follow-up to https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/5556#issuecomment-5360575599.

With `"python.analysis.completeFunctionParens": true`, function completions get parentheses for builtins, but for objects already in the console namespace, the completion list shows two entries for the same name. The first one is selected by default and inserts no parentheses.

This is because Pyrefly is contributing the one with parentheses, and the positron-python LS is contributing the user-namespace one without parentheses. They aren't deduplicated because they have different `insert_text`. The positron-python completion is always sorted higher by our logic.

We should make the positron-python LS respect `python.analysis.completeFunctionParens` too, so that we only see one completion with parentheses.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Set `"python.analysis.completeFunctionParens": true` in user settings. Then reload Positron.
2. Start a Python console.
3. Run `import pandas as pd` and `df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1]})`.
4. Type `df.index.ma` in the console or in a Python file. Try to complete it.

Two `max` entries appear. The default one inserts `max`. The second one inserts `max()`.

title: Positron AWS: UI freezes after browser tab is in the background
description:
## What happens

On **_Positron Server in SageMaker Studio_**, the UI freezes after the browser tab has been in the background for about 5-6 minutes. It stays frozen until the page is reloaded. R and Python sessions are still there after the reload.

It happens no matter what the session is doing: an active console, a running Shiny app, or a Posit Assistant session doesn't prevent it.

Right before each freeze, the server logs:

```text
SyntaxError: Unexpected non-whitespace character after JSON at position 7485
    at deserialize (server-main.js:33723)
    at ChannelServer.onRawMessage
    at PersistentProtocol._receiveMessage
    at ProtocolReader.acceptChunk
```

After that, the server logs nothing: no disconnect and no reconnect. Is it possible that the server is trying to deserialize a message and it fails at deserialization?

**Environment:** Positron 2026.09.1-2, `positron-sagemaker` image, SageMaker Studio JupyterLab app (ml.m5.xlarge), Chrome on macOS. Not a resource problem: no OOM kills, and health checks pass.

**Workarounds:** keep the Positron window visible, or disable `chrome://flags/#intensive-wake-up-throttling`.

## What we know

**One message from the browser arrived corrupted.** Each message has a length field in front of its content. In this one, the length was longer than the JSON it pointed to, so the server read the full JSON plus some extra bytes. Messages after it parsed fine, so the stream as a whole stayed in sync.

**The UI never recovers because nothing treats this error as a broken connection.** The server logs the error and drops the message. The connection still counts as healthy, because it only checks whether data is arriving, and data keeps arriving. Reconnects can only be started from the browser, and the browser doesn't know anything went wrong. It just waits forever for a reply to the dropped request.

**The timing points at Chrome's background-tab throttling.** The freezes came 5-6 minutes after a reload. After a tab has been hidden for 5 minutes, Chrome runs its timers much less often. Turning that throttling off seems to prevent the freeze.

## Where it could be failing

- **The browser side, when sending.** The corrupted message was sent by the browser. The browser queues outgoing messages and sends them on a timer, and that timer is the kind Chrome slows down in hidden tabs.
- **The network between the browser and the server.** SageMaker puts its own proxy in front of the server. A proxy that damaged the data would normally break the stream for good, but here only one message is affected, so this seems less likely.

## Not the cause

- **The `/idle` endpoint.** SageMaker checks it with ordinary HTTP requests that don't go over this connection.
- **Positron's idle-activity heartbeat.** It only runs while the user is active, and that stops about a minute after the last mouse or keyboard input. So it doesn't run in a hidden tab.

## Related

#15560 had similar symptoms: Safari dropped messages because a buffer was freed while it was still in use. That fix is already in 2026.09.x, and this report is on Chrome, so it's a separate issue.

CC @blairj09 feel free to add or edit anything!

title: Dedicated session for Assistant
description:
## Context 

Related to https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/14771 

Currently Assistant shares a single console with the user. This makes it difficult to review and audit work written by hand vs. agent. 

In an Agent/ Assistant first chat mode, this becomes more important for spot checking AI generated work so a user can decide what to merge into their work 
 
## AC 
1. When Assistant executes code, the user's console does not get flooded with the Assistant's code execution
2. If the user wants to review a log of the Assistant's code execution, they can easily access it 

## Potential implementation 
1. Dedicated agent session - Agent gets its own console/kernel instance; user's interactive console stays untouched unless they explicitly pull agent output in.
- we'll need to reconcile environment changes i.e. package installs 

2. Shared kernel, separate execution log - Same underlying kernel/environment but the console view/history is partitioned by actor 
- we'll need to tag each console entry as user/assistant

## Open questions 
1. Are there startup and performance concerns with spinning up separate sessions 
2. Is this attractive for some of the customer asks around constraints or sandboxing of the Assistant R/Python session? Can we launch a session in a sandbox [bubblewrap](https://github.com/containers/bubblewrap) style or [Landlock](https://landlock.io/)?

    at async ExtensionManagementService2.installGalleryExtensions (file:///Applications/Positron.app/Contents/Resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-utility/sharedProcess/sharedProcessMain.js:26040:5)
    at async ExtensionManagementService2.installFromGallery (file:///Applications/Positron.app/Contents/Resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-utility/sharedProcess/sharedProcessMain.js:26013:23)
```

## Environment
- **Positron:** 2026.05.2 build 3
- **Code - OSS:** 1.109.2

- **Date:** 2026-05-13T18:52:31.020Z

title: Quarto: Virtual doc should have an option for only including the current chunk in the document
description:
Opening this in Positron, because we will likely make the PR to Quarto's vs code extension.
See also https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto/pull/436

Currently, Quarto's virtual docs include _all_ of that language's chunks in the document. For example, with a Quarto doc like this:

``````
---
title: "Untitled"
format: html
---

```{r}
1 + 1
2 + 2
3 + 3

```

a
asdf

```{r}
4 + 4
5 + 5
```
``````

The virtual doc when your cursor is in the first chunk looks like this

``````
# ---
# title: "Untitled"
# format: html
# ---
# 
# ```{r}
1 + 1
2 + 2
3 + 3

# ```
# a
# asdf
# ```{r}
4 + 4
5 + 5
# ```
``````

This form trips up the statement range provider when the cursor is on `3 + 3`, as it causes the cursor to jump down to `4 + 4`, thinking that that is the next line of code to execute. The sequence of events is something like:
- We find `3 + 3` and use that as our code to execute
- The statement range provider code in Positron moves down 1 line to the newline still within the chunk, and executes the statement range provider again to find where to put the cursor
- Because we are still in an R chunk, quarto gives us the R virtual doc and we jump down to `4 + 4` as the next line to execute

Notably, if you remove the newline after `3 + 3` this problem doesn't occur, because in the 2nd bullet from above when we move down 1 line we step _out_ of the R chunk, so on the quarto side we aren't in an R virtual doc anymore, and Ark doesn't even get a chance to provide a statement range. That ends up putting us on the triple backtick line of the chunk, which is actually good behavior.

To fix the problem of jumping the cursor from one chunk to the next, I think Quarto's virtual docs should have an option to request that the virtual doc ONLY contain the _current_ chunk, rather than all of them for that language. That would look like this

``````
# ---
# title: "Untitled"
# format: html
# ---
# 
# ```{r}
1 + 1
2 + 2
3 + 3

# ```
# a
# asdf
# ```{r}
# 4 + 4
# 5 + 5
# ```
``````

So now at `3 + 3` we'd move to the newline, but we'd see that there is no code to execute after that and we'd just stay on that line.

I imagine there may be other language features that could also benefit from tightly scoping the virtual doc to just the current chunk.

title: Quarto LSP does not reconnect after extension host restart
description:
<!--

Thanks for taking the time to file an issue!

Take a look at our guidance on feedback and issues:
https://positron.posit.co/feedback.html

General questions about Positron should start in GitHub Discussions rather than as an issue:

https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues
If you find an existing bug or feature request, please gives it a thumbs-up reaction or
additional information to help us prioritize the issue.

-->

## System details:

- Positron 2026.02.0 build 10
- macOS 14 (Darwin arm64 25.2.0)
- Quarto 1.6.11
- Affects both R and Python .qmd files

## Describe the issue:
Quarto LSP does not come back online after restarting the extension host, causing outline to stop working in .qmd files.

Note: Related to #9069. The fix for outline restoration needs to be implemented in the Quarto extension to ensure LSP reconnects after extension host restart.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a .qmd file with code blocks (R or Python)
2. Verify outline appears in Outline panel
3. Run command "Developer: Restart Extension Host"
4. Outline no longer works for .qmd files
5. Closing/reopening file or running "Developer: Reload Window" does not restore functionality

## Expected behavior

Quarto LSP should reconnect after extension host restart and outline should continue working.

## Actual behavior

Quarto LSP does not reconnect. Outline remains broken until Positron is fully restarted.

title: Formatting `.qmd` with Air can bork entire file contents
description: This is a follow-up to [issue](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/11100) #11100, where it appeared that positron assistant code completion was causing triple backtick `'```'` indentations which would lead to syntax errors. Positron/OS/session details are the same as before. I now suspect the issue here is the built-in air formatter being confused by dangling pipes. See reproducible example below: **First, some mtcars code** **then, insert a dangling pipe between two code chunks:** **saving the .qmd file, the air formatter reformats the code:** This will lead to a syntax error, "no `'```'` in scope". I'm now uncertain whether the earlier issue #11100 was caused by the positron assistant or the air formatter (or a combination of both) but wanted to let you know!

title: Reconnection always fails behind proxies that remove the WebSocket query string (SageMaker Studio)
description:
## System details:

#### Positron and OS details:

- Positron Server 2026.09.1-2 (Code OSS 1.130.0, commit `467ff390dd8b4ffc8972ebb84d9e05a1fd5a4fe2`).
- A SageMaker Studio JupyterLab space with the `positron-sagemaker` image: jupyter_server 2.20.0, jupyter-server-proxy 4.5.0, and tornado 6.5.
- Instance types `ml.m5.xlarge` and `ml.m5.4xlarge`.
- Chrome 154 on macOS.

#### Session details:

R 4.6.1. The problem does not depend on the session.

## Describe the issue:

In SageMaker Studio, Positron cannot reconnect after its WebSockets close. The browser logs `reconnected!`, but after that, files, terminals, and the console do not respond. Positron shows no error. Only a page reload recovers the session.

**Cause.** The SageMaker Studio proxy removes the query string from WebSocket upgrade requests. It keeps the query string on HTTP requests. The browser sends the reconnection token in that query string. As a result, the server never receives the token. The server makes a new random token and treats each reconnection as a new connection.

**Why the session then stops.** The browser does not know that the server made a new connection. It logs `reconnected!` and continues with its old protocol state. It sends its unacknowledged messages again and continues its message IDs. The new connection on the server starts its message IDs at 1. Each side then ignores the messages of the other side. We found this part by reading the code. We did not trace it.

**Which features stop.** The management connection carries files, terminals, and the other server requests. The console uses the extension host connection, so it continues to work. The extension host connection has the same flaw when its own WebSocket closes. Then the server starts a second extension host process, and the console stops too.

**When it occurs.** Any close of the management WebSocket starts the problem. The server keeps a disconnected session for 3 hours so that the browser can reconnect. Behind this proxy, the session cannot survive one close. We do not know all the causes of the closes in SageMaker. The close in our test had code 1006 (`wasClean: false`).

## Steps to reproduce the issue:

### A. In SageMaker Studio (we did these steps on 2026-10-02 at 22:09 UTC)

1. Start a SageMaker Studio JupyterLab space with a Positron Server image.
2. Open Positron and start an R console.
3. Open the Developer Tools console in Chrome.
4. Find the line `Creating a socket (renderer-Management-<token>)`. Record the first 8 characters of the token.
5. Open the server log in CloudWatch: log group `/aws/sagemaker/studio`, stream `<domain-id>/<space-name>/JupyterLab/default`.
6. Find the line `[ManagementConnection] New connection established.` and compare its 8-character ID with the token.
   - Result: the two values are different. In a correct installation, they are the same.
7. Turn off the network of the computer for 90 seconds. Then turn it on again.
8. Wait until the console shows `[reconnect] reconnected!` for `Management` and for `ExtensionHost`.
9. Find the new lines in the server log.
   - Result: the server logs `New connection established.` with new IDs for both connections.
   - Result: the server logs `Starting extension host process...` again.
   - Result: the server does not log `The client has reconnected.`
10. Type `1 + 1` in the R console.
    - Result: the console shows no output.
11. Open a file from the Explorer.
    - Result: the file does not open.
12. Open a new terminal.
    - Result: the terminal does not open.

If only the management WebSocket closes, the console continues to work. Files and terminals still do not open. We saw this case at 17:54 UTC on 2026-10-02.

### B. Without SageMaker (faster, but we did not do these steps with Positron)

The script below does what the SageMaker proxy does. It removes the query string from WebSocket upgrade requests only. We did a test of the script alone. We did not run it with Positron Server.

1. Start Positron Server on `127.0.0.1:8000`, for example with `--host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --without-connection-token`.
2. Save the script below as `strip_ws_query.py`.
3. Run `python3 strip_ws_query.py`.
4. Open `http://127.0.0.1:8080/` in Chrome and start a console.
5. Do steps A3 to A6.
   - Expected result: the two values are different.
6. Stop the script with Ctrl+C. Start it again within 5 seconds.
7. Wait until the console shows `[reconnect] reconnected!`.
8. Open a file. Then open a new terminal.
   - Expected result: the file and the terminal do not open.
9. For a control test, set `STRIP = False` in the script. Then reload the page and do steps 6 to 8 again.
   - Expected result: the server logs `The client has reconnected.`, and the file and the terminal open.

In step 6, both WebSockets close. Thus we expect the same result as the SageMaker test: a second `Starting extension host process...` in the server log, and a console that does not respond.

```python
"""Forward 127.0.0.1:8080 to 127.0.0.1:8000.

Remove the query string from WebSocket upgrade requests only, as the
SageMaker Studio proxy does. Forward all other requests unchanged.
"""
import asyncio

LISTEN = ("127.0.0.1", 8080)
TARGET = ("127.0.0.1", 8000)
STRIP = True  # Set to False for the control test.


async def pipe(reader, writer):
    try:
        while data := await reader.read(65536):
            writer.write(data)
            await writer.drain()
    except ConnectionError:
        pass
    finally:
        writer.close()


async def handle(client_reader, client_writer):
    try:
        head = await client_reader.readuntil(b"\r\n\r\n")
    except (asyncio.IncompleteReadError, asyncio.LimitOverrunError):
        client_writer.close()
        return
    if STRIP and b"\r\nupgrade: websocket" in head.lower():
        line, rest = head.split(b"\r\n", 1)
        method, target, version = line.split(b" ", 2)
        print("removed query from:", target.decode(errors="replace"), flush=True)
        head = b" ".join((method, target.split(b"?", 1)[0], version)) + b"\r\n" + rest
    server_reader, server_writer = await asyncio.open_connection(*TARGET)
    server_writer.write(head)
    await asyncio.gather(pipe(client_reader, server_writer),
                         pipe(server_reader, client_writer))


async def main():
    server = await asyncio.start_server(handle, *LISTEN)
    print(f"Forwarding {LISTEN} to {TARGET}", flush=True)
    async with server:
        await server.serve_forever()


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Expected or desired behavior:

- After a reconnection, files, terminals, and the console continue to work.
- If the server cannot continue the old connection, Positron shows an error and asks for a reload. Positron does not stop with no message.

## Were there any error messages in the UI, Output panel, or Developer Tools console?

No error shows in the UI. These logs come from the test in steps A1 to A12 on 2026-10-02.

The browser opened the page at 22:09 UTC with these two tokens:

```
Creating a socket (renderer-Management-dd9da04e-e996-44f2-89ce-91bdb9541f5d)...
Creating a socket (renderer-ExtensionHost-73a00b6c-b64e-4e37-861f-426d7a0b1647)...
```

While the network was off, the browser showed the URL that it uses. The URL contains the token:

```
WebSocket connection to 'wss://<app-id>.studio.us-east-2.sagemaker.aws/jupyterlab/default/positron/positron/releases-467ff390dd8b4ffc8972ebb84d9e05a1fd5a4fe2?reconnectionToken=dd9da04e-e996-44f2-89ce-91bdb9541f5d&reconnection=true&skipWebSocketFrames=false' failed:
```

When the network came back, the browser reconnected both connections:

```
[remote-connection][ExtensionHost][73a00…][reconnect] reconnected!
[remote-connection][Management   ][dd9da…][reconnect] reconnected!
```

The server log shows different IDs from the start, and new connections instead of reconnections:

```
[22:09:04] [127.0.0.1][d99c6541][ManagementConnection] New connection established.
[22:09:05] [127.0.0.1][dbc48c6b][ExtensionHostConnection] New connection established.
[22:09:05] [127.0.0.1][dbc48c6b][ExtensionHostConnection] Starting extension host process...
[22:11:13] [127.0.0.1][2826e022][ExtensionHostConnection] New connection established.
[22:11:13] [127.0.0.1][2826e022][ExtensionHostConnection] Starting extension host process...
[22:11:16] [127.0.0.1][1e3c14ae][ManagementConnection] New connection established.
[22:11:42] [127.0.0.1][d99c6541][ManagementConnection] The client has disconnected, will wait for reconnection 3h before disposing...
```

The browser tokens start with `dd9da04e` and `73a00b6c`. The server IDs are `d99c6541` and `dbc48c6b`. After the reconnection, the server started a second extension host process (`2826e022`). The server never logged `The client has reconnected.`

In an earlier case at 17:54 UTC, only the management WebSocket closed (code 1006). The browser logged `reconnected!`, and the server logged a new connection. The console continued to work, but files and terminals did not open.

## Evidence that the proxy removes the query string

We sent one HTTP request and one WebSocket request from the browser console, each with a query string. Jupyter logged what arrived:

| Request from the browser | What reached Jupyter |
|---|---|
| `fetch('/jupyterlab/default/positron/proxy/1/http-probe?probe=http-query')` | `403 GET /jupyterlab/default/positron/proxy/1/http-probe?probe=http-query` |
| `new WebSocket('wss://<host>/jupyterlab/default/positron/proxy/1/ws-probe?probe=ws-query')` | `uri='/jupyterlab/default/positron/proxy/1/ws-probe'` |

A second test sent a WebSocket request to a small server in the space that logs all request headers. The request arrived as `GET /ws-probe HTTP/1.1`. No header contained the query string, and the proxy added no `X-Forwarded-*` headers. Thus, the token cannot be recovered behind the proxy.

Only the SageMaker proxy is between the browser and Jupyter. tornado logs the request target as it receives it.

## Code references (tag 2026.09.1-2)

- The browser puts the token and the reconnection flag in the query string: [browserSocketFactory.ts#L288](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/2026.09.1-2/src/vs/platform/remote/browser/browserSocketFactory.ts#L288) and [remoteAgentConnection.ts#L235](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/2026.09.1-2/src/vs/platform/remote/common/remoteAgentConnection.ts#L235).
- The server reads the token from the query string. If the token is missing, it makes a new random token: [remoteExtensionHostAgentServer.ts#L247-L263](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/2026.09.1-2/src/vs/server/node/remoteExtensionHostAgentServer.ts#L247-L263).
- The server log ID is the first 8 characters of the token: [remoteExtensionHostAgentServer.ts#L331](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/2026.09.1-2/src/vs/server/node/remoteExtensionHostAgentServer.ts#L331).
- After a reconnection, the browser sends its unacknowledged messages again: [ipc.net.ts#L974-L990](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/2026.09.1-2/src/vs/base/parts/ipc/common/ipc.net.ts#L974-L990).
- The server ignores a Regular message with an unexpected ID and asks for a replay: [ipc.net.ts#L1015-L1022](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/2026.09.1-2/src/vs/base/parts/ipc/common/ipc.net.ts#L1015-L1022).

## Impact

- In SageMaker Studio, each close of the management WebSocket stops files and terminals until a reload. Users report this as "Positron locked up".
- In one space, the server log shows no `The client has reconnected.` line in 10 days.
- The same log shows about 18,000 new management connections in 3 bursts, one every 2 to 3 seconds. Each burst started when the main management WebSocket closed. One burst continued for 11 hours. We think that these are failed reconnection attempts. We do not know why each attempt closes after about 1 second.
- The same log shows 34 extension host starts with no page load. No old host exited immediately before these starts. We think that these are failed reconnections of the extension host. Each extra process uses memory.
- During a burst, jupyter-server-proxy records the traffic as activity. If idle shutdown is on, the bursts can keep the app running.

## Suggested fixes

1. Send the reconnection token and the reconnection flag in a place that proxies keep:
   - the URL path, for example `/<base>/reconnect/<token>/<true|false>`, or
   - the first handshake message (`auth` or `connectionType`).

   Keep the query string as a fallback for compatibility.
2. Make the failure visible. In the `ok` reply of the handshake, send the token that the server uses. If the browser asked for a reconnection and gets a different token, show the "Cannot reconnect" dialog. This change alone removes the silent failure.
3. On the server, close a new connection if its first Regular message has an ID that is not 1. A new browser connection always starts at 1. A different ID shows a reconnection that the server did not recognize.

For the SageMaker image, we can add a workaround. A small WebSocket shim in the page moves the query string into the path. Then jupyter-server-proxy moves it back. This workaround helps only our image. A fix in Positron also helps any other proxy that removes the query string.

## Related issues

- #16248: a corrupted message from the browser causes the same symptom (files and terminals stop, but the console works). The trigger is different.
- #16276: on Workbench with session SSL, a closed connection stops the extension host. The cause is different.
- #15901: navigation away from the tab stops the extension host. The cause is different.

title: Variables pane shows a stale summary after an environment is modified in place
description: Found while reviewing https://github.com/posit-dev/ark/pull/1436. I've searched for a pre-existing issue, because I basically expected one, but didn't find one (yet?). When an environment is modified in place, its row in the Variables pane keeps the summary from when the variable was first assigned. ```r e <- new.env() e$x <- 1 ``` Run these lines one at a time. After the second line, `e` still shows "Empty Environment [0 values]", and it has no expand arrow, because it was marked as having no children when it was assigned. `e <- e` doesn't update either. (For an S7 object built on an environment, which has properties and so can be expanded, expanding shows the new bindings even though the collapsed summary is still stale.) The Variables pane decides which rows to rebuild by comparing each variable's object address before and after. Modifying an environment in place doesn't create a new object, and assigning an environment to itself doesn't copy it, so the row never looks changed. This probably affects other things that are modified in place too, such as R6 objects (which are environments) and data.tables changed with :=. I've only confirmed it for plain environments and S7 objects built on environments.

title: data explorer: sort/filter ~40-70% slower since #16166
description:
Since #16166 merged on Sep 23, Data Explorer sort and filter have been about 40-70% slower in the e2e performance metrics.

|---|---|---|---|
| sort, pandas | 1208 | 2028 | +68% |
| sort, tibble | 1083 | 1863 | +72% |
| filter, pandas | 1441 | 2095 | +45% |
| filter, tibble | 1359 | 1891 | +39% |

Windows went up about 35-55%. File loads (csv, tsv, parquet) went up about 20-30%. `to_code` and loading an in-memory data frame didn't change. 

The jump falls between two runs:
* Build 92 (`492c845`, [run](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/actions/runs/35883611958)) had a Linux sort median of 1142ms. 
* Build 94 (`f6c4d9c`, [run](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/actions/runs/35890545062)) hit 2289ms, and it has stayed there. 

The only other commit in that range is #16063 (rstudioapi console document id), which doesn't touch the data explorer. Ark is the same build on both sides, and the test and page objects didn't change.

The test that identified it:
`data-explorer-performance.test.ts`: open the column menu, click Sort Descending, then wait for the status bar idle icon.

Claude's guess:
It is the new cell placeholders. Cells that are still loading used to render nothing. They now render `TableDataCellPlaceholder` with a fade-in and an infinite 1.5s pulse. A sort refetches every visible cell, so the grid fills with animated elements for a moment. CI runners have no GPU, which would fit the Linux/Windows slowdown with no visible change on macOS.

To confirm, run the perf spec on Linux at `492c845` and `f6c4d9c`. Or turn off the placeholder animations on `f6c4d9c` and see whether sort drops back to ~1.1s.

title: Refresh tables opened from Data Connections
description:
## Data Explorer: Refresh tables opened from Data Connections

### Problem

When a table is opened in the Data Explorer from the Data Connections pane, changes made to that table outside Positron never appear. Rows added, removed, or updated by another tool, a script, or another user stay invisible until the Data Explorer tab is closed and the table is opened again, which also loses the user's sort and filters.

Each Data Connections driver builds its Data Explorer view once, when the table is opened, and caches the schema and row counts. SQLite also reads through a snapshot it copies when the table is opened. For drivers that read the live table, this means the grid can show new rows under a stale row count.

Other Data Explorer sources already stay current:

- Data frames from the Python and R consoles update automatically, because the kernel notifies the Data Explorer when the variable changes.
- Data files opened with DuckDB (CSV, Parquet, etc.) are re-imported when the file changes on disk.

### Proposal

Add a **Refresh** action to the Data Explorer for tables opened from Data Connections.

- Refresh appears as the leftmost button in the right group of the Data Explorer toolbar, matching where refresh sits in the Data Connections and Variables panes. It is also available from the Command Palette as "Data Explorer: Refresh".
- It is shown only when the table's driver supports refresh: SQLite, PostgreSQL, Redshift, Snowflake, Databricks, and ODBC. It is not shown for console data frames or data files, which already update on their own.
- Refresh rebuilds the view from the table's current contents (schema, row counts, and the SQLite snapshot), then reloads the grid and the summary panel.
- The user's sort and row filters are kept, matched to the refreshed table by column name:
  - A sort on a column that no longer exists is dropped.
  - A filter on a column that no longer exists stays in the filter bar, marked invalid with "Column was removed", and is not applied. This matches how the Python and R backends handle a data frame whose columns change.
  - A filter that can no longer be evaluated (for example, because its column changed type) is marked invalid with the database's error, and the remaining filters still apply.
- If the table can't be read (it was dropped, or the connection is down), the existing data stays on screen and an error notification explains why.
- The button is disabled while a refresh is in progress.

### Out of scope

- `.duckdb` databases opened through Data Connections. The connection holds the database file's lock, so nothing outside Positron can change the file while it's connected.
- Refreshing pins.
- Automatic refresh (polling or change notifications from the database).

### Notes

- Extensions that provide Data Explorer backends opt in by implementing a new optional `refreshDataset(datasetId)` method on `positron.DataExplorerRpcHandler`.
- Refresh reloads through the same path as a schema change, so the grid scrolls back to the top, as it does when a DuckDB data file is reloaded.

title: Assistant: Third-party reasoning models silently drop reasoningEffort due to missing forceReasoning: true in providerOptions
description:
## System details:

#### Positron and OS details:
- Positron Assistant: 1.3.1
- OS: macOS (Apple Silicon) / Linux / Windows

#### Session details:
- LLM model: Any third-party or custom endpoint reasoning model (e.g. DeepSeek Reasoner, Qwen, Gemini, GLM via custom endpoint / local proxy)
- Cross-ref: https://github.com/posit-dev/assistant-feedback/issues/101

## Describe the issue:

When using third-party reasoning models (or models accessed via custom endpoint / OpenAI-compatible proxy using either `completions` or `responses` protocol) with `thinkingEffort` enabled, the `reasoning` / `reasoning_effort` parameters are silently dropped by `@ai-sdk/openai` before the request is sent over the network.

### Root Cause Analysis

Positron Assistant uses `@ai-sdk/openai` under the hood. In `@ai-sdk/openai`:
1. Whether a model is a reasoning model is determined by regex matching the model ID (`/^o(\d+)/` or `gpt-5+`):
   ```ts
   let U = (h = P?.forceReasoning) != null ? h : T.isReasoningModel;
   ```
2. For custom / third-party models, `T.isReasoningModel` evaluates to `false`.
3. Positron Assistant constructs `providerOptions.openai` as:
   ```ts
   // In extension.js
   providerOptions: {
     openai: {
       store: false,
       reasoningEffort: t.thinkingEffort,
       reasoningSummary: "detailed"
     }
   }
   ```
   Notice that `forceReasoning: true` is missing.
4. Because `forceReasoning` is `undefined` and `isReasoningModel` is `false`:
   - Under **Responses API**: `@ai-sdk/openai` skips generating `{ reasoning: { effort: ... } }`.
   - Under **Chat Completions API**: `@ai-sdk/openai` explicitly strips the field (`T.reasoning_effort = undefined`).
   - In both cases, reasoning effort is silently dropped and the backend model never performs reasoning.

## Steps to reproduce the issue:

1. Configure any OpenAI-compatible or Responses API endpoint with a non-o-series reasoning model (e.g. `deepseek-reasoner`, `qwen-3.8-flash`, etc.).
2. Select the model in Positron Assistant and choose any thinking effort level (e.g. `medium`, `high`, or `max`).
3. Send a prompt and inspect the HTTP request payload arriving at the proxy/endpoint.
4. Observe that neither `reasoning_effort` nor `{ reasoning: { effort: ... } }` is present in the request body.

## Expected or desired behavior:

When `thinkingEffort` is enabled (`yd(t.thinkingEffort)`), Positron Assistant should pass `forceReasoning: true` in `providerOptions.openai`:

```diff
- ...b ? { store: false, reasoningEffort: t.thinkingEffort, reasoningSummary: "detailed" } : {}
+ ...b ? { store: false, forceReasoning: true, reasoningEffort: t.thinkingEffort, reasoningSummary: "detailed" } : {}
```

This tells `@ai-sdk/openai` to skip the model ID regex heuristic and preserve the reasoning parameters.

## Temporary Workaround:

Patching `extension.js` directly:
```bash
perl -pi -e 's/store:!1,reasoningEffort:/store:!1,forceReasoning:!0,reasoningEffort:/g' ~/.positron*/extensions/posit.assistant-*/dist/extension.js
```

title: Copilot models are missing from the model picker on first load
description:
Copilot models are missing from Posit Assistant on first load.

Positron core resolves provider enablement from the AI provider catalog, and both lookups return `false` while that state is still loading — so `selectLanguageModels` filters out Copilot models that were already discovered. 

## Steps to reproduce

1. Authenticate GitHub Copilot.
2. Open the model picker in Posit Assistant.
3. No Copilot models are listed.

## Expected behavior

Copilot models appear in the picker when Copilot is authenticated

## Evidence

Same session, four seconds apart:

```
09:29:45.247 [info]  [vscode.lm] Fetched 26 models (providers: copilot (26))
09:29:49.982 [info]  Posit Assistant is now active!
09:29:49.982 [trace] [vscode.lm] Starting a fresh model discovery host call
09:29:50.689 [trace] [vscode.lm] Reusing completed model discovery from 696 ms ago
09:29:50.689 [warning] [vscode.lm] Fetched 0 models
```

The `696 ms` is measured from the fresh flight at `49.982`, not the successful discovery at `45.247` (which would read ~5400 ms) — so the second activation queried the host and got nothing back. Credentials did not change in that window. Also `[PositronDirectModelService] 0 models from 17 providers`: 17 providers known, zero models.

## Root cause

Three gates in `selectLanguageModels` (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/languageModels.ts:1726`) call `isProviderEnabled`. Gate 3 (line 1765) produces the observed `Fetched 0 models` — the 26 models are already in `_modelCache` and each is skipped on the way out.

Two independent defects make `isProviderEnabled('copilot')` return `false` when the truthful answer is "not known yet":

**1. Unmatched registration reads as disabled** — `positronAssistantService.ts:212`

```ts
isProviderEnabled(providerId: string): boolean {
    for (const source of this._providerRegistrations.values()) {
        if (source.provider.id === providerId || source.provider.catalogId === providerId) {
            return this.isSourceEnabled(source);
        }
    }
    return false;   // "not registered yet" is indistinguishable from "disabled"
}
```

**2. Empty catalog reads as everything disabled** — `abstractAiProviderService.ts:89`

```ts
isEnabled(id: string): boolean { return this._byId.get(id)?.enabled === true; }
```

`_byId` is empty until the catalog fetch completes, and initialization is async (`whenInitialized`, line 46). Nothing in `selectLanguageModels` awaits it. `isSourceEnabled` routes `catalogId`-declaring sources straight to this with no fallback, while sources *without* a `catalogId` get an explicit "catalog never heard of it, stay enabled" grace.

The same pattern appears at `positronAssistantService.ts:296` (`areCompletionsEnabled`) with no registration fallback at all.

The failure is silent because `extHostLanguageModels.selectLanguageModels` (line 498) filters unresolvable identifiers out via `.filter()` without raising, so a gated-out provider looks identical to one with no models.

## Precedent for the fix

`providerStatusCommand.ts:198-224` hits this exact problem and already solves it — it awaits `whenInitialized` under `raceTimeout`, checks `status === 'ready'`, and reports enablement as `undefined` rather than `false` when the catalog was not read, suppressing only on a *known* `false`. `selectLanguageModels` collapses those three states into a boolean.

## Introduced by

| Date | Commit | PR | Defect |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-07-24 | `7861f5e397e8` | #15094 | `isEnabled()` returns `false` for an unloaded catalog |
| 2026-07-29 | `b5f496b442c2` | #15121 | `isProviderEnabled()` rewritten with the `return false` fallthrough |

Before #15121 the lookup was settings-based and consulted no async state, so the race was not reachable. The three gates in `selectLanguageModels` date to #11490 and were correct against the synchronous lookup.

## System details

- Positron 2026.09.1 build 2
- Posit Assistant 1.4.1
- Affects `release/2026.08`, `release/2026.09`, and `main` (both functions verified byte-identical on `release/2026.09`)
- Downgrading Assistant has no effect — the defect is in Positron core

## Related

- #11033 (closed) — inverse case on 2026.01, predates the catalog migration
- #11452 — earlier "zero models for every vendor" failure guarded in this same code path

title: MCP: `positronViewer.screenshot` fails with the 32 KB result limit when called through `run_positron_command`
description:
_Originally posted by @jeffkeller-einc in https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/discussions/16280#discussioncomment-18881848_:

Not sure if this is the right place for this feedback, @jmcphers, but I'm loving the new Positron MCP server from #16196. Being able to use Claude Code, rather than a Claude Console API key, is a nice cost saving. I've been using it with the Claude Code for VS Code extension.

One snag: the 32 KB tool output cap makes `positronViewer.screenshot` unusable in most cases. With a Shiny for Python app in a normal-sized Viewer pane, the screenshot came back as:

> The command returned 95212 bytes, over the 32768 byte limit, in a shape that cannot be shortened. Ask for less, or run the equivalent code with execute_code.

The command takes no arguments, so the agent has no way to "ask for less". By contrast, `get_plot` returns a Plots pane image fine, which I assume is because it comes back as MCP image content instead of going through `run_positron_command`'s result.

-------

## Problem

When an MCP client (for example, Claude Code) calls `positronViewer.screenshot` through `run_positron_command`, the agent gets an error and no image. With a Shiny for Python app in a Viewer pane of normal size, the result was:

```
The command returned 95212 bytes, over the 32768 byte limit, in a shape that cannot be shortened. Ask for less, or run the equivalent code with execute_code.
```

The command has no arguments, so the agent cannot ask for less. In the same setup, `get_plot` returns the Plots pane image correctly.

## Cause

The MCP path does not know that a command can return an image. Three layers are involved:

1. **Positron core.** `positronViewer.screenshot` returns an `IAgentCommandImage` (`{ kind: 'image', mimeType, data, note }`, with base64 PNG data). See `src/vs/workbench/contrib/positronPreview/browser/positronViewerAgentCommands.ts`. The `positronCommand` tool in Posit Assistant knows this shape and shows it as an image.
2. **positron-supervisor.** `McpFrontendChannel.runCommand` sends every command result through `budgetCommandResult` (`extensions/positron-supervisor/src/mcpCommandResult.ts`). The budget is 32 KB of JSON. A screenshot has no array to make shorter, so the function replaces the result with the message above.
3. **Kallichore.** If the result did get through, `run_positron_command` (`crates/kcserver/src/mcp/handler.rs`) puts it into structured JSON. It does not make an MCP image content block. The agent would get approximately 95 KB of base64 text, not an image.

`get_plot` works because it has its own path at each layer. The channel handles `positron.mcp.getCurrentPlot` before the budget, and Kallichore decodes the data URI into an image content block.

I think the order of the PRs kind of explains how we ended up with this problem. First #16196 added the MCP server, then #16304 added the Viewer commands with image results, and connected images only to Posit Assistant. Today `positronViewer.screenshot` is the only command that returns `AgentCommandImage` but a new image command in the future will have the same problem.

## Possible fix

- **Kallichore:** In `run_positron_command`, find results with the shape `{ kind: "image", mimeType, data, note? }`. Return them as `get_plot` does: an image content block, with `note` and `status` in the structured body. Add a test next to `test_get_plot_returns_the_current_plot_as_an_image`.
- **positron-supervisor:** In `runCommand`, do not apply `budgetCommandResult` to results with the image shape. Add a test case in `mcpCommandResult.test.ts` or `mcpFrontendChannel.test.ts`.

title: Navigating away from a browser tab kills the extension host
description:
In web/server deployments, navigating away from the Positron tab (browser back gesture, clicking a link) terminates the extension host immediately instead of honoring the reconnection grace period. Hitting forward does not get the original extension host back: the reconnect is rejected because its token no longer maps to a live connection ("Unknown reconnection token (seen before)"), so the client falls back to a fresh connection and the server forks a new host.

The `positron-server` process itself is unaffected and stays healthy throughout. It forks an extension host on demand when a client requests one, and normally hands an existing host a new socket when a client reconnects with a known token, so the machinery for surviving a disconnect is already there and simply is not reached here.

Reported in rstudio/rstudio-pro#12590: a user triggered the trackpad back gesture while Posit Assistant was working, hit forward to return, and the chat had stopped. Assistant's agent loop runs in the extension host, so it dies with the host. R and Python kernels survive because they belong to the detached Kallichore supervisor, which is why only Assistant appears to stop.

## Cause

The browser workbench listens for `pagehide` and treats it as an orderly shutdown. But `pagehide` fires on ordinary navigation, not just tab close, so a back gesture makes the client send the server a graceful "I'm quitting" disconnect rather than simply letting the socket drop.

That distinction determines whether the extension host survives:

| How the client goes away | Server behavior |
|---|---|
| Graceful disconnect message | Immediate teardown, no grace period |
| Socket just drops | Waits for reconnection (3h by default) |

So a network outage preserves the session for three hours, while a tab navigation kills it instantly -- even though the grace period and its buffered message replay exist precisely so the extension host can survive a disconnected client and pick up where it left off.

Relevant code:

- `src/vs/workbench/services/lifecycle/browser/lifecycleService.ts:45` -- the `pagehide` listener that starts the shutdown
- `src/vs/workbench/services/extensions/common/abstractExtensionService.ts:220-229` -- shutdown handler that ends the remote connection
- `src/vs/workbench/services/remote/common/abstractRemoteAgentService.ts:253` -- sends the graceful disconnect
- `src/vs/server/node/remoteExtensionManagement.ts:74-82` -- server's two paths: immediate teardown vs. 3h grace
- `src/vs/workbench/api/node/extensionHostProcess.ts:245-252` -- same split inside the extension host process
- `src/vs/server/node/remoteExtensionHostAgentServer.ts:517-548` -- reconnect with a known token reuses the existing host (`acceptReconnection`); an unknown token is rejected and a fresh host is forked
- `src/vs/server/node/extensionHostConnection.ts:350` -- where the extension host process is actually forked

## Expected

Navigating away should be treated as a disconnect that honors the grace period, not a user-initiated quit, so returning reconnects to a still-running extension host.

Affects Positron Server / Posit Workbench (web only, not desktop).

title: Epic: 2026.11 Agentic Data Science
description:
## Why this matters

Last milestone, Positron became reachable from any agent harness via MCP and skills, but an agent that works through Positron still sees less than the user does. It cannot see Quarto chunks that run inline, the Data Viewer, widget output, or the help pages installed on the machine. This milestone, we plan to close these gaps so that agents act on the same state that the user looks at.

## Theme 1: Make Quarto documents a first-class agent surface

Agents treat a `.qmd` as a notebook or as plain text, but it is sort of neither and both at the same time. As a result, agents cannot reach chunks that run inline, visual mode removes the document from context, and generated documents come out broken. In #14733 we'll look at the core API, and then deal with the other issues for symptoms on the same path.

- [ ] #14733
- [x] #9326
- [x] #13077
- [x] #10666
- [ ] #12838

## Theme 2: Let agents see what the user sees

Positron gives the active editor to the agent as context only when it is a plain text file. Positron does not include data frames, rendered output, or the R and Python help installed on the machine. As a result, the agent uses its memory instead of what the user can see.

- [x] #8709
- [ ] #16377
- [ ] #15724
- [x] #16040

## Theme 3: Make the skills surface work everywhere

We built and tested the `positron-commands` skill on Desktop. Workbench and other remote hosts need different paths and different instructions, and the skill invocation needs to be more polished.

- [ ] #15914
- [ ] #15953
- [ ] #15778

## Theme 4: The Final Theme

title: Positron notebook loses dirty state after window reload on web
description: **Note for Triage:** I'm adding the `workbench` tag here, because this would potentially impact these users once that gets released to them, but I can't guarantee if it'd be reproducible there. --- On web (Chromium), an unsaved untitled Positron notebook is restored after a window reload **without** its dirty state. The tab comes back showing the close (X) affordance instead of the dirty dot, and `.tab.active.dirty` matches no element. On Electron the same notebook stays dirty after reload. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Run Positron on web (e.g. the `e2e-chromium` server build). 2. Create a new Positron notebook (`Untitled-1.ipynb`) - the tab is dirty. 3. Reload the window (Developer: Reload Window). 4. The notebook is restored from its working-copy backup and `Untitled-1.ipynb` is active again, but the tab is no longer marked dirty. ## Expected vs. actual - Expected: a restored unsaved notebook keeps its dirty state (as on Electron), so the user still sees it has unsaved changes. - Actual (web): the restored notebook is clean; no dirty indicator. ## Context Found while fixing the e2e test `notebook-untitled-naming.test.ts` (added in #14262). The post-reload `isDirty` assertion failed only on Chromium; #14285 relaxed that assertion and left a comment pointing here. The name-increment behavior (#13561) is unaffected; this is specifically about the dirty marker _not_ surviving a reload on web. ## To do (when this is addressed) If wanted, https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/14285/changes#diff-408d16e6b990479ccc99df9cf96e7bb5e646aa8cf7923727256fe80b0ab1f535R48-R50 can be changed back to older version with stricter assertion (although that would be like testing two different things in a single test). Alternatively, separate test.step or test to assert dirtiness could be added. TBD depending on how complex the fix for this would be.

title: Notebooks: Up/Down arrow at first/last line of a cell should move the cursor to the adjacent cell
description:
In Positron notebooks, pressing Down arrow on the last line of a cell editor (or Up arrow on the first line) does nothing - the cursor stops at the cell boundary.

User feedback:

> Something else I was hoping to fix but probably requires more work: to make j/k work across cells. So that when I'm at the last line of cell, and I press j, I go the first line of the next cell (and vice versa with k).

> FWIW: VS Code does this out of the box for notebooks. You can go through all the lines across cells using arrow keys without needing to exit and enter cells. It makes the notebook feel more like a single document.

## Expected behavior

- Pressing Down on the last line but mid-column should first move the cursor to the end of the line (stock Monaco behavior, matching browser textboxes and JupyterLab)
- A second Down should cross into the next cell
- Reverse for Up

## Bonus: vim j/k

It would be great if j/k traversed across cells in vim mode too: in normal mode, `j` on the last line of a cell moves to the first line of the next cell, `k` on the first line moves to the last line of the previous cell, ideally preserving the column as vim vertical motions do.

In insert mode, arrow keys can match the standard behavior.

If we add boundary context keys and focus-next/previous commands, vim users could opt in with a user keybinding, or we could add it as an alternate keybinding like in https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/15740.

```json
{
    "key": "j",
    "command": "positronNotebook.focusNextCellEditor",
    "when": "positronNotebookCellEditorFocused && vim.mode == 'Normal' && notebookEditorCursorAtBoundary != 'top'"
}
```

```

N/A

## Describe the issue:

VS Code Customizations (extensions and settings) aren't supported in Positron's Dev Containers implementation.

These customizations aren't formally part of the Dev Container spec; it simply provides for tools to define their own `customizations`:

https://containers.dev/implementors/json_reference/#image-specific

The actual VS Code customizations are documented here:

https://containers.dev/supporting#visual-studio-code

## Steps to reproduce the issue:

Create a dev container file with a VS code customization, e.g. from https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/devcontainers/containers#_create-a-devcontainerjson-file

```json
{
  "image": "mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/typescript-node",
  "forwardPorts": [3000],
  "customizations": {
    // Configure properties specific to VS Code.
    "vscode": {
      // Add the IDs of extensions you want installed when the container is created.
      "extensions": ["streetsidesoftware.code-spell-checker"]
    }
  }
}
```

Open the devcontainer in Positron and observe that the customizations are not applied.

## Expected or desired behavior:

VS Code customizations also apply to Positron.

It's debatable whether we should use a `positron` key instead of (or in addition to) `vscode`, but I suspect most people using devcontainers will be sharing with people using VS Code, so reading the `vscode` key seems like a good start.

title: Data Connections: a slow look-ahead query delays the whole tree level
description:
### Problem

The Data Connections tree fetches some children before it shows a level. We call this a look-ahead. Two places in `dataConnectionsTreeInstance.tsx` do a look-ahead:

- `_breadcrumbNamespaceGroups` (#15859) fetches the children of a namespace group, such as "Schemas" or "Databases". The tree uses the result to show a single schema as a breadcrumb, or to hide it.
- `_wrapViewsGroup` (#16641) fetches the children of a "Views" group. The tree uses the result to hide the group when it is empty.

The tree waits for these fetches before it shows any row at that level. If one fetch is slow, all rows at that level wait. For example, the "Tables" row does not show until the Views query is complete. If a fetch never returns, the level never shows, because the look-ahead has no timeout.

The risk is highest on cloud warehouses such as Redshift, Snowflake, and Databricks. On these, a metadata query can take several seconds.

The Views look-ahead in #16641 makes this problem more frequent. The namespace look-ahead runs about once for each connection while the Views look-ahead runs each time the tree shows a schema.

### Expected behavior

A slow look-ahead must not stop the tree from showing a level. If the tree does not get an answer in a short time, it shows the group row, as it did before the look-ahead existed.

### Possible approach

Race each look-ahead against a short timeout (for example, 1 second) with `raceTimeout`. If the timeout occurs first, the tree keeps the row and does not cache the children. The tree already does this when a look-ahead fails. When the user expands the row, the tree fetches the children in the usual way.

Questions to answer:

- What is the correct timeout value? Is the timeout for each call, or one budget for each level?
- If the result arrives after the timeout, does the tree discard it or use it? If the tree uses it, it must not write to `_lookAheadChildren` after a reload. A late write leaves a stale entry in memory.
- Can the expand use the query that is still in progress, instead of a second query?

### Testing

Add a Vitest case with fake timers. Make `nodeGetChildren` never resolve for the group. Advance the timers past the timeout. Make sure that all rows at the level show, including the group row.

title: Log an info message when the Posit AI provider is disabled by the Workbench default
description:
## Problem

On Workbench, the authentication extension disables the Posit AI provider on first activation so that admins control AI access — it writes `providers.positai.enabled: false` into `~/.posit/ai/providers.json` (`applyPwbPositAIDefault` in `extensions/authentication/src/pwbDefaults.ts`).

This is intentional and desirable, but it is currently silent. Someone trying to enable Posit AI sees the provider simply missing from the provider list (core drops disabled providers before the modal renders) with nothing in the logs explaining why. Debugging requires knowing to look at `~/.posit/ai/providers.json` and knowing that the Workbench default exists at all.

Today the only log emitted from this path is a `log.warn` on failure.

## Proposal

Emit an info-level log message when the Workbench default is applied, including:

- that Posit AI is being disabled because of the Workbench default (and that admins can enable it)
- the path of the file being written (e.g. `~/.posit/ai/providers.json`)

Something like:

```
[info] Posit AI is disabled by default on Workbench; wrote providers.positai.enabled=false to /home/user/.posit/ai/providers.json. An administrator or user can enable it in that file.
```

Nice-to-haves, if cheap:

- also log when the default is skipped because it was already applied or the provider was already configured, so the "why isn't this showing up?" question is answerable from the log alone
- more generally, log when any provider is resolved as disabled and from which file, since a missing or `false` catalog entry both count as off (see the comment in `extensions/authentication/src/extension.ts`)

## Files

- `extensions/authentication/src/pwbDefaults.ts`
- `extensions/authentication/src/providerCatalog.ts` (`saveProviderEnabled`, config path resolution)

## Related

- #12954 — original issue introducing the Workbench default

title: Quarto: have core tell each extension its hidden notebook URI
description:
Positron core builds a hidden notebook for every open Quarto document. `quartoNotebookUri` in `src/vs/workbench/contrib/positronQuarto/browser/quartoVirtualNotebookService.ts` computes that notebook's URI from the source URI, in four pure lines.

The extensions need the same URI. After #16153, a Quarto session uses it for two things: 

- the selector of its language client
- the ownership key it claims for its cells

Core does not tell the session what the URI is, so `positron-r` and `positron-python` each derive it again from `RuntimeSessionMetadata.notebookUri`.

That makes three copies of one rule, and core owns the original. A drift between them is a correctness bug rather than a style problem. The extension then names a notebook that core never built, and its selector matches nothing. The document loses the features its own session exists to serve.

The extension copies also have to guess. An untitled document from _Quarto: New Document_ carries no file extension. The path alone cannot say whether the session belongs to a Quarto document or to a real notebook. `isQuartoDocumentUri` answers that with a language id, a `.ipynb` clause, a notebook-type-in-the-query clause, and a fallback for a document that has not opened yet. Core needs none of this. There is nothing left to guess once the extension is told the answer.

### What goes away

About 100 lines per extension, all of it one question: what is the hidden notebook URI for this document?

- `QUARTO_PATH_PATTERN`, `QUARTO_LANGUAGE_IDS`, and `NOTEBOOK_PATH_PATTERN`
- `isQuartoDocumentUri` and `quartoCellsUriFor`
- the `_quartoCellsUri` lazy getter and its `_resolvedQuartoCellsUri` cache
- `QUARTO_CELLS_SCHEME` and `quartoCellsNotebookPath` in `quarto-cells.ts` and `quartoCells.ts`

### What stays

About 30 lines per extension: `quartoNotebookOf`, `quartoCellsKey`, `isOwnedQuartoCellUri`, `QUARTO_CELL_SELECTOR`, and `_claimOwnQuartoCells`. This half reads the ownership registry instead of re-encoding a rule that core encodes separately. It is the half least likely to drift in silence.

Each extension keeps a registry of its own. Ownership is per language, so an R session's claim must not silence the Python console client for the same document's Python chunks.

### Proposed shape

Add an optional field to `RuntimeSessionMetadata` (`src/positron-dts/positron.d.ts:794`). `quartoNotebookUri` is pure in the source URI, so core can answer at session creation time, before the hidden notebook exists.

A command such as `positron.quarto.getCellsNotebookUri(sourceUri)` is the alternative. A field is better IMO for two reasons. It needs no await when the language client is created, and it cannot fail because the Quarto contribution has not loaded yet. Either shape touches the Positron API surface, so I am _not_ doing this as part of https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/16153.

### Considered and rejected

**A shared package for the duplicated code.** Local packages are normal here, in the shape of `extensions/positron-data-explorer-{protocol,formatting,duckdb}`. Two things argue against one. A shared package wraps core's own facts in a nicer container instead of deleting them. A `file:` dependency resolved through plain Node rather than a bundler also gives both extensions one module instance. That merges the two registries and brings back the cross-language bug the separate copies avoid.

**Core owns the routing, or the registry.** Ownership is per language, and a core-owned registry has no language dimension. Core also cannot route a request to the right provider on its own. Completion, hover, and definition arrive through `vscode.languages` by way of the language client, so core cannot attribute a provider to a session. `registerStatementRangeProvider(selector, provider)` carries no session identity either. The decision has to stay with the extensions.

### Fallback, if this turns out to be really difficult

Guard the duplicated block with a raw-text test of about 25 lines, in the shape of `extensions/quartoCells-copies.vitest.ts`. That guard cannot cover these two copies as it stands, because they differ in comments and in Prettier wrapping. It needs no product change, and it can be deleted once the handoff lands.

### Why this is not in #16153

The selector, the ownership key, and the claim all change shape. That retires the `quartoCellsUriFor` unit tests in both extensions, the untitled classification cases, and the e2e acceptance and regression runs that branch already passed. It is a second full validation pass for a maintainability change that fixes no user-visible bug.

title: uv Python setup fails on Windows: "spawn uv ENOENT" after fresh uv install
description:
When Positron installs uv for the user and then tries to install a Python version, the install step fails with `Failed to install Python 3.14: Error: spawn uv ENOENT` even though uv installed successfully moments earlier. This happens mostly because `uv` isn't on the path yet. 

Reported via reddit:

https://www.reddit.com/r/RStudio/comments/1vybexp/question_on_positron_and_python_failed_to_install/

## Root cause

`installPythonVersionAndGetPath()` in `extensions/positron-python/src/client/pythonEnvironments/common/environmentManagers/uvPythonInstaller.ts` calls `execUv` with the literal command `'uv'`:

```ts
execUv('uv', ['python', 'install', installTarget], ...)
execUv('uv', ['python', 'find', version], ...)
```

Every other uv call routes through `UvUtils`, which locates the binary and uses the resolved path (`uvUtils.command`, e.g. `~\.local\bin\uv.exe`). Right after a fresh install, uv is **not** on the running extension host's PATH -- the installer only updates shell rc / registry PATH, which the already-running process doesn't pick up. So the bare `'uv'` spawn fails with `ENOENT`, while the resolved absolute path works.

## Evidence (from the user's log)
```
> uv --color never python dir                    (bare 'uv' probe -> fails, falls back)
> ~\.local\bin\uv.exe --color never python dir   (resolved path -> works)
> ~\.local\bin\uv.exe --color never python list  (resolved path -> works)
Installing Python 3.14 via uv...
> uv --color never python install 3.14           (bare 'uv' -> ENOENT)
Failed to install Python 3.14: Error: spawn uv ENOENT
```

The bare-`'uv'` probe already failing (and the fallback to `~\.local\bin\uv.exe` succeeding) confirms uv is not on this session's PATH.

> Note: this is not strictly "uv" vs "uv.exe" -- bare `'uv'` would resolve fine if it were on PATH. The bug is that this one code path uses the literal `'uv'` instead of the located binary path that the rest of the flow already resolved.

## Fix (suggested)

Use the resolved uv command in `installPythonVersionAndGetPath` instead of the literal `'uv'` (route through the located `UvUtils` / `uvUtils.command`, same as the other callers). The existing comment there says it avoids `installUvPython` "to avoid cache issues," but `resetUvCache()` has already run after install, so the located command is current -- the resolved path can be used safely.

**Platform:** Windows. Not reproducible where uv is already on PATH.
