title: Saving a notebook replaces its session when the kernel is not the preferred interpreter
description:
## Summary

When you save an untitled notebook, its session moves to the new file. If the notebook uses an interpreter that is not your preferred interpreter, Positron then replaces that session with a new session for the preferred interpreter. You lose your variables and loaded packages, and this error shows:

```
Error refreshing variables: The language runtime exited before RPC completed for client 'positron-variables-r-6-cddd2a40'. Error (-32603)
```

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a new R notebook. Positron starts your preferred R version (for example, R 4.6).
2. Change the kernel to a different R version (for example, R 4.4).
3. Run a cell with `x <- 1`. The Variables pane shows `x`.
4. Save the notebook to a file.

**Result:** The error above shows. The kernel log shows a new session for the preferred R version. The Variables pane is empty until you run the cell again.

**Expected:** The session that ran `x <- 1` continues under the new file name, with the kernel that you selected.

If you keep the preferred interpreter in step 2, the problem does not occur.

Positron version: daily build, 2026-10-07, macOS.

## Cause

1. Save As calls `updateNotebookSessionUri`, which moves the session to the new URI ([notebookEditorInput.ts](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/f7a361ee31dab72905c82930051d9dc30edfe3f0/src/vs/workbench/contrib/notebook/common/notebookEditorInput.ts#L271), [PositronNotebookEditorInput.ts](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/f7a361ee31dab72905c82930051d9dc30edfe3f0/src/vs/workbench/contrib/positronNotebook/browser/PositronNotebookEditorInput.ts#L253)).
2. Positron keeps the kernel selection for each notebook URI, so the new URI has no selected kernel. `getOrSelectKernel` then selects the kernel for the preferred runtime ([runtimeNotebookKernelService.ts](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/f7a361ee31dab72905c82930051d9dc30edfe3f0/src/vs/workbench/contrib/runtimeNotebookKernel/browser/runtimeNotebookKernelService.ts#L427-L445)).
3. `ensureSessionStarted` finds the moved session at the URI, but the runtime of that session does not match the selected kernel ([runtimeNotebookKernel.ts](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/f7a361ee31dab72905c82930051d9dc30edfe3f0/src/vs/workbench/contrib/runtimeNotebookKernel/browser/runtimeNotebookKernel.ts#L482)). It calls `selectRuntime` ([runtimeNotebookKernel.ts](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/f7a361ee31dab72905c82930051d9dc30edfe3f0/src/vs/workbench/contrib/runtimeNotebookKernel/browser/runtimeNotebookKernel.ts#L547)), which replaces the moved session.
4. The old session exits while the Variables pane refreshes. As a result, the refresh fails with the error above.

The rename path calls `updateNotebookSessionUri` too ([notebookEditorInput.ts](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/f7a361ee31dab72905c82930051d9dc30edfe3f0/src/vs/workbench/contrib/notebook/common/notebookEditorInput.ts#L344), [PositronNotebookEditorInput.ts](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/f7a361ee31dab72905c82930051d9dc30edfe3f0/src/vs/workbench/contrib/positronNotebook/browser/PositronNotebookEditorInput.ts#L376)), so a rename probably has the same problem. I did not test a rename.

## Possible fix

Move the selected kernel to the new URI in the same step that moves the session, for Save As and for rename. Another option: if a notebook has a session but no selected kernel, select the kernel that matches the runtime of the session, not the preferred runtime.

## Related

- #8737 reported a kernel reset after Save As as a CI flake. A user report in that issue has the same steps as above. The team closed it because nobody could reproduce it. The interpreter mismatch is a probable reason.
- #9070 (language features after Save As) is a different problem. #11988 closed it with a fix to session restore.

title: Go to References shows an unknown service error while an R console session runs
description:
### Environment

- Positron 2026.10.0 build 266 (VS Code 1.134.0), macOS 27.0.1, R 4.6.1
- Also reproduced on Positron 2026.09.1-2 (VS Code 1.130.0), macOS 26.6.2 arm64, R 4.6.0
- Fresh profile, launched with `--user-data-dir`, `--extensions-dir` and `--logsPath` pointing into it, and `HOME` set to an empty folder
- Settings: `files.simpleDialog.enable: true`, `window.dialogStyle: custom`, `window.menuStyle: custom`
- `GitHub.copilot-chat` disabled with `--disable-extension`

### Steps to reproduce

1. Launch Positron with no folder open and wait a few seconds for startup to finish.
2. Click Start Session.
3. In the list of interpreters, choose R.
    - The console shows the R startup banner and the R prompt.
4. Choose Go -> Go to References from the menu bar.
    - An error notification appears:

```
[invokeFunction] unknown service 'editorProgressService'
```

    - The developer console gets:

```
Error: [invokeFunction] unknown service 'editorProgressService'
    at _InstantiationService._throwIfStrict (workbench.desktop.main.js:437863:13)
    at Object.get (workbench.desktop.main.js:437645:18)
    at GoToReferencesAction.runEditorCommand (workbench.desktop.main.js:149531:38)
    at _InstantiationService.invokeFunction (workbench.desktop.main.js:437650:14)
    at CodeEditorWidget.invoke
```

### What happened

Go to References fails with an error notification while an R console session is running. No file is open, only the Welcome tab.

On Positron 2026.10.0 build 266, one run showed the notification and console error above. The R session was started from the Start Session button and Go -> Go to References was chosen from the menu bar by hand. With no session running, Go -> Go to References did nothing visible and logged no error in one run.

On Positron 2026.09.1-2, a script of these steps reproduced it in 5 of 6 runs. With no session running, 3 scripted runs showed no error. The same steps have not been tried in VS Code.

### What I expected

Go to References to show references or say there are none, without an error.

See issue #9915, which reported the same error from Go to References, and other right-click commands, in a Positron Notebook cell. It is closed.

title: positron-r logs a TypeError reading 'uri' after Save Workspace As with no folder open
description:
### Environment

- Positron 2026.09.1-2 (VS Code 1.130.0), macOS 26.6.2 arm64
- Also reproduced on Positron 2026.10.0 build 266 (VS Code 1.134.0), macOS 27.0.1
- Fresh profile, launched with `--user-data-dir`, `--extensions-dir` and `--logsPath` pointing into it, and `HOME` set to an empty folder
- Settings: `files.simpleDialog.enable: true`, `window.dialogStyle: custom`, `window.menuStyle: custom`
- `GitHub.copilot-chat` disabled with `--disable-extension`

### Steps to reproduce

1. Launch Positron with no folder open, and wait a few seconds for startup to finish.
2. Choose File -> Save Workspace As... from the menu bar.
    - The Save Workspace dialog opens in the home folder.
3. Click OK, keeping the suggested name.
    - The workspace is saved as `~/workspace.code-workspace` and the window reloads into it.
    - A few seconds after the reload, the developer console gets:

```
[positron.positron-r]Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'uri')
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'uri')
	at Jk (/Applications/Positron.app/Contents/Resources/app/extensions/positron-r/dist/extension.js:79:3526)
	at La (/Applications/Positron.app/Contents/Resources/app/extensions/positron-r/dist/extension.js:79:3146)
	at Zk (/Applications/Positron.app/Contents/Resources/app/extensions/positron-r/dist/extension.js:79:3042)
	at B2 (/Applications/Positron.app/Contents/Resources/app/extensions/positron-r/dist/extension.js:347:1713)
	at AbstractExtHostExtensionService._callActivateOptional (extensionHostProcess.js)
```

    - The same TypeError is logged a second time from `Vk` and `Uk`, followed by "An unknown error occurred. Please consult the log for more details."
    - The extension host log (`window1/exthost/exthost.log`) gets:

```
[error] TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'uri')
```

### What happened

positron-r throws a TypeError as it activates in a workspace that has no folders. Nothing on screen shows it: no error notification appears.

On Positron 2026.09.1-2, a script of these steps reproduced it in 4 of 4 runs, 2 of them with a new Jupyter notebook open first. With a folder opened first (File -> Open Folder..., then <kbd>Enter</kbd> to accept the home folder), the same scripted steps logged no TypeError in 3 runs.

On Positron 2026.10.0 build 266, these steps followed by hand once (File -> Save Workspace As...) logged the same TypeError in `exthost.log`. Running Workspaces: Save Workspace As... from the Command Palette instead of the File menu, scripted once, gives the same result.

The frame at `extension.js:79:3526`, read in the installed positron-r, reads `workspace.workspaceFolders[0].uri` after checking only that `workspaceFolders` is defined. In a workspace with no folders the list is empty.

### What I expected

positron-r to activate in a workspace with no folders without an error.

See issue #11217, which also starts from Save Workspace As and is about the restart that follows it, but reports a different symptom. See also issue #9612, which reports the same TypeError after removing the last folder from a workspace.

title: Propagate Connect credentials from Publisher to R/Python sessions
description: ## System details: #### Positron and OS details: ``` Positron Version: 2026.10.0 build 285 Code - OSS Version: 1.134.0 Commit: d8c7bc7a9d9e5202bddd7d53a1fad9d48e1f09db Date: 2026-10-06T14:03:50-07:00 Electron: 42.8.1 Chromium: 148.0.7778.280 Node.js: 24.18.1 V8: 14.8.178.38-electron.0 OS: Darwin arm64 27.0.0 ``` ## Steps to reproduce the issue: Sign into Connect via the Publisher extension. Then start an R session, make sure `pins` is installed, then run: For searchability: ``` Error in `check_auth()`: ! auth = `auto` has failed to find a way to authenticate: • `server` and `key` not provided for `auth = 'manual'` • Can't find CONNECT_SERVER and CONNECT_API_KEY envvars for `auth = 'envvar'` • Can't find any rsconnect::accounts() for `auth = 'rsconnect'` ``` The R session doesn't know about your Connect account, so you have to sign into Connect again with the rsconnect package, or manually put the env var values somewhere. ## Notes It shouldn't be necessary to sign into Connect multiple times inside Positron. The Publisher extension already registers a `posit-connect` auth provider; the work here would be on the Positron side to read credentials from that provider and propagate them to the R session in a useful way.

title: Feature Request: Data Explorer support for `.sas7bdat` and `.xpt` files.
description:
### Discussed in https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/discussions/16461
Originally posted by **samiulhq** October 6, 2026 > sas7bdat or xpt files types are very common in Pharma. Duckdb has an extension for it https://duckdb.org/community_extensions/extensions/read_stat > Can we find a way to incorporate this into Positron Data Viewer?
Currently, these file types can be loaded into an R/Python session and opened in the Data Explorer that way. However, bundling additional DuckDB extensions would allow the same quick-open behavior from the Explorer pane we see with e.g. .csv files. One possible path to consider would be to allow users to specify a list of extensions to install into the DuckDB instance backing Data Explorer, which then get transformed into `INSTALL [extension] FROM community;` calls. From 🤖: > > For example, a list of extension names plus a mapping from file extension to table function: > > "dataExplorer.duckdb.extensions": ["read_stat"], > "dataExplorer.duckdb.fileReaders": { "xpt": "read_stat", "sas7bdat": "read_stat" } > > The backend would run INSTALL ... FROM community; LOAD ..., and the editor resolver would register the extra file types. Today that list is the hard-coded DUCKDB_SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS, so it would need to read the setting instead. It's flexible, but there are three problems: > - Security on macOS. The file viewer's DuckDB is created with allow_unsigned_extensions so our re-signed Excel extension will load. As far as I know DuckDB only lets you set that at startup, so any extension users load into that same instance would skip DuckDB's signature check. User extensions would need their own worker that keeps signature checking on. > - Admin control. In Posit Workbench, admins would want to be able to turn this off. Enforcing the setting through POSITRON_ENFORCED_SETTINGS would handle that. > - Offline installs. INSTALL needs network access, so this wouldn't work in airgapped environments. That's acceptable for an opt-in feature.

title: Packages pane: filtering a scrolled list renders an empty pane
description:
## System details: #### Positron and OS details: Positron dev build from source (`main` @ 9684f4d133, version 1.130.0), Electron. macOS (Darwin 25.5.0). #### Session details: Python 3.10.12 (Pyenv) — but the bug is not language-specific; it reproduces for any Packages list long enough to scroll. ## Describe the issue: Filtering the Packages list while it is scrolled renders an **empty pane**, even though packages match the filter. The list has to be scrolled by only one row for this to happen. The state is stable — it does not recover on its own (verified over 2.5 minutes of polling). Scrolling back up, or resizing the pane, restores the rows immediately. **Root cause:** `PositronListInstance.setEntries()` updates the row count and calls `fireOnDidUpdateEvent()`, but never clamps the grid's vertical scroll offset to the shrunken content height: https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/browser/positronList/classes/positronListInstance.tsx#L211 The only clamp against `maximumVerticalScrollOffset` on a content change lives in `DataGridInstance.setSize()`, which runs on resize: https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/browser/positronDataGrid/classes/dataGridInstance.tsx#L1907 So when a filter shrinks the model, the stale offset can sit past the new end of the content and the virtualized render window contains no rows at all. This is also why resizing the pane "fixes" it — that is the code path that clamps. **Blast radius:** this is in the shared list instance, not the Packages pane, so any `PositronList` consumer whose entry count can shrink while scrolled is affected (Packages pane, Connections schema navigation, the control gallery). **Suggested fix:** clamp the vertical scroll offset in `setEntries` (or have it call the same clamp `setSize` uses), rather than fixing it per consumer. ## Steps to reproduce the issue: 1. Start a Python session in an environment with enough packages to make the Packages list scrollable (~200 packages, e.g. the e2e `requirements.txt` environment). 2. Open the Packages pane. 3. Scroll the list down — one row is enough. 4. Type a package name into "Filter packages" that narrows the list to a small number of matches (a single match is the clearest case). 5. The list renders no rows. 6. Scroll up, or drag the sidebar edge to resize the pane — the matching row appears. ## Expected or desired behavior: Filtering shows the matching packages regardless of the list's prior scroll position. ## Were there any error messages in the UI, Output panel, or Developer Tools console? No errors. The rows are simply absent from the DOM: the accessibility tree shows a `grid` node with no children, and a DOM query for `.packages-list-item` returns 0 while the filter is applied. Measured directly during an e2e run — filter applied, then one wheel-up, no other change: ``` [PROBE filtered] rows=0 :: [PROBE after-wheel-up] rows=1 ::

title: Python kernel stops responding to all requests when a session starts shortly after a prior session exits (wedges mid-startup, before the LSP handshake)
description:
When a new Python console session starts within a few seconds of a previous Python session's kernel exiting, the new kernel can go completely unresponsive: code execution is accepted but never runs, and no error is ever surfaced. ### Evidence Caught via e2e flake triage on `Console Pane: Python > Python - Verify console commands are queued during execution` (`test/e2e/tests/console/console-python.test.ts`). [See test history here](https://connect.posit.it/e2e-test-insights/?author=Marie+Idleman&time=today&tab=test_health&date=0&branch=main&search=test/e2e/tests/console/console-python&sort=pain&test=Console+Pane:+Python+%3E+Python+-+Verify+console+commands+are+queued+during+execution%7C%7C%7Ctest/e2e/tests/console/console-python.test.ts). I pulled full log evidence (kernel logs, supervisor logs) for 2 representative occurrences (one electron/ubuntu, one chromium/ubuntu web) to confirm the mechanism. Both show the identical signature: - A prior Python session's kernel exits cleanly (`status 'idle' => 'exited'`). - A new Python session starts 2-9 seconds later. - The new kernel logs `Starting Positron LSP server`, but **never** logs the following `Starting Positron LSP client on port ` confirmation that a healthy startup always produces within ~10ms (confirmed against the healthy first session in the same run, which got this line 9ms after its own `Starting Positron LSP server`). - From that point on, the kernel's own log shows zero further activity of any kind — no comm handling, no execute_request. - The supervisor log confirms a subsequent `execute_request` (submitted by the test, e.g. `456 + 456`) *was* sent to the correct kernel over the shell channel, but got no `busy` transition and no reply, for the remainder of the capture (11+ seconds). This is a full kernel freeze, not a wrong-session-targeting issue — the request reaches the right kernel, the kernel just stops answering anything after starting its LSP server. Usually hits the *second* session started in a run, but not always: one occurrence (`4564d9ba`) wedged a standalone first session with no prior session in the log at all. Seen on ubuntu electron, ubuntu web, and windows electron, which e2e-test-insights groups as a single pattern (49 occurrences over 30 days). Consistent with a CI-load/timing-sensitive threading race rather than a deterministic bug. ### Suspected mechanism **Update:** the fault is confirmed to be inside the kernel process, not the supervisor. See [this comment](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/15060#issuecomment-5181388272) for the current state; the next step is a `py-spy dump` on a hung kernel. - ~~`PositronLanguageServer.start_tcp()`~~ **RULED OUT** (see [this comment](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/15060#issuecomment-5181388272)): the `positron.lsp` comm_open is sent about 1s *after* the kernel has already stopped reading its shell socket, so the missing `LSP client on port` line is a symptom, not the trigger. Original text: `PositronLanguageServer.start_tcp()` (`extensions/positron-python/python_files/posit/positron/positron_lsp.py:508-568`) spawns a daemon thread that creates its own event loop and calls `run_until_complete(start_server())`. Something on this thread appears to stall in a way that also blocks the kernel's main thread/loop (not just the LSP subsystem), which would point at a GIL-holding or otherwise non-yielding call somewhere in that path — worth a `py-spy dump` on a hung repro. - Separately, and independent of the above: `PythonRuntimeSession.activateLsp()` (`extensions/positron-python/src/client/positron/session.ts:701-712`) awaits `KallichoreSession.startPositronLsp()` (`extensions/positron-supervisor/src/KallichoreSession.ts:515-533`) with **no timeout**. That promise only resolves on a `server_started` comm message; if the kernel never sends it, the wait is permanent. Adding a timeout there wouldn't fix the underlying kernel stall, but it would turn a silent, permanent freeze into a visible, recoverable error. ### Repro 1. Start a Python console session. 2. Let its kernel exit (e.g. delete the session). 3. Immediately start a new Python console session. 4. Try to execute code in the new session. 5. Check whether `Starting Positron LSP client on port ` ever appears in the Kernel Supervisor log for the new session. Steps 1-3 raise the odds but are not required: the kernel has also wedged on a first session with no prior session in the run. The reliable tell is the kernel's own debug log (`Python Kernel.log`) stopping partway through the startup comm burst, right after a message it finished handling. ### E2E Triage Diagnosis
🟢 High confidence -- Product bug, already filed as #15060. The Python kernel of the run's second session stops answering the shell channel entirely; the execute_request for '456 + 456' is delivered to its ZMQ Shell socket and never produces execute_input, iopub busy, or execute_reply. New multi-occurrence evidence overturns #15060's suspected trigger: the wedge begins ~950-980ms BEFORE the positron.lsp comm_open is sent, so the never-completed LSP handshake is downstream of an already-wedged kernel, not its cause. - **Test:** [Console Pane: Python > Python - Verify console commands are queued during execution](https://connect.posit.it/e2e-test-insights/?tab=test_health&repo=positron&test=Console%20Pane%3A%20Python%20%3E%20Python%20-%20Verify%20console%20commands%20are%20queued%20during%20execution%7C%7C%7Ctest%2Fe2e%2Ftests%2Fconsole%2Fconsole-python.test.ts) - **Targeted failure:** waitForConsoleContents('912', { expectedCount: 1, timeout: 10000 }) at console-python.test.ts:52 -- locator('.console-instance[style*="z-index: auto"] div span').getByText('912') resolved to 0 elements - **Signal:** Three occurrences examined (A 41d49167 ubuntu/electron, B c9e25fd1 ubuntu/electron, C 6a315bee ubuntu/chromium). Shell is serial, so the Nth kernel busy/idle transition pairs with the Nth send; pairing validated on A and B (send-type sequence == busy-reason sequence exactly, serial-pairing-consistent=true). A: 12 sends, 8 answered, last answered 17:14:08.105 comm_msg setConsoleWidth, first unanswered 17:14:08.122 comm_open positron.help, lsp comm_open 17:14:09.103 (+981ms), execute_request 17:14:10.774. B: 12 sends, 9 answered, last answered 21:16:10.131 comm_open positron.help, first unanswered 21:16:10.137 comm_msg setConsoleWidth, lsp comm_open 21:16:11.086 (+949ms), execute_request 21:16:15.648. Neither session ever logged 'Starting Positron LSP client on port N'; healthy first sessions get it 11-17ms after 'Starting Positron LSP server'. Both preceded by a clean prior-session exit (A: 17:14:00.915 code 0, 2s before; B: 21:15:59.545, 11s before). Kernel process alive but frozen: cpu_percent 0, memory_bytes byte-identical (163471360) across 12 consecutive samples; heartbeat socket connected with initial heartbeat received and no failure logged. C confirms the coarse signature (prior exit 21:36:28.245 -> new session 21:36:32.811 -> LSP server started 21:36:40.600, no LSP client line, execute_request forwarded at 21:36:43 unanswered) but its lane logs at [info] so it cannot test the ordering claim. - **Frequency:** 32/405 runs (7.9%) on main, ubuntu/electron, ubuntu/chromium - **Hypothesis:** Duplicate of #15060. Two refinements. (1) The LSP is not the trigger: in both occurrences with debug-level logs the kernel had already stopped answering ~1s before the positron.lsp comm_open was sent, so PositronLanguageServer.start_tcp() cannot be what stalls the kernel, and the missing 'LSP client on port' line is a symptom. (2) No single message's handler is at fault: across an otherwise identical 12-message startup sequence the wedge lands at index 8 in A and index 9 in B (one message apart), which is the signature of a timing-sensitive race in the startup comm burst rather than a poisoned handler. That also rules out the setConsoleWidth handler (ui.py _set_console_width takes no locks), PositronComm.handle_msg's send_lock (acquired inside the handler, after ipykernel publishes busy -- and no busy was published for the first unanswered message in either occurrence), and the post-handler stdout/stderr flush of the preceding message (which completed, since its idle was published). Remaining candidates, not discriminated by these logs: (a) the kernel's main asyncio loop / _main_asyncio_lock, or a blocking IOPubThread._event_pipe.send inside _publish_status('busy'), versus (b) a block or silent non-delivery on the supervisor side -- kcserver logs 'sending to Jupyter socket Shell' for every unanswered message, and the '#15060 precondition' that a prior session exited seconds earlier is more naturally explained by shared state in the long-lived kcserver process than by anything inside a brand-new Python process. Discriminating (a) from (b) needs a py-spy dump on a hung kernel plus a kcserver-side send confirmation log; the control-channel discriminator was unavailable because every capture ends before session teardown.

title: Testing: Automated tests with latest assistant against older Positron versions
description:
## Description

Posit Assistant supports Positron 2026.04.0 and later, but our e2e tests only run it against the newest Positron builds (dev builds in `positron`, daily release builds in `positron-builds`). Nothing checks that a new Assistant release still works on the older Positron versions it claims to support.

Extension host tests cover part of this, but not real UI flows against a real model provider. We need e2e coverage that installs an older Positron release plus the Assistant build being released, and runs the Assistant tests against them.

### Motivating case: auth moving into Assistant

Auth is moving out of Positron core and into Assistant. After that change, Assistant has to keep working on older Positron versions where core still owns sign-in. Today nothing tests that combination.

## Challenges

1. **Supported range.** Which Positron versions do we test? Every release since 2026.04, or a rolling window (e.g. the last N monthly releases)? Where is the support policy recorded?
2. **UI drift between versions.** The e2e tests on `main` target the current Positron UI. Positron-side page objects (console, settings, quick access, toasts) may not match an older build, so we can't just run `main`'s tests against an old release.
3. **Hidden fixture dependencies.** The Assistant tests also rely on shared fixture data, not just code. For example, `test/e2e/fixtures/settings.json` sets `assistant.sidebarView` and `assistant.experimentalFeatures`. When code drifts, the TypeScript compile fails. When data drifts, the test just fails at runtime with an unrelated-looking error.
4. **Where the tests live.** Moving the Assistant e2e tests into the assistant repo would split the test infrastructure across two repos that have to be kept in sync. Preference is to keep everything in `positron`.

## Proposed approach: overlay

Positron already has a `release/YYYY.MM` branch per release, and those branches carry the e2e tests matching that build. A compatibility run could:

1. Check out `release/<positron version>`, which provides the harness, fixtures, and Positron-side page objects.
2. Overlay the Assistant page objects and specs from `main`, which match the Assistant build being tested.
3. Install that Positron release plus the Assistant build under test, pinned rather than the floating dev build from `checkForDevBuildUpdate`.
4. Run only the Assistant tests.

For the overlay to stay reliable:

- **Isolate the Assistant test files** under their own directories (e.g. `test/e2e/pages/assistant/`, `test/e2e/tests/assistant/`), so the overlay is a single path.
- **Keep Assistant-specific data out of shared fixtures.** Move the `assistant.*` settings out of the shared `settings.json`, and have the Assistant specs apply them with stable APIs like `settings.set()`.
- **Limit what the Assistant files import from the harness** to a small set of long-lived APIs (`Code`, `Toasts`, `HotKeys`, `_test.setup`, ...).
- **Check the boundary on PRs.** For PRs touching the Assistant e2e files, overlay onto the oldest supported release branch and compile only. This is fast and catches harness drift when it's introduced.

Version checks inside page objects should be the exception, kept to flows whose ownership actually changes between versions. Sign-in is the clear case: core-owned before the auth change, Assistant-owned after.

### Alternatives considered

- **Versioned or forked page objects per Positron version:** every locator fix has to be backported to N copies, and the copies drift apart.
- **Version checks throughout the page objects:** fine for a few spots, but they pile up if this is the main mechanism.
- **Move the tests to the assistant repo:** see challenge 4.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A workflow that takes a Positron version and an Assistant build, and runs the Assistant e2e tests against that pair
- [ ] Assistant e2e files isolated, with no Assistant-specific data in shared fixtures
- [ ] PR check that compiles the overlay against the oldest supported release branch

title: Data Connections: rewriting an ODBC config file silently kills open connections while the pane still shows them connected
description:
## System details: #### Positron and OS details: Positron 1.134.0 (dev build, `midleman/odbc-flake` off `9fdec31e64`), macOS 26.6.2 (arm64) #### Session details: No interpreter session needed. ODBC via unixODBC + the SQLite ODBC driver. ## Describe the issue: Rewriting an ODBC configuration file kills every open data connection's handle, but the Data Connections pane goes on showing those connections as connected. Clicking anything in the dead subtree fails with `Connection handle N not found`. The ODBC extension watches each config file it resolved and re-registers all of its drivers when one changes ([extension.ts:108](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/extensions/positron-data-driver-odbc/src/extension.ts#L108)). Re-registering disposes the previous registration first, and the disposable returned by `registerDriver` releases every connection handle that driver ever minted ([extHostDataConnections.ts:87](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/api/common/positron/extHostDataConnections.ts#L87)). `_releaseConnectionHandle` deletes the entry from `_connections` and `_nodes` on the extension host side only. `PositronDataConnectionsService` is never told, so its instance list, the Connected badge, and the expanded subtree all survive a connection that no longer exists. Every handle-bearing call then throws: `$nodePreview` and `$nodeGetChildren` reject with `Connection handle N not found`, no Data Explorer opens, and the user is left with a toast and a tree that still looks healthy. This is not limited to a tool rewriting the file. Any create, change, or delete event on a watched path does it, including installing a driver or editing a DSN by hand while Positron is open. ## Steps to reproduce the issue: 1. Define a working ODBC DSN (this used SQLite via `brew install unixodbc sqliteodbc`, with `ODBCSYSINI` and `ODBCINI` pointed at a scratch directory). 2. Open the Data Connections pane and expand the detected connection down to a table. The tree loads, and the connection shows as connected. 3. Rewrite `odbc.ini`. The contents can be byte-for-byte identical; the watcher fires on the write, not on a diff. The ODBC extension logs `ODBC configuration changed (...); reloading drivers.` 4. Double-click the table. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a2455a0a-f746-4087-bee2-c340a1c7e876 ## Expected or desired behavior: Either the connection keeps working across a driver reload, or the pane reflects that it is gone. What should not happen is the pane reporting a connection as live when its handle has been released. The core fix is for driver removal to tear its instances down through `PositronDataConnectionsService` rather than dropping handles behind the service's back. That fixes this for every driver, not just ODBC. A narrower ODBC-side fix (skip the dispose-and-re-register when the rediscovered config is unchanged) would close the common path but leaves the underlying mismatch in place for any other driver that unregisters while connections are open. ## Were there any error messages in the UI, Output panel, or Developer Tools console? A toast on the double-click: ``` Could not open 'elements' in the Data Explorer: Connection handle 1 not found ``` ## CI impact This is the mechanism behind a flake in `Workbench: Posit Pro Drivers > Browses a detected connection to data in the Data Explorer` (`test/e2e/tests/workbench/pro-drivers/pro-drivers-odbc-discovery.test.ts`). The test double-clicks a table, no Data Explorer opens, and `waitForIdle` burns its full 60s waiting on `.status-bar-indicator .icon.idle`. ### E2E Triage Diagnosis
🟢 High confidence -- A file-watcher event on any watched ODBC config file makes the ODBC extension re-register its drivers; the disposal that precedes re-registration releases every connection handle the driver minted, on the extension-host side only. PositronDataConnectionsService is never told, so the pane keeps the Connected badge and the expanded subtree over a dead handle, and the double-click that follows throws 'Connection handle N not found' instead of opening a Data Explorer. - **Test:** [Workbench: Posit Pro Drivers > Browses a detected connection to data in the Data Explorer](https://connect.posit.it/e2e-test-insights/?tab=test_health&repo=positron&test=Workbench%3A%20Posit%20Pro%20Drivers%20%3E%20Browses%20a%20detected%20connection%20to%20data%20in%20the%20Data%20Explorer%7C%7C%7Ctest%2Fe2e%2Ftests%2Fworkbench%2Fpro-drivers%2Fpro-drivers-odbc-discovery.test.ts) - **Targeted failure:** toBeVisible() timeout on .status-bar-indicator .icon.idle after double-clicking a table in a detected ODBC connection - **Signal:** Reproduced locally on e2e-electron with all three CI symptoms. extHostDataConnections.ts:87 registerDriver's Disposable calls _releaseConnectionHandle for every handle in _driverConnections; _releaseConnectionHandle (line 311) deletes from _connections and _nodes with no main-thread notification. extension.ts:108 logs 'reloading drivers' on any create/change/delete of a watched path. A vitest (extHostDataConnections.vitest.ts, 3/3) proves $nodePreview and $nodeGetChildren reject with 'Connection handle N not found' after dispose, and that re-registering does not restore the handle. - **Frequency:** 8/36 runs (22.2%) on main, ubuntu/chromium - **Hypothesis:** Driver disposal releases connection handles behind PositronDataConnectionsService's back, leaving the UI's instance list describing connections that no longer exist.

title: Data Connections: Databricks OAuth U2M flow cannot complete on Posit Workbench
description:
## System details:

#### Positron and OS details:

Positron on Posit Workbench 2026.09.0+174.pro3, "Autumn Hawkbit" (4851e698), reported by @samiulhq in posit-dev/positron#16387.

#### Session details:

N/A (Data Connections pane)

## Describe the issue:

On Posit Workbench, connecting to Databricks from the Data Connections pane with the OAuth User-to-Machine (U2M) mechanism redirects the browser to a `localhost` URL instead of the Databricks sign-in completing, and the connection cannot be established.

Root cause, from reading the driver and the bundled SDK:

- The U2M mechanism maps to `authType: 'databricks-oauth'` in `extensions/positron-data-driver-databricks/src/databricksClient.ts`, which delegates the entire OAuth flow to `@databricks/sql`.
- The SDK's authorization-code flow starts an HTTP listener on `localhost` (default port 8030) in the extension host process and opens the authorize URL with the `open` npm package.
- On Workbench, the extension host runs on the remote server while the user's browser runs on their own machine. The browser launch happens server-side, and the `redirect_uri` of `http://localhost:8030` resolves on the user's machine, where nothing is listening.
- The driver does nothing remote-aware. There is no use of `vscode.env.openExternal` or `vscode.env.asExternalUri`. The bundled `@databricks/sql` v2.0.0 also doesn't expose its internal `openAuthUrl` hook through the client's connect options, so the browser-open step can't be intercepted through the public API.

The Snowflake driver's `externalbrowser` mechanism follows the same pattern and is likely affected as well, though I haven't verified yet.

What we'll want to do is run the authorization-code flow Positron-side (loopback listener plus `vscode.env.openExternal`, mapping the callback through `vscode.env.asExternalUri` and port forwarding), then hand the resulting token to the SDK through the `external-token`/`tokenProvider` path already used for Workbench managed credentials.

## Steps to reproduce the issue:

1. On Posit Workbench, enable `dataConnections.enabled` and open the Data Connections pane.
2. Add a Databricks connection and choose OAuth User-to-Machine (U2M).
3. Enter the Server Hostname and HTTP Path, then connect.

## Expected or desired behavior:

The OAuth flow opens the user's local browser, sign-in completes, and the redirect reaches the callback listener, as it does in desktop Positron.

## Were there any error messages in the UI, Output panel, or Developer Tools console?

The browser is redirected to a `localhost` URL (default port 8030) where nothing is listening. Exact error text from the reporter still to be confirmed.

## Workarounds:

Any of these should work in the meantime:

- Workbench Managed Credentials (requires admin-provisioned Databricks credentials for the session)
- Personal Access Token
- OAuth Machine-to-Machine (M2M) with a service principal

title: Agents cannot execute or observe Quarto documents in inline execution mode (epic: positron.quarto context API)
description:
## Problem

When a Quarto document runs in inline execution mode (`positron.quarto.inlineOutput.enabled`), its kernel session is started as a **notebook-mode** session with `notebookUri` pointing at the `.qmd` file (`quartoKernelManager.ts`, deliberate). When the `.qmd` editor is focused, that session becomes the foreground session, and `positron.runtime.getForegroundSession()` reports `sessionMode === 'notebook'`.

Posit Assistant (and any other agent surface) is therefore steered into notebook tools and away from `executeCode` -- but no notebook editor instance backs the session, so **every notebook tool fails**, and there is no tool-reachable way to execute code in the document's live kernel or observe its outputs at any level:

| Agent action | Result |
|---|---|
| `executeCode` | Error: "active session is a notebook session ... use notebookEdit/notebookRunCells" |
| `notebookRead`/`notebookEdit`/`notebookRunCells` (no path) | Error: "No notebook is open in the editor." |
| same tools with `path: report.qmd` | Error: "not a Jupyter notebook (.ipynb). Use the text tools" |
| `read`/`edit` on the `.qmd` | Works, but blind: cannot run chunks, cannot see chunk outputs or execution state |
| shell (`Rscript -e`, `quarto render`) | Fresh out-of-process interpreter: no access to the live session's state; prompt discourages it |

The error messages form a loop (executeCode says "use notebook tools"; notebook tools say "no notebook is open" / "use text tools"; text tools cannot run anything). The model typically burns several failing tool calls, then edits the document blind or falls back to out-of-session shell execution.

### Repro

1. Set `positron.quarto.inlineOutput.enabled: true`.
2. Open a `report.qmd` with an `{r}` chunk (e.g. `mean(mtcars$mpg)`), run the chunk inline so the kernel starts.
3. With the `.qmd` editor focused, ask the assistant: "Run the first chunk and tell me the result."
4. Observe the failure loop in the tool calls.

### Why this is not #14250

#14250 is the same symptom family for `.ipynb` in the legacy Jupyter editor, where the workaround is "reopen in the Positron Notebook Editor". A `.qmd` can never be opened in a notebook editor: the session is notebook-mode by design and the document is plain text by design, so **no in-session workaround exists**. Tightening the notebooks API around PNE instances (the likely #14250 direction) cannot resolve this case.

## The gap, precisely

Every piece of state an agent needs already exists in workbench services under `src/vs/workbench/contrib/positronQuarto/` -- parsed chunk structure (`IQuartoDocumentModelService`), execution state (`IQuartoExecutionManager`), outputs with content-hash staleness (`IQuartoOutputManager` + `IQuartoOutputCacheService`) -- but none of it crosses the extension-host boundary. Meanwhile the session metadata *does* cross the boundary and actively misidentifies the document class ("notebook") with no discriminator other than sniffing the `notebookUri` file extension.

The only ext-host-facing surfaces today are `positron.runtime.executeInlineCell(uri, ranges)` (returns `void` -- caller observes nothing) and session-targeted `positron.runtime.evaluateCode` (text-level results only, silent side-band evaluation).

## Plan (recommended design from the investigation)

Full analysis with candidate designs A-D lives in the investigation branch (`investigate/quarto-inline-agent-context`, `PROPOSAL-quarto-inline-agent-context.md`). Recommendation: **Design B (first-class `positron.quarto` context API in core), with C.1 (assistant-side session classification + prompt fix) shipped first as an immediate mitigation.** C.1 is a strict subset of B's assistant half.

Design A (overloading `positron.notebooks` to resolve Quarto documents) was rejected: it deepens the notebook/Quarto conflation that caused this bug and pulls against #14250. Design D (console-mode Quarto sessions) was rejected: session mode is load-bearing for lifecycle and variables-pane integration.

### API sketch (Design B)

```ts
positron.quarto.getContext(): Thenable<QuartoDocumentContext | undefined>
// { uri, executionMode, primaryLanguage, kernelState, sessionId?,
//   chunks: [{ id, label?, language, startLine, endLine, content,
//              executionStatus, hasOutput, outputStale }] }
positron.quarto.getChunkOutputs(uri, chunkId): Thenable<NotebookCellOutput[]>
positron.quarto.executeChunks(uri, chunkIds): Thenable<ChunkExecutionResult[]>
```

Anchored on the text editor + document model (mirroring how the notebook context anchors on the notebook editor instance). Decisions already made:

- Namespace: `positron.quarto` (rename only if a second inline-document format materializes).
- `.Rmd` in scope (core services already accept it via `isQuartoOrRmdFile`).
- Flag off (`positron.quarto.inlineOutput.enabled: false`): `getContext()` resolves **read-only** (chunk structure, no kernel/execution state); `executeChunks` errors clearly.
- Visual editor mode: deferred; v1 anchors on the active text editor.
- Staleness/read path anchors on the contentHash-keyed output cache (chunk IDs rotate on edit; the live output map has no id-remap).
- `executeChunks` re-resolves chunk addresses server-side (label where present, else content hash / containing line) and errors on ambiguity.
- Outputs carrying `webviewMetadata` (interactive/HTML view zones) get a defined downgrade (text fallback or explicit marker).

## Tasks

- [ ] **C.1 (posit-dev/assistant):** classify `quarto-inline` sessions (by `notebookName` extension), add a `quarto-session.md` prompt include replacing the misfiring `notebook-session.md`, and make the `executeCode` refusal message document-class-aware (keep the refusal: falling through would route code to a console, not the document's kernel).
- [ ] **Core (this repo):** `positron.quarto` API -- ext-host/main-thread pair over the four existing positronQuarto services, DTOs, `positron.d.ts`, tests.
- [ ] **Assistant adoption:** `quartoRead` (allow) + `quartoRunChunks` (ask) tools over the new API; edits stay with text tools; update vendored typings.
- [ ] **Follow-up:** core-side document-type discriminator in session metadata, so agent surfaces stop sniffing file extensions.
- [ ] **Related UX (separate issue):** #14732 -- stale output view zones are not marked/cleared when chunk source is edited.

title: Spike: Runtime cache: add external read-only cache and command to create it
description:
The runtime cache currently lives entirely in user storage and can only be populated by starting Positron itself and waiting for discovery to complete. This means that Positron's very first startup for a user will always be slower, since it needs to discover everything on the system before starting anything.

We can do better with two changes:

### Add ability to read cache from an external file

An external JSON file -- named by an environment variable, command-line parameter, or known path -- can be specified. When it is, the file's contents are loaded into the cache if it does not exist (or is empty), and the cache is treated as "warm" without doing a full discovery pass to populate it. Positron still does the cache revalidation in the background, and from then on the per-user cache is independent.

### Add command line argument to generate a cache file

Positron adds a new command-line argument that causes it to start in a headless mode, perform a full discovery pass, and write the results to a JSON file that can be read as described above. Environments that want to reduce first session startup time can run this command to generate a cache file for Positron to use later, in an interactive startup.

### Applications

This would make meaningful performance improvements in:

- tests, which currently do a full discovery pass on every test startup since tests do not share user state, and
- Posit Workbench, which is looking to minimize startup time for the first session

Relevant thread: https://positpbc.slack.com/archives/C04FPQK3H9C/p1779319317402859

title: R test explorer is polluted by "always on" behaviour of the Python test controller
description: In an R package, the test explorer's top toolbar shows several icons, including one for "Debug Tests" (play + bug) and one for "Run Tests with Coverage" (play + check). The R test explorer only supports *running* tests. There is no R test debugging or coverage integration at this time. Clicking either button does nothing (silent no-op), which is confusing. The situation is made worse by the lack of tooltips, tracked separately in #13854. Until/unless we add support for debugging (not even sure what this would mean or gain us?) or coverage (much more compelling, tracked in #2716), I think it would be nice to not see these icons up there. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Open an R package that uses testthat. 2. Open the test explorer. 3. Look at the TESTING view's title-bar icons: Refresh, Run, Debug (play+bug), Coverage (play+check), Show Output, `...`. 4. Click Debug or Coverage -> nothing happens. ## Root cause The title-bar Debug/Coverage buttons are upstream actions (`DebugSelectedAction` / `CoverageSelectedAction` in `src/vs/workbench/contrib/testing/browser/testExplorerActions.ts`), shown via `ExecuteSelectedAction` when: view == testing && !isRunning && hasDebuggableTests (resp. hasCoverableTests) Crucially, `hasDebuggableTests` / `hasCoverableTests` are **window-global** context keys. `testProfileService` (`capabilityContextKeys` in `src/vs/workbench/contrib/testing/common/testProfileService.ts`) ORs the capability bits across **every** registered test controller's profiles into a single key for the whole window. - **positron-r** registers a **Run-only** profile (`extensions/positron-r/src/testing/testing.ts`, `createRunProfile(..., Run, ...)`), so it contributes neither Debug nor Coverage. - **positron-python**'s test controller registers **Debug** (and Coverage) profiles (`extensions/positron-python/src/client/testing/testController/controller.ts`), and that controller is live in essentially every Positron window -- even one with zero Python tests. So Python flips the window-global Debug/Coverage flags to `true`, which renders those buttons in the **R** Testing view. Clicking runs the selected R tests in the Debug/Coverage group (`ExecuteSelectedAction.runInView` -> `runTests({ group: Debug })`); R has no profile for that group, so nothing runs. ## Experiment If I disable the Python extension and reload the window, the Debug and Coverage buttons go away, leaving only Run / Show Output / overflow. That's my evidence that the buttons are lit by positron-python's controller, not R's. The registered controllers are also visible via the Run-button chevron -> "Select Default Profile", which lists both "Python Tests" and "R Package Test Explorer" even when no Python tests exist. ## Possible ways forward The gate is one window-global flag, not per-controller or per-selection. R's controller can't suppress a capability advertised by Python's controller. So I don't see anything we could do in positron-r. 1. **positron-python: register the test controller / its Debug+Coverage profiles lazily** -- only once Python tests are actually present. Side effect: in R-only (or any non-Python) windows the Debug/Coverage buttons would correctly disappear. 2. **Upstream: scope the view-title Run/Debug/Coverage buttons** to the capabilities of the controller(s) that actually have items in the current selection/view, rather than a window-global OR. This is the "correct" fix but a behavioral change in core VS Code. 3. **At minimum, give feedback on click** -- e.g. surface the existing "no debuggable tests found" message instead of a silent no-op. (Mitigation, not a real fix.) ## System details Positron Version: 2026.07.0 build 308 Code - OSS Version: 1.118.0 Commit: 57648dbdb85d8f6996448ea6ccea1cf6a9d97df7 Date: 2026-06-27T05:46:10+02:00 Electron: 39.8.8 Chromium: 142.0.7444.265 Node.js: 22.22.1 V8: 14.2.231.22-electron.0 OS: Darwin arm64 25.5.0

title: R: Decide what to do with `.ps.*()` functions that live in positron-r
description:
The packages pane work has brought a question to the fore that really already existed: where to define R functions used to deliver some of the functionality in positron-r.

Up 'til #11897, we've always defined such functions in https://github.com/posit-dev/ark/tree/main/crates/ark/src/modules/positron and used `#' @export` to mark functions to put on the search path in a `tools:positron` namespace.

This comes with the downside that certain features require coordinated work in 2 repositories and an ark release.

Some of the options on the table:

* Keep putting all such functions in ark and the `tools:positron` namespace.
* Create a similar namespace with R code that lives in positron-r. Morally this is just a companion to `tools:positron`.
* Create a way for positron-r to register functions in `tools:positron` after the R session has launched.

title: Workspace symbols should not affect local diagnostics
description:
Diagnostics for defined symbols currently use workspace symbols as a source of definitions. This causes definitions in a file to silence "undefined symbol" diagnostics in another file:

```r
# file1.R
foo <- 1


# file2.R
foo # No diagnostic
```

RStudio is much less liberal. It requires that you `source()` a script to populate symbols explictly. For instance:

```r
# file2.R
source("file1.R")
foo # Correctly defined
```

These features should behave more like "document symbols" than "workspace symbols":
- [ ] Diagnostics for undefined symbols
- [x] Go to definition, find references, rename

Ideally we'd populate the definitions statically if the sourced file has a static file path. In the meantime we can rely on the dynamic search path, which is what RStudio does as well.

title: Add a `.here` file from "New Folder from Template" for an R project
description: We should consider adding a `.here` file to the top-level folder when user walks through "New Folder from Template" and selects "R project" AND does not request Git or renv. The presence of the `.here` file helps a lot of R tools recognize the top-level folder as a project. Some of the packages that place and/or use specific file-based indicators of "YO this is a project I might want to open as a workspace": [usethis](https://usethis.r-lib.org/), [here](https://here.r-lib.org/), [rprojroot](https://rprojroot.r-lib.org/). This is all related to the load-bearing role that RStudio's `.Rproj` file has taken on in the R realm and adapting to the lack of a real equivalent in Positron. More about that: **Contents of `.here`**: the contents don't matter in terms of the function of the file. It can be empty. But it would probably make sense to put something like "Created with 'New Folder from Template (R project)' in Positron {VERSION NUMBER} on {DATE}. Read more at https://positron.posit.co and https://here.r-lib.org.". Basically something to explain the file's presence and links to more info. **UI thoughts**:: I honestly think we might not need any UI. Positron could just silently place this file if it's being asked to create a workspace folder and there will be no obvious indicators of project-hood, i.e. the user has not checked the boxes for Git or renv. I'm not too sure where we would put any sort of checkbox, since the choice to use Git and renv are on two different screens/steps in the flow. There could be some indication on the Project Configuration screen that we are placing `.here` if Git was not selected in the previous screen and renv is not selected here. This is most concretely motivated by https://github.com/r-lib/usethis/issues/2125, but there has been a lot accumulated head-scratching over the lack-of-project file in Positron.

title: Ark: `$` and `@` could be even smarter, especially with lists and environments containing functions (which includes R6)
description: In RStudio, completions after `x$` and `x@` use `x` for 2 things: - Determines the possible names of the things on the RHS with `.DollarNames()` and `.AtNames()` - Determines the possible _types_ of the things on the RHS as well We only do the 1st of these, which means when there is a function on the RHS and we accept it, we don't add parentheses automatically for the user. RStudio can do this, and it is particularly nice with R6 (and lists too). https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/assets/19150088/cc2ee637-4751-4b69-a0cb-b37be3a838c0

title: R: Get `DYLD_FALLBACK_LIBRARY_PATH` and `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` from `etc/ldpaths`
description:
In https://github.com/posit-dev/ark/pull/205, one of the things we did was attempt to set the env vars `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` on Linux and `DYLD_FALLBACK_LIBRARY_PATH` on macOS.

We did this by utilizing R's `etc/ldpaths` script, which sets the corresponding env var to the correct value and exports it. We were able to first set `R_HOME`, then run that script, then print out the corresponding env var, and then we could be confident that we were going to be setting it to the right thing.

Notably, `etc/ldpaths` also contains information about Java, and will include Java related paths in the corresponding env var. This is used by rJava in particular.

---

Now, we have since realized that setting those env vars _after ark has started_ does absolutely nothing. They _must_ be set in the parent process before ark has started up, and on macOS we also must enable the `allow-dyld-environment-variables` entitlement (which we already do) for it to get passed to the child process.

So the correct thing to do is to set these from Positron (or a "wrapper" script for ark that would also be used in standalone Jupyter kernels) as we do in https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/3921 and https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/2809.

The problem with those 2 PRs is that they ignore `etc/ldpaths` entirely, missing information about Java.

We need to go back and add support for extracting these env vars from `etc/ldpaths` instead, either by finally writing that wrapper script or by sourcing `etc/ldpaths` from positron-r. When we do this, go back to https://github.com/posit-dev/ark/pull/205 and reference the tooling used in `source_ldpaths_script()`, as that has all the smarts to set `R_HOME` and use the most portable bash incantation to get the env var out.

---

The other half of this issue is that we need to go ahead and remove the dead tooling from ark, since we have determined it is not doing anything. I will go ahead and do that and link to this.

title: Include help topics in completions for `?`
description:
*I'm splitting this out of #1818, because it's a separate piece of work.*

What we're talking about here is that in RStudio, if you attach dplyr, then trigger completions via `?`, those completions include help *topics* (i.e. topics that aren't also exported functions).

Positron does not offer these perfectly valid completions.

Here's RStudio helping me read the help for `dplyr-package` and `dplyr-locale`:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f1f5d6e6-af78-4ae7-8bef-6b196747839d

Positron gives the impression that it doesn't even know about these help topics with its completions (you also see double entries here 😬 which is tracked in #5708):

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6aaae693-db76-4520-b43a-d6d12935cd07

Just so I don't trap everything in videos, the examples above involve:

```r
library(dplyr)
?dpl<COMPLETIONS OFFERED HERE>
# imagine you want to read the help for dplyr-package or dplyr-locale
```

We want the completions to help us get to topics like `` ?`dplyr-package` ``. This means that (1) `dplyr-package` and the like should appear in the list of completions and (2) Positron should also be smart enough to finesse the issue of backticks.


## Describe the issue:

Howdy! Trying out positron for the first time today. Coming from RStudio, some of the indentation behavior is unexpected:

* function args don't line up on enter
* on auto-format (Cmd + I), args on their own lines just get indented by the default (2 spaces), rather than matching the indentation of the prior line's function arg

## Steps to reproduce the issue:

(open up a new R script & run the following)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/582db4b6-d0d6-45d9-a74d-424ebcaac852

## Expected or desired behavior:

Ideally, formatting/indentation would automatically follow RStudio's built-in styling/indentation, with the expected output of:

```R
mtcars %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = qsec,
             y = hp)) +
  geom_point()
```

I'm a fan of RStudio's built-in styling/indentation, so the only reason that I don't use VSCode for R is because [RStudio-style formatting isn't available](https://github.com/REditorSupport/vscode-R/issues/62) and there are no plans in REditor to support this. I am not a fan of `styler`-style formatting, so in an ideal world, positron would mirror RStudio-style formatting for R scripts by default. 

It sounds like there is [possibly an upcoming release](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/5534#issuecomment-2513301994) that addresses formatting, so maybe this issue will be out of date shortly.

Thanks for all the work here, really excited to use a single IDE for R/python!


# Problem

When I go to R/targets.R, position my cursor on bar() call and press fn-F12 (go-to-definition on my Mac), I get the error `no definition found for 'bar'`.

# Additional information

I did some tracking with kernel and LSP logging and found the following. Verbose LSP tracing identifies where the failure occurs.

At 8:08:48, Positron sends:

```text
textDocument/definition - (9)
uri: file:///.../R/targets.R
position: { line: 1, character: 9 }
```

The language server receives and handles the corresponding `GotoDefinition` request, but its exact response is:

```text
Received response 'textDocument/definition - (9)' in 3ms.
No result returned.
```

Therefore, Positron is not receiving a valid location and then failing to navigate. The R language server returns no definition location. This suggests that the language server is not resolving the cross-file definition introduced through `targets::tar_source("R")`. The complete verbose `lsp.txt` is attached.

[lsp.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33192293/lsp.txt)

title: Race condition between prompt updates and closing of execute request
description:
I can't reproduce this race condition all the time but when it does happen the behaviour is sticky for a while. What happens is that after leaving a debugging session, the debugger prompt is incorrectly displayed:

```
Browse[1]>
```

Evaluating something (even empty evaluation) then restores the expected prompt:

```
>
```


#### The race condition

Here is the flow of the prompt update when we leave a debugging session:

- Ark emits the configuration for the next prompt via the UI comm: https://github.com/posit-dev/ark/blob/af8b0849c0ab294fbf728ef1ef4b55c307f39346/crates/ark/src/interface.rs#L1261-L1266

  This happens right before closing the active execute_request.

- On the frontend side, UI client handling propagates: https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/6c45e8c66215551479af65dd8d6b9c0578f2d190/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeSession/common/activeRuntimeSession.ts#L202

- Session handling propagates: https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/6c45e8c66215551479af65dd8d6b9c0578f2d190/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeSession/common/activeRuntimeSession.ts#L202

- Runtime session service handling propagates: https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/6e931234bf6f1e977d5de4afff39ce40ad645cec/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeSession/common/runtimeSession.ts#L1762

- Runtime service handling emits a PromptConfig event: https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/api/browser/positron/mainThreadLanguageRuntime.ts#L207

- Console Input consumes the event and updates the prompt: https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/6c45e8c66215551479af65dd8d6b9c0578f2d190/src/vs/workbench/contrib/positronConsole/browser/components/consoleInput.tsx#L1066


AFAICT the event propagation on the main thread side is all synchronous. So I think the race condition comes from the very first step, sending an event via the UI comm before closing the active request. The comm event is sent via IOPub whereas the closing of the execute_request is via Shell. If something in the IOPub messaging is a little slower, the prompt update might arrive in the extension host _after_ the closing of the execute request.

To fix this, we could include the prompt information in the response to the `execute_request` instead of sending it separately.

#### Weirdness in `dynState` ownership and synchronisation

Relatedly I've noticed a weirdness in the ownership and synchronisation model of `dynState`. The sessions on the extension hosts are required to have a `dynState` containing things like the session name and the prompts, but prompts are never actually updated after initialisation. I think a simpler setup for the `dynState` would be for it to live entirely on the main thread side, perhaps allowing extensions to retrieve it (although this might not even be needed).

title: Python protocol tests for `ggsql-jupyter` are stale, mostly skipped, and not run in CI
description:
The Python protocol tests under `ggsql-jupyter/tests/` have been failing since at least January 2026 and nothing runs them. We should decide whether to invest in them or remove them, because the middle state is worse than either IMO.

## What happens if you run them today

`test_integration.py`: 8 passed, 1 failed, in 50 seconds.

`test_compliance.py`: 9 skipped, 4 passed, 1 failed, then it hangs and never finishes.

### Stale assertions

Three places assert things the kernel has not sent for months:

- `test_compliance.py:114` and `:117`, and `test_integration.py:188` and `:191`, assert `application/vnd.vegalite.v6+json`. The kernel sends `text/html` and `text/plain` (`ggsql-jupyter/src/display.rs`). It last sent a Vega-Lite mime type in 79280dc (January 2026), and even then it was `v5`, so the `v6` assertion has never matched anything.
- `test_compliance.py:69` asserts `implementation == "ggsql"`. The kernel sends `"ggsql-jupyter"` (`ggsql-jupyter/src/kernel.rs`). `test_integration.py:115` asserts the correct value, so the two files disagree with each other.

The `mimetype`, `file_extension` and `language_info.name` assertions are all correct.

### Most of the compliance suite does not run

`jupyter_kernel_test` silently skips its inherited tests when the corresponding sample attribute is not defined on the subclass. Nine tests skip this way. The file reads like broad protocol coverage but tests very little of it.

### It hangs

The run stalls partway through and has to be killed. `test_shutdown` shuts the kernel down, and unittest runs tests in alphabetical order, so `test_status_messages` comes after it and blocks on a kernel that is gone.

### It destroys your kernelspec

`setup_module` in `test_compliance.py` installs a kernelspec named `ggsql` pointing at `target/debug`, overwriting whatever you had. `teardown_module` then runs `jupyter kernelspec remove -f ggsql`, which deletes it. Anyone with a working ggsql kernelspec loses it by running this file. Setting `JUPYTER_DATA_DIR` to a scratch directory avoids this, but nothing in the tests or the README says so.

### It is slow for what it checks

About three minutes total. The `kernel_manager` fixture in `test_integration.py` is function-scoped and contains a hard `time.sleep(3)`, so every test starts a new kernel and sleeps. `test_compliance.py` shells out to `cargo build` in `setUp`, so once per test.

## Why the suite is worth something anyway

These tests cover the one thing the Rust unit tests cannot reach: the actual wire protocol. ZMQ framing, HMAC signing, busy/idle ordering, `execute_input` echo, state persisting across cells. That surface breaks silently.

We have a concrete example. The kernel stopped sending the Vega-Lite mime type in January 2026 and nobody noticed for seven months, because the only suite that would have flagged it was not running. If it had been, someone would have had to update those assertions deliberately, and the change would have been visible.

## The decision

**Option A: invest.** Roughly:

- Fix the stale assertions, and make the two files agree on `implementation`.
- Isolate the kernelspec so running tests cannot damage a developer's environment.
- Fix the ordering so `test_shutdown` runs last, or give it its own kernel.
- Make the `kernel_manager` fixture session-scoped and replace `sleep(3)` with `wait_for_ready`.
- Either define the sample attributes so the skipped `jupyter_kernel_test` cases actually run, or drop the inheritance and keep only the tests we wrote.
- Build the kernel once in the workflow rather than per test, and set `GGSQL_SKIP_GENERATE=1` where the grammar is not in play.
- Add a CI job. `requirements.txt` should also drop `jupyterlab` and `ipykernel`, which the tests never import.

**Option B: remove them.** If we are not going to maintain protocol tests, deleting them is more honest than keeping a suite that has been red for seven months. We would want to note what coverage we are giving up.

I lean towards A, because the mime type regression is exactly the class of bug this catches and nothing else does. But A is real work, and it is worth agreeing on that before starting.

## Reproducing

```sh
cd ggsql-jupyter/tests
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt

# JUPYTER_DATA_DIR keeps test_compliance.py away from your real ggsql kernelspec
JUPYTER_DATA_DIR=$(mktemp -d) pytest test_integration.py
JUPYTER_DATA_DIR=$(mktemp -d) pytest test_compliance.py   # will hang, needs killing
```

Building the kernel needs `tree-sitter-cli` on `PATH`, or `GGSQL_SKIP_GENERATE=1` if `tree-sitter-ggsql/src/parser.c` already exists.

title: Windows + conda: interpreter discovery takes minutes and one conda env is not discovered
description:
## System details:

#### Positron and OS details:

- Positron 2026.09.1, build 2
- Windows 11 (10.0.26200)
- Conda 26.5.3

#### Session details:

- Intended runtime: Conda environment `met`, Python 3.14.6
- Other installed runtime: Conda environment `keras`, Python 3.11.15
- Reproduced with Python scripts, the Python console, and Jupyter notebooks

## Describe the issue:

Positron does not reliably retain my Conda environment named `met` as the Python runtime for a workspace. The environment itself is valid, and the Positron logs show that it is both discovered and registered. Nevertheless, the workspace automatically starts or returns to another Conda environment, `keras`. Notebook sessions also start with `keras`, and Ruff briefly switches to `met` before switching back to `keras`.

The relevant interpreter paths are:

- `C:\Users\<username>\miniconda3\envs\met\python.exe`
- `C:\Users\<username>\miniconda3\envs\keras\python.exe`

Both interpreters run normally outside Positron. Positron's bundled `interpreterInfo.py` also succeeds when invoked through:

```text
conda.exe run -p C:\Users\<username>\miniconda3\envs\met ...
```

and reports the expected `sysPrefix` and Python version.

My user settings include:

```json
{
  "python.condaPath": "C:/Users/<username>/miniconda3/Scripts/conda.exe",
  "python.interpreters.override": [
    "C:/Users/<username>/miniconda3/envs/met/python.exe",
    "C:/Users/<username>/miniconda3/envs/keras/python.exe"
  ]
}
```

This partly resembles #11992, but in my case the selected runtime also changes at the workspace/tooling level, including Ruff. It may also be related to the stored-affiliation mechanism discussed in #13521, although that issue was fixed before the Positron version used here.

## Steps to reproduce the issue:

1. Install Miniconda on Windows and create two environments, here named `met` and `keras`.
2. Add both Python executables to `python.interpreters.override`.
3. Open a workspace in Positron and select `met` as the Python interpreter/runtime.
4. Start a Python console or open and run a notebook.
5. Reload and reopen the workspace, then check the active interpreter and the Python extension logs.

## Expected or desired behavior:

An environment that is successfully discovered, registered, and explicitly selected should start the Python console and notebook and remain selected for that workspace after reload. Ruff and other Python tooling should use the same selected runtime.

## Were there any error messages in the UI, Output panel, or Developer Tools console?

The Python Locator log confirms that `met` is discovered:

```text
Discovered env: C:\Users\<username>\miniconda3\envs\met\python.exe
```

The Python Language Pack log confirms that it is registered:

```text
pythonRuntimeDiscoverer: registering runtime for interpreter
C:\Users\<username>\miniconda3\envs\met\python.exe
with id 605fd7895133934c33296d0380d4959b
```

However, the same workspace subsequently reports:

```text
Python interpreter path: ~\miniconda3\envs\keras\python.exe
```

I also observed the Conda picker running the following command for approximately five minutes:

```text
conda search *xarray* --json
```

It then reported:

```text
CondaPythonPickerContribution returning 0 items
```

I am not sure whether this slow package search is part of the same problem, but it occurs during the affected interpreter-selection workflow.

As a workaround, I have restricted the workspace to `met` with `python.interpreters.override`, set `python.defaultInterpreterPath`, and used **Python: Clear Workspace Interpreter Setting** followed by a window reload. The environment itself has also been verified independently: it starts successfully and imports `ipykernel` and `xarray` without errors.

description:
In https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/12160, I am working on more tasks that involve looking up all the installed R packages and finding stuff in them and I built out additional caches, similar to the existing `_packageCache`.

@bricestacey points out that instead of this approach, we could use events and listeners for package mutations, which would be nice!
