title: Assistant: add Snowflake partner tag to authentication extension
description:
## Background

The Snowflake partner tag (`posit_positron` / `posit_workbench_positron`) is currently resolved in the positron assistant extension, sent as an HTTP `User-Agent` header on Cortex requests: https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/3d20fb210794ac4c75abb479c889e97d5cbc34cf/extensions/positron-assistant/src/providers/snowflake/snowflakeProvider.ts#L99-L104

positron-assistant is being deprecated in favour of Posit Assistant, which reads credentials and headers from the authentication extension. The partner-tag resolution logic needs to move into the authentication extension so Posit Assistant (and any future consumer) gets the User-Agent without re-implementing the lookup, and so we have one source of truth for the value.

https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/13664 added the `authentication.snowflake.customHeaders` setting, but it is not initialized with the partner user agent header.

## Proposed change

Move the resolution logic to the authentication extension. Resolve `SF_PARTNER` (or `posit_positron` default) inside the snowflake auth provider and expose it through `authentication.snowflake.customHeaders` as the `User-Agent` header that Posit Assistant will consume.

Consider if positron-catalog-explorer should leverage the auth extension, but no changes are needed.

title: With startupBehavior set to always for Python and R, only one language starts
description:
## What happens

With `interpreters.startupBehavior` set to `always` for both Python and R, and no affiliated runtime in the folder, only one language starts when the folder opens. Which one depends on which extension registered its interpreters first, so it can change from run to run.

Decided in #16380 (item 6): both languages should start, because `always` applies to each language it's set for.

## Repro

Confirmed on `main` with a unit test. It registers one Python and one R interpreter, sets `interpreters.startupBehavior` to `always`, and finishes discovery. `autoStartRuntime()` is called for Python only.

To see it in the app (not yet run by hand):

1. Set `interpreters.discoveryCache.enabled` to `false`, so #16376 can't start something first.
2. Set `interpreters.startupBehavior` to `always`, either for all languages or for both `"[python]"` and `"[r]"`.
3. Make sure `python.defaultInterpreterPath` and `positron.r.interpreters.default` aren't set.
4. Make a new folder that has only a `README.md`. No Python or R files, project files, or environments.
5. Open the folder. Only one console starts. The Window log says "The configuration specifies that a runtime should always start for the '<language>' language."

## Why

When discovery finishes, the `onDidChangeRuntimeStartupPhase` handler in the `RuntimeStartupService` constructor ([runtimeStartup.ts](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeStartup/common/runtimeStartup.ts)) runs a fallback:

1. It does nothing if any language has an affiliated runtime or any console is running.
2. Otherwise it starts the first interpreter that its extension marked `Immediate`, and stops.
3. Otherwise it walks the registered interpreters and keeps only the first language whose `interpreters.startupBehavior` is `always`. It starts one interpreter for that language and stops. The code comment there says "Only one language ID can be auto-started."

## Expected

Each language whose `interpreters.startupBehavior` is `always` starts an interpreter. A language-specific value still wins over the value for all languages; that part works today.

## Open question

Step 1 turns the fallback off for every language when any one language has an affiliated runtime. So if Python is affiliated and R is set to `always`, R never starts. Should the fix also start R in that case?

title: Use short lived tokens for Bedrock
description:
When a user has AWS access configured, the Auth extension hands the user's full AWS credentials (an access key, a secret, and a session token) to Posit Assistant and this is what Assistant uses to auth with AWS Bedrock. Instead, the Auth extension should mint a short-lived Bedrock token.
The extension can automatically refresh this token so the user isn't interrupted.

Consumers should ask the Auth extension for the scoped credential they want. Today this would just be Bedrock but we can implement it so other kinds can be added later without reworking how consumers ask.

## User experience

Sign-in and provider selection are unchanged. The user sees the same flow; what changes is what the Auth extension shares with Posit Assistant.

title: Investigate how interpreter startup settings behave in unclear cases
description:
## Why

Users and the team can't predict how the interpreter startup settings combine. For example, they can't tell what `interpreters.startupBehavior` set to `recommended` allows, whether `python.interpreters.exclude` stops an affiliated runtime, or when a change takes effect.

Before we write the rules down in a wiki page (posit-dev/positron-wiki#241), we need to know which of today's behaviors are intended. A read through the code turned up 11 behaviors that are either bugs or intended behavior nobody has written down. This issue is for reproducing each one and deciding which it is.

## What to do for each behavior

1. Reproduce the behavior. Write repro steps and record a video, on macOS unless the item says otherwise. If it doesn't reproduce, note that and move on.
2. Agree with other developers on whether it's a bug or intended.
3. If it's a bug, file an issue with the repro steps and video. Add it as a sub-issue of #15729, assign @dhruvisompura for review, and link it here.
4. If it's intended, note that here. The behavior then goes into the wiki page.

Each item below has the same five parts: **What happens**, **Repro**, **Why**, **Question**, and **Status**. **Why** lists the code steps in the order they run. Code links go to the whole file on `main`, so search the file for the function or name given with each link. **Question** asks one question and says what each answer would mean. If an item's **Status** says it hasn't been reproduced, it comes from reading the code. Treat it as a lead until someone runs the repro.

## Settings and terms

The items compare these settings. Each item names the full setting key, and this table lists them all in one place.

| Setting | Language | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `interpreters.startupBehavior` | All, or one language with `"[python]"` or `"[r]"` | `always`, `auto` (the default), `recommended`, `manual`, `disabled` |
| `python.interpreters.include` | Python | Extra interpreter paths to search |
| `python.interpreters.exclude`, `positron.r.interpreters.exclude` | Python, R | Interpreter paths to hide |
| `python.interpreters.override`, `positron.r.interpreters.override` | Python, R | The only interpreter paths to use |
| `python.defaultInterpreterPath`, `positron.r.interpreters.default` | Python, R | One interpreter path to recommend |
| `interpreters.discoveryCache.maxAgeDays` | All | Days a cache entry stays fresh (default 30) |
| `interpreters.discoveryCache.refreshIntervalDays` | All | Days between full discoveries (default 1) |
| `python.environmentProviders.enabled` | Python | `Venv`, `Conda`, and `uv`, each `true` or `false` (item 10) |

These terms come up throughout:

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Affiliated runtime | The one interpreter per language that Positron remembers for a workspace. |
| Registered | Added to Positron's list of known interpreters. |
| `Immediate`, `Implicit`, `Explicit` | A startup marking that an extension puts on each interpreter it registers or recommends (`LanguageRuntimeStartupBehavior`). These are not values of `interpreters.startupBehavior`. `Immediate` means start right away. `Implicit` means start when a file of that language is opened. `Explicit` means start only when the user asks. |

## Behaviors to check

- [x] **1. With `interpreters.startupBehavior` set to `recommended`, should opening a Python or R file start a session?**

  **What happens**

  Opening a Python or R file starts a session today. A folder that has only `analysis.py` opens with no session. Opening `analysis.py` starts Python, and opening a new `analysis.R` starts R. The log gives the reason as "A file written in python was opened" for Python and "A file written in r was opened" for R.

  **Repro**

  1. Set `interpreters.discoveryCache.enabled` to `false`. This keeps #16376 from starting R at launch.
  2. Set `interpreters.startupBehavior` to `recommended`.
  3. Open a folder that has only `analysis.py`, with no `.venv`, `.conda`, or R files. Neither extension recommends anything at launch, so nothing starts.
  4. Open `analysis.py`. Python starts.
  5. Create and open `analysis.R`. R starts.

  **Why**

  Opening a file runs the [`onDidRequestRichLanguageFeatures` handler in the `RuntimeSessionService` constructor](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeSession/common/runtimeSession.ts). The handler picks a registered interpreter for that language that its extension marked `Implicit`. Then it calls [`autoStartRuntime()`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeSession/common/runtimeSession.ts). That function [blocks only the `manual` and `disabled` values of `interpreters.startupBehavior`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeSession/common/runtimeSession.ts). It has done so since the `recommended` value was added in #6145. But the [Settings editor description of the `recommended` value](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/languageRuntime/common/languageRuntime.ts) (the `positron.runtime.startupBehavior.recommended` string) says only that an interpreter starts "when the extension providing the interpreter recommends it."

  **Question**

  When `interpreters.startupBehavior` is `recommended`, should opening a Python or R file start a session?

  - If yes, the code is right and the description is incomplete. Draft PR #16411 updates the description.
  - If no, `autoStartRuntime()` should also block the `recommended` value for starts caused by opening a file.

  **Status**

  This was reproduced on macOS.

  Video: 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/13646008-f60f-4f4f-96d9-5a2e112b1188

- [x] **2. With `interpreters.startupBehavior` set to `recommended`, should the affiliated runtime start when a folder reopens?**

  **What happens**

  It depends on whether the Python extension recommends the same interpreter. These two setups give different results:

  | Setup | Result on reopen | Start reason in the console info popup |
  |---|---|---|
  | A: `python.defaultInterpreterPath` isn't set | The affiliated runtime starts. | "Positron found the last interpreter used in this workspace and started it" |
  | B: the folder sets `python.defaultInterpreterPath` to the same Python | Nothing starts. **Interpreter: Clear Saved Interpreter** still lists the Python. | -- |

  **Repro**

  1. Set `interpreters.discoveryCache.enabled` to `false`. This keeps #16376 from starting something first.
  2. Make a folder that has only `analysis.py`.
  3. With `interpreters.startupBehavior` set to `manual`, open the folder and start a global Python with the **Start Session** button in the top bar. That Python becomes the folder's affiliated runtime.
  4. For setup B only, add a `.vscode/settings.json` that sets `python.defaultInterpreterPath` to that Python.
  5. Set `interpreters.startupBehavior` to `recommended`.
  6. Open another folder, then reopen this one.

  **Why**

  When a window opens, [`startupSequence()`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeStartup/common/runtimeStartup.ts) runs these steps in order:

  | Step | Function | What it does |
  |---|---|---|
  | 1 | `restoreSessions()` | Reconnects sessions that are still running. |
  | 2 | [`startAffiliatedLanguageRuntimes()`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeStartup/common/runtimeStartup.ts) | Starts the affiliated runtime, [only when `interpreters.startupBehavior` is `always` or `auto`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeStartup/common/runtimeStartup.ts). When it's `recommended`, this step is skipped. |
  | 3 | [`startRecommendedLanguageRuntimes()`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeStartup/common/runtimeStartup.ts) | Asks each extension for a recommendation and [registers it](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeStartup/common/runtimeStartup.ts), which adds it to Positron's list of known interpreters. Starts it only if the extension marks it `Immediate`. |
  | 4 | `discoverAllRuntimes()` | Loads the discovery cache and runs discovery. Each interpreter is registered as it's found. |

  Every registration during step 4 runs [`onDidRegisterRuntime()`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeStartup/common/runtimeStartup.ts). If the interpreter is the affiliated runtime and no console is running, the handler starts the interpreter unless `interpreters.startupBehavior` is [`manual` or `disabled`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeStartup/common/runtimeStartup.ts). So steps 2 and 4 treat the `recommended` value differently. Both rules come from #6145.

  - In setup A, step 2 is skipped. Step 4 then finds the Python and starts it.
  - In setup B, step 3 already registered the same Python. Calling `registerRuntime()` for an interpreter that is already registered [returns early without an event](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/languageRuntime/common/languageRuntime.ts), so step 4 never checks the Python.

  **Question**

  When `interpreters.startupBehavior` is `recommended`, should the affiliated runtime start when the folder reopens?

  - If no, setup A is the bug. `onDidRegisterRuntime()` should use step 2's rule and start the affiliated runtime only when `interpreters.startupBehavior` is `always` or `auto`.
  - If yes, setup B is the bug. Step 2 should also start the affiliated runtime when `interpreters.startupBehavior` is `recommended`.

  **Status**

  This was reproduced on macOS.

  Videos:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9d13ef51-8fef-4fd2-b794-0b8be19f0a4a

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0dc300f7-b64a-4576-aaab-1a61123c0dde

- [x] **3. With `interpreters.startupBehavior` set to `disabled` for a language, should that language's session reconnect after the extension host restarts?**

  **What happens**

  It depends on whether the window reloads or only the extension host restarts.

  - After a window reload, or after quitting and reopening, the session never reconnects. Positron tries to restore it before it works out which languages have `interpreters.startupBehavior` set to `disabled`. But registering a disabled language's interpreter throws an error, so the restore fails every time.
  - After an extension host restart in the same window, the session reconnects. The interpreter is still registered from before `interpreters.startupBehavior` changed to `disabled`, so the restore skips the step that checks for `disabled`.

  **Repro**

  1. Start a Python console.
  2. Set `"[python]": { "interpreters.startupBehavior": "disabled" }`.
  3. Run **Developer: Restart Extension Host**. You should see the Python session reconnect.
  4. For contrast, run **Developer: Reload Window** instead. You should see a reconnecting placeholder appear and then go away. The log should say "Cannot register ... the 'python' language is disabled."

  **Why**

  1. [`startupSequence()`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeStartup/common/runtimeStartup.ts) restores sessions first, and only then builds the list of languages set to `disabled`. [`findRestoredSessions()`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeStartup/common/runtimeStartup.ts) and [`restoreWorkspaceSessions()`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeStartup/common/runtimeStartup.ts) don't check `interpreters.startupBehavior`.
  2. [`restoreRuntimeSession()`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeSession/common/runtimeSession.ts) registers the interpreter only if it isn't registered yet.
  3. [`registerRuntime()`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/languageRuntime/common/languageRuntime.ts) throws for a disabled language. In a fresh window, nothing has registered the interpreter yet, so the restore always fails.
  4. Nothing reacts when `interpreters.startupBehavior` changes, so an interpreter registered before you picked `disabled` stays registered. When the extension host exits, the session is [queued to reconnect](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeSession/common/runtimeSession.ts) in `attachToSession()`, and it [reconnects when the extension activates again](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeSession/common/runtimeSession.ts), through the `onDidChangeExtensionsStatus` handler in the `RuntimeSessionService` constructor. In step 2, `restoreRuntimeSession()` skips registration because the interpreter is already registered, so the `disabled` check never runs.

  By contrast, [`autoStartRuntime()`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeSession/common/runtimeSession.ts) checks `interpreters.startupBehavior` itself.

  **Question**

  If a language's `interpreters.startupBehavior` is `disabled`, should its session reconnect after an extension host restart in the same window?

  - If no, `restoreRuntimeSession()` should check `interpreters.startupBehavior` itself instead of relying on `registerRuntime()`. Also decide whether changing a language's `interpreters.startupBehavior` to `disabled` should shut down or unregister what's already running.
  - If yes, the behavior is intended. The docs can say that reloading or reopening never reconnects a session for a language set to `disabled`.

  **Status**

  This hasn't been reproduced yet. It comes from reading the code. The same-window case isn't certain. Interpreters don't appear to be unregistered when the extension host stops, but no one has confirmed that.

- [ ] **4. Should an affiliated runtime that the exclude or override settings filter out be refused at launch?**

  **What happens**

  This item is about `python.interpreters.exclude`, `python.interpreters.override`, `positron.r.interpreters.exclude`, and `positron.r.interpreters.override`. Python and R handle them differently.

  - For Python, the excluded affiliated runtime starts at launch. It then also appears in the interpreter picker for that window.
  - For R, the excluded affiliated runtime is refused at launch, so no R console starts. Positron doesn't clear the affiliated runtime, so this repeats on every launch until you pick another R.

  This is a different bug from #7445, which is about Python discovery running when `interpreters.startupBehavior` is `disabled`.

  **Repro**

  1. In a folder, start a console on Python X. It becomes the folder's affiliated runtime.
  2. Quit Positron fully. A window reload reconnects the running session instead and skips this path.
  3. Add X to `python.interpreters.exclude`, or set `python.interpreters.override` to a different Python.
  4. Reopen the folder. You should see X start at launch and appear in the picker.
  5. Repeat with R and `positron.r.interpreters.exclude`. You should see no R console. The Window log should show "could not be validated ... Installation path was excluded via user settings" and "Error starting affiliated runtimes".

  **Why**

  At launch, the affiliated runtime starts before discovery runs, so it isn't registered yet. Core asks the extension to check it first:

  1. [`startAffiliatedLanguageRuntimes()`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeStartup/common/runtimeStartup.ts) picks the affiliated runtime to start, and [`startAffiliatedRuntime()`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeStartup/common/runtimeStartup.ts) starts it.
  2. [`doAutoStartRuntime()`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeSession/common/runtimeSession.ts) sees that the runtime isn't registered and calls the extension's `validateMetadata()`. On success it registers the result. If validation throws, it logs "could not be validated" and rethrows.
  3. Python's [`validateMetadata()`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/extensions/positron-python/src/client/positron/manager.ts) only checks that the path exists and resolves. The filter that applies `python.interpreters.include`, `python.interpreters.exclude`, and `python.interpreters.override` [runs only during discovery](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/extensions/positron-python/src/client/positron/discoverer.ts), in `filterInterpreters()`.
  4. R's [`validateMetadata()`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/extensions/positron-r/src/runtime-manager.ts) builds a new `RInstallation`. [Its constructor checks `positron.r.interpreters.exclude` and `positron.r.interpreters.override`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/extensions/positron-r/src/r-installation.ts) through [`isExcludedInstallation()`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/extensions/positron-r/src/interpreter-settings.ts). The constructor marks an excluded installation as not usable, and `validateMetadata()` throws when an installation isn't usable.
  5. In [`startupSequence()`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeStartup/common/runtimeStartup.ts), the error is caught and logged. The affiliated runtime isn't cleared. The recommendation step is in the same `try` block, so it is skipped too. The [fallback after discovery](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeStartup/common/runtimeStartup.ts), in the `RuntimeStartupService` constructor, runs only when no affiliated runtime exists, so nothing starts R.

  **Question**

  Should an affiliated runtime that `python.interpreters.exclude`, `python.interpreters.override`, `positron.r.interpreters.exclude`, or `positron.r.interpreters.override` filters out be refused at launch?

  - If yes, Python's `validateMetadata()` is the bug. Core should also clear the affiliated runtime, or fall back to another interpreter, when validation fails. Otherwise R ends up with no console.
  - If no, because the user picked it, R's constructor check is the bug when it's used to validate an affiliated runtime.

  **Status**

  This hasn't been reproduced yet. It comes from reading the code. One edge case is open. Suppose the stored R affiliated runtime is marked as the system's current R. Then `validateMetadata()` checks today's current R path instead of the stored path, so an exclude entry for the stored path might not match.

- [ ] **5. Should `python.defaultInterpreterPath`, `positron.r.interpreters.default`, and Python's project environments get past the exclude and override settings?**

  **What happens**

  Today, nothing filters these recommendations. The extension and the extension host don't filter them, and neither does [`registerRuntime()`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/languageRuntime/common/languageRuntime.ts). `registerRuntime()` only checks whether `interpreters.startupBehavior` is `disabled`. When the excluded interpreter starts depends on how the extension marks the recommendation:

  | Case | The extension marks it | When the excluded interpreter starts |
  |---|---|---|
  | Python, no folder open, user-level `python.defaultInterpreterPath` | `Immediate` | At launch. |
  | Python, folder has `.venv`, `.conda`, or `*/bin/python` | `Immediate` | At launch. `python.defaultInterpreterPath` isn't used. |
  | Python, folder has none of those, so `python.defaultInterpreterPath` is used | `Implicit` | When you first open a `.py` file, then at the next launch. |
  | R, `positron.r.interpreters.default` | `Implicit` | When you first open an R file. On the next launch, it is refused and no R console starts (see item 4). |

  Python marks the recommendation `Implicit` when `interpreters.startupBehavior` is `manual`. The recommendation is marked `Explicit` if Python has no usable ipykernel. In every case, the recommendation appears in the interpreter picker even though it's excluded, and discovery never removes it.

  **Repro**

  1. Use a new folder with no `.venv` or `.conda`, and no affiliated runtime for Python.
  2. Set `python.defaultInterpreterPath` to Python X and add X to `python.interpreters.exclude`.
  3. Open the folder. You should see X in the picker, and no console should start.
  4. Open a `.py` file. You should see X start.
  5. Quit and reopen. You should see X start at launch.
  6. Repeat steps 1-4 with R and `positron.r.interpreters.default` plus `positron.r.interpreters.exclude`. On the next launch, you should see no R console and the validation error from item 4.

  **Why**

  1. Python's [`recommendedWorkspaceInterpreterPath()`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/extensions/positron-python/src/client/positron/manager.ts) picks the path and decides whether it should start right away. [`recommendedWorkspaceRuntime()`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/extensions/positron-python/src/client/positron/manager.ts) builds the recommendation without calling [`shouldIncludeInterpreter()`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/extensions/positron-python/src/client/positron/interpreterSettings.ts). `createPythonRuntimeMetadata()` in [`runtime.ts`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/extensions/positron-python/src/client/positron/runtime.ts) turns that decision into the `Immediate` or `Implicit` marking.
  2. R's [`recommendedWorkspaceRuntime()`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/extensions/positron-r/src/runtime-manager.ts) always marks the recommendation `Implicit`. It builds an `RInstallation`, which already knows the path is excluded (`inst.usable` is false). But `recommendedWorkspaceRuntime()` never checks that value.
  3. [`startRecommendedLanguageRuntimes()`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeStartup/common/runtimeStartup.ts) registers the recommendation. If the recommendation is marked `Immediate`, it starts. Otherwise, it becomes the affiliated runtime when none exists, with `lastStarted` and `lastUsed` both set to 0.
  4. On file open, the `onDidRequestRichLanguageFeatures` handler [starts the first registered `Implicit` interpreter for the language](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeSession/common/runtimeSession.ts). The recommendation was registered before discovery, so it's first.
  5. On the next launch, the affiliated runtime starts. The "never used" check in `startAffiliatedLanguageRuntimes()` is [skipped when only one language has an affiliated runtime](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeStartup/common/runtimeStartup.ts) (see #16383).

  **Question**

  Should `python.defaultInterpreterPath`, `positron.r.interpreters.default`, and Python's project environments get past `python.interpreters.exclude`, `python.interpreters.override`, `positron.r.interpreters.exclude`, or `positron.r.interpreters.override`?

  - If no, the exclude and override settings should win, and each `recommendedWorkspaceRuntime()` is the bug. Python should call `shouldIncludeInterpreter()`, and R should check `inst.usable`.
  - If yes, the default interpreter settings should win, and R's `validateMetadata()` refusing it on the next launch is the bug (item 4). The docs for the exclude and override settings should also say that the default interpreter settings aren't affected.

  **Status**

  This hasn't been reproduced yet. It comes from reading the code, including when the interpreter starts after a file opens.

- [ ] **6. With `interpreters.startupBehavior` set to `always` for both Python and R, and no affiliated runtime, should both start?**

  **What happens**

  Only one language starts. Which language starts depends on which extension added its interpreters first, so it can change from run to run.

  **Repro**

  1. Set `interpreters.discoveryCache.enabled` to `false`. Otherwise #16376 can reuse an `Immediate` marking from another folder and start that interpreter first.
  2. Set `interpreters.startupBehavior` to `always`, either for all languages or for both `"[python]"` and `"[r]"`.
  3. Make sure `python.defaultInterpreterPath` and `positron.r.interpreters.default` aren't set. If either is set, its extension recommends that interpreter, Positron saves it as the folder's affiliated runtime, and the fallback described under **Why** does nothing.
  4. Make a new folder that has only a `README.md`. It can't be empty, because R treats an empty folder as an R folder for RStudio users. It also can't have any of these, or that extension marks an interpreter `Immediate` and Positron starts it before reaching the `always` step:
     - Python: `*.py`, `*.ipynb`, `pyproject.toml`, `Pipfile`, `*requirements.txt`, `.python-version`, `environment.yml`, `.venv`, `.conda`, or `*/bin/python`
     - R: `*.R`, `*.Rmd`, `.Rprofile`, `renv.lock`, `.Rbuildignore`, `.Renviron`, or `*.Rproj`
  5. Open the folder. You should see only one console. The Window log should show "The configuration specifies that a runtime should always start for the '<language>' language."
  6. To see whether the language changes between runs, repeat steps 4 and 5 with another new folder. Reopening the same folder won't show it, because the console that started is now that folder's affiliated runtime and starts on its own.

  To see an affiliated runtime turn the fallback off for every language, start a Python console in a new folder like the one in step 4, quit Positron fully, and reopen the folder. Python starts as the affiliated runtime, and R never starts.

  **Why**

  When startup finishes, a [fallback in the `RuntimeStartupService` constructor](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeStartup/common/runtimeStartup.ts) runs. It's the `onDidChangeRuntimeStartupPhase` handler:

  1. It does nothing if [any language has an affiliated runtime or any console is running](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeStartup/common/runtimeStartup.ts). So if R's `interpreters.startupBehavior` is `always` and only Python has an affiliated runtime, R never starts. A recommendation that wasn't started at launch also becomes an affiliated runtime, which turns the fallback off too.
  2. [Otherwise it starts the first interpreter that asked to start immediately](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeStartup/common/runtimeStartup.ts), and stops.
  3. [Otherwise it starts the first interpreter whose language has `interpreters.startupBehavior` set to `always`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeStartup/common/runtimeStartup.ts), and only that one. The code comment there calls the case where `interpreters.startupBehavior` is `always` for every language "probably not what is desired."
  4. "First" means first in the [order interpreters were registered](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/languageRuntime/common/languageRuntime.ts), which is what the `registeredRuntimes` getter returns. That order isn't sorted.

  The [Settings editor description of the `always` value](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/languageRuntime/common/languageRuntime.ts) (the `positron.runtime.startupBehavior.always` string) says "the last used interpreter will start if available, and a default will be chosen otherwise." Read per language, the description promises a default for each language whose `interpreters.startupBehavior` is `always`. The fallback came from #6145, which doesn't say what should happen with several languages.

  **Question**

  With `interpreters.startupBehavior` set to `always` for both Python and R, and no affiliated runtime, should both start?

  - If yes, two parts of the fallback are bugs. Its `always` step starts only one language. Its first check turns the whole fallback off when any language in the workspace has an affiliated runtime.
  - If no, the description of the `always` value should say that only one language starts. Also decide whether the language should be picked in a fixed order instead of by registration order.

  **Status**

  This hasn't been reproduced yet. It comes from reading the code.

- [ ] **7. Once a cached interpreter is older than `interpreters.discoveryCache.maxAgeDays`, should it ever be loaded from the cache again?**

  **What happens**

  With the default cache settings, entries rarely expire. A full discovery runs about once a day, because `interpreters.discoveryCache.refreshIntervalDays` defaults to 1. It deletes and re-adds each language's fresh entries, which resets their age. An entry expires only when no full discovery has run for `interpreters.discoveryCache.maxAgeDays` days (default 30), for example when Positron wasn't opened for a month.

  Once an entry expires, it never becomes fresh again, and only **Interpreter: Clear Interpreter Cache** resets it. Other paths leave it expired:

  - The cleanup before a full discovery deletes only fresh entries, so expired ones stay.
  - When discovery finds the interpreter again, the cache keeps the entry's original `firstSeen` date.
  - **Interpreter: Discover All Interpreters** doesn't reset the entry either.

  The effect depends on what else is in that language's part of the cache:

  - If all of the language's entries expired, every launch treats the cache as empty and runs a full discovery, so the cache never speeds up startup for that language.
  - If some of the language's entries are still fresh, no full discovery is forced, so the expired interpreters are left out on warm starts. They show up only on launches that happen to run a full discovery.

  **Repro**

  - The simplest check is a Vitest test. Next to the ["age cap" test](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeStartup/test/common/runtimeDiscoveryCache.vitest.ts), call `upsert`, move the clock past the age limit, and call `upsert` again for the same path. Then check `getEntries`. Today it returns `[]`.
  - To check by hand, set `interpreters.discoveryCache.maxAgeDays` to 1, open Positron, then quit it. The cache is in application storage (`User/globalStorage/state.vscdb`). In its `positron.discoveryCache.v4` value, move every `firstSeen` back 2 days. Then open Positron twice. **Developer: Runtime Startup Diagnostics** should show a "cold-start" full discovery on both opens.

  **Why**

  - [`upsert()` keeps an existing `firstSeen`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeStartup/common/runtimeDiscoveryCache.ts). [`markValidated()`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeStartup/common/runtimeDiscoveryCache.ts) updates only `lastValidated` and the file fingerprint.
  - [`_freshEntries()`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeStartup/common/runtimeDiscoveryCache.ts) hides an entry once `firstSeen` is past the limit, but never deletes it.
  - The [cleanup before a full discovery](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeStartup/common/runtimeStartup.ts), in `discoverAllRuntimes()`, deletes only fresh entries.
  - [`managersNeedingFullDiscovery()`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeStartup/common/runtimeStartup.ts) treats a language with no fresh entries as a cold start.
  - [`loadFromDiscoveryCache()`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeStartup/common/runtimeStartup.ts) registers only fresh entries.

  The intent is stated in a [comment above `RUNTIME_DISCOVERY_CACHE_MAX_AGE_DAYS_SETTING` in `runtimeDiscoveryCacheService.ts`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/runtimeStartup/common/runtimeDiscoveryCacheService.ts): an entry "must be re-validated by a real discovery pass at least once every 30 days." #13291 also says `interpreters.discoveryCache.maxAgeDays` "caps how long a cache entry can live without revalidation." Its [Settings editor description](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/languageRuntime/common/languageRuntime.ts) (the `positron.runtime.discoveryCache.maxAgeDays` string) says "Number of days a cached interpreter is reused before it is rediscovered."

  **Question**

  When a full discovery finds an expired interpreter again, should it become fresh again, either by resetting the entry's `firstSeen` date or by checking age against its `lastValidated` date?

  - If yes, that matches the stated intent. Expired entries should be reset or deleted when discovery sees them again.
  - If no, the description of `interpreters.discoveryCache.maxAgeDays` and the code comment are wrong, and someone needs to decide how an expired entry is meant to recover.

  **Status**

  This hasn't been reproduced yet. It comes from reading the code. It's unknown whether Python's own environment events add expired Python interpreters back on a warm start.

## Small fixes, no investigation needed

These are known and easy to fix, but they aren't scheduled.

- `interpreters.restartOnCrash` has no `interpreterSettings` tag, so it doesn't show up with the other interpreter settings in the Settings editor (`languageRuntime.ts`).
- **Developer: Runtime Startup Diagnostics** doesn't report `positron.r.interpreters.pathDiscoveryMode`, so a report can look complete while leaving out a setting that changed R discovery.

## Done when

- Every behavior above has repro steps and a video, or a note that it didn't reproduce.
- Every behavior has a decision, bug or intended, that other developers agree with.
- Every bug has its own issue under #15729, linked here.

title: Assistant: broader model support for Bedrock provider
description:
## background

Currently, for the Bedrock provider, we only support Anthropic models by default.

It is possible to manually override the list of models for Bedrock using the `positron.assistant.models.overrides.amazonBedrock` setting, if non-Anthropic models are desired.

However, not all models available in Bedrock are compatible with a chat use case. In particular, compatible models must support tool calling, image input, are available for chat use, and have an AWS inference profile.

## proposal

Can we loosen the Anthropic-only default restriction, or provide an easier way to add alternative models, helping ensure that the models fulfill the technical requirements to be usable in chat?

title: Quarto inline output does not capture incremental base R plot layers
description:
**Description**
When Quarto inline output is enabled in Positron, additions to an existing
base R plot are not displayed in the inline output.

The first plotting command appears, but later commands like `points()`,
`lines()`, and `curve(..., add = TRUE)` don't appear.

**Example**

I created a Quarto .qmd file with this R code chunk:

```{r}
y <- 2 * c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
x <- c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)

plot(y ~ x)
points(3, 9, col = "red", pch = 16, cex = 2)
```

I then ran the entire code chunk with inline output enabled.

**Expected result**

The graph should contain:

- Five points from plot(y ~ x)
- One additional large red point at x = 3, y = 9

**Actual result**

The initial plot appears, but the point added by points() does not appear
in the inline output.

The same problem occurs with this example:

```{r}
curve(exp(-x), from = 0, to = 4, lty = 2)
curve(exp(-x^2), add = TRUE)
```

Only the first curve shows up. The second curve is not layered at all.

**Additional information**
Rendering the complete Quarto document works. So it's just the inline output as far as I can tell.

A single completed ggplot2 object displays correctly. 

**Environment**
- Positron Version: 2026.08.0 build 331
- Code - OSS Version: 1.124.0
- Commit: a3a370d4187484ce962794408c76dab702978eaf
- Date: 2026-08-05T17:02:37-07:00
- Electron: 42.2.0
- Chromium: 148.0.7778.97
- Node.js: 24.15.0
- V8: 14.8.178.14-electron.0
- OS: Darwin arm64 25.5.0
- R version: 4.5.3
- Quarto inline output: enabled

title: test: add React component tests for histogram bin ranges
description:
### Summary

A recent e2e test (#10792) was added to verify the rounded values shown in histogram bin ranges. Since this logic is primarily presentation/formatting and handled in the Data Explorer frontend, it would be a better fit at the React component unit-test level.

We already have related component tests at:
`src/vs/workbench/services/positronDataExplorer/test/browser/columnSummaryCell.test.tsx`
These can serve as a model for adding targeted coverage for histogram bins (including rounding and display formatting).

### Goal

Add new React component tests that validate the rendered bin ranges so this coverage can be migrated out of e2e and into the appropriate unit layer.

### Notes

Once these tests are in place, the existing e2e test can be simplified or removed if it becomes redundant.

title: Assistant: Can't see a diff of changes Assistant made to the files
description: When Posit Assistant edits files, the edits just silently appear in the file. There is no UI that lets you see an overview of changes it made, nor one that lets you reject unwanted or unexpected changes. You need to see the proposed changes in the Assistant UI panel itself, which is pretty small. Compare the experience with Copilot, which lets you see the diff right in the file itself, and allow you to keep or undo any change the assistant made. It also has a "changes from chat" diff window you can open. This is really helpful for understanding what the assistant did and reverting unwanted changes individually. We should integrate the API Copilot is already using with Assistant so that the diff editing experience is just as good.

title: Improve bootstrap extension experience when using Profiles
description: Users may miss out on bootstrapped extensions if they are using Profiles and haven't configured the Profile to inherit all extensions from the Default profile. See discussion: https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/discussions/10900#discussioncomment-15170624 When creating a new profile, users are given the option to Source the Extensions for that profile from the Default profile (where bootstrapped extensions exist), but it isn't the default option and likely isn't what the user wants to do when creating their profile. We should consider adding a new option that is enabled by default to include bootstrapped extensions in new profiles or consider other ways to make sure users are aware of new bootstrapped extensions.

title: Support debugging `#%%` cells in Python scripts
description:
Add support for debugging individual cells (delimited by `#%%` separators) in `.py` files via the Python debugger.

Currently, cell debugging is available for Jupyter notebook cells but not for `#%%` cells in Python scripts. VS Code's Python extension supports "Debug Cell" for these, and users expect the same in Positron.

Raised in https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/discussions/13595.

> Thank you for the answer. I prefer to work with .py files instead of jupyter notebooks, because they are just plain text files, which makes some things easier. I often work with time-heavy read and write tasks, so then it is often very helpful to just separate a certain code block into a cell and debug only this cell, avoiding to have to run everything above it also through the debugger.
> 
> I mainly use Spyder, where this is possible, and it helps me a lot.

title: Workbench: Bundle File Navigator extension
description: There's a nice File Navigator extension by @wch: https://github.com/wch/file-navigator This extension helps address a very common frustration with Positron compared to RStudio (and even other IDEs like Jupyter), which is that the Explorer tab in Positron doesn't let you browse outside the workspace. File Navigator presents files and folders in a flat list with breadcrumbs and lets you navigate outside the project. It's functionally very similar to RStudio's Files pane: However, getting this extension isn't very easy as it isn't published anywhere and doesn't have any downloadable releases. Maybe it should be published to OpenVSX? At any rate, we should consider bundling this extension, or something like it, in Positron. It isn't a perfect solution, but might be worthwhile as a stopgap for people who need this kind of interface. Some questions to resolve: - Would we want it enabled by default? Probably not, two file explorers is confusing. Possibly we could have this second explorer live somewhere else in the UI by default, or require a setting to enable it. - It uses a web view which isn't great. Ideally we'd have native UI to reduce resource usage, improve theming and responsiveness, etc. - This is definitely Workbench only; desktop users have plenty of other options for browsing their disks.

title: Tests: Add a CI test to the PR suite that performs a release build
description:
All our tests currently compile sources with `npm run compile` ... or equivalent.

https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/cb0c11f9d372b0184f4b1d00f4d2d89e12d0f9e1/.github/actions/setup-build-env/action.yml#L18-L21

However, that isn't how we compile release builds. It's how we compile _dev_ builds. Release builds use `gulp`, e.g.:

```bash
npm run gulp vscode-darwin-arm64
```

A major difference between development and release builds is that extensions are built with a basic Typescript compiler in development, but are Webpacked in release mode. 

Because none of our tests actually perform a release build, commits that break the release build can and do occasionally slip through, despite passing all tests (this just happened today in https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/10206). 

A PR test should be added that performs the fastest possible release build test (~6 minutes) to ensure that PRs are not merged if they break release builds. This could be done cheaply and in parallel with other PR tests.

(as an aside, it would also be worth investigating whether some of our CI Playwright tests could be made to run on builds compiled in release mode; it has also happened, though is less common, that tests that work fine on dev builds don't work fine on release builds due to e.g. subtleties in webpack bundling).

title: Use workspace-specific DESCRIPTION files in R projects used for testing
description:
Currently https://github.com/posit-dev/qa-example-content has a top-level DESCRIPTION file that holds the cumulative-over-time union of R packages used by Positron testing efforts (at least, I think that's the basic origin story).

I've gotten support in a slack discussion that it would be better for individual R-flavored workspaces there to use their local DESCRIPTION to advertise the R packages they need or, more accurately, needed by tests that use that workspace.

One concrete reason for this is so that the list of needed packages doesn't just grow and grow. Also, as it stands, if you see a package in the mega DESCRIPTION, you don't really know how load-bearing it is.

Currently the mega DESCRIPTION is used in CI like so when building images:
https://github.com/posit-dev/positron-ci-images/blob/main/ubuntu24_04/Dockerfile.ubuntu24_04#L168-L171

So that move would need to be refactored to first identify the relevant DESCRIPTION files and derive the combined dependency list.

title: Follow up on failing windows test for packages pane help button
description:
I believe this was temporarily resolved in this commit https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/commit/18a0a48a0ae655e04e9fc62d0a88159cb97e18fe but we should resolve the issue moving forward.

## Describe the issue:

The packages pane e2e tests fail on windows when trying to open the help pane..

This PR introduced the issue, you can find the failing windows check on the commit on main: https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/13501

Here is some early investigation from Claude about the possible issues:

```
## Summary

Ark's help proxy fails to read response bodies from R's dynamic help server on
Windows GitHub-hosted runners. Headers come back fine (`content-type: text/html`),
but `reqwest::Response::bytes()` errors with `error decoding response body`,
which causes the proxy to return 502 and the help iframe in Positron stays empty.

100% reproducible on win/electron in Positron CI, 100% green on
ubuntu/{chromium,electron}. Not reproducible on local Windows.

## Impact

The Positron e2e test "R - Opens package help in Help pane" (introduced by
posit-dev/positron#13499) fails deterministically on win/electron — 0/15 passes
over the last 30 days. The product-side symptom: opening R help for a base
package via the Packages pane help button shows the correct URL in the help
pane title bar but the iframe stays blank.

## Evidence

Failing CI run: posit-dev/positron#26308765270 (e2e/windows, attempt 0 and 1
both fail identically).

R kernel log (`R Kernel.log`, both attempts identical except port):

> 2026-05-22T20:42:55.553091Z TRACE  Sending frontend event `ShowHelp` with R
>   url 'http://127.0.0.1:14842/library/base/html/00Index.html' and proxy url
>   'http://127.0.0.1:50078/library/base/html/00Index.html'
> 2026-05-22T20:42:56.332633Z  INFO  Proxying URL
>   "http://localhost:14842/library/base/html/00Index.html"
>   path '/library/base/html/00Index.html' content-type is 'Some("text/html")'
>   at crates\ark\src\help_proxy.rs:151
> 2026-05-22T20:42:56.333041Z ERROR  Error proxying
>   http://localhost:14842/library/base/html/00Index.html:
>   error decoding response body
>   at crates\ark\src\help_proxy.rs:194

The failure is at `crates/ark/src/help_proxy.rs:191`:

> http_response_builder.body(match response.bytes().await {
>     Ok(body) => body,
>     Err(error) => {
>         log::error!("Error proxying {}: {}", target_url_string, error);
>         return HttpResponse::BadGateway().finish();
>     },
> }),

Status and headers came back (we logged content-type), but the body stream
fails. Reqwest's "error decoding response body" is typically:

1. Stream truncation / connection close mid-body
2. Content-Length mismatch
3. Malformed chunked transfer encoding
4. Failed Content-Encoding (gzip/deflate) decompression

## Possible contributing factors

1. **`localhost` vs `127.0.0.1` resolution race on Windows.** Line 115:

   > let target_url_string = format!("http://localhost/:{target_port}{target_path_and_query}");

   R hands us `http://127.0.0.1/:<port>/...` but we rewrite to `localhost`.
   On Windows, `localhost` resolves to both `::1` and `127.0.0.1`. R's
   `tools::startDynamicHelp()` binds IPv4 only. This doesn't obviously
   explain a body-decode failure (the request would either succeed or be
   refused), but it's a needless ABI change at the edge and easy to
   eliminate by using `127.0.0.1` directly.

2. **R HTTPD chunked/Content-Length quirk on Windows.** R's internal HTTPD
   is small and may close the socket the moment the response finishes; on
   the slow disks of GH-hosted Windows runners, reqwest could see the
   close before fully buffering the chunked body.

3. **Windows Defender on the runner intercepting localhost HTTP.**
   Real-time scanning has been known to truncate localhost HTTP streams
   on hosted Windows runners. Worth confirming whether disabling Defender
   on the runner unblocks the test.

## Proposed fixes (low to high effort)

1. **Use `127.0.0.1` instead of `localhost`** in `proxy_request`
   (`help_proxy.rs:115`). Matches what R hands us; eliminates the
   IPv4/IPv6 ambiguity.

2. **Retry on body-read failure.** `RetryTransientMiddleware` (line 139)
   only retries the request setup; once headers are received, a body-decode
   failure is final. Wrap `response.bytes().await` in a small retry loop
   (or restructure to retry the full GET on body-decode failures), since
   the underlying R HTTPD will gladly re-serve the page.

3. **Add diagnostics.** Log `content-length` and `transfer-encoding`
   headers before calling `.bytes()`, plus the full `error.source()`
   chain. Reqwest's top-level error message hides the actual cause
   (truncated chunk vs. decompression failure vs. socket close).

4. **Stream the body instead of buffering** (`bytes_stream()`) so we can
   forward partial bodies and let the webview render whatever arrives.
   Larger change; not necessarily worth it for help pages, but would
   degrade more gracefully under truncation.

## Repro

- Run posit-dev/positron e2e `test/e2e/tests/environment-pane/environment-pane.test.ts`
  with `--project e2e-windows` against a recent build. Test
  `R - Opens package help in Help pane` (added in
  posit-dev/positron#13499) fails 100%.
- The bug is not specific to the test; the test merely exercises the path
  for the first time. Any flow that opens R package help (Packages pane
  help button, or `help(package=..., help_type="html")` from the console)
  reproduces the same proxy error on the affected runner.

## References

- Positron PR adding the failing test: posit-dev/positron#13499
- Failing run: posit-dev/positron actions/runs/26308765270
- Source: `crates/ark/src/help_proxy.rs` lines 115, 143, 191
```



## Steps to reproduce the issue:

1. Revert the temporary fix and include `@:win` and `@:packages-pane` test tag in a PR.
2. It should run the tests and fail.

@:packages-pane @:help @:ark

title: `openFolder` e2e fixture breaks on Windows when path contains backslashes
description:
`file-ops.fixtures.ts` line 33 does `folderPath.split('/')`, leading to failure if the caller passes a Windows-normalized path (backslashes).

**Fix:** Replace `folderPath.split('/')` with `folderPath.split(/[/\\]/)` in `test/e2e/fixtures/test-setup/file-ops.fixtures.ts`.

title: CI: only run tests when applicable
description:
### Problem

Every PR runs the same three required suites regardless of what changed: unit (~31m), ext-host (~31m), and e2e electron (~65m). On a change that touches only Markdown (for example), none of that work can tell us anything, because there is no code for those tests to exercise. In addition, we run the Full Suite of tests on windows, chromium and electron on merge as well!

_We want to stop running suites that cannot fail for a reason related to the change, without weakening the gate on real code changes._

### Why this is not a one-line change

The three required checks are produced by *inner* jobs of reusable workflows, so their names are composed as `<caller job> / <inner job>`. That makes them fragile in ways worth writing down.

Findings from a throwaway probe, [#15497](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/15497), which hardcoded `if: false` on each inner job:

| Required context | Published as | Satisfied? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test / unit` | `test / unit`, conclusion `skipped` | yes |
| `test / ext-host` | `test / ext-host`, conclusion `skipped` | yes |
| `e2e / electron` | `e2e / inputs.display_name \|\| 'e2e-linux'` | **no** |

1. A skipped job satisfies a required check. GitHub treats `skipped` as success.
2. A skipped inner job still publishes its composed context, but only when both halves of the name are literals.
3. `e2e / electron` fails because the inner job's name is `${{ inputs.display_name || 'e2e-linux' }}`, and a skipped job's name expression is never evaluated. GitHub publishes the raw expression text, so the required context never appears and the PR sits on "Expected -- Waiting for status to be reported" forever.

Point 3 is a latent trap regardless of what we decide here. Any future attempt to conditionally skip e2e at the job level will silently make `e2e / electron` unmergeable.

Constraints that rule out the obvious fixes:

- **e2e job names cannot simply be made static.** `display_name` is load-bearing across 13 workflows: shard jobs append `-${{ matrix.shard }}` and a separate aggregator reuses the bare name. The Slack notifier also filters on those names with `filter_jobs: "(e2e / ([^0-9]*)|unit|ext-host)$"`, where the `[^0-9]*$` anchor deliberately excludes `electron-win-1/2/3` so only aggregator rows are reported.
- **`paths-ignore` and `[skip ci]` are non-starters.** Both leave required checks in Pending forever. GitHub's own advice is "avoid requiring workflows that can be skipped," and the only documented workaround is a shadow workflow duplicating every job name.
- **Label-driven gating is ruled out.** Labels do not re-trigger with the default `pull_request` types, so one applied after the run starts does nothing until the next push, and fork contributors cannot self-label at all. There is also no prior art for it here: no workflow reads `pull_request.labels`, and across the last 200 merged PRs the only labels applied came from Dependabot.
- **`@:` tags fail open in the wrong direction for skipping.** `scripts/pr-tags-parse.sh` matches with an unanchored `grep`. Every tag today fails open toward *more* testing, so a stray match costs minutes; a skip tag would fail open toward an untested merge, and the likeliest stray match is a PR documenting the feature.
- **A merge queue would break PR-payload detection.** `merge_group` events carry no `pull_request` object, and `pr-tags` reads `github.event.pull_request.number`.


### Approaches

| # | Approach | Ruleset change | Config cost | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | One always-run `required-tests` gate job; suites gated with one caller-level `if:` | Yes: 3 contexts to 1 | ~8 lines + 3 `if:` | Leaves all job names alone, so Slack and the merge box are unaffected. Matches how 20 tag-gated e2e suites already work. |
| 2 | Keep jobs running, guard every step (implemented on `mi/mesquite-territory`) | No | ~52 step guards across 5 files | Works today. Verbose, and the PR and merge paths end up using different mechanisms. |
| 3 | Make all job names static so job-level `if:` works everywhere | Yes: context rename | Rename across 13 workflows | Breaks shard naming and the Slack regex, and reads worse (`e2e-electron / run`). |
| 4 | Ruleset "require workflows to pass" instead of check names | Yes: rule type | ~0 | Covers every e2e variant automatically, but makes all 24 jobs gating, so Windows e2e flakiness would start blocking merges. |
| 5 | `paths-ignore` / `[skip ci]` | n/a | n/a | Leaves required checks Pending. Non-starter. |

Approach 1 is the pattern used by cpython, pytest, and crate-ci/typos. Note the footgun: the gate needs `if: always()`, or a failed or skipped dependency skips the gate itself and a skipped gate reads as success. It must also check for `failure` and `cancelled` specifically, so an intentionally skipped suite still passes.

### Deciding what to skip (orthogonal to the mechanism)

Whatever mechanism we choose, the decision is one boolean and each reason is one term in it:

- **Docs-only detection from the diff.** A script and unit test already exist on `mi/mesquite-territory`. Allowlist is Markdown anywhere, `docs/**`, and root `LICENSE*`/`CHANGELOG*`/`NOTICE*`, failing safe to full CI on any error or empty diff. This is the term that actually fires without anyone remembering.
- **A wider allowlist** covering `.claude/skills/**` and `.devcontainer/**` would mechanically catch the 8 "almost docs-only" PRs from the sample.

This is the same problem the repo already solves at a finer granularity: `@:` tags gate 20 optional e2e suites, and `scripts/derive-test-change-tags.mjs` plus `test-tag-paths-map.json` already map changed paths to test tags. Skipping everything is the far end of that same spectrum.

### Open questions

- Approach 1 or approach 2. Approach 1 is cleaner but needs a ruleset edit.
- Widen the allowlist beyond docs now, or start narrow?
- Do we care about merge-queue compatibility yet? It would rule out PR-payload-based detection.

title: Check PPM per platform instead of building Positron in the bootstrap extensions nightly
description:
## Describe the issue:

The nightly bootstrap extensions check builds Positron on Linux and Windows just to find out whether PPM has a newer version, and even then it only covers Windows x64.

Right now the nightly launches Positron, lets it update each bootstrap extension, and treats any newer installed version as drift. The bump script then takes whatever PPM lists as latest without checking platforms. That's how meta.pyrefly 1.3.2, which has no win32-x64 build, got bumped in #16294.

## Expected or desired behavior:

Ask PPM directly in the nightly and skip the builds:

1. Get each extension's latest stable version from PPM. `update-extensions.sh` already does this.
2. If it's newer than the pin, probe the download for every platform we ship (win32, darwin, linux; x64 and arm64). For pyrefly, PPM returns 403 for 1.3.2 on win32-x64 and 206 for 1.3.1.
3. Bump only if every platform has it. Otherwise hold it back and post the held-back Slack message from #16329 (e.g. `meta.pyrefly 1.3.1 -> 1.3.2: no win32-x64 build`).
4. Drop the `extensions-linux` and `extensions-windows` build jobs.

The bump PR's tagged e2e tests then confirm the install actually works, which is the part the nightly's real Positron launch covers today. Optional extras: have the bot add `@:win` to bump PRs, and allow pyrefly in the Windows e2e run when the PR is tagged `@:pyrefly` (it's blocked there now).

Tradeoff: if a version exists for Windows but is broken there, we only catch it when the bump PR runs on Windows.

Follows #16329.

title: Headless LM service: support local providers (Ollama, LM Studio, OpenRouter)
description:
Follow-up to #13730. Part of #13729.

The headless LM service only registers providers the bridge has an auth mapping for (`MAPPED_PROVIDER_IDS`). Local/endpoint providers (Ollama, LM Studio, OpenRouter) are excluded via the bridge's `allowedProviders` filter, so users running local models get no ghost cell suggestions.

The omission is deliberate and documented in code: local providers need an endpoint-based credential path the headless service does not implement.

## What's needed

- An endpoint-credential path in the renderer/engine credential flow (these providers key off a user-configured endpoint URL, not an auth session).
- Register Ollama / LM Studio / OpenRouter once that path exists.
- Place them in the priority policy (`headlessLanguageModelSelection.ts`).

## Reference

- Omission documented: `src/vs/platform/positronHeadlessLanguageModel/node/headlessLanguageModelEngine.ts:107-114`
- Likely related to the bridge's credential-shaping work and the provider registry refactor (#14126).

R 4.5.0 (which sort of is the issue…)

## Describe the issue:

When starting Positron with a project using renv, it will activate the default R version, even though a different R version is recorded in `renv.lock` which is also available on the system.

I have a project that I last worked on using R 4.4.2. I use rig to manage my R installations and have since installed R 4.4.3  and R 4.5.0, with the newer one being the default.

```
❯ rig list
* name       version    aliases
------------------------------------------
  4.4-arm64  (R 4.4.3)  release
* 4.5-arm64  (R 4.5.0)
```

Both versions are visible to Positron and I can switch between them manually. But when I open Positron with this project, it activates R 4.5.0 – which among other problems, leaves me with an empty renv library because all packages were installed for R 4.4. When I change `renv.lock` to R 4.4.3, the 4.4. version I currently have installed, it still activates 4.5.0. I have to manually switch to 4.4.3 once and when I subsequently open the project, it will activate 4.4.3.

It would be great if Positron could read `renv.lock` and start the minor version of R recorded there if it's available.

title: Explore UX for opening a new agent tab
description:
## Problem

Users want to run several Posit Assistant conversations concurrently in editor tabs — start a long-running task (e.g. some slow data exploration), then begin a separate conversation while it chugs along in the background. This mirrors how people already work with multiple terminal tabs of an agent CLI.

There is no discoverable way to do this today:

- `Open Posit Assistant in editor panel` from the Command Palette does open an additional tab, but nothing surfaces it as "new tab".
- Re-invoking `View: Agent Layout` also spawns an extra Assistant tab, apparently unintentionally.
- The conversation history lets you switch between conversations, but not open one in a new tab — and it's many clicks to manage several at once.
- The experimental `features.conversationTabs` setting (`"top"` / `"side"`) gives tabs *within* the Assistant panel, which is not the same as separate editor tabs, and requires a restart.

## Ask

Design the UX for intentionally opening a new agent/Assistant tab. Ideas to consider:

- An explicit "New tab" affordance (button in the Assistant UI, `+` in the tab bar) rather than only a Command Palette entry.
- A clearly named command, e.g. `Posit Assistant: New Conversation in Editor Tab`.
- Opening an existing conversation from history into a new tab.
- Showing per-tab status so you can tell which conversations are still working.
- How this interacts with the agent layout, and with the in-panel `conversationTabs` experiment.

title: Windows e2e: CDP session for the reloaded renderer goes mute for ~25s while the app boots normally
description:
Windows e2e reload tests fail because the CDP session for the reloaded renderer goes mute in
both directions for ~25s while both endpoints are alive and the app boots normally.

#16001 raises the post-reload budget from 30s to 60s so the tests tolerate this. That is a
mitigation. This issue holds the evidence and the open questions, because the underlying
freeze is not understood.

## Symptom

`hotKeys.reloadWindow` polls `.monaco-workbench` on a 30s budget
([hotKeys.ts:341](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/test/e2e/pages/hotKeys.ts#L341)).
On Windows it intermittently reports:

```
Error: post-reload workbench probe did not settle within 2500ms
- Timeout 30000ms exceeded while waiting on the predicate
```

Ten specs carried this fingerprint across 93 fail/flaky events in a 14-day window (table in
#15942), all Windows-only. Five reload tests are currently `test.skip` for it, one annotated
only `// skipping because reloadWindow is unreliable`.

## Evidence

From [run 34239981288](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/actions/runs/34239981288),
`electron-win-2`, *Python - Verify interactive HTML widget persists correctly after window
reload* (`quarto-inline-output-dataframe.test.ts:181`), which failed both attempts.

**The probes were parked, not failing.** They passed once the channel drained:

| attempt | worst probe (2s timeout) | probes settled at | budget |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 19.4s | 33.80s | 30s |
| 1 | 17.0s | 30.86s | 30s |

**Messages sat in transit for ~25s.** Matching the trace's receipt timestamps against
`renderer.log` (the file logger, unaffected by #15942), restricted to post-reload
occurrences -- 150 records matched, **24.0s median, 26.2s worst case**:

| emitted by renderer | received by Playwright | delay |
|---|---|---|
| 16:15:05.943 | 16:15:29.5 | 23.6s |
| 16:15:06.409 | 16:15:31.8 | 25.4s |
| 16:15:07.118 | 16:15:33.2 | 26.1s |

During that window the CDP session delivered **zero** console events and **zero** screencast
frames, then flushed pushes and probe replies together at one instant.

**Both endpoints were alive.**

- Renderer: `renderer.log` wrote ~100 non-trace (console-eligible) records inside the freeze.
  They were generated and then sat.
- Runner: `e2e-test-runner.log` timestamped Electron stdout every second, never a gap over
  4s. That read is a direct OS pipe in the same process that owns the CDP connection
  (`code.ts:99`, `playwright._electron.launch`), so the node event loop was turning.

**The app was not slow.** The attached `renderer.log` covers the whole worker, so it contains
all three boots including the reload that *passed* 82 seconds earlier. Comparing the 364-381
log markers that appear exactly once per boot:

| boot | | median marker offset | ext host started |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16:11:46 | initial launch | 2.3s | +1.5s |
| 16:13:43 | passing reload | 2.1s | +0.9s |
| 16:15:05 | **failing** reload | 2.1s | +1.2s |

The failing reload booted at the same speed as the passing one on the same machine. So the
app was ready on schedule and the channel was 24-26s late.

*Caveat:* median-of-shared-markers is a coarse speed proxy and the three windows are not
equal length. The +1.2s ext-host start agrees, and the delivery delay is measured
independently.

## What this rules out

- **Console-echo volume.** #15942 pinned the smoke-driver console echo at Debug and it works:
  **zero** TRACE records reached the console echo in both attempts (614 of 791 were TRACE in
  the run measured for that PR), and window volume fell 791 -> 190. The failure is unchanged.
  Pre-fix the picture was 791 messages flowing with a 2.19s max gap -- push flowing while
  round trips starved. Now nothing flows at all. Different mechanism.
- **A slow runner / renderer too busy to answer.** See the boot comparison above.
- **A blocked node event loop.** See the stdout timestamps above.
- **A never-rendered workbench.** `.monaco-workbench` was in the DOM throughout.

## The open question

**Did the whole CDP connection go silent, or only the page session?**

CDP multiplexes sessions over one connection and every message carries a `sessionId`, but
everything measured above -- console pushes, screencast frames, DOM snapshots -- rides the
*same* page session. This evidence cannot distinguish the two, and the fork decides where to
look:

- **Other sessionIds still flowing** -> scoped to the renderer DevTools agent. Then the
  attach sequence (`Target.detachedFromTarget` / `attachedToTarget` /
  `Runtime.executionContextsCleared`) gives the re-attach duration directly, instead of
  inferring ~25s from when messages surfaced.
- **Whole connection silent** -> the transport or the browser process dispatch.

## Next steps

1. **Two-session liveness probe** (~10 lines, no log volume). Per probe iteration, race
   `page.evaluate(() => 1)` against `electronApp.evaluate(() => 1)` -- the Electron main
   process is a different process *and* a different session -- and log both latencies. The
   `ElectronApplication` is already held at `playwrightDriver.ts:68` and cast at line 114.
   Cheapest answer to the question above.
2. **`DEBUG=pw:protocol` on a targeted Windows repeat run.** Adds what (1) cannot: whether the
   probe request was written to the wire at probe start, the attach/detach sequence with
   timestamps, and the drain shape (one ordered burst vs gradual catch-up). Pair with
   `MAX_LOG_LENGTH=200` -- the default is `Infinity` and screencast frames otherwise dump full
   base64 payloads, adding real I/O load to the channel under measurement. The Windows
   workflow has `grep` / `repeat_each` / `upload_logs` inputs but no env passthrough, so this
   needs a small plumbing change.
3. **If renderer-session-scoped:** test whether Electron creates a *new* renderer target on
   reload while `this.code.driver.currentPage` still points at the old one. That would park
   queries like this. It does not cleanly explain the eventual pass, so it is a hypothesis to
   kill rather than a prediction -- but it is visible in the (2) log via
   `Target.targetInfoChanged`, and it is the shape of bug that would explain why five reload
   tests were skipped as "unreliable" without anyone finding the reason.
4. **If whole-connection:** establish whether `_electron.launch` connects over a pipe or a
   loopback websocket. Windows TCP loopback stalls under load are a known class, and
   `--remote-debugging-pipe` would be a direct A/B.
5. **Local repro.** Run the spec with `--repeat-each` under synthetic CPU load. Launch from an
   ordinary terminal, not from inside an agent session -- the agent process tree breaks the
   libzmq Windows poller and you will chase a kernel failure that is not real.

**Deliberately not on this list:** the existing `enable_diagnostic_logging` workflow input
(free memory / process list / load average per test, `_test.setup.ts:413`). It tests CPU
pressure, which the boot-speed comparison above already undercuts -- the failing reload
booted as fast as the passing one. Worth reaching for only if a later measurement puts
runner load back in play.

## Reproducing the analysis

The merge job for that run failed separately on `Download all blob reports` with a 403 from
`actions/download-artifact`, so the merged report is empty. The shard artifact
`blob-report-e2e-windows-2` is intact and contains both attempts' traces plus the attached
app logs, which is where all of the above came from.

## Notes

- Not a regression from any commit in that run; the head commit only bumps the quarto
  bootstrap extension in `product.json`.
- If the freeze is understood and fixed, the five skipped reload tests are re-enable
  candidates and the 60s budget from #16001 can come back down.

title: new folder flow: `Escape` does not close the Browse... folder picker inside a Positron modal
description:
<sub>Reported by [exploratory test](https://d38p2avprg8il3.cloudfront.net/exploratory-report-36480933114-1-opus-ubuntu-x64/index.html#f3) of #16161 (`midleman/allow-uv-installation-from-the-new-project-flow` @ `327a709fa5`)</sub>

## System details
**Positron and OS:**  
Positron 2026.10.0 build 0 (dev build of `327a709fa5`)  
Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, Linux x86_64

**Session:**  
Python 3.14.6 (conda-forge, /opt/conda) as the base for the uv environments; Python 3.12.3 at /usr/bin/python; uv 0.12.9 on PATH for the pre-launched instance, uv 0.12.19 installed by the flow in the uv-absent instances  
R 4.5.2

## Describe the issue
**Confirmed the issue reproduces on `main`** https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/commit/361e87e3db5e1cceee0e9cf0ce32938432fc28c3 despite being discovered in a branch.
Picker can only be dismissed by choosing a folder

## Steps to reproduce
- The New Folder from Git dialog (New in the top action bar, then New Folder from Git...) is open, and its Browse... folder picker is showing.
- Only with `files.simpleDialog.enable: true`, which the launcher sets in every profile. Native dialogs were not checked.

1. Focus the picker's input and press Escape.
2. Verify the picker closes → **FAIL** (observed: The picker is still open, 519 px tall, with focus in its input.)
3. Focus the picker's input again and press Escape.
4. Verify the picker closes → **FAIL** (observed: The picker is still open; only its OK button dismisses it.)

## Expected
Escape closes the picker and returns focus to the dialog, as it does for a quick pick in the workbench (S23).

## Actual
With focus in the picker, Escape does nothing. The dialog beneath is inert, so its Cancel does nothing either. The only way out is to pick a folder with OK. The New Folder flow's name step behaves the same way (S17).

## Error messages
None recorded by the run.

## Evidence
Screenshots and logs are in the [exploratory test](https://d38p2avprg8il3.cloudfront.net/exploratory-report-36480933114-1-opus-ubuntu-x64/index.html#f3) report for this run.

<details><summary>Likely cause (hypothesis, not verified)</summary>

Escape probably never reaches the quick input's close keybinding while the widget sits inside a Positron modal. `useModalDialogKeyboard` in `src/vs/workbench/browser/positronComponents/positronModalDialog/useModalDialogKeyboard.tsx` returns early for quick-pick targets (`isFromQuickPick`, line 82) but does not close them. The `inQuickOpen` keybinding context may not be set for a widget that was reparented out of the workbench container. The older New Folder from Git dialog behaves the same way, so this predates the change. Escape was not checked on this exact picker outside a modal. The workbench control in S23 used the help quick pick.

</details>

<details><summary>Regression test (suggestion; the verifier left this finding unresolved)</summary>

- Pressing Escape in a quick pick that was reparented into a Positron modal hides it → add to src/vs/platform/quickinput/test/browser/quickinput.test.ts (Unit)
Other tests that touch this code: src/vs/workbench/browser/positronComponents/positronModalDialog/test/useModalDialogKeyboard.vitest.tsx (Unit)

</details>
