title: Bundled ipykernel discards pixi [activation.env] PYTHONPATH due to collision
description:
<!--

Thanks for taking the time to file an issue!

Take a look at our guidance on feedback and issues:
https://positron.posit.co/feedback.html

General questions about Positron should start in GitHub Discussions rather than as an issue:
https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/discussions

To avoid creating duplicates, please take the time to search our existing issues:
https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues
If you find an existing bug or feature request, please gives it a thumbs-up reaction or
additional information to help us prioritize the issue.

-->

## System details:

#### Positron and OS details:

Positron Version: 2026.09.1 build 2
Code - OSS Version: 1.130.0
Commit: 467ff390dd8b4ffc8972ebb84d9e05a1fd5a4fe2
Date: 2026-09-04T09:54:04-07:00
Electron: 42.6.0
Chromium: 148.0.7778.280
Node.js: 24.18.0
V8: 14.8.178.38-electron.0
OS: Darwin arm64 25.6.0

#### Session details:

Python 3.14.7 | packaged by conda-forge | (main, Sep 2 2026, 21:04:32) [Clang 20.1.8 ]
<!-- LLM model used in for Positron Assistant, e.g. `Claude 3.7 Sonnet v1` -->

## Describe the issue:

When using a Pixi Python environment, `PYTHONPATH` defined in `pixi.toml` under `[activation.env]` is ignored by a newly launched Positron Python console.

For example:

```toml
[activation.env]
PYTHONPATH = "/path/expected/in/python"
````

The Python console does not contain that value in `os.environ["PYTHONPATH"]`.

### User-side workaround
Based on the diagnosis outlined below, I successfully implemented the following workaround: I installed `ipykernel` in the Pixi environment and set:

```
"python.useBundledIpykernel": false
```

After starting a new Python console, the `PYTHONPATH` defined in `pixi.toml` was no longer ignored.

### AI-assisted code-analysis diagnosis

This diagnosis was prepared with AI assistance from static source review only. It was not verified by building Positron, running its test suite, or debugging a local Positron build. Please treat the implementation details below as a focused hypothesis to confirm, rather than a definitive root-cause claim.

The apparent cause is environment-variable precedence during Python kernel startup:

1. Positron’s Python activation service captures Pixi’s activated environment using `pixi run ... python`.
2. Those activated variables are contributed to the kernel supervisor as process-creation environment actions.
3. The supervisor applies kernel-spec environment variables afterwards, as replacement actions.
4. When `python.useBundledIpykernel` is enabled, Positron adds its bundled ipykernel directories to `PYTHONPATH` in the Python kernel spec.
5. That later kernel-spec `PYTHONPATH` replacement overwrites the `PYTHONPATH` captured from Pixi activation.

This explains why disabling the bundled ipykernel and using an environment-installed `ipykernel` avoids the issue.

The underlying precedence behavior may not be limited to Pixi or to `PYTHONPATH`. Any Python environment manager whose activation contributes a variable that also appears in the final kernel spec may be affected. This could include Conda and other environment types, depending on their activation output. `PATH` may be another especially relevant collision.

## Steps to reproduce the issue:

<!-- For example, are you using a Jupyter notebook, R script, Quarto document, etc? -->

1. Create or open a Pixi project with a Python environment.
    
2. Define `PYTHONPATH` under `[activation.env]` in `pixi.toml`.
    
3. Ensure Positron’s default setting is in effect:
    
    ```
    "python.useBundledIpykernel": true
    ```
    
4. Select the Pixi Python interpreter in Positron and launch a new Python Console.
    
5. Run:
    
    ```
    import os
    print(os.environ.get("PYTHONPATH"))
    ```
    
6. Observe that the `PYTHONPATH` value from `pixi.toml` is absent or does not contain the expected activation value.
    
7. Install `ipykernel` in the Pixi environment, set `"python.useBundledIpykernel": false`, and launch a new console.
    
8. Observe that `PYTHONPATH` now contains the value from `pixi.toml`.
    

## Expected or desired behavior:

The Python console should receive both:

- environment variables materialized by Pixi activation, including `[activation.env]` values; and
- any Positron-specific paths required for its bundled ipykernel.

If both require `PYTHONPATH`, Positron should merge them with a documented ordering rather than replacing Pixi’s activated value.

More generally, activated environment variables should not be silently discarded merely because an identically named variable appears in the Python kernel spec.

## Were there any error messages in the UI, Output panel, or Developer Tools console?

I did not observe any error messages

title: python: kernel fails to start on ARM64 Windows when the interpreter is not ARM64 or x64
description:
## Summary

On ARM64 Windows, installing Python 3.9 through Positron's "Install Python via uv" flow and then starting a session with it fails during kernel startup. The interpreter uv installs is not native ARM64, so Positron appends the **ARM64** ipykernel bundle to its `PYTHONPATH`, and the ARM64 `psutil` binary then cannot load into the non-ARM64 process:

```
The process exited abnormally (exit code: 1)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../positron_language_server.py", line 10, in <module>
    from positron.positron_ipkernel import (
  File ".../positron/positron_ipkernel.py", line 23, in <module>
    import psutil
  File ".../python_files/lib/ipykernel/arm64/cp3/psutil/__init__.py", line 101, in <module>
    from . import _pswindows as _psplatform
  File ".../python_files/lib/ipykernel/arm64/cp3/psutil/_pswindows.py", line 30, in <module>
    from ._psutil_windows import ABOVE_NORMAL_PRIORITY_CLASS
ImportError: DLL load failed while importing _psutil_windows: %1 is not a valid Win32 application.
```

`%1 is not a valid Win32 application` is Windows' error for loading a DLL whose CPU architecture does not match the process. The bundled binaries themselves are correct (the `arm64` bundle really is ARM64 and the `x64` bundle really is x64/AMD64) -- the problem is that the **wrong bundle is selected** for the interpreter.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 ARM64 (`Windows_NT arm64 10.0.26200`)
- Positron: 2026.07.1 (user setup) build 5
- Affected interpreter: Python 3.9 installed via Positron's "Install Python via uv" flow (non-ARM64)
- Other Python interpreters (detected as native ARM64 or x64) start fine.

## Steps to reproduce

1. On an ARM64 Windows machine, use Positron's "Install Python via uv" flow to install Python 3.9.
2. Select that interpreter in Positron and start a session.
3. The kernel fails to start with the `_psutil_windows` / `%1 is not a valid Win32 application` traceback above.

To confirm the interpreter's architecture from within that Python:

```python
import sysconfig, struct
print(sysconfig.get_platform(), struct.calcsize("P") * 8, "bit")
# win32 ... 32 bit   -> x86 fallback case
# win-amd64 ... 64 bit -> detection returned undefined/Unknown and defaulted to arm64
```

## Expected behavior

The kernel should either start with the correct bundle or degrade gracefully -- it should never load a wrong-architecture native extension.

title: positron-commands skill: data connections commands
description:
Part of #15343.

## Description

Give Assistant the data connections commands: the reference file that documents reading the user's configured connections and walking a live connection's schema. This covers the skill side of the plan in #14664.

## Commands

| Command ID | Agent-compatible in | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `positronDataConnections.getConnections` | #15452 | Done |

title: Variables pane: long variable names clip without an ellipsis
description:
Noticed while working discussion https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/discussions/15763. Visible in that screenshot: names are cut mid-character with no `...`, while values in the same rows truncate with a proper ellipsis.

## Cause

The ellipsis declarations are on an ancestor that does not directly contain the text.

- `.variable-item .name-column` sets `overflow: hidden`, `white-space: nowrap`, `text-overflow: ellipsis`, but is `display: flex` (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/positronVariables/browser/components/variableItem.css:61`).
- The name text is rendered in `.name-value` (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/positronVariables/browser/components/variableItem.tsx:456`), nested inside `.name-column-indenter`. `.name-value` is `display: flex` with no overflow rules (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/positronVariables/browser/components/variableItem.css:91`).

`text-overflow` applies to the block container that directly holds the overflowing inline content, so the declaration on `.name-column` is inert and the name hard-clips.

For contrast, `.details-column .value` carries all three properties on the element holding the text (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/positronVariables/browser/components/variableItem.css:101`), which is why values ellipsize correctly.

## Suggested fix

Move or add `overflow: hidden`, `white-space: nowrap`, `text-overflow: ellipsis` to `.name-value`, and give it `min-width: 0` so it can shrink inside its flex parent. A tooltip carrying the full name would help too, since the name column cannot grow past its default width.

Analysis by Claude during intake, reviewed before posting. Verified: the markup and CSS. Not verified: no fix was written or tested in a running build.


Related: #15770 covers the redundant signature text and the column sizing behavior from the same report.

title: Data Connections: every driver extension activates when the pane opens
description:
Opening the Data Connections pane activates all seven data connection driver extensions at once. Each one then loads its database SDK, because the SDK is required at the top of the module chain. A user who only wants SQLite still pays for the Databricks and Snowflake SDKs.

### Why they all activate

Every driver declares the same activation event:

```json
"activationEvents": ["onView:workbench.panel.positronDataConnections"]
```

They have to. The only way a driver becomes known to Positron is `positron.dataConnections.registerDriver(driver)`, which the extension calls from `activate()`. The Add Connection dialog needs each driver's id, name, description, icon, and parameter definitions before the user picks anything, so every extension must run first.

### What that costs

Activation is not just registering a small object. The require chain reaches the SDK at the top level:

```
extension.js
  -> databricksDriver.js
    -> databricksConnection.js
      -> databricksClient.js
        -> require("@databricks/sql")
```

Snowflake, PostgreSQL, and Redshift have the same shape. On-disk package sizes for what this pulls in:

| Package | Size on disk |
| --- | --- |
| `@databricks/sql` | 16M |
| `snowflake-sdk` | 5.8M |
| `pg` | 144K |

On-disk size overstates what the runtime actually parses, so the honest next step is to time `activate()` rather than trust these numbers. The order of magnitude still looks worth acting on.

SQLite and DuckDB already avoid this. They externalize their native modules and run queries in a worker process, so the extension host pays nothing for them at activation.

### Option 1, cheap, no core change

Break the top-level require chain in the four SDK-backed drivers. Load the SDK with a dynamic `await import(...)` inside the connect path instead of importing it at the top of the client module. All seven extensions still activate, but activation costs only what it should: registering a metadata object.

This gets most of the benefit and can ship on its own. Measure activation time before and after.

### Option 2, proper, needs a core change

Declare drivers statically so the dialog can list them without running any extension code.

1. Add a `contributes.dataConnectionDrivers` contribution point carrying id, name, description, icon path, and the mechanism and parameter declarations.
2. Core reads those from the extension registry without activating anything, and renders the pane and the Add Connection dialog from them.
3. Add an `onDataConnectionDriver:<id>` activation event, fired when the user selects that driver or opens a saved connection of that type.
4. Keep `registerDriver` as the runtime API for the implementation, matched to the static declaration by id.

VS Code solves this same shape in several places, so there is precedent to copy: `contributes.debuggers` with `onDebugResolve:<type>`, `contributes.authentication` with `onAuthenticationRequest:<id>`, and terminal profiles with `onTerminalProfile:<id>`.

The hard part is step 1. Mechanisms and parameters are rich TypeScript today, with localized labels and conditional fields. Moving them into the manifest needs a declarative schema and `package.nls.json` entries, and then something to stop the manifest and the TypeScript from drifting apart. `configurationAttributes` on `contributes.debuggers` shows this is tractable, but it is most of the work.

Option 2 also lets an out-of-repo driver appear in the dialog without running its code, which Option 1 does not.

### Suggested order

Do Option 1 first and measure. If activation drops to noise, Option 2 becomes a design tidiness argument rather than a performance one, and can wait until there is a reason to want third party drivers listed without activation.

### Related

Found while working on #14905, which gives each driver a lazily created log output channel. That work stops the visible symptom, which was every driver adding an empty entry to the Output panel as soon as the pane opened. It does not change the activation cost described here.

title: kcserver (kallichore) burns ~13 CPU cores after starting a kernel session in REH 2026.09.1-2 (futex/sched_yield storm, /proc scan flood)
description:
# kcserver (kallichore) burns ~13 CPU cores after starting a kernel session in REH 2026.09.1-2 (futex/sched_yield storm, /proc scan flood)

## Environment

- Positron client on Windows, Remote-SSH into Linux server (REH)
- Server component: Positron REH **2026.09.1-2** (commit `467ff390dd8b4ffc8972ebb84d9e05a1fd5a4fe2`), Linux x86_64
- Bundled kallichore: `kcserver 0.1.68`
- Server is a busy multi-user machine: 16 cores, ~50 concurrent users, ~3,000+ processes
- Language sessions involved: Python (conda env) and R (ark) — same behavior with either

## Summary

After connecting via Remote-SSH and **starting a console/kernel session**, `kcserver` begins spinning at a sustained **12.5–13.2 of 16 cores** and never stops on its own (observed 28+ minutes until manually killed). During the spin:

- Its own debug log (`--log-level debug`) is completely **silent**
- The kernels it supervises are idle (<0.3% CPU) — no user code is running
- Thread count is **513** = 1 main + 512 `tokio-runtime-w` (blocking pool at its default max)

The machine admin flagged the account for excessive CPU usage. Reproduced **3/3 times**; each recurrence was on session creation. Killing kcserver immediately restores normal load; the extension restarts it.

## Control experiments (all with the same 0.1.68 binary, same flags as production)

1. **No session → no spin.** Simulating the extension's client-owned handshake socket (per kallichore #73) and running kcserver standalone with the exact production flags (`--resource-sample-interval 1000 --transport socket --idle-shutdown-hours 1`): idles at **0.00 cores**, 257 threads, all parked in `futex_do_wait`.
2. **`GET /status` is cheap and unlogged.** 0.30 ms/call, zero log lines — a plain polling loop cannot account for 13 cores.
3. **Same binary was fine for two months.** 2026.08.1-2 bundled the same kallichore 0.1.68 (0.1.67→0.1.68 has zero code changes) and never exhibited this across ~84 kernel sessions. The trigger appears to be the new supervisor/extension-side driving pattern in 2026.09.1-2.

## Thread forensics (during spin)

Per-thread `utime+stime` snapshot ~10 s after session creation:

- Baseline ~257 threads: ~0 CPU each (normal parked pool)
- ~256 **newly spawned** threads in the first 10 s: **~1 CPU-second each**, all `tokio-runtime-w`, mostly `futex_do_wait` with several in R state

This is a flood of short-lived blocking tasks saturating the pool to its 512 cap.

## strace evidence (decisive)

Ran kcserver under `strace -f -c` (wrapper script, since ptrace attach is restricted) and created a session; collected the summary over a ~30 s window of the spin — **1,018,611 syscalls total**:

```
% time     seconds  usecs/call     calls    errors syscall
 86.45 7958.744354       22601    352137     97895 futex
  8.19  753.860667        1724    437264           sched_yield
  2.31  212.663891        3446     61703     35093 openat
  1.39  127.830193        4027     31743         4 getdents64
  0.73   66.923941        2720     24597           fstat
  0.70   64.694923        2422     26711           close
  0.17   15.325816       21023       729           epoll_wait
 ... (read/lseek/statx/stat similar shape)
```

Interpretation: `openat`(35k ENOENT)+`getdents64`+`fstat`+`close` at this rate is consistent with **/proc being scanned far more often than the configured 1000 ms sample interval**, with each scan dispatched as blocking tasks; 512 threads then burn CPU on `futex` contention + `sched_yield`. On a host with 3,000+ processes the per-scan cost amplifies the storm. (Note: under `strace -f -c` the visible CPU is suppressed to ~1 core, but the syscall counts expose the loop.)

Possibly related: #15943 (supervisor log level for web/server pre-warming) and kallichore #76 (no boundary logging on the `server_status` handler — matches the log silence during the spin).

## Reproduction

1. Install REH 2026.09.1-2 on a Linux server (ideally with many processes running).
2. Connect with Remote-SSH from a matching client.
3. Open a Python (or R) console → kernel session starts.
4. `kcserver` ramps to ~13 cores within seconds and stays there.

## Workaround

Pinning kcserver to a single core (`taskset -apc 0 <pid>`) caps the damage at 1 core and keeps sessions usable; killing kcserver restores the cores but breaks sessions.

Happy to provide the full debug logs (`kallichore-*.log`), the complete strace summary, and the per-thread forensics on request.

title: Data connections: Expose Snowflake data lineage as context to Assistant
description:
Requested by @chetan-posit 

## Context

Snowflake natively tracks data lineage i.e. how data flows between objects (upstream sources → downstream targets). 

Reference doc: https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/ui-snowsight-lineage

What lineage covers:
* Two relationship types: data movement and object dependencies.
* Supported objects: all "table-like" objects — tables, dynamic tables, external tables, Iceberg tables, views, materialized views, semantic views — plus stages and ML objects (Datasets, Feature Views, Models).
* Column-level lineage between any two table-like objects (with a "distance" indicating hops).

## AC

1. We want to surface lineage as context to Assistant so it can answer questions like "where does this table's data come from?", "what breaks if I change this column?", and "is this derived from PII-tagged sources?".

2. Spike on best way to expose this information 
3. Implement or create followup tickets 


## What Snowflake provides
No dedicated REST endpoint. Programmatic access is via SQL, callable through the SQL API (POST /api/v2/statements), connector, or Snowpark:

- SNOWFLAKE.CORE.GET_LINEAGE (table function) — the primary interface. Near-real-time; returns upstream or downstream lineage for a given object, with a max traversal depth of 5. Snowflake notes it returns a subset of what the Snowsight Lineage tab shows.

```
SELECT * FROM TABLE(SNOWFLAKE.CORE.GET_LINEAGE(
    'MY_DB.MY_SCHEMA.MY_TABLE',  -- object name
    'TABLE',                      -- object domain: TABLE, COLUMN, STAGE, ...
    'DOWNSTREAM',                 -- or UPSTREAM
    3                             -- depth (max 5)
  ));
```

```
ACCOUNT_USAGE views (OBJECT_DEPENDENCIES, ACCESS_HISTORY) — bulk/graph-building alternative, but with 45min–3h refresh latency. Better for periodic sync into our own store; worse for interactive queries.
```

## How might we expose this
1. Extend the existing Snowflake skill - add a lineage section to the Snowflake SKILL.md in posit-dev/assistant with GET_LINEAGE query patterns, the object-domain/direction/depth parameters, and the gotchas. 
2. On-demand structured tool - a first-class get_lineage(object, direction, depth) tool alongside the schema-context tooling from #14658. 
3. Context injection on selection — when the user has an object focused in the Data Connections pane, prefetch 1–2 hops up/downstream and include a compact serialization in the Assistant's context, alongside the schema context 

## Notes 
1. Enterprise Edition (or higher) required for data lineage feature.
2. Lineage is not available for the following kinds of objects:
- Objects in a shared database.
- Objects in the shared SNOWFLAKE database.
- Objects in the INFORMATION_SCHEMA of a database.
- Semantic views created before early February 2026.

https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/ui-snowsight-lineage#limitations-and-considerations

title: Show the oauth device code in the provider modal instead of a separate dialog
description:
## Describe the issue

Signing in to Posit AI from the new Configure LLM Providers modal opens a smaller dialog on top of the current one, just to show the one-time device code.

Current: provider list -> connect view -> "Posit AI Sign In" dialog with the code
Wanted:  provider list -> connect view, with the code shown in the connect view

## What the connect view should show

While a Posit AI sign-in is in flight, the connect view should show:

- the one-time code, large enough to read and select
- a Copy button (the code is still copied to the clipboard automatically)

Nice to have, depending on how much of the sign-in logic has to change:

- the verification URL, with a way to reopen it
- a line saying we are waiting for the browser

The existing Cancel path stays as it is. On success the view advances to the connected view as it does today.

## Decide when the browser opens

The dialog does two jobs today: it shows the code, and its OK button is what
opens the browser. Moving the code into the modal only replaces the first job,
so we have to pick what triggers the browser. Either works; decide once the
implementation is underway.

1. Open it as soon as the code comes back. Fewest clicks. The browser takes focus a beat after you click Connect, with no warning, but the code stays visible in the modal so nothing is lost.
2. Show an "Open Browser" button in the connect view next to the code. One more click, and closer to today's behavior.

## Open question: sign-in started outside the modal

`next-edit-suggestions` can trigger a Posit AI sign-in through `vscode.authentication.getSession`, with no modal on screen to show the code in. The existing dialog has to stay for that case.

The simplest way to tell the two apart: `providerAction` in `configDialog.ts` is
the only modal-originated entry point, so it can set a flag that `signIn()`
reads.

## GitHub Copilot

The device code UI lives in `extensions/github-authentication/src/flows.ts`, an upstream VS Code file we would pay a merge conflict for on every upstream merge (if we changed this flow), and `vscode.authentication.getSession` gives the caller no way to observe the flow and report the code back. Worth some thought if this is worth doing.

title: Data Explorer format options are hard-coded and unreachable for backends without a language runtime
description:
The Data Explorer's `FormatOptions` are hard-coded in the frontend and cannot be changed by anyone -- not by a setting, and not by a backend. For backends with a language runtime this is at least addressable in principle, via the language-pack approach explored in #4818 and the WIP in #11326. For a database connection there is no such escape hatch: there is no R or Python session behind a PostgreSQL, Databricks, Snowflake, Redshift, ODBC, SQLite, or DuckDB connection, so no language pack can supply its options.

### Problem

There is exactly one source of `FormatOptions` for every Data Explorer backend, set in the constructor of `languageRuntimeDataExplorerClient.ts` and never modified afterwards:

```ts
this._dataFormatOptions = {
	large_num_digits: 2,
	small_num_digits: 4,
	max_integral_digits: 7,
	max_value_length: 1000,
	thousands_sep: '',
};

this._profileFormatOptions = { /* the same, with thousands_sep: ',' */ };
```

Despite the class name, this is not language-runtime specific -- these options are sent over the protocol to *every* backend, including the extension-provided data drivers. `max_integral_digits` appears nowhere else in `src/vs` outside the generated comm types.

The practical consequence is `max_integral_digits: 7`: any value with more than seven integral digits is rendered in exponential notation, no matter what the backend sends and no matter what the user would prefer.

| Stored value | Displayed |
| --- | --- |
| `9999999.99` | `9999999.99` |
| `10000000` | `1.00e+7` |
| `123456789012345678901234567890.12` | `1.23e+29` |

A `NUMERIC(38,2)` financial column, or an identifier column of wide integers, is unreadable in the grid and there is no way to change that.

### Why this is not covered by the existing issues

- **#4818** asks the Data Explorer to respect R's `options(scipen = ...)`. Same symptom, but the proposed remedy is language-pack driven, and #11326 (WIP, closed) built `dataExplorer.useLanguagePackFormatOptions` along those lines. Landing that would close #4818 while leaving every database connection exactly as it is today.
- **#11525** asks for presentation formatting -- European separators, percentages, per-column display formats. Adjacent and complementary, but about how a value is styled rather than how many of its digits survive.
- **#13493** asks for trailing `.00` to be suppressed on integer-valued columns. Also a digits question, but at the opposite end of the magnitude range.

The gap none of them covers: a backend that has no language runtime has no path to these options at all.

### Why it matters now

#15366 made the SQL drivers format a `DECIMAL`/`NUMERIC` from its exact digit string rather than coercing it through a JS number, and #15885 and #15887 will do the same for DuckDB and Snowflake. Those changes are correct and tested, but the exact digits arrive at the formatter and are then discarded by the display cap: a wide value still renders as `1.23e+29`, byte-identical to before. The precision work is real but currently invisible, and it stays invisible until this is addressed.

Exports are unaffected and already exact, so CSV/TSV export is the only current workaround for reading a wide value.

### Options

1. **Expose the format options as settings.** The most direct fix, works for every backend regardless of runtime, and generalizes what #11525 asks for. Needs a decision on granularity: global, per-connection, or per-column.
2. **Make the grid decide from the data.** Let a column widen to fit its values and fall back to exponential notation only when it genuinely cannot, rather than at a fixed threshold of seven. Better default behavior with no user configuration, but a larger change to column sizing.
3. **Keep the cap, make the exact value reachable.** Leave the grid rendering as it is and surface the full value on cell selection, hover, or copy. Cheaper, and it addresses "I need to read this one value" without touching layout -- but not "this column is unreadable."

Options 1 and 3 are not mutually exclusive and 3 is the smallest useful step.

### Acceptance criteria

- A wide `DECIMAL`/`NUMERIC` value in a database connection can be read at full precision in the Data Explorer, without exporting the data.
- Whatever mechanism is chosen works for backends with no language runtime.
- The default behavior for ordinary values is unchanged, or changed deliberately with the current defaults documented as the baseline.

### Related

- #4818 -- scientific notation vs. R's `scipen` (same symptom, language-pack framing)
- #11525 -- presentation formatting options
- #13493 -- trailing `.00` on integer-valued columns
- #11326 -- closed WIP for `dataExplorer.useLanguagePackFormatOptions`
- #15366, #15885, #15887 -- exact decimal delivery, currently masked by this cap

This is problematic in a few ways: - makes files unnecessarily long - introduces inconsistencies: - between lists when authors switch between Source and Visual modes - between unordered and ordered lists (ordered lists don't have that issue) - but also inside a single list (when adding an element inside an existing list) - might create unnecessary noise in version control (e.g. when trying to make things consistent again in Source mode) - it does not match the [Quarto manual](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/markdown-basics.html#lists) - the rendered document (e.g. HTML) has different spacing between lists with and without spaces (because of paragraph tags in the list elements when there are empty lines) Note that RStudio behaves in a similar way, so ideally the issue would be fixed in conjunction in both IDEs. Side-by-side of Visual Mode, Source Mode and rendered HTML: The source HTML for the same two lists: ```html

test list from source:

  • first
  • second
    • third indented
    • added in Visual mode
  • fourth not

Another from Visual:

  • first

  • second

    • third indented
    • added in Visual mode

  • fourth not

out of list.

``` Thankfully, the resulting structure is consistent for screen readers (i.e. it does not consider each element to be a separate list). ## Steps to reproduce the issue: 1. Create a new .qmd file 2. Turn on Visual Mode from the three-dot menu: "Edit in Visual Mode" 3. Insert a list by using the toolbar or starting a line with a hyphen followed by a space 4. Switch to source editor with the three-dot menu: "Edit in Source Mode" 5. See that there are empty lines between elements 6. Switch back to Visual Mode 7. Add an item in the middle of the list 8. Switch back to Source Mode 9. See that the new item was added without an empty line 10. Render the document to HTML 11. See the HTML and its source ## Expected or desired behaviour: * No empty lines between list elements * Lists that are visually consistent * Rendered document structure that is simpler and matches the author's expectation of a single list. ## Were there any error messages in the UI, Output panel, or Developer Tools console? NA

title: Extension host crashes repeatedly after updating to Positron 2026.09.1-2 on Windows (createProxyAuthorizationLookup export error)
description:
## Describe the issue
After updating Positron to 2026.09.1-2 on Windows, the local Extension Host crashes repeatedly immediately after startup.

As a result, the Environment Setup checks on the Welcome page cannot complete for either Python or R:

- "The Python check could not be completed."
- "The R check could not be completed."

The notification repeatedly reports: `Extension host terminated unexpectedly 3 times within the last 5 minutes.`

This problem started after the Positron update. Positron was working normally before the update.

I initially suspected an extension compatibility issue, but Extension Bisect disabled all 14 installed extensions and the crash still occurred. The Developer Tools console also reports: `No extensions were activated.`

This suggests that the failure occurs during Extension Host startup, before user extensions are activated.

## Environment
Positron Version: 2026.09.1 (user setup) build 2
Code - OSS Version: 1.130.0
Commit: 467ff390dd8b4ffc8972ebb84d9e05a1fd5a4fe2
Date: 2026-09-04T09:54:04-07:00
Electron: 42.6.0
Chromium: 148.0.7778.280
Node.js: 24.18.0
V8: 14.8.178.38-electron.0
OS: Windows_NT x64 10.0.26200

## Steps to reproduce
1. Start Positron 2026.09.1-2 on Windows.
2. Open the Positron Welcome page.
3. Observe that both Python and R environment checks cannot be completed.
4. Wait for the local Extension Host to start.
5. The Extension Host terminates unexpectedly and is automatically restarted.
6. After several attempts, Positron reports:
   "Extension host terminated unexpectedly 3 times within the last 5 minutes."
7. Run "Start Extension Bisect".
8. Allow Bisect to disable all 14 installed extensions.
9. The same Extension Host crash still occurs.

## Expected behavior
The local Extension Host should start successfully, extensions should be activated normally, and Positron should be able to complete the Python and R environment health checks.

## Actual behavior
The local Extension Host exits with code 1 before any extensions are activated. The Extension Host is automatically restarted several times and continues to crash. 

Because the Extension Host never becomes ready, commands required by the environment health checks are unavailable, including:
- `python.getEnvironmentHealth`
- `r.getEnvironmentHealth`

The Welcome page therefore reports that both Python and R checks could not be completed.

## Relevant Developer Tools console error
```text
SyntaxError: Named export 'createProxyAuthorizationLookup' not found. The requested module '@vscode/proxy-agent' is a CommonJS module, which may not support all module.exports as named exports.
CommonJS modules can always be imported via the default export, for example using:
import pkg from '@vscode/proxy-agent';
const { LogLevel: LogLevel4, createHttpPatch, createProxyAuthorizationLookup, createProxyResolver, createTlsPatch, createNetPatch, loadSystemCertificates } = pkg;    
    at #asyncInstantiate (node:internal/modules/esm/module_job:327:21)    
    at async ModuleJob.run (node:internal/modules/esm/module_job:431:5)    
    at async onImport.tracePromise.__proto__ (node:internal/modules/esm/loader:643:26)    
    at async file:///d:/Program%20Files/Positron/resources/app/out/bootstrap-fork.js:1046:1
Node.js v24.18.0
```

## Related upstream issues
I searched the existing Positron issues but did not find an issue with the same `createProxyAuthorizationLookup` error signature. There are other Positron issues involving Extension Host startup/restart problems, but they appear to have different root causes.

The closest matching issue I found is upstream: microsoft/vscode#328700

That issue reports an Extension Host startup crash in VS Code / Code OSS 1.130 and 1.131 with Node.js 24.18.0 and the same `createProxyAuthorizationLookup` / `@vscode/proxy-agent` error.

My Positron installation reports Code - OSS 1.130.0 and Node.js 24.18.0, so this may be the same upstream regression or a related integration issue.

title: Local model providers (Ollama, LM Studio) only work in Posit Assistant chat, not other Positron AI features
description:
Support local model providers (Ollama, LM Studio) in other Positron AI features, not just Posit Assistant.

## Summary

Posit Assistant lets users configure two local model providers, Ollama and LM Studio, through the "Configure LLM Providers" dialog (`registerLocalProviders` in `~/dev/assistant/packages/positron/src/positron-ai/local-provider-registration.ts`). It's not obvious to a user that setting one of these up only makes it usable in Assistant's own chat, and not in Positron's other AI features (notebook AI, Next Edit Suggestions). We should verify this gap is intentional, and if so, make it visible to users instead of a silent limitation.

## What we found

Positron has three separate model-selection paths that don't share state:

1. **`positron.ai.registerProvider()` / `updateProvider()`** (used by Assistant to register Ollama and LM Studio): lands in `PositronAssistantConfigurationService._providerRegistrations` (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/positronAssistant/browser/positronAssistantService.ts:45,72-128`). `getRegisteredSources()` only feeds the "Configure LLM Providers" dialog. Nothing else in Positron reads this list.

2. **Notebook AI (ghost cell)** (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/positronNotebook/browser/contrib/ghostCell/controller.ts:91,288`) goes through `IHeadlessLanguageModelService`, which is backed by a separate provider catalog (`IAiProviderService`, `providers.json`) and authentication sessions. The headless engine explicitly excludes local endpoint providers:

	```ts
	// src/vs/platform/positronHeadlessLanguageModel/node/headlessLanguageModelEngine.ts:104-119
	// Register exactly the providers the bridge has an auth mapping for
	// (MAPPED_PROVIDER_IDS) ... Providers without an auth mapping (e.g. the local
	// Ollama / LM Studio endpoints) need an endpoint-based credential path the
	// headless service does not implement, so the bridge's `allowedProviders`
	// filter excludes them.
	```

3. **Next Edit Suggestions** (`extensions/next-edit-suggestions/src/model.ts:127-163`) is hardcoded to the `posit-ai` authentication provider and the Posit AI completions gateway. It doesn't touch `vscode.lm`, `IAiProviderService`, or Assistant's provider registry at all, so it was never going to see Ollama/LM Studio.

So: configuring Ollama or LM Studio in Assistant's settings only lights up Assistant chat. Notebook AI silently skips them (by design, per the comment above, because there's no credential path for endpoint-based providers in the headless service). NES can't use any user-configured provider, local or otherwise.

## Questions to resolve

- Is excluding local providers from notebook AI intentional long-term, or just an unimplemented credential path (per the comment in `headlessLanguageModelEngine.ts`)?
- Should the Assistant config UI or Positron's settings say anywhere that a configured local model is chat-only, so users don't assume it applies everywhere?
- Is there an existing tracking issue for wiring `IHeadlessLanguageModelService` up to endpoint-based providers, or should this issue become that?

## Suggested next step

Confirm the above with whoever owns `IHeadlessLanguageModelService` / the headless engine (this looks like it needs an endpoint-based credential path added to `ai-provider-bridge`'s registry, mirroring what Assistant's own chat path already does for Ollama/LM Studio). If closing the gap isn't planned soon, add a note in the config dialog so it's not a surprise.

title: drive-positron: launch.sh does not supply its own required launch arguments
description:
`drive-positron`'s SKILL.md documents four **Required launch arguments**, but `scripts/launch.sh` does not supply any of them; they are caller-supplied pass-through, so omitting one fails silently.

`launch.sh` captures everything after `--` into `EXTRA_ARGS` (line 134) and appends it to `ARGS` (line 291). Nothing defaults `--disable-workspace-trust`, `--use-mock-keychain`, `--skip-welcome`, or a `--folder-uri`.

The practical failure is `--disable-workspace-trust`. Without it the disposable profile has no trust state, so the app starts in restricted mode with extensions disabled. Interpreter discovery never runs, and an empty interpreter picker looks like a product bug rather than a launch-configuration artifact. This bit an agent-driven exploratory testing run: it explored a crippled instance and needed a human to click through the trust prompt mid-run.

## Steps to reproduce the issue:

1. `.claude/skills/drive-positron/scripts/launch.sh -- --folder-uri file:///private/tmp/myworkspace`
2. Observe the workspace trust prompt and the restricted-mode banner; no Python interpreters are discovered.

## Expected or desired behavior:

`launch.sh` defaults the arguments its own docs call required, with a way for a caller to override them. Arguments that are required for the script to work belong in the script, not in every caller's memory. Consumers today are `drive-positron`, `drive-positron-web`, the `launch-positron` command, personal skills, and anyone driving by hand; each has to remember the same four flags.

Once the script owns them, the Required launch arguments table can document the defaults and what overriding them costs.

title: Posit AI Pass sign-in ignores positaiLogin connection config from providers.json
description:
## System details:

#### Positron and OS details:

Positron Version: 2026.09.0 build 177
Code - OSS Version: 1.130.0
Commit: dda83ed949da3639159f10d800a34b2a175cf957
Date: 2026-08-26T17:09:04-06:00
Electron: 42.6.0
Chromium: 148.0.7778.280
Node.js: 24.18.0
V8: 14.8.178.38-electron.0
OS: Darwin arm64 25.5.0

#### Session details:

N/A (provider sign-in flow)

## Describe the issue:

When `~/.posit/ai/providers.json` configures the built-in `positai` provider with a custom `positaiLogin` block (`host`, `clientId`, `scope`), the Posit AI Pass sign-in flow ignores it: after signing out and signing back in through the provider configuration dialog, the OAuth device-authorization request goes to the hardcoded production defaults (`https://login.posit.cloud`, client `positron`, scope `prism`) instead of the configured values.

Other Posit surfaces that own their own Posit AI sign-in flow honor the same providers.json file correctly, so the same config works outside Positron but not inside it.

What I found reading current `main`:

- `extensions/authentication/src/positOAuthProvider.ts` → `getOAuthParameters()` reads only the legacy `authentication.positai.{authHost,scope,clientId}` settings — user/global scope only, via `inspect()?.globalValue` — and falls back to the production defaults. It never consults the providers.json catalog.
- The legacy-settings → providers.json migration map (in ai-config's `legacy-positron-settings`) does not include the `authentication.positai.*` keys at all, so even users who previously set the legacy setting never have it migrated; it is simply orphaned.
- `providerCatalog.ts` exposes no positai connection config to the authentication extension, so there is currently no catalog path the OAuth provider could use.
- The same pattern exists in `extensions/next-edit-suggestions/src/config.ts`, which reads `authentication.positai.baseUrl` (global-only) with a production default, ignoring providers.json `positai.baseUrl`.

Every other provider with an interactive sign-in resolves its endpoint from the providers.json catalog: Databricks reads its workspace host via `getCachedProvider`, AWS SSO takes region/profile from the catalog, and API-key providers' `authentication.*.baseUrl` values are migrated into providers.json. Posit AI is the outlier.

This regressed when Posit AI auth moved from the Assistant extension into the authentication extension in #12681 — the previous Assistant-owned flow honored providers.json.

## Steps to reproduce the issue:

1.  In `~/.posit/ai/providers.json`, configure the `positai` provider with a `positaiLogin` block pointing at a non-default Posit login host, e.g. `"positaiLogin": { "host": "login.example.com", "clientId": "my-client" }`.
2.  In Positron, sign out of Posit AI Pass (if signed in), then sign in again via the provider configuration dialog.
3.  The browser is sent to the production login host instead of the configured one.

## Expected or desired behavior:

Posit AI Pass sign-in resolves `positaiLogin.host` / `clientId` / `scope` from the resolved providers.json catalog (with the usual enforced/default/env precedence other connection config gets), falling back to the production defaults only when unconfigured.

Workaround until then: set the (undeclared) legacy keys in *user* settings.json — workspace scope is ignored — noting that `authHost` takes a full URL with scheme, unlike the bare-host convention in providers.json:

    "authentication.positai.authHost": "https://login.example.com",
    "authentication.positai.clientId": "my-client",
    "authentication.positai.scope": "prism"

## Were there any error messages in the UI, Output panel, or Developer Tools console?

No — the flow silently targets the wrong host.

title: Quarto: a document whose first cell is a diagram cell gets the wrong primary language
description:
When a `.qmd` document has no `jupyter:` kernel in its frontmatter, the primary language is taken from the first cell's fence language:

```ts
// quartoDocumentModel.ts
const primaryLanguage =
    (jupyterKernel ? kernelToLanguageId(jupyterKernel) : undefined)
    ?? cells.at(0)?.language;
```

If that first cell is a diagram or markup cell, the document's primary language becomes something that can never be a kernel language.

### Repro

````
```{mermaid}
graph TD; A-->B;
```

```{python}
x = 1
```
````

### What happens

- The kernel picker shows "mermaid" as the document language, and starting the kernel fails with "No mermaid runtime is available. Please install an interpreter for mermaid."
- The Python cell is now a non-primary language, so it is sent to the console instead of the document kernel. It does not share state with the rest of the document.
- The fix for #15819 (skipping non-executable cells during a multi-cell run) does not help here. The skip test asks whether the cell language is the primary language, and for a leading mermaid cell the answer is yes, so the mermaid cell is not skipped and Run All still aborts on it.

Moving the mermaid cell below a Python cell makes everything work, which is the tell that this is about the fallback and not about mermaid support.

### Suggested fix

The fallback should choose the first cell whose language could plausibly host a kernel, rather than literally the first cell. That means the notion of "executable language" currently living in `quartoExecutionManager._isExecutableLanguage` needs to be shared with the document model, probably by moving it into `positronQuarto/common`.

Doing it that way also lets the multi-cell skip test drop its primary-language special case: a cell is skipped when its language is not executable, full stop, instead of being rescued by having accidentally defined the primary language.

If no cell has an executable language, the primary language should stay undefined, which is the existing "blank document" path and already degrades quietly.

title: Connections should expose semantic layer
description:
Currently the Data Connections pane exposes the name and structure of volumes/objects and databases/tables, but is lacking in Metadata/Semantic layer such as: https://www.snowflake.com/en/fundamentals/what-is-a-data-catalog/

> Metadata powers a data catalog by providing the descriptive information that allows users to discover, understand and manage data assets effectively. Metadata is often described as data about data. There are several types of metadata, including descriptive, structural, administrative and statistical metadata. 
> 
> - Descriptive metadata includes information like title, author and keywords, aiding in data identification and location. 
> 
> - Structural metadata defines relationships between data elements – for example, a customer’s name and address. 
> 
> - Administrative metadata provides details on how, when and by whom data was created and accessed. The "last modified" timestamp on a file is a simple example of administrative metadata, showing when the data was last changed.
> 
> - Statistical metadata offers insights into the data's quality, reliability and methodology – for example, the percentage of complete customer addresses in the database.
> 
> The importance of metadata in data management cannot be overstated. It enhances data governance, helping ensure data accuracy, consistency and accessibility. By providing a clear structure and context, metadata facilitates better data management practices, making it easier for organizations to comply with regulatory requirements and maintain data integrity. Effective metadata management also reduces the time spent searching for data, enabling teams to focus on analysis and decision-making.
> 
> Metadata plays a crucial role in supporting data discovery. By enriching data with descriptive information, it allows users to quickly find the right data. In a data catalog, robust metadata helps users understand the content, purpose and relevance of dat asets, leading to more informed decisions.

description: VS Code 1.109 includes an integrated browser that is vastly superior to its previous "Simple Browser" component. https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_109#_integrated-browser-preview This browser has a number of advantages over "Simple Browser": - Developer tools are easy to access and, once invoked, scoped only to the browser itself (vs. the whole Positron window)\ - Easy to reference portions of the content in an AI chat session (this is pretty much impossible in the Viewer pane, Positron Assistant can't even see the URL) - It appears to use an actual independent browser instance, rather than a 3-deep stack of IFrames - Event handling is much better coordinated, so that e.g. copy and paste work correctly - There may also be performance improvements Positron uses effectively the same approach as "Simple Browser" (i.e. it's IFrames all the way down). title: Windows background update leaves stale resources\app\node_modules that shadows node_modules.asar
description:
## Summary

On Windows, an automatic (background) update leaves behind every file the previous version shipped that the new version no longer ships. After the Code OSS 1.130 merge (#15243) moved ~500 packages out of `resources\app\node_modules` and into `node_modules.asar`, those leftover package folders are still on disk, and 1.130's new ESM loader hook **prefers them over the archive**. Affected installations therefore run 1.130 code against a mix of 1.129 dependencies.

Usually that is invisible, because most packages did not change across the merge. It is fatal when a package's API changed, which is what #16012 reports: a leftover `@vscode/proxy-agent@0.42.0` is loaded instead of the shipped 0.44.0, `createProxyAuthorizationLookup` does not exist in it, and the extension host crashes on startup in a loop.

#16012 is the user-visible symptom and has a workaround. This issue tracks the underlying defect.

## Mechanism

1. **The update merges, it does not replace.** `IsBackgroundUpdate()` is true whenever the updater runs the installer, which it always does (`/update=` in [`updateService.win32.ts`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/platform/update/electron-main/updateService.win32.ts#L583-L585)). Every entry in `[InstallDelete]` in [`build/win32/positron.iss`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/build/win32/positron.iss#L69-L76) is guarded with `Check: IsNotBackgroundUpdate`, including `{app}\resources\app\node_modules`. The staging directory `{app}\_` is merged over the live install by `inno_updater.exe`, which overwrites what the new build contains and leaves everything else in place. `product.json` does not set `win32VersionedUpdate`, so there is no versioned resources folder to sidestep this either.

2. **1.130 changed the layout.** Verified against the published Windows x64 archives:
   - `2026.08.2-4` (1.129): `resources/app/node_modules` contains **509 top-level packages** as real files, including `@vscode/proxy-agent` **0.42.0**, alongside a `node_modules.asar`.
   - `2026.09.1-2` (1.130): `resources/app/node_modules` contains **4** packages (`@vscode/sandbox-runtime`, `@pondwader/socks5-server`, `shell-quote`, `zod`, kept out of the archive on purpose). Everything else, including `@vscode/proxy-agent` **0.44.0**, lives only in `node_modules.asar`.

   So an install that background-updated across this boundary keeps ~505 stale package folders that the current build has no knowledge of.

3. **Resolution prefers the stale copy.** ESM cannot walk into `node_modules.asar`, so 1.130 added a loader hook in [`src/bootstrap-esm.ts`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/bootstrap-esm.ts#L46-L250) (upstream code, identical in microsoft/vscode 1.130.0 and 1.134.0). It runs the default resolution first and accepts the result if it lands anywhere under `resources/app`, so that a built-in extension shipping its own copy of a package wins over the app archive. A leftover folder in `resources\app\node_modules` satisfies that rule. The default `node_modules` walk from `out/vs/workbench/api/node/extensionHostProcess.js` reaches `resources/app/node_modules` before anything else, so the stale copy is accepted and the archive is never consulted.

4. **Result:** `import { createProxyAuthorizationLookup } from '@vscode/proxy-agent'` instantiates against 0.42.0, which does not export it. The extension host exits with code 1 before activating anything, restarts, and loops. No extension commands are ever registered, so e.g. the Welcome page environment checks fail with "The Python check could not be completed."

## Verification already done

- Extracted `@vscode/proxy-agent` from the shipped `node_modules.asar` of `Positron-win32-2026.09.1-2-x64` (commit `467ff390dd`, the exact build in #16012): version 0.44.0, exports present in a form `cjs-module-lexer` detects, byte-identical to our checked-in copy apart from the build's sourceMappingURL rewrite. It is the only copy in the shipped tree. **A fresh install of that build is not affected.**
- Extracted `resources/app/node_modules/@vscode/proxy-agent/package.json` from `Positron-win32-2026.08.2-4-x64`: version 0.42.0, no `createProxyAuthorizationLookup`.

## Scope

- Affects Windows installations that took the automatic update path from 2026.08.x (1.129) or earlier to 2026.09.x (1.130) or later. Fresh installs and manual installer runs are not affected, because a non-background run performs the `[InstallDelete]` cleanup.
- Not Positron-specific in its resolution half: upstream microsoft/vscode#328700 reports the identical crash on Linux, where users extracted a new tarball over an existing directory, which leaves the same stale files behind. That issue is still `info-needed`; we should answer it with this mechanism.
- The crash is the loud case. The quiet case is worse to reason about: on an affected machine, any of the ~505 stale packages shadows its shipped counterpart at whatever version 1.129 had, with no diagnostic.

## Proposed fixes

1. **Update path (ours).** Make an updated installation match a fresh one, so files a new version no longer ships are removed. Options worth weighing: run the cleanup against `{app}` before the swap rather than skipping it on background updates; have `inno_updater` prune paths the new build does not contain; or adopt `win32VersionedUpdate` so each update lands in a clean versioned resources folder and the whole class disappears.
2. **Resolution (upstream).** The loader hook should not treat `<appRoot>/node_modules` as a "closer copy that wins" - the archive *is* the application's own `node_modules`, and a package that the app ships only in the archive should never be satisfied from a sibling directory. Copies under `resources/app/extensions/**` should still take precedence, which is the case the rule exists for. Worth proposing upstream on microsoft/vscode#328700 rather than forking.

Either fix alone resolves #16012. Both are worth doing: (1) stops shipping mixed installations, (2) makes the archive authoritative even if a mixed installation exists.

## Reproduction

1. Install Positron 2026.08.2 or earlier on Windows.
2. Let it update automatically to 2026.09.1 or later (do not run the installer manually).
3. `Test-Path "<install>\resources\app\node_modules\@vscode\proxy-agent"` returns `True` and its `package.json` reads 0.42.0.
4. The extension host crash loops on startup.

Setting `VSCODE_ASAR_TRACE=<path>` before launching writes a resolution trace showing the accepted path; the affected line ends in `resources/app/node_modules/@vscode/proxy-agent/out/index.js (in app, ACCEPT)`.

title: Viewer: only the first HTML preview renders on Firefox (web)
description:
## System details: #### Positron and OS details: Positron dev build (1.130.0) from source, `main` @ `dda83ed9`, running Positron Web. Reproduced by hand on macOS in Firefox 149, and in CI on ubuntu/Firefox. Chrome is unaffected. #### Session details: R 4.5.1 (manual repro), R 4.4.2 / 4.5.2 (e2e) ## Describe the issue: In Positron Web on Firefox, the first HTML preview shown in the Viewer renders. Every one after that is blank, for the rest of the session. The Viewer header updates each time -- the filename in the toolbar changes to the new temp file -- so Positron is tracking the new preview. Only the content is missing. No packages are involved. Two calls to `getOption("viewer")()` on a temp HTML file are enough to show it. Under the hood the webview is created, mounted, sized, and marked `ready`, and the wrapper HTML is delivered to it. But the webview's document stays empty (no `#active-frame`), and its inner iframe never requests the proxied content URL -- zero proxy requests appear in the network log for a failing preview. A working preview has the nested `#active-frame` plus a content frame at `localhost:/proxy//index.html`. Nothing is disposed while this happens. I instrumented `OverlayWebview`, `WebviewElement`, `PositronPreviewService` and `PreviewContainer`; the working and blank cases are identical all the way through content delivery -- same `setHtml` length, same `_show`, same `doUpdateContent ... state=Initializing`, same `mountTo` resolution with `disposed=false`, same `READY`. One difference I found, offered as a lead rather than a conclusion: the first preview gets a second `claim()`/`_show()` cycle, because the pane moves from x=0,y=0 to its final position and `PreviewContainer`'s effect has `props.x`/`props.y` in its dependencies. Later previews inherit the final position and are claimed exactly once. I have not confirmed that this is the cause. ## Steps to reproduce the issue: 1. Open Positron Web in Firefox with an R session. 2. In the console, define a helper that writes a temp HTML file and opens it in the Viewer: ```r vf <- function(t) { f <- tempfile(fileext = ".html") writeLines(paste0("

", t, "

"), f) getOption("viewer")(f) } ``` 3. Run `vf("FIRST")`. The Viewer shows FIRST. 4. Run `vf("SECOND")`. The Viewer goes blank. The toolbar shows the new filename. 5. Run `vf("THIRD")`. Still blank. Repeating the same steps in Chrome, against the same server and the same R session, renders every preview. ## Expected or desired behavior: Every HTML preview renders, not just the first one per session. ## Were there any error messages in the UI, Output panel, or Developer Tools console? No. Nothing in the console, the R kernel log, or the extension host logs. R sends `show_html_file` normally and Positron creates the preview normally. ## Impact on the e2e suite `Viewer > R - Verify Viewer displays reactable table output` has failed every Firefox run (4/4) for the last 28 days. The dashboard reports it as flaky rather than failing because CI's retry re-runs the failed test on its own, where it becomes the first preview in the session and passes. The test is correct and is currently the only thing detecting this, so it should be left as-is rather than "fixed". Locally the failure is deterministic and follows position, not content -- whichever viewer test runs second fails: | Order (`--project e2e-firefox`) | 1st | 2nd | 3rd | |---|---|---|---| | modelsummary, reactable, reprex (x3) | pass | **fail** | pass | | reactable, reprex | pass | **fail** | -- | | reactable alone | pass | -- | -- | | same order on `--project e2e-chromium` | pass | pass | -- | The third test passing is an artifact of the spec's `afterEach` calling `clearViewer()`; in the manual repro above, where nothing clears the Viewer, every preview after the first stays blank. ### E2E Triage Diagnosis
🟢 High confidence -- Product bug, Firefox/web only: the SECOND HTML preview shown in the Positron Viewer pane never renders. The webview element is created, mounted and marked ready, and the wrapper HTML is delivered, but the webview document stays empty and its inner iframe never requests the proxied content URL. - **Test:** [Viewer > R - Verify Viewer displays reactable table output](https://connect.posit.it/e2e-test-insights/?tab=test_health&repo=positron&test=Viewer%20%3E%20R%20-%20Verify%20Viewer%20displays%20reactable%20table%20output%7C%7C%7Ctest%2Fe2e%2Ftests%2Fviewer%2Fviewer.test.ts) - **Targeted failure:** expect(locator).toBeVisible() failed for the viewer content locator; 60s toPass budget exhausted. Reported by the dashboard as 'flaky' at 100% of ubuntu/firefox runs (4/4) over 14 days. - **Signal:** Local repro on --project e2e-firefox: whichever viewer test runs SECOND fails, regardless of content. modelsummary(1)=PASS, reactable(2)=FAIL, reprex(3)=PASS, repeated 3/3. reactable alone = PASS in 8s. reactable(1)=PASS, reprex(2)=FAIL. Same ordering on --project e2e-chromium = both PASS. Instrumented overlayWebview/webviewElement/positronPreviewService/previewContainer: pass and fail cases are byte-identical through content delivery (setHtml len=1392, _show creates element, doUpdateContent htmlLen=1392 state=Initializing, mountTo async-init disposed=false, WebviewElement READY). Nothing is disposed during the test. Frame dump at failure: pre/index.html has iframes=0, bodyLen=0 and there is no proxy content frame; trace.network contains zero requests to the proxy URL. Passing case has the nested #active-frame plus a content frame at localhost:PORT/proxy//index.html. - **Frequency:** 4/4 runs (100%) on main, ubuntu/firefox - **Hypothesis:** On the Firefox web path, the second webview created in the pane completes its ready handshake but the flushed 'content' message is never applied to the webview document, so the inner iframe is never created and no proxy request is issued. The only observed structural difference is that the first preview gets a second claim()/_show() cycle (the pane moves x=0,y=0 -> x=901,y=99, re-running PreviewContainer's effect whose deps include props.x/props.y), while later previews inherit the final position and are claimed exactly once. Likely lead: the per-origin webview service-worker / MessagePort handshake binding to a stale client in Firefox. Not proven. - **Supersedes:** Earlier hypotheses that the webview was destroyed by a console-panel-maximize relayout, and that OverlayWebview._isDisposed latched after an onWillStop dispose. Both falsified by instrumentation: no dispose occurs during the test and content is delivered identically in the passing and failing cases.

title: positron-commands skill: Run interactive R and Python web apps (esp. in Workbench)
description:
Assistant has been known to struggle to run apps such as Flask, Dash, and Shiny in Positron, and when it does so successfully, it often uses a nonstandard mechanism to do so, with the result that it isn't integrated well with Positron's UI and may be missing code needed to integrate with Workbench.

We should:

- add a positron-commands skill to run apps correctly in Positron
- guide Assistant to use the skill over running the app directly

title: Strip unused ONNX Runtime and build-tool payloads from the packaged app (about 122 MB of the .deb)
description:
## Summary

The Linux x64 `.deb` grew from 498.6 MB to 725.4 MB between the `2026.08.0-184` daily (Jul 22) and the `2026.09.0-124` daily (Aug 20). Discussion #15651 reported this.

The growth happened in two steps. The first step is new features. The second step is almost all dead weight that we can strip. About 122 MB of the current `.deb` is content that Positron never loads.

## Measurements

Method: download the dailies from the CDN, extract `data.tar.xz`, and compare the file listings.

| Daily | Date | `.deb` size |
|---|---|---|
| 2026.08.0-184 | Jul 22 | 498.6 MB |
| 2026.08.0-331 | Aug 6 | 599.5 MB |
| 2026.09.0-22 | Aug 10 | 597.4 MB |
| 2026.09.0-35 | Aug 11 | 721.5 MB |
| 2026.09.0-124 | Aug 20 | 725.4 MB |

**Step 1, late July, +101 MB.** New features, as expected. Uncompressed content: the new Data Connections drivers add 162 MB (Posit Connect pins, Snowflake, Databricks), the ai-lib packages add 117 MB, and a Quarto update adds 25 MB.

**Step 2, Aug 11, +124 MB.** The merge of Code OSS 1.130 (#15243). This issue covers that step.

## 1. ONNX Runtime CUDA and TensorRT providers: 111.4 MB of the `.deb`

Code OSS 1.130 added `onnxruntime-node` and `@huggingface/transformers` to the root `package.json`. `build/gulpfile.vscode.ts` keeps the binaries of the target platform only, but it keeps the whole `bin/napi-v6/<platform>/<arch>/` tree.

Contents of that tree in the `2026.09.0-35` daily (linux/x64):

| File | Uncompressed | Needed |
|---|---|---|
| `libonnxruntime_providers_cuda.so` | 315.7 MB | no |
| `libonnxruntime.so.1` | 35.2 MB | yes |
| `libonnxruntime_providers_tensorrt.so` | 0.9 MB | no |
| `onnxruntime_binding.node` | 0.4 MB | yes |
| `libonnxruntime_providers_shared.so` | 0.01 MB | yes |

Positron asks for the CPU execution provider only. See `src/vs/platform/localTranscription/node/nemotronTranscriber.ts:197`:

```ts
const opts = { executionProviders: ['cpu'] } as const;
```

I compressed `libonnxruntime_providers_cuda.so` with `xz -6` and got 111.4 MB. This one file is 90% of the Aug 11 step.

CUDA is a Linux payload, so Linux takes the largest increase. Between the `2026.09.0-22` and `2026.09.0-35` dailies: `.deb` +124 MB, `.rpm` +149 MB, Windows x64 +59 MB, macOS arm64 +66 MB.

## 2. onnxruntime-web WebAssembly bundles: 10.9 MB of the `.deb`

Four files under `onnxruntime-web/dist/` add 77.2 MB uncompressed:

- `ort-wasm-simd-threaded.jsep.wasm` (26.1 MB)
- `ort-wasm-simd-threaded.asyncify.wasm` (23.6 MB)
- `ort-wasm-simd-threaded.jspi.wasm` (14.6 MB)
- `ort-wasm-simd-threaded.wasm` (12.9 MB)

Only `@huggingface/transformers` needs them. The packaged app contains no files from that package, because npm hoists its native dependencies into the root `node_modules` and the package itself is not shipped.

## 3. Build tools from the ai-lib packages: about 122 MB uncompressed

These packages are devDependencies of `ai-provider-bridge`, which the root `package.json` includes as `file:./ai-lib/packages/ai-provider-bridge`. npm hoists them into the root `node_modules`, and they ship. The app does not run any of them.

Sizes from the `2026.08.0-331` daily, where each package was still a separate directory:

| Package | Uncompressed |
|---|---|
| `@typescript/typescript-linux-x64` | 24.1 MB |
| `esbuild` | 20.9 MB |
| `@oxlint/binding-linux-x64-gnu` | 16.3 MB |
| `vite-node` | 13.9 MB |
| `tsx` | 12.1 MB |
| `@esbuild/linux-x64` | 11.4 MB |
| `oxfmt` | 8.2 MB |
| `@oxfmt/binding-linux-x64-gnu` | 6.9 MB |
| `happy-dom` | 3.4 MB |
| `rollup` | 2.8 MB |
| `terser` | 2.2 MB |

This is the same route as the lightningcss strip in #15156. The `@oxlint` and `@oxfmt` native bindings are still visible in `node_modules.asar.unpacked` in the `2026.09.0-35` daily, so the leak is current.

## Proposed work

- [ ] Exclude `libonnxruntime_providers_cuda.so` and `libonnxruntime_providers_tensorrt.so` from the packaged app. `getOnnxRuntimeExcludeFilter()` in `build/gulpfile.vscode.ts` is the natural place.
- [ ] Exclude `onnxruntime-web` through `build/.moduleignore`.
- [ ] Exclude the build tools in item 3 through `build/.moduleignore`.
- [ ] After the strip, do a test of dictation on Linux and Windows. ONNX Runtime must not load the unused providers eagerly.

## Notes

Upstream removed both `@huggingface/transformers` and `onnxruntime-node` in Code OSS 1.131. A later upstream merge removes items 1 and 2 for us. Until that merge lands, every Linux build carries the CUDA provider, so the strip is still worth doing now.

For reference, the upstream Code OSS 1.134 `.deb` is 238 MB and contains no ONNX Runtime files.

title: Moving code lines with Alt+Up/Down messes up tab spacing
description: ## System details: #### Positron and OS details: Positron Version: 2026.09.0 (user setup) build 256 Code - OSS Version: 1.130.0 Commit: 58e9b87506d4132bf7f3340e883f16b4a982c266 Date: 2026-09-02T16:44:31-07:00 Electron: 42.6.0 Chromium: 148.0.7778.280 Node.js: 24.18.0 V8: 14.8.178.38-electron.0 OS: Windows_NT x64 10.0.26100 #### Session details: R 4.6.1 ## Describe the issue: While writing code in an R script, I moved a few lines of code from one section down to a different section using Alt+Down. Positron unexpectedly shifted lines of code left and right as I moved the lines down, resulting in unwanted added or removed spacing. I use Visual Studio Code daily, and I've never seen this very unexpected and undesirable behavior. If there is some setting causing this, please have it turned off by default. Note: This happens specifically with R scripts. I tested it in a .txt file and I got what I wanted (no changes to spacing). As soon as I changed that .txt to a .R file, this problem happened again. ## Expected or desired behavior: I would expect that every line of code -- including lines that are moving, lines being moved past, and lines before and after -- will all stay exactly the same as they were before the move, except only in different locations. ## Steps to reproduce the issue: 1. In an R script, paste these lines: ```r df_to_share1 <- df_group_details |> dplyr::filter(!(status == "not in any")) |> dplyr::mutate( ... ) |> dplyr::select( group_name ) df_to_share2 <- df_to_share1 |> dplyr::select( group_name ) |> dplyr::rename( `Group Name` = group_name ) ``` 2. Select the "dplyr::mutate()" statement (or really any part of the code), and use Alt+Up/Down to move it around. See the image for what happened to me. The first column is the original code. The middle column is the desired outcome. The right column is the result of moving those lines with Alt+Down. Note that the lines marked with red have undesirable spacing.

description:
## Context

Positron does not currently have intellisense for SQL support i.e. no keyword/function completion, no statement-structure awareness. 


## AC
1. Decide on the LSP strategy. Analyze whether we should adopt an existing open source SQL extension https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/tree/main/extensions/sql 
https://github.com/joe-re/sql-language-server


2. Completions should provide basic keyword/function completion, syntax errors and linting 

3. Wire completions to show up inside of .ipynb, .qmd, .sql and .gsql files 

## Out of scope (handled in followup tickets)

title: AI: Expose `providers.json` settings migration in Positron CLI
description:
## Summary

Expose the Posit Assistant provider-settings -> `providers.json` migration (added in [#14928](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/14928)) as a Positron CLI subcommand. Given a settings file, it emits a JSON object on stdout with the migrated `providers.json` fragment, the settings with the migrated provider keys removed, and the key mapping, so external tooling like the Workbench migration script gets a fully migrated result without re-implementing Positron's translation logic.

## Background

[#14928](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/14928) migrates provider settings into `~/.posit/ai/providers.json` via `ai-config` from [ai-lib](https://github.com/posit-dev/ai-lib). Today it runs only inside Positron (on the authentication extension's activation and via the `Migrate Provider Settings to providers.json` command), and the mapping lives in the extension ([`migrateToProvidersJson.ts`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/extensions/authentication/src/migration/migrateToProvidersJson.ts)).

Workbench needs the same migration but can't reach that logic. Duplicating the mapping table would be a maintenance burden and drift out of sync over time.

## Proposal

A subcommand that runs the existing migration headlessly as a **pure transform**: it reads a settings file and emits the result on stdout, writing no files itself (the caller decides what to persist and where).

- **Input:** a Positron `settings.json` (path or stdin).
- **Output:** a JSON object on stdout with three fields:
  - `providers` — the migrated config as a fragment in the `providers.json` schema.
  - `settings` — the input settings with the migrated keys removed.
  - `migrated` — the `from -> to` key mapping, for logging and previews.

Rough shape (CLI surface TBD):

```
positron migrate-providers --settings <settings.json>
```

emits:

```json
{
  "providers": { "providers": { "anthropic": { "baseUrl": "https://…" } } },
  "settings": { "…": "input minus the migrated keys" },
  "migrated": [ { "from": "authentication.anthropic.baseUrl", "to": "providers.anthropic.baseUrl" } ]
}
```

Conventions: stdout carries the JSON, stderr carries errors; exit non-zero on parse/schema failure; an empty `migrated` means nothing to migrate. It should reuse the same code path as [#14928](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/14928) so behavior matches the in-app migration and there's a single source of truth.

## Use case: Workbench migration

Workbench maintains provider configuration as enforced settings. The migration script would produce a `settings.json`, run the subcommand against it, parse the JSON from stdout, and place `providers` and `settings` where it needs them. All translation and key removal stay in Positron; all file writing stays in Workbench.

## Related

- [#14928](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/14928): Migrate provider settings to providers.json ([review thread](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/14928#discussion_r3617167572))
- [#14708](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/14708): resolved by #14928
- [#14710](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/14710): Positron `providers.json` read path

title: "Run Cells Above" fails on a Mermaid cell when `quarto.inlineOutput.enabled` is true
description:
With `quarto.inlineOutput.enabled: true`, running "Run Cells Above" in a `.qmd` document fails when one of the preceding cells contains a Mermaid diagram (a ```{mermaid} code block ). The command aborts partway through instead of executing all cells above the cursor, requiring each remaining cell to be run individually.

Steps to reproduce:

Set `quarto.inlineOutput.enabled: true` in settings.
Create a .qmd document with several executable code cells, including at least one Mermaid diagram cell (e.g. a ```{mermaid} block) somewhere in the middle.
Place the cursor in a cell below the Mermaid cell and invoke "Run Cells Above".
Expected behaviour: All cells above the cursor run in order, including the Mermaid cell, with inline output rendered for each.

Actual behaviour: Execution fails silently on the Mermaid cell, leaving later cells un-run. Cells from that point onward must be run one at a time to reproduce the same state as a normal top-to-bottom "Run All".

macOS Tahoe Version 26.6.2 (25G83)
quarto.inlineOutput.enabled: true

title: Packages pane flags current packages when older copies exist in another library
description:
Environment: Positron 2026.10.0 build 56, commit f7d370069a03f7c940d5c77579f4af4f3fc6ede0; R 4.6.1; macOS arm64.

With my user library first in `.libPaths()`, the Packages pane’s `@outdated` filter flags current packages that also have older copies in the system library.

For example, I updated {ellmer} today to 0.5.0 in my user library, while an older 0.4.1 copy remains in the system library. The repository check also returned 0.5.0, yet the Packages pane displays 0.5.0 with an update arrow and includes it under `@outdated`. The flag therefore appears to reflect the older system-library copy rather than the current copy displayed in the pane. A separate R check found the same pattern for 27 packages.

Expected: Update indicators should reflect the installed copy displayed in the pane.

This differs from [#14294](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/14294): both original fixes remain present, but an older copy in a lower-priority library supplies an update flag that is applied by package name to the current copy.

title: Assistant: Queues code behind a busy console with no timeout or feedback
description:
When the console is busy, Assistant behaves no differently to if it were idle: it queues the next execution, which waits until the previous execution completes. 

If whatever is running takes really long (like an R Shiny app serving, or a long-running job from another agent) Assistant waits really long. A user might have leave the computer hoping to come back to a completed task, and instead see the agent still waiting.

Could the `executeCode` tool timeout if the execution does not _start_ quickly? Note that it should not necessarily timeout if the execution takes a while to _complete_, since it might just be a slow computation.

Relates to https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/16089, but this issue focuses on improving Assistant's awareness of busy consoles and how to deal with them, and #16089 is a more specific bug where the Stop button doesn't always work.

title: Assistant: Pending console executions can't be stopped
description:
When Assistant runs code in a console that is already busy, the code is queued, and:

1. Clicking Assistant's Stop button does not interrupt the previous execution and does not remove the new one from the queue.

    If whatever is running never finishes (an R Shiny app serving, a long-running job) Assistant waits forever, and there is no way to get it unstuck.

    <details>
    <summary>Video</summary>

    https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3252978e-f8e7-4194-a48b-595fe2c334cb

    </details>

2. If you click the Stop button: when the previous execution finishes, Assistant's queued execution still runs, even though the "Response cancelled" is shown in the chat pane. This could be really bad if the user tried to intervene to stop something destructive from running.

    <details>
    <summary>Video</summary>

    Not much happens for ~50 seconds so fast forward to the last few.

    https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a6342763-72f9-4b20-a079-6b2e26753f3c

    </details>

To reproduce: run `Sys.sleep(600)` or start a Shiny app in the R console, ask Assistant to run any R code, then try to stop it.

Reported by @gadenbuie and @nrohr, hit with a Shiny app in the console and with several agent sessions running at once.

## Describe the issue:

Text selected in Positron's Visual Editor cannot be copied to the system clipboard.

The text is visibly selected in the Visual Editor, but neither `Cmd+C` nor the context-menu **Copy** command copies the selection. Pasting into another application or editor produces no copied text.

The same document and the same text can be copied immediately after switching from Visual Editor to Source mode. 3. Select ordinary paragraph text using the mouse.
4. Press `Cmd+C`.

8. Observe that the context-menu copy action also does not copy the selected text.
9. Switch the same document to **Source** mode.

Selected text in Visual Editor should be copied to the system clipboard when the user presses `Cmd+C` or chooses **Copy** from the context menu, matching the behavior of Source mode and standard macOS applications.

## Actual behavior:

Switching the same document to Source mode immediately restores normal copying behavior.
