title: DuckDB parallel queries lose ~4–6x throughput in RStudio/Positron consoles, but not in Rgui/Rscript on the same machine
description:
# Context
I maintain [`mpathsenser`](https://github.com/koenniem/mpathsenser/tree/move-to-duckdb), an R package whose import pipeline reads JSON exports from mobile sensing data and writes them into DuckDB: R orchestrates the whole pipeline (staging the raw JSON into a DuckDB temporary table, running the sensor-specific ingest SQL, deduplication, table optimization, etc.) while essentially all of the wall time is inside DuckDB execution. On the same machine, the identical pipeline run through `Rscript` takes 284 s, through the Positron console 772 s, and through the RStudio console 795 s, with identical output (130,530,512 sensor rows, identical deduplication counts). The slowdown is not specific to my package: an attached self-contained script (`minimal_repro.R`, no package code, no data) that creates a table in DuckDB and sorts it reproduces it.

Note that this investigation was mostly done with help from AI, as I lack the skills to search so deeply into Positron and duckdb. As a result, there may be more content and analyses than strictly necessary.

# Environment
Positron 2026.09.1 (system setup) build 2 (R kernel `ark.exe`); RStudio `2026.09.0 Build 174` (`rsession.exe`); R 4.6.1 (ucrt); duckdb R package 1.5.5 (all hosts load the identical `C:\Workdir\MyApps\R-Library\4.0\duckdb\libs\x64\duckdb.dll`); Windows 11; AMD Ryzen 7 PRO 7840HS (8C/16T); 64 GB RAM.

# Minimal reproducible example
```r
# minimal_repro.R -- the smallest self-contained reproduction of the
# "multithreaded DuckDB work is many times slower in IDE-hosted R" problem.
#
# Run the same file two ways and compare the output lines:
#
#   1) in the IDE console (Positron / RStudio):
#        source("minimal_repro.R")
#   2) in a terminal:
#        Rscript minimal_repro.R
#
# Every line prints elapsed seconds and `par` = (user+sys)/elapsed, i.e. how
# many cores were effectively busy. On a 16-core machine the parallel lines
# (group-by, ordered copy, window) should show par ~6-12 in both runs. If the
# IDE run shows par ~1-3 and a several-fold larger elapsed time, this file
# alone reproduces the problem -- it is suitable for an upstream issue report
# (Positron/RStudio) with no package code or data needed.
#
# Nothing here touches any data: everything is generated inside DuckDB, and
# the temporary database file is deleted at the end.
#
# Optional: `n <- 2e7` before sourcing (or pass a number as the first
# command-line argument) for a quicker run; default is 4e7.

run_minimal_repro <- function(n = NULL) {
  # Resolve n from the caller's global env (sourced console use) or args.
  if (is.null(n) && exists("n", envir = globalenv(), inherits = FALSE)) {
    n <- get("n", envir = globalenv())
  }
  if (is.null(n)) {
    a <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)
    n <- if (length(a) >= 1 && nzchar(a[1])) as.numeric(a[1]) else 4e7
  }

  suppressPackageStartupMessages({
    library(DBI)
    library(duckdb)
  })

  cat("== minimal repro ==\n")
  cat("time:        ", format(Sys.time()), "\n")
  cat("R:           ", R.version.string, "\n")
  cat("interactive: ", interactive(), "\n")
  cat("pid:         ", Sys.getpid(), "\n")
  cat("host env:     POSITRON=", Sys.getenv("POSITRON", unset = "<unset>"),
      " RSTUDIO=", Sys.getenv("RSTUDIO", unset = "<unset>"), "\n", sep = "")
  cat("tempdir:     ", tempdir(), "\n")
  cat("n_rows:      ", format(n, scientific = FALSE, big.mark = ","), "\n")

  drv <- duckdb::duckdb()
  dbf <- tempfile(fileext = ".duckdb")
  con <- dbConnect(drv, dbdir = dbf)
  on.exit(
    try(if (DBI::dbIsValid(con)) dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE), silent = TRUE),
    add = TRUE
  )
  on.exit(unlink(dbf, recursive = TRUE), add = TRUE)

  invisible(dbExecute(con, "SET threads = 16"))
  invisible(dbExecute(con, "SET preserve_insertion_order = false"))
  invisible(dbExecute(con, "PRAGMA disable_progress_bar"))
  st <- dbGetQuery(
    con,
    "SELECT name, value FROM duckdb_settings()
     WHERE name IN ('threads','memory_limit','temp_directory') ORDER BY name"
  )
  cat("settings:    ", paste(sprintf("%s=%s", st$name, st$value), collapse = "  "), "\n\n")

  report <- function(label, expr) {
    t0 <- proc.time()
    ok <- tryCatch(
      {
        force(expr)
        TRUE
      },
      error = function(e) {
        cat(sprintf("%-28s ERROR: %s\n", label, conditionMessage(e)))
        FALSE
      }
    )
    if (ok) {
      p <- proc.time() - t0
      cat(sprintf(
        "%-28s %9.2fs  par=%5.1f cores  (user %.2f sys %.2f)\n",
        label, p[["elapsed"]],
        (p[["user.self"]] + p[["sys.self"]]) / max(p[["elapsed"]], 1e-9),
        p[["user.self"]], p[["sys.self"]]
      ))
    }
    invisible(NULL)
  }

  report("create table", dbExecute(
    con,
    sprintf("CREATE TABLE t AS
             SELECT range AS i, (range %% 1000000)::INT AS g, repeat('abcdefgh', 5) AS pad
             FROM range(%s)", format(n, scientific = FALSE))
  ))
  report("group by (1M groups)", dbGetQuery(
    con, "SELECT g, COUNT(*) AS n, AVG(i) AS m FROM t GROUP BY g"
  ))
  report("ordered copy (sort)", dbExecute(
    con, "CREATE TABLE t_ord AS SELECT * FROM t ORDER BY pad, i"
  ))
  report("partitioned window", dbExecute(
    con, "CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP TABLE w AS
          SELECT i, g, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY g ORDER BY i DESC) AS rn FROM t"
  ))
  report("second ordered copy", dbExecute(
    con, "CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE t_ord2 AS SELECT * FROM t ORDER BY pad DESC, i DESC"
  ))
  invisible(dbExecute(con, "SET threads = 1"))
  report("ordered copy (threads=1)", dbExecute(
    con, "CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE t_ord3 AS SELECT * FROM t ORDER BY pad, i"
  ))
  report("pure R: sum(sqrt(1:2e7))", invisible(sum(sqrt(seq_len(2e7)))))

  cat("\n== done ==\n")
  invisible(NULL)
}

run_minimal_repro()
```

# Evaluation
Effective cores (`par` = (user+sys)/elapsed) for the same ordered copy of a 20M-row table at each configured DuckDB `threads`:

| host | t=1 | t=2 | t=4 | t=8 | t=16 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Rscript (terminal) | 0.9 | 1.9 | 3.5 | 6.2 | 8.8 |
| Rgui (R for Windows GUI) | 1.0 | 1.9 | 3.6 | 7.4 | 12.3 |
| RStudio console | 1.0 | 1.9 | 3.1 | 3.1 | **3.2** |
| Positron console | 1.0 | 1.6 | 2.0 | 2.1 | **2.1** |

The two IDE-hosted processes stop scaling at 2–3 cores; R's own front-ends scale to 9–12. The end-to-end effect is proportional: an 8,000-file synthetic import run from the Positron console via a child `Rscript` process takes 30 s, while the same import in the console itself takes 50 s (same data; all 32 sensor tables match row-for-row).

Everything I can measure is clean and identical between the fast and the slow hosts (details in the attached report):

* All 155 DuckDB settings are identical (including `external_threads`, `threads`, `worker_threads`, `pin_threads`, `scheduler_process_partial`, the allocator settings).
* No Job Object CPU-rate cap (`job_cpu_rate_control=0x0`), normal priority, full 16-CPU affinity, no power throttling.
* Per-thread affinity, CPU sets, priority and per-thread EcoQoS, read from inside newly created threads: full 16-CPU mask, none, normal, unset — in every host, including the slow ones.
* No debug-heap / Application Verifier / gflags flags (`NtGlobalFlag=0x0` in all hosts; no IFEO entries for any R or IDE executable), identical mitigation policy, normal memory priority.
* Module dump: no MinGW runtime DLL is loaded anywhere (statically linked), the identical `duckdb.dll` in all hosts, and the only modules present in ark/rsession but not in Rgui/Rscript are your own executables/libraries. `Start10_64.dll` (Stardock Start11) is injected into all four processes, including the fast ones.
* Timer resolution is not the mechanism: RStudio already runs on a 1 ms timer and is slow; Rgui/Rscript run on the default 15.625 ms timer and are fast; calling `timeBeginPeriod(1)` in the Positron process changed the query by 0.97x.
* Memory (~35 GB free), temp-directory location, filesystem and the R-level progress callback (88,950 calls during the probe query; timed ratio with/without 1.00) are all neutral.
* The same process can run native threads at full speed: a 16-thread OpenMP kernel inside `ark` reaches par 9.93, faster than the Rscript child (8.91). So the process is not CPU-capped; DuckDB's execution specifically stalls.

During the slow queries, the process has its ~16 DuckDB worker threads plus your own (thread count rises by ~16 during a query), but for most of the query window only 1–2 threads are Running; there are brief bursts up to Running+Ready = 11. The waiting threads sit in `WrAlertByThreadId` / `WrQueue` / `UserRequest` waits, with `max WrCpuRateControl = 0`, while the machine is otherwise idle. So the workers exist and can run together — most of the time they do not.

Question: what does ark/rsession change in the R process compared to Rgui/Rscript that could affect a C++ thread pool which parks and wakes its workers per task (DuckDB's scheduler), while a spin-based OpenMP pool in the same process scales to ~10 cores? I have run out of candidate mechanisms I can measure from outside or inside the process; I would be glad to run any diagnostic, dump, or instrumented build you suggest.

r-f0db872e [R]   2026-09-09T13:09:13.926454Z ERROR  at crates/ark/src/console/console_repl.rs:927: Line count mismatch: location spans 0 lines, but code has 3 newlines

title: Runtimes: Provide a way to disable affiliation (auto/guess) altogether; replace with explicit setting
description:
Positron's runtime affiliation feature has a lot of benefits around ease of use.


| Name                    | Language | Version | Source | Has Session | Session ID(s)       |
| ----------------------- | -------- | ------- | ------ | ----------- | ------------------- |
| R 4.6.0                 | r        | 4.6.0   | System | Yes         | r-notebook-33f1d4f3 |
| Python 3.13.9 (uv: evs) | python   | 3.13.9  | uv     | No          | -                   |


- No need to set up, configure, or make any explicit choices. Positron finds the best R/Python and chooses for you.
- Change your mind? No problem, start the R/Python you want and it becomes the new default. 
- Don't want an interpreter? No problem, shut it down and in the future it won't auto start. 
- Automatically project scoped.
- Speed! Positron saves all the info needed to launch the interpreter. When there is an affiliation, the runtime is heavily prioritized at startup and starts up much faster while other work is deferred.

However, to achieve these, it has also made some tradeoffs that have proven uncomfortable.

- The implicit nature of the choices makes them too opaque. The binding of your project to a specific interpreter is important, but you can't tell when it happens, and the only place you can see the binding is in the startup diagnostics report.
- You can't manually change the affiliation if it is wrong. The affiliation is only updated _implicitly_ when you make gestures like starting and stopping interpreters.
- The "affiliation" signal is weighted very high, above configuration. Once a runtime becomes affiliated with your workspace (which it does implicitly) it takes precedence over configuration, which means you may see a different runtime starting than the one your config tells you should start.
- For this reason, changes to your environment (new versions installed, updated lock files, etc) do not propagate to your affiliation, which can also be confusing.

These tradeoffs are suitable for many casual desktop users, because they make things "just work" without poking around in the settings. However, in controlled environments on Workbench and for advanced users, they may find themselves fighting the implicit nature of the affiliation system more often than benefiting from it.

### Proposal

- Make it possible to fully disable affiliation, although perhaps it needs a friendlier name than "affiliation". With affiliation disabled, Positron will need to reason about which interpreter to start every time it opens the project, which will be slower but also more likely to be correct. and/or more ambitiously:
- Replace implicit affiliations with a setting that is configurable in `settings.json` and indicates the interpreter(s) to use with the project. Provide UI that lets users see and change the value and settings indicating whether Positron can update the setting on its own. This setting replaces affiliation as the eager-start source of truth. Positron can still cache info on the interpreter to speed startup but will throw away its cache if the setting changes, etc.

title: R test explorer runner spawns R without the active module runtime's environment (LD_LIBRARY_PATH), breaking module-provided shared libraries
description:
## Summary

On Linux with Environment Modules configured, the R test explorer's test runner spawns the module's R binary **without** the environment that `module load` contributes. The interactive R console works, but running the same tests through the Test Explorer fails immediately because module-provided shared libraries are not on the loader path.

Observed error:

```
The R test run ended before completing (exit code 127).
/apps/.../software/R/4.5.1-foss-2023b/lib64/R/bin/exec/R: error while loading shared libraries:
libiconv.so.2: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

The same `libiconv.so.2` is present and resolvable once the module is loaded; the library lives in a separate module lib directory (e.g. `.../software/libiconv/1.17-GCCcore-13.2.0/lib`) that only `module load` adds to `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`.

## Impact

Package tests cannot be run from the Test Explorer on any module-backed R interpreter whose runtime dependencies come from environment modules (a common HPC / EasyBuild setup). `test()` from the console succeeds, so the failure is specific to the Test Explorer and is confusing for users, since everything else about the interpreter works.

## Environment

- Posit Workbench-managed Positron, Linux (Rocky 9).
- Environment Modules (EasyBuild), e.g. `Bioconductor/3.21-foss-2023b-R-4.5.1`.
- Reproduces on 2026.08.0. The env-var forwarding added in #15609 (2026.09.0) does **not** address this: it forwards `RSTUDIO_PANDOC`/`QUARTO_R`/`LANG`, and the module environment was explicitly kept out of that PR's scope.

## Reproduction

1. Configure a module-backed R interpreter whose runtime shared libs (e.g. `libiconv`) are supplied by environment modules, not by the base OS.
2. Start an R console session for that interpreter and confirm it reaches the `>` prompt. `test()` from the console passes.
3. Run the package tests from the Test Explorer.
4. Observe exit code 127 with a `cannot open shared object file` error for a module-provided library.

Confirming that it is the module environment (not a broken interpreter), in a Positron Terminal:

```bash
module purge
/apps/.../software/R/4.5.1-foss-2023b/bin/R --version   # fails: libiconv.so.2 not found
module load Bioconductor/3.21-foss-2023b-R-4.5.1
R --version                                              # succeeds
```

## Root cause

The runner spawns R as a bare child process (necessary, because it parses R's JSON result stream and must be able to cancel the process):

- `extensions/positron-r/src/testing/runner-testthat.ts:133` — `binpath = RSessionManager.instance.getLastBinpath()` (the module's `bin/R`).
- `extensions/positron-r/src/testing/runner-testthat.ts:139,143` — `const env = await buildRProcessEnv(); spawn(binpath, args, { cwd, env });`
- `extensions/positron-r/src/r-process-environment.ts:242` — `buildRProcessEnv()` starts from `{ ...process.env }` plus contributed mutations (read with the **ProcessCreation** filter, lines 176-177) plus a short `FORWARDED_R_SESSION_ENV_VARS` list (`LANG`, `TESTTHAT_MAX_FAILS`).

None of those layers carries the module environment:

- The **console** gets its module environment from the `module load` **startup command** the supervisor runs when launching the Ark kernel — not from `getEnvironmentContributions()`. So a runner that reads contributions "like the console does" still misses the module env.
- The **captured** module environment (`extensions/positron-r/src/runtime-manager.ts:289`, `api.captureEnvironmentVariables(...)`) is registered `applyAtProcessCreation: false` (`runtime-manager.ts:305`), deliberately, so that process-creation consumers skip it (to avoid double-applying on kernels and leaking one language's module env into another kernel). The runner uses exactly the ProcessCreation filter, so it never receives these.

Net: the module-backed R launcher script `bin/R` sets only `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$R_HOME/lib`; the module lib directories (where `libiconv.so.2` lives) are never added, so the spawned test process cannot link.

For contrast, the console preserves `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` correctly since #15191 (`extensions/positron-r/src/kernel.ts:271`, `prependLibDir(...)`), which is why the same interpreter works interactively.

## Expected behavior

When the active R runtime is module-backed, the Test Explorer runner should execute with the same module environment the console session has, so module-provided shared libraries resolve.

A minimal candidate, mirroring the existing precedent, is to add `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` (and `DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH` on macOS) to `FORWARDED_R_SESSION_ENV_VARS` (`extensions/positron-r/src/r-process-environment.ts:201`). That list is already read from the live console session via `Sys.getenv` (`getForwardedSessionEnvVars`, same file), and after #15191 the console session's `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` reflects the full module-inclusive value, so the runner would inherit the correct paths. Unlike the terminal-mutation case, this does not broaden `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` to a shell: it applies only to the single R process the runner spawns, so the pollution concern documented in `getRTerminalEnvironmentMutations` does not apply here. Note this "console value is module-inclusive" point is a working theory, inferred from the reported environment (the console loads the module libraries successfully while a `module purge`d R does not), rather than confirmed in code; it is worth verifying against the runtime path, along with whether the forwarded value could carry any unwanted extension-host entries.

An alternative is to apply the active runtime's captured module environment to the runner's spawn specifically, keyed to that runtime, rather than as a global process-creation contribution, so it does not reintroduce the double-apply / cross-language-leak problem that motivated `applyAtProcessCreation: false`.

## Workarounds

- Use an R wrapper script as the interpreter: the wrapper runs `module load` then `exec`s R, so `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` is set inside whatever process launches R, including the runner's spawn.
- Load the module at session startup (Workbench session-init / login-shell profile) so it is present in the extension host `process.env`, which the runner clones. Trade-off: pins that module for the session.
- Add the module lib directories to the system loader (`/etc/ld.so.conf.d/` + `ldconfig`) or rebuild with `--rpath` so bare `bin/R` resolves the libraries without `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`.

## Related

- #15609 — forwarded `RSTUDIO_PANDOC`/`QUARTO_R`/`LANG` to the runner (2026.09.0); module env intentionally out of scope.
- #15711 — centralize environment-contribution merging; would not cover this on its own, since the module env is registered `applyAtProcessCreation: false` and so is excluded from the ProcessCreation view the runner reads, even after merging.
- #15587 — related but distinct: the initial default *console* startup bypassing module activation. This report is about the *test runner*, a separately spawned process, not the console.
- #15191 — console `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` clobbering (fixed 2026.08.0); the reason the console works and reports the module-inclusive path.
- #15501 (terminals), #15509 (Python module probe) — same "module env not reaching a directly-spawned/adjacent process" family.

title: Remote SSH does not honor RemoteForward directives from SSH config
description:
## System details

#### Positron and OS details

Positron Version: 2026.09.1 (user setup) build 2
Code - OSS Version: 1.130.0
Commit: 467ff390dd8b4ffc8972ebb84d9e05a1fd5a4fe2
Electron: 42.6.0
Chromium: 148.0.7778.280
Node.js: 24.18.0
V8: 14.8.178.38-electron.0
Local OS: Windows 11 x64 (10.0.26100)

#### Session details

Remote SSH session
Remote OS: Linux

## Describe the issue

Positron Remote SSH currently appears to ignore `RemoteForward` directives defined in the SSH configuration.

Example:

```ssh
Host remote-server
    ProxyJump bastion-host.example.com
    HostName remote-server.example.com
    User username
    IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_rsa
    ForwardAgent yes
    RemoteForward 12345 target-host.example.com:12345
```

The SSH connection itself works, but the remote port forwarding is not established.

## Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Configure a host in `~/.ssh/config` with a `RemoteForward` directive.
2. Connect to the host using Positron Remote SSH.
3. Check whether the configured remote port forwarding is active on the remote host.

## Expected behavior

`RemoteForward` directives defined in `~/.ssh/config` should be honored by Positron Remote SSH in the same way as a standard OpenSSH client.

## Additional information

The same SSH configuration works as expected when connecting with the standard OpenSSH client.

title: Data Connections: support Motherduck
description:
_Originally posted by @ajjitn in https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/discussions/14571#discussioncomment-17723839_:

> This is niche but since you all already support DuckDB, a Motherduck connection would be awesome!

----

MotherDuck is a cloud service built on DuckDB, and it connects through the exact same `@duckdb/node-api` entry point our DuckDB driver already uses: `DuckDBInstance.create('md:my_db', { motherduck_token: '...' })` (or a connection string `md:my_db?motherduck_token=...`). All the hard infrastructure (out-of-process native binding, worker pooling, IPC, crash recovery, and the full Data Explorer protocol backend) already exists and is reusable via the shared `positron-data-explorer-duckdb` package, so the engine work is essentially zero.

I think this would be a small-to-medium thing to add, with no new engine and no new protocol work.

Already in place:
- The `DuckDBInstance.create(path, options)` call is identical; MotherDuck just needs an `md:` path plus a `motherduck_token` option.
- The pinned `@duckdb/node-api ^1.5.3-r.3` supports the MotherDuck Node API path.
- The token maps cleanly onto a secret `Password` parameter (auto-persisted, auto-redacted).

Concrete work items (all pretty small, honestly):
- Thread the token (and optional database name) through `WorkerOpenConfig` into the worker's `DuckDBInstance.create` options.
- Add a mechanism with a `Password` token field.
- Fix the worker pool key (currently `mode + databasePath` only) so multiple `md:` sessions with different tokens do not share a worker, or skip pooling for `md:` entirely (it is remote, no file lock, same reasoning we used for pins `:memory:`).
- Emit `md:` variants from the R/Python connection code generation.
- Ship it as a separate provider (own icon) that consumes the shared backend.

Risks to verify before committing:
- Extension autoload + network: opening `md:` triggers DuckDB to auto-install/load the signed `motherduck` extension matching the engine build. Smoke-test this against the pinned node-api; if autoload is flaky we may need an explicit `INSTALL motherduck; LOAD motherduck;` bootstrap step in the worker.
- Multi-database tree: a MotherDuck account exposes multiple databases (plus `sample_data`), not a single file, so the tree may need a database/catalog level that the file-based DuckDB browsing does not have today.
- Read-only semantics for `md:` (vs. the file `access_mode: 'READ_ONLY'`).
- Auth scope: start with the non-interactive access token pasted into a `Password` field; defer interactive browser/SSO auth.

Both of the "could turn small into medium" items (extension autoload, multi-database tree) are checkable with a timebox investment of prototyping against a real MotherDuck token. 

I don't think we have any accounts with MotherDuck right now FWIW.

title: Make the Positron IPython kernel a standalone package
description:
**Note: Actually distributing the package e.g. via PyPI is out of scope for this issue.**

We initially started the Positron IPython kernel by modifying the upstream's existing jedi language server support. However, we've now drifted so far away from upstream that we could package the kernel separately.

The main benefit would be that by following a more standard Python approach, onboarding would be easier for future and external developers. Secondly, it would be much easier to distribute if we eventually decide to go that route.

In the simplest implementation, this would be achieved by just adding a `pyproject.toml` file to `positron-python/python_files/posit`.

Notes:

1. We would want to keep the same approach to pinning test requirements, as well as testing certain test dependencies at older versions.
2. We would also want to be able to bundle this package in the extension with pinned hashes (as in `jedilsp_requirements/requirements.txt`). I think this can be done by moving the `positron` dependencies out of the `requirements.in` file and into the `pyproject.toml`, then adding only `positron` to `requirements.in`.

Related thoughts:

1. It could still live as a sub-folder of `python_files`, or in the root of `positron-python`.
2. At the same time, we might want to consider re-organizing the package's modules. For instance, moving `*_comm.py` generated files into `comm/*.py`, and any other suggestions folks have.

title: Proposal: "Import" from data explorer to R/Python when viewing CSV, Parquet, XLSX, etc.
description: The data explorer currently has a nice way to view CSV, Parquet, etc. directly, and perform extremely basic operations such as sorting and filtering. However, this view is effectively a dead end as far as analysis goes. You can't get this data into an R or Python session for further processing or visualization without writing some code, and there are no tools to help you write the code you need to import the data. Proposal: an affordance on the Data Explorer editor action bar named something like _Import_ or _Open In..._. Selecting this would bring the data into R or Python for further work. ### Option A: One-click import (no code) Since the data is already being read by DuckDB, we could send it directly to R or Python using DuckDB libraries and primitives. In this approach you'd effectively get a copy of the data to work as an R or Python data frame without having to use code at all. The advantage of this approach is that it is (almost) frictionless and dependency-free. Click button, get data frame, go on your way. The disadvantage of this approach is that it is not very reproducible; you don't get any code you can use to read the data into a future R or Python session. Your workflow may become reliant on UI gestures. ### Option B: Launchpad for Import feature Another possibility is that this just becomes a launch point for the planned import dataset feature (https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/5515). Since you're already looking at the data you want to import in the Explorer, we would already know which file you want to import and settings like 'first row contains column names', and would just need a little additional information to generate the code for you.

title: Split getPackages into a compact list and a per-package getPackage
description:
Follow-up from review on #15671.

### Problem

`positronPackages.getPackages` returns full metadata for every installed package: `name`, `version`, `latestVersion`, `outdated`, `attached`, `description`, `url`, and (since #15629) a `vulnerabilities` array carrying up to nine fields per advisory. Every caller pays for all of it, on every call.

Two consequences:

- **Token cost.** Roughly 280 characters per package before advisories, more after. Assistant's `positronCommand` tool caps result size (raised and made structure-aware in posit-dev/assistant#2194, but still a cap), so a real environment of 100-300 packages gets truncated. A minimal three-field entry is ~50 characters, so the compact form fits several times as many packages in the same budget.
- **Lookups are the common case and the worst-served one.** "Is pandas installed?" and "what's the version of X?" are single-package questions answered by returning the whole environment. If the package sits late in the list, truncation can drop exactly the entry being sought -- and the model cannot distinguish "not installed" from "truncated away."

### Proposal

Two commands instead of one:

- **`positronPackages.getPackages`** -- compact metadata for all packages. Enough to answer "what's installed, at what version, is anything outdated." Candidates to drop: `description`, `url`, and the per-package `vulnerabilities` array (a count or a boolean would preserve the signal at a fraction of the size).
- **`positronPackages.getPackage`** -- full metadata for a single package by name.

### Why this is cheaper than it looks

`getPackageDetail(name, token)` already exists -- on `IPositronPackagesInstance` (`positronPackagesInstance.ts:158`) and on the package-manager interface (`runtimeSessionService.ts:661`). It is what the package detail editor already opens for. So `getPackage` is mostly wiring an existing RPC to a new agent-compatible command.

It also returns **fields the list command cannot carry at all**: `license`, `publishedDate`, `title`, `author`, `sourceRepository`. Today those are absent from every `getPackages` entry because including them would cost a round trip per package -- there is a comment saying exactly that at `positronPackagesCommands.ts:38-44`. So this is not only a slimming exercise; it makes genuinely richer per-package data reachable for the first time.

### Prior art

The same wall was hit on Data Connections and resolved the same way -- moving the connection code snippet out of the listing into a separate command.

### Notes

- Both commands should stay `agentCompatible`, with `getPackage` taking a single `name` argument.
- The `positron-commands` skill picks up `Arguments`/`Returns` from live metadata, so the mechanical half updates itself. The hand-written guidance in `references/packages.md` will need a pass: it currently tells the model to read advisories straight off `getPackages`, which stops being true.
- Worth deciding whether `getPackage` should accept several names at once. That would serve "do I have pandas and numpy?" in one call rather than N.
- An alternative (or complement) raised during the same discussion: add query arguments to `getPackages` (`names`, `outdatedOnly`) so a lookup can be answered completely without a second command.

title: `providers.<id>.models.allow` / `.deny` are ignored by core's language model registry
description:
`POSIT_AI_PROVIDERS_ENFORCED` carries both `providers.<id>.enabled` and `providers.<id>.models.allow`. Posit Assistant's model menu honors all three. The feature-scoped quick-picks fed by core's `languageModelsService` honor only `enabled` — models excluded by `models.allow` or removed by `models.deny` stay selectable there.

Positron `2026.08.0` build `331` (VS Code `1.124.0`, commit `a3a370d418`), `posit.assistant` `0.9.1` and `0.10.0-universal`.

## Reproduction

Launch Positron from a shell with:

```bash
export POSIT_AI_PROVIDERS_ENFORCED='{"providers":{"default":{"enabled":false},"anthropic":{"enabled":true,"models":{"allow":["claude-opus-5"]}}}}'
```

Sign in to Anthropic, then compare:

- **Posit Assistant** — model chip at the bottom-right of the chat input.
- **Core quick-pick** — Command Palette → `Git: Select Git Suggestions Model` (same for `Positron Notebook: Select Notebook Suggestions Model`, `Select Ghost Cell Model`, `Select Visualize Model`).

| Surface | `enabled` | `models.allow` | `models.deny` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Posit Assistant menu | honored | **honored** — only `Claude Opus 5` | **honored** |
| Core quick-pick | honored | **ignored** — all 10 models | **ignored** — all 10 models |

`deny` behaves identically. With `{"providers":{"anthropic":{"enabled":true,"models":{"allow":["claude-opus-5","claude-sonnet-5"],"deny":["claude-sonnet-5"]}}}}` the assistant menu correctly shows only `Claude Opus 5`, while the quick-pick in the same session still lists all ten Anthropic models including the denied `claude-sonnet-5`.

Expected: both apply the enforced catalog. A model excluded by `models.allow` or `models.deny` should not be offered anywhere in the session.

`default.enabled=false` only keeps other providers out of the comparison. The quick-pick does read this variable — swap the fragment for `{"providers":{"anthropic":{"enabled":false}}}` and it drops to 0 models — so the gap is the model-list filter specifically, not the enforcement channel.

## Impact

Partial enforcement. An administrator restricting models gets them blocked in the assistant but still called by Git commit-message suggestions, notebook suggestions, ghost cells, and visualize.

title: Consolidate Download URL settings for remote extensions
description: Currently there are three separate "Download URL" settings for Positron's remote extensions (SSH, WSL, Dev Containers). This setting controls the URL where Positron Server will be fetched. It's important for testing remote extensions since local builds often don't have an exact matching server version, or for using custom server builds. It's also important for customizing environments wherein fetching arbitrary files from the internet might not be possible in the remote environment. This is kind of silly. It's easy to choose the wrong one if you just type "Download URL", and this choice wasn't intentional -- it's an artifact of the way we added these extensions one at a time, each with its own setting. We should probably just have one "download URL template" setting shared by all three remote extensions.

title: Wide DECIMAL values are displayed incorrectly in the Data Explorer
description:
## Title

Wide DECIMAL values are displayed incorrectly in the Data Explorer, because formatting coerces them through a JS number

## Body

Follow-up from review of the Databricks data driver PR [15337](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/15337), where the same root cause was fixed for the `Integer` display type. The `Decimal` case needs a different fix and is filed separately.

### Problem

In `_formatValue`, the `Decimal` branch coerces the value to a JS number before formatting:

```ts
case ColumnDisplayType.Floating:
case ColumnDisplayType.Decimal: {
    const num = typeof value === 'number' ? value : Number(value);
    ...
    return formatFloat(num, opts);
}
```

For `Floating` that is correct -- the value really is a double. For `Decimal` it is not: these drivers receive the exact decimal as a string precisely because a double cannot represent it, and `Number()` throws that away. The damage is not confined to the fraction; once the integral part passes 2^53 the whole-number digits are wrong too.

Two failure shapes, with `decimal(38,2)`:

| Stored value | Displayed today | Should display (with default format options) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `123456789012345678901234567890.12` | `1.23e+29` | `123456789012345678901234567890.12` |
| `9007199254740993.01` | `9007199254740992.00` | `9007199254740993.01` |

The first is visibly broken. The second is worse in practice: it looks like an ordinary number and is silently wrong in its last digits, which is exactly the kind of value a financial or identifier column holds.

### Where

The same block is duplicated in each driver:

- `extensions/positron-data-driver-databricks/src/databricksTableView.ts` -- `_formatValue`
- `extensions/positron-data-driver-postgresql/src/postgresqlTableView.ts` -- `_formatValue`
- `extensions/positron-data-driver-redshift/src/redshiftTableView.ts` -- `_formatValue`
- `extensions/positron-data-driver-snowflake/src/snowflakeTableView.ts` -- `_formatValue` (see caveat below)

The SQLite and DuckDB drivers were not audited; they share the copy-pasted formatting helpers, so they should be checked as part of this.

The exact value **is** available in three of the four: the Databricks driver sets `preserveBigNumericPrecision`, so DECIMAL arrives as an exact string, and `pg` returns `numeric` as a string for PostgreSQL and Redshift. Snowflake is different: `snowflake-sdk` yields a JS number at the SDK boundary, so the precision is already gone before the table view sees it. Fixing Snowflake means changing how its results are parsed, which is separable work and arguably its own issue.

### Why the Integer fix does not transfer

For `Integer` the fix was simply to stop coercing: pass the exact digit string to `formatInteger`, which only stringifies and groups textually. `Decimal` cannot do that, because `FormatOptions` requires actual arithmetic on the value:

- round to `small_num_digits` or `large_num_digits` depending on magnitude,
- switch to exponential notation past `max_integral_digits`,
- then apply `thousands_sep`.

Doing that faithfully without a JS number means decimal arithmetic on the digit string.

### Options

1. **A string-based decimal formatter.** A pure function that takes the exact digit string plus `FormatOptions` and returns the display string: split sign, integral, and fractional parts; round half-up on the fractional digits; decide exponential form from the integral digit count; group with the separator. No new dependency, easily unit-tested against a table of cases, and it can reuse the existing `applyThousandsSep`.
2. **A decimal library** (`decimal.js`, `big.js`). Less code to own, but a dependency added to each driver extension, and these are packaged into the product.
3. **Widen the protocol so the frontend formats.** Larger change and cross-cutting; noted only for completeness.

Option 1 looks right, with one design question attached: this formatting code is copy-pasted across four or five driver extensions today, and so is `formatFloat`, `formatInteger`, `applyThousandsSep`, and `truncate`. A fix should probably land in one shared place rather than being pasted a fifth time -- but there is no shared module for driver-side helpers today (the only shared package is the generated protocol types). Deciding where it lives is part of this work.

### Scope notes

- **Exports are unaffected.** `stringifyExportCell` passes a string through unchanged, so CSV and TSV exports of a wide decimal are already exact. This is a display-path bug only.
- **The median in summary stats has the same coercion.** `_summaryStatsFromRow` does `fmt(Number(medianRaw))`, so a wide decimal median is also rounded. `min_value` and `max_value` use `String(...)` and are already exact. Mean and standard deviation are computed from SQL `sum()` over a float cast and are approximate by construction, which is a separate design choice and not part of this.

### Repro

```sql
-- Databricks
CREATE TABLE decimal_precision_demo (id INT, amount DECIMAL(38,2));
INSERT INTO decimal_precision_demo VALUES
  (1, 123456789012345678901234567890.12),
  (2, 9007199254740993.01);

-- PostgreSQL and Redshift: same, with amount NUMERIC(38,2)
```

Open the table in the Data Explorer. Row 1 shows exponential notation; row 2 shows `...992.00` instead of `...993.01`. Export the same rows to CSV and note that the exported values are correct, which confirms the loss is in display formatting rather than in transport.

### Acceptance criteria

- A `DECIMAL`/`NUMERIC` value whose integral part exceeds 2^53 displays its digits correctly, rounded according to `FormatOptions` rather than converted to a double, in the Databricks, PostgreSQL, and Redshift drivers.
- The `Floating` display type keeps its current behavior; only `Decimal` changes.
- The shared formatting helpers live in one place rather than being duplicated again, or there is a recorded decision not to.
- Unit tests covering: a wide integral part, a value near 2^53, negative values, rounding at the digit limit, exponential-notation thresholds, and the thousands separator.

### Out of scope

- The Snowflake driver, unless its SDK result parsing is changed first (worth its own issue).
- The `Integer` display type, already fixed.
- Changing what `FormatOptions` means or how many digits the grid shows by default.

Currently, we have a new set of commands for the new UI. For example, we have `positronNotebook.cell.executeAndSelectBelow` instead of upstream's `notebook.cell.executeAndSelectBelow`.

(Note that we don't always match their commands e.g. we have `positronNotebook.cell.executeOrToggleEditor` but they handle the "toggle editor" part in the `notebook.cell.execute` command.)

title: Memory metrics: set a regression threshold and alert on it
description:
#15001 asks for an alert when memory goes up without a plausible explanation. Nothing fails or notifies today, deliberately: we do not yet know how much a number moves run to run for reasons unrelated to a code change.

Each run already takes a per-process median over three cold launches, so the spread is recorded and the variance can be read off the history once there is some.

Two things to settle: what threshold, and where it fires.

Last in the sequence. Monitoring and alerting are not set up in the e2e-test-insights dashboard at all yet, so this needs that infrastructure to exist first, on top of the publish endpoint and a few weeks of nightly runs.

Refs #15001

title: Data Apps: Run App and Debug App run the active editor's file, not the file whose button was clicked
description:
Interactive app Run and Debug commands ignore the file whose menu button is clicked and always use the active (i.e. focused) editor.

Affects Shiny, Streamlit, Dash, Flask, FastAPI, Gradio, and marimo.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open two Streamlit app files side by side in a split editor: `app_one.py` (left) and `app_two.py` (right).
2. Click into `app_one.py` so it is the active editor.
3. Click the Run button in the *right* group's title bar, above `app_two.py`.

**Expected:** `app_two.py` runs.

**Actual:** `app_one.py` runs. The terminal, the Viewer, and the progress notification all name the app, so nothing indicates the wrong file was picked.

Clicking an editor title action deliberately does not activate that editor group (`editorGroupView.ts`, "not when clicking on actions or breadcrumbs"), so the active editor genuinely stays on the other file. The same mismatch applies to any invocation that passes a URI, such as a keybinding with `args`.

## Also blocks URI-driven invocation

Because the commands only ever act on the active editor, Assistant (#15704) must open the app file and make it active before running it. That is slower and steals the user's current focus e.g. they may be editing another file.

title: Add tests & gather metrics for memory usage
description:
Over time, Positron's memory usage has crept up substantially. Because there are no tests or metrics that track the overall system memory usage, we've had a number of changes go in that silently pushed RAM usage up by quite a lot.

For example, https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/13998 created an isolated worker for the DuckDB task that reads CSV/TSV files. This worker added ~100mb to Positron's RAM usage in every session. When we merged the upstream Copilot extension into Positron, we did it in such a way that Copilot loads at startup, taking ~200mb of RAM for its tokenizer and other features. The catalog explorer loads the entire Snowflake SDK into memory at startup (~10mb). Bundling the Quarto extension caused us to start loading a 100mb language server at startup. And so on. 

It can be difficult for us to notice this heavy usage since most of us are on newer laptops with a lot of fast RAM. To keep usage reasonable moving forward, we should:
- Have performance metrics that capture the RAM usage of the entire Positron process tree and alert us when it goes up without plausible explanation, and/or
- Have CI tests that fail if RAM usage is dramatically larger than expected

## Steps

- [x] **1. Idle memory collector + nightly workflow** https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/15430
- [x] **2. Publish idle runs to the insights API** https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/15489
- [x] **3. Decide which scenarios to measure past idle** https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/15490
- [x] **4. Session-start scenario** https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/15491
- [x] **5. Feature scenarios (data explorer, notebooks)** https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/15492
- [x] **6. Server lane** https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/15493
- [x] **7. Per-extension heap attribution** https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/15494
- [x] **8. Dashboard: idle memory over time** https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/15495
- [x] **9. Regression threshold + alerting** https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/15496

Step 2 comes before the rest: a per-run report cannot show a trend. Step 9 comes last, since monitoring and alerting are not set up in the e2e-test-insights dashboard yet.

description:
On Posit Workbench, MCP server OAuth sign-in fails after the user approves the grant. The browser lands on a 404 page and the MCP server never starts.

The callback URL Positron registers as the OAuth redirect leaves out the session prefix, so the redirect never reaches the session.

Follow-up to #13446.

1. Open a Positron session in Posit Workbench.
2. Add an MCP server that uses OAuth, for example Atlassian.
3. Start the sign-in flow and approve the grant.
4. The browser lands on a 404 page and the account does not appear in the Accounts menu.

title: Standalone mode: let Positron launch as a stripped-back app surface that extensions control
description:
## Context

Positron is a system for doing data science, but not everyone doing data science wants code in their face, or a full IDE surface at all. Especially in the new agent-based way of working, a streamlined interface is a real benefit.

So we want to surface a way of using Positron that behaves like a standalone app, showing just what is important for data science at that given point. To do that we need a new way of launching Positron: a standalone mode that extensions can contribute a surface to.

This needs to be a real application mode, not just a layout preset. We looked into approaches like popping out an editor, but an editor window carries chrome that does not make sense here, things like minimize affordances and tab behavior. We want it as stripped back as possible, a very minimal window, while keeping all the nice benefits of the workbench underneath it. Kernel management and the rest of that machinery should still be there, just behind the scenes. What we present is a very simplified interface that the application, in this case an extension, controls.

For the work we are doing now the first consumer is the Positron Assistant extension, with a data science tool we are building out. We have that specific use case in mind, but we want to keep this as general-purpose as possible so we are not tying it down. If other use cases come up later that want a focused Positron mode with none of the main IDE chrome around it, they should be able to use this too.

This is very similar in spirit to #14771 (Assistant focused chat mode), but it feels like a bigger thing. That issue is tied closely to that one experience, whereas this keeps things even simpler and gives us a clean target to build a fresh surface against.

## Why this belongs in Positron and not just in the extension

Positron needs to know a decent amount about how to handle this mode: opening into the right thing, staying in that mode, and generally not surfacing the IDE behind the user's back. Those are things an extension's surface cannot do, by definition of how extensions get loaded. We looked into options like prioritizing a given extension, but there is still a buffer while everything is loading. If we want a polished standalone app experience, we need to bypass the main IDE workspace view entirely, and that has to happen below the extension layer.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A window in standalone mode presents its hosted surface with no Positron IDE chrome or editor affordances: no editor tabs, panels, or status bars.
2. Users can launch directly into the mode (command, setting, or command-line flag) without passing through the IDE first.
3. Nothing the user does inside the mode creates, reveals, or focuses the Positron IDE unless they explicitly ask for it. This holds during session starts and restarts, code execution, output production, and error conditions.
4. Reload, and quit-then-relaunch, restore the mode and the user's content. Restoration never leaves the user in an empty or unusable frame.
5. There is an explicit, user-initiated way into the full Positron IDE, and taking it carries the user's live content into the IDE rather than discarding it.
6. Only one window holds the mode at a time, and an externally requested open (second-instance CLI, Finder Open With, Dock drop) never silently lands behind the standalone window.
7. While the surface is loading or starting, that state is visibly communicated. It never appears frozen, empty, or broken.
8. Computational sessions may not survive restoration. When a session restarts, the surface explains what happened and offers an understandable recovery action; preserving the user's content is the stronger guarantee.
9. The assistant-facing consumer is gated on the `ai.enabled` main switch.

## Implementation notes

This is a fair amount of work, so it will land as a stack of PRs rather than one change. The lower layers are general window and platform work with no knowledge of the hosted surface; the consumer-specific pieces sit on top.

title: Connections pane does not reliably display two simultaneous SQL Server connections as separate entries
description:
## System details:
#### Positron and OS details:
- Positron version: 2026.06.0
- OS: Linux x86_64

#### Session details:
- R 4.6.0
- Packages:
  - `connections` 0.2.1
  - `odbc`
  - `DBI`


## Describe the issue:
When using Positron's documented R connections workflow with the `connections` package and `odbc`, the Connections pane does not reliably display two simultaneous SQL Server connections as separate entries.

Both connections are created successfully and both work for queries, but the Connections pane may show only one connection, may label it generically as `Default`, or may fail to keep DEV and PRD-style entries separate even when `connection_view()` is called with distinct `name` values.

In the R session, both objects are valid `connConnection` objects, both can run `DBI::dbGetQuery()`, and both have distinct internal IDs.

## Steps to reproduce the issue:
Using an R script or the R console in Positron:

1. Create two SQL Server ODBC connections through `connections::connection_open()` using different DSNs.
2. Confirm both connections are valid and can execute simple queries.
3. Call `connections::connection_view()` on each connection with distinct `name =` values.
4. Open or inspect the Connections pane.

Minimal DSN-based example:

```r
library(connections)
library(odbc)
library(DBI)

con_dev <- connections::connection_open(
  odbc::odbc(),
  .connection_string = "DSN=DB_DEV"
)

con_prd <- connections::connection_open(
  odbc::odbc(),
  .connection_string = "DSN=DB_PRD"
)

class(con_dev)
class(con_prd)

slot(con_dev, "id")
slot(con_prd, "id")

DBI::dbGetQuery(con_dev, "SELECT TOP 3 TABLE_NAME FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES")
DBI::dbGetQuery(con_prd, "SELECT TOP 3 TABLE_NAME FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES")

connections::connection_view(con_dev, name = "DB_DEV")
connections::connection_view(con_prd, name = "DB_PRD")
```

## Expected or desired behavior:
Two distinct SQL Server connections opened from R should appear separately in the Connections pane so their schemas can be browsed independently.

## Were there any error messages in the UI, Output panel, or Developer Tools console?
There was no consistent UI error message for the main issue.

Observed behavior in the Connections pane was inconsistent:
- sometimes only one connection appeared
- sometimes it appeared with a generic label like `Default`
- distinct `name =` values in `connections::connection_view()` did not reliably produce two separate visible entries

Additional experiments produced these R-side errors, though they were part of workaround attempts rather than the main reproduction:

```text
Error: No metadata was found for this connection
```

This occurred when overriding `connection_id` in `connection_view()` with an arbitrary value.

```text
Error: external pointer is not valid
```

This occurred in a separate experiment involving repeated `connection_view()` calls while varying `host` and `name`.

Potentially relevant detail: the two connection objects are distinct in R and have different internal IDs, but they share the same backend metadata pattern:
- `host = "odbc"`
- `type = "Microsoft SQL Server"`

That may be relevant if the Connections pane is grouping or reusing entries too aggressively for R-side ODBC connections.

title: Safari breaks webviews in browser-hosted Positron due to detached `ArrayBuffer`
description:
Note: I believe this issue is fixed in dev builds of Positron, but not in any released versions. I'm filing it here so we have something to refer to for users who encounter this problem.
This is for an issue I have seen with Positron in Workbench when used with Safari: with this setup, some versions of Posit Assistant (1.0.0 and 1.0.1 as of this writing) hang when loading the UI. I'm working on a workaround in Posit Assistant for this.

## Summary

Safari can detach an `ArrayBuffer` that the browser-hosted VS Code remote protocol still uses. The next protocol read fails with the following error:

```text
Underlying ArrayBuffer has been detached from the view or out-of-bounds: subarray
```

The failure drops remote-protocol messages and can leave extension webviews blank. Large `webview.html` assignments, large webview messages, and webview resource loads make the failure easier to reproduce.

The problem affects browser-hosted products, including Positron Server and VS Code web deployments. Desktop Positron and desktop VS Code do not use the affected browser transport. Chromium-based browsers do not reproduce the problem against the same server and workspace.

## Affected versions

The following table separates tested versions from versions confirmed by source inspection.

| Product | Version | Status | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Safari | 26.5.2 (21624.2.5.11.8) on macOS 26.5.2 | Affected | Reproduced with browser-hosted Positron |
| Safari and other WebKit browsers | Safari 18 on macOS and iPadOS | Affected | Reproduced in the upstream VS Code and code-server reports |
| VS Code web | 1.107.x through 1.124.0 | Affected | Upstream reproduction and source inspection |
| VS Code web | 1.125.0 and later | Fixed | The 1.125.0 source includes the upstream buffer-copy fix |
| Positron | 2026.07.1-5, Code OSS 1.118.0 | Affected | Original Positron reproduction |
| Positron | 2026.08.0-331 | Affected | The release uses the vulnerable Code OSS 1.124.0 implementation |
| Positron | 2026.08.1-2 | Affected | The release predates the Code OSS 1.130.0 merge and retains the vulnerable implementation |
| Positron source | `main` after commit `99d1945d` | Fixed in source | The Code OSS 1.130.0 merge includes the upstream fix |
| Positron stable releases | No fixed stable release as of August 14, 2026 | Not fixed | The latest stable release is 2026.08.1-2 |

The VS Code defect dates to a non-copying buffer optimization from 2019. The table lists the versions covered by current upstream reports and direct source inspection; it does not claim that VS Code 1.107.x is the first affected version.

## Symptoms

An affected session can show one or more of the following symptoms:
- An extension webview opens but remains blank.
- The webview content frame remains at `pending-frame (fake.html)`.
- The browser never requests the extension's client JavaScript.
- Jupyter or other extension-rendered output does not appear.
- Safari logs errors from `slice`, `_read`, `deserialize`, or `acceptChunk` in `workbench.js`.
- The extension-host message channel stops processing messages until you reload the page.

Content Security Policy reports can appear at the same time, but report-only policy violations do not cause this failure.

## Cause
Safari does not support the transferable-stream path that VS Code uses to load webview resources. VS Code therefore sends resource data as chunk messages through `postMessage` with a transfer list.
The vulnerable implementation creates a `Uint8Array` view over the chunk's existing buffer:

```ts
const data = new Uint8Array(
chunk.buffer.buffer,
chunk.buffer.byteOffset,
chunk.buffer.byteLength,
);
this._send("did-load-resource-chunk", { id, data }, [data.buffer]);
```

In a remote session, the chunk can share its underlying `ArrayBuffer` with other views in the inter-process communication deserializer. WebKit detaches the transferred buffer synchronously. This action also detaches the sibling views that the protocol reader still needs.

The next read then calls `subarray` on a detached buffer and throws an exception. The protocol drops the message that it was processing.

## Fix

VS Code [PR #321291](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/321291) copies each chunk before transferring it:

```ts
const data = chunk.buffer.slice();
this._send("did-load-resource-chunk", { id, data }, [data.buffer]);
```

The new buffer belongs only to the outgoing message. Transferring it cannot detach views that the protocol reader uses. The VS Code team verified that this change fixes both observed Safari error paths.

The change is present in [VS Code 1.125.0](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/1.125.0/src/vs/workbench/contrib/webview/browser/webviewElement.ts) and later versions.

Positron merged Code OSS 1.130.0 in [Positron PR #15243](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/15243). The merge commit, [`99d1945d`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/commit/99d1945d4b218f47d88d6b2fd6abb4d4c46a049b), contains the fix. However, Positron published [2026.08.1-2](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/releases/tag/2026.08.1-2) before that merge. A stable Positron release does not contain the fix as of the report date.

## Reproduce the problem

### Prerequisites

- Browser-hosted Positron 2026.07.1-5, 2026.08.0-331, or 2026.08.1-2
- Safari 26.5.2
- Posit Assistant 1.0.0 VSIX
- Posit Assistant enabled in the Workbench configuration

You do not need a model account, an API key, or an Assistant sign-in.

### Procedure

1. Open the browser-hosted Positron session in Safari.
2. Open Safari Web Inspector for the Positron page.
3. In Positron, open the Extensions panel and make sure Posit Assistant 1.0.0 is installed
4. Run **Developer: Reload Window**.
5. Click on the Posit Assistant icon in the sidebar.

### Actual result

The Assistant editor panel remains blank. Safari logs the detached-buffer error with `slice`, `_read`, or `acceptChunk` frames in `workbench.js`. The webview content frame can remain at `pending-frame (fake.html)`, and the browser does not request `dist/client/main.js`.

### Expected result

The Assistant panel displays its loading interface and then displays the chat interface.

### Control test

Repeat the procedure in Chrome against the same Positron server and workspace. The Assistant panel loads normally.

## References

- [VS Code PR #321291: Fix webview resource loading detach in Safari and WebKit](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/321291)
- [VS Code issue #316841: Webview extensions are blank on Safari and WebKit](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/316841)
- [VS Code fix commit `17e8b7d`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/17e8b7d4acf44afae14127ac846a8b7b58dfae82)
- [code-server issue #7801: Webview-heavy extensions render blank on Safari and iPad](https://github.com/coder/code-server/issues/7801)
- [code-server issue #7803: Jupyter output does not render in Safari](https://github.com/coder/code-server/issues/7803)
- [Positron release 2026.08.1-2](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/releases/tag/2026.08.1-2)

title: python: standalone interpreters in `/opt/python` are labeled "Unknown" instead of "Global"
description:
Positron searches `/opt/python` for interpreters, because that's the recommended Python location on Workbench. Any standalone/base interpreters in there show up in the interpreter picker with the source "Unknown", but the expected source is "Global". This was reported before as #6270 and closed, but I think it was only fixed for the `js` locator.

### Steps to reproduce 

1. Install a base Python at `/opt/python/3.12.13/bin/python` on macOS or Linux. It must be a base install and not a virtual environment. Move it into place rather than symlink it:

   ```sh
   mkdir -p /tmp/pystage
   UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR=/tmp/pystage uv python install 3.12.13
   sudo mv /tmp/pystage/cpython-3.12.13-* /opt/python/3.12.13
   ```

2. Start Positron and wait for interpreter discovery to finish.
3. Open the console session picker.
4. The interpreter shows as `Python 3.12.13 (Unknown)`, under an "Unknown" heading.

### Expected or desired behavior

The interpreter shows as `Python 3.14.5 (Global)`, under a "Global" heading.

### Impact

An unknown kind sorts last in the recommendation ranking, so these interpreters sink to the bottom of the picker. This might also affect how these interpreters are used when creating virtual environments or the new health check.

title: Extension installs fail in Workbench sessions with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'isAcademic')`
description:
Installing any extension in a Positron session on Workbench fails. The notification reads "Error while installing 'Databricks' extension. Please check the log for more details." Reproduced on 2026.09.0-daily+147.pro1 ("Autumn Hawkbit"); 2026.08.1+195.pro1 ("Yellow Yarrow") installs the same extension successfully.

The defect is in the shared server startup path, so standalone Positron Server is likely affected as well. Only Workbench was tested.

The Window log shows:

```
[error] [Window] TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'isAcademic')
    at positronGalleryParams (server-main.js:23777:261)
    at ExtensionGalleryServiceWithNoStorageService.getExtensionsUsingResourceApi (server-main.js:23779:16)
    at ExtensionGalleryServiceWithNoStorageService.getExtensions (server-main.js:23685:49)
    at async ExtensionGalleryServiceWithNoStorageService.getCompatibleExtension (server-main.js:23917:24)
    at async ExtensionManagementService2.getCompatibleVersion (server-main.js:27654:35)
    at async ExtensionManagementService2.checkAndGetCompatibleVersion (server-main.js:27599:33)
    at async ExtensionManagementService2.installGalleryExtensions (server-main.js:27128:9)
    at async ExtensionManagementService2.installFromGallery (server-main.js:27094:27)
```

## Cause

`AbstractExtensionGalleryService` takes `IPositronAcademicLicenseService` as a constructor dependency (`src/vs/platform/extensionManagement/common/extensionGalleryService.ts:646`) and reads it on both gallery request paths, at lines 804 and 1481.

In the server main process that dependency is registered too late. `serverServices.ts:266` calls `createInstance(NativeLanguagePackService)`, and `NativeLanguagePackService` declares `@IExtensionGalleryService` (`src/vs/platform/languagePacks/node/languagePacks.ts:38`), so the gallery service is constructed there. `serverServices.ts:364` registers `IPositronAcademicLicenseService` about a hundred lines further down.

At construction time the identifier is not in the service collection, so `_createAndCacheServiceInstance` calls `_throwIfStrict` (`instantiationService.ts:240`). `InstantiationService` is created without the strict flag at `serverServices.ts:265`, so that emits a `console.warn` and continues instead of throwing. The gallery service is then cached with `academicLicenseService` undefined for the life of the process, and every later gallery request throws when it reads the property.

`remoteExtensionHostAgentCli.ts:147` and `cliProcessMain.ts:243` register the license service before the gallery service, so those processes are unaffected. `serverServices.ts` is the only one with the order inverted.

## Regression

#15507 added the constructor dependency and the late registration in the same change. It is on `main` and not on `release/2026.08`, which matches 2026.08.1 working and the 2026.09.0 daily failing.

## Fix

Move the `IPositronAcademicLicenseService` registration above `serverServices.ts:265`. `PositronAcademicLicenseService` has no service dependencies, and both of its inputs, `positronLicenseeInfo` and `licenseHash`, are parameters of `setupServerServices`, so it can be registered as early as needed.

title: Auth dialog needs region/profile inputs for AWS Bedrock, and should show when env vars override UI settings
description:
Currently the auth dialog UI has no way to set the AWS region or profile used for Bedrock. PA falls back to the default `us-east-1` unless `AWS_REGION` is set, or (after [posit-dev/assistant#2180](https://github.com/posit-dev/assistant/pull/2180)) the user hand-edits `providers.json`.

**Proposed changes:**
- Add a region input and a profile input to the auth dialog modal for Bedrock.
- When env vars are overriding a setting entered in the UI, show that in the UI. Right now there's no indication anywhere that env vars are winning over what the user configured.

**Open question:**
Precedence between `AWS_REGION`/profile env vars and `providers.json` isn't confirmed. Env vars are believed to take precedence today, but this needs to be pinned down, especially since admins enforcing a region/profile for Assistant would likely do it through `providers.json`. If env vars win over `providers.json`, that's a gap for admin enforcement.

title: {cli} links for runnable code and help topics have stopped working after extension host restart
description: I request that Positron handle console links from the {cli} package more like RStudio does. For example, RStudio underlines links and shows a tooltip that reveals the link destination. In Positron, links are not underlined (and thus not obviously clickable) and there's no tooltip when hovered (so it's a mystery what clicking the link will do). Here's a simple example creating a link to the help page for the `lm()` function: ```r cli::cli_text("{.fn stats::lm}") ``` And here's what it's like interacting with the link in RStudio. Prior to hovering, the link has a dotted underline. Then on hover, the underline turns solid and I get a popup tooltip showing some function help info. And here's what it's like in Positron. The mouse turns into a hand, which is better than nothing, but that's it. There are some possibly related issues (e.g., https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/1769, https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/12975) but I don't think they're asking the same thing as I am. I'm using Positron Version 2026.08.2 build 4 on macOS 14.6.1.

title: Help topics and vignettes don't render after an extension host restart
description: Follow-on to #15726 / #15757. #15757 repairs the console-side dispatch for cli's `x-r-help:` / `x-r-run:` / `x-r-vignette:` links, so after an extension host restart the click reaches a live R session again. With that, `{.run}` works end to end. However, `{.help}` and `{.vignette}` still fail, for a second, unrelated reason: the Help pane renders nothing (blank pane, no error). It turns out the problem has nothing to do with cli links at all. It's a more general problem about stale help proxy info. Broken cli links are just how I ended up stress testing this area. ## Repro In fresh Positron window with a single fresh R console, in the R console: * Do `?stats::acf`. Help for `stats::acf` opens. (the exact function is not important) * Restart the extension host, presumably via the *Developer: Restart Extension Host* command. * Do `?stats::lm`. Help for `stats::lm` does not render. You see `/library/stats/html/lm.html` as the URL the viewer is trying to go to. (exact function not important, but should be different from what help was already viewing) * Reload the window, presumably via the *Developer: Reload Window* command. * Do `?stats::add1`. Help for `stats::add1` opens. (the exact function is not important, but just try something new) You can experience the same with a set of tickles based on vignette listings. Pick 3 packages that you have installed and that have vignettes. * `browseVignettes("dplyr")`. Good. * *Developer: Restart Extension Host* * `browseVignettes("tidyr")`. No joy. * *Developer: Reload Window* * `browseVignettes("ggplot2")`. Good again. Or tickle with individual vignettes. * `vignette("grouping", package = "dplyr")`. Good. * *Developer: Restart Extension Host* * `vignette("rectangle", package = "tidyr")`. No joy. * *Developer: Reload Window* * `vignette("profiling", package = "ggplot2")`. Good again. It's nice that *Reload Window* fixes things, but we should fix this properly.

title: Consider options for how/when new editor action bar UI affordances appear
description:
In https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/7237 we added a new checkbox control and toggle control for the editor action bar, for extensions to use. In https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto/pull/698 we then added these controls for use in the Quarto extension. Super exciting to see these in use! 🎉 

If I open a project where a Quarto file was previously opened, the "Preview" button with its label shows up immediately, but the other two new controls take quite a while to show up:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/05c19f77-a5d9-49d6-903a-ccd1d90bd93b

This screen recording was done with a dev build and the delay is ~5 sec. Certainly it will be much less in a release build, but we can expect it to be similar to the experience we currently get with the Posit Publisher extension (>1 sec easily). From my perspective, it feels a bit more disorienting than that example, though, because whole new UI affordances show up quite "late", rather than a single icon.

The current alternative we could use to is to have the UI affordances themselves show up at the same time as the "Preview" button, but then, for example, the checkbox would check _itself_ a second or two later.

- Which is better UX for now, to have the whole UI show up "late" or to have them adjust themselves "late"?
- Do we have any options to have less delay overall for this kind of treatment? (We don't currently know of any.)

Custom Provider is meant to be a generic OpenAI-compatible provider, with BYOK and bring your own OpenAI-compatible baseUrl.

However, umbrella providers may expose models that require different request formats, beyond a more general/less-strict OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions request format.

Some examples:

- Some providers may offer both Anthropic and OpenAI models, but expect requests to the Anthropic models to use the messages API

We should be able to specify which of Chat Completions, Messages, and Responses APIs should be used.

Related: https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/customization/language-models#_add-a-custom-endpoint-model

Perhaps we add a property to the model overrides setting, like apiType, which can be responses, chat-completions, messages, etc., which we then route to the appropriate provider SDK.

title: test and adapt `marimo` support within positron (experimental)
description:
#### Screenshot from dev build. This is just a proof of concept, and any feedback would be highly appreciated!

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/31ec5276-0d2c-44a6-b4a7-5bfa909f15a2

---

### Summary
Add **safe, viewer-pane support** for Marimo notebooks in Positron using **CLI delegation**, without changing Positron’s execution model.

### Problem
- Users encounter Marimo notebooks (`.py` with `import marimo`)
- Positron cannot open them easily
- Users must switch to VS Code or the terminal
  - Depending on how savvy the user is, they may be able to remove the token manually and run the Marimo (already in the current release). 
  - However, this is cumbersome and it'd be better to have a straightforward, pleasant experience. 
- Notebook interactivity is a known gap

### Proposal (Phase 1)
Provide **open-only** support via the Marimo CLI:

**P1** 
Already partially implemented, although extra steps are needed to skip the step of `Cmd+Click` the link in order to open it in the Viewer pane.
- Detect Marimo notebooks
- Open Marimo editor UI in the viewer pane
  (`marimo edit <file>`)

**P2** 
Easy win but not essential, just to enable user to install marimo with a button instead of `pip install`.
- Environment-scoped install guidance (pip/conda)

**P3** 
That could be a nice addition to enable users to convert between `.ipynb` and `.py` files.
- Non-destructive conversion Jupyter ↔ Marimo  
  (`marimo convert ...`)

**P4** 
This would perhaps be the most challenging part, but perhaps high value.
- Run Marimo app (`marimo run <file>`)

### Non-goals (Phase 1)
- Embedded/runtime Marimo execution
- Kernel-managed Marimo
- Native Marimo editor (non-CLI)
- Widget fixes
- VS Code Marimo extension support

### UX & Safety
- Open ≠ Execute (no auto-run)
- Viewer-pane only (also opens in the Editor)
- No file mutation
- Explicit user intent
- Surface CLI errors verbatim

### Acceptance Criteria
- Marimo notebooks open reliably in the viewer pane
- No execution regressions
- No file modification
- Clear user messaging about open-only behavior (run is P3)

title: python: create the no-workspace global venv in `~/.virtualenvs` and ask first
description:
## Problem

When the "Install Python via uv" flow runs with no workspace open, Positron creates a virtual environment at `~/.venv` without asking and without saying where.

Besides being silent overreach into the home directory, `~/.venv` is invisible to environment discovery: we find global venvs by scanning well-known parent directories (`$WORKON_HOME`, `~/.venvs`, `~/.virtualenvs`, `~/.local/share/virtualenvs`, ...) for children, and `~/.venv` is a venv rather than a parent of venvs.

It only appears to work today because the install flow registers the exact interpreter path right after creating it; nothing ever rediscovers it, which is most visible on Windows.

## Proposal

Create the global venv at `$WORKON_HOME/positron`, defaulting to `~/.virtualenvs/positron`, creating the parent directory if needed. Prior art is strong: virtualenvwrapper's default `WORKON_HOME`, pipenv on Windows, and reticulate's `virtualenv_root()` all use `~/.virtualenvs`. The path is identical on all three OSes, and the `positron` directory name gives clear provenance in the interpreter picker.

Ask before creating anything: after Python installs with no workspace open, prompt with a recommended **Open Folder...** action (nudging users toward a project venv) and a secondary **Create Global Environment** action that names the literal path. Dismissing falls back to the base interpreter, as today.

Use the same prompt when the Create Environment command is invoked with no workspace open: recommended **Open Folder...**, secondary **Create Global Environment** delegating to the same uv-backed flow, replacing today's dead-end error.

Hook this same prompt up to the new modal introduced in https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/15458 in workspaceless scenarios too.

title: Reduce the default tree indent from 18px to 16px
description:
## Background

[#2688](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/2688) observed that VS Code's default `workbench.tree.indent` of 8px made the sidebar tree read as too dense, and proposed raising it. [#2705](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/2705) landed that change with a default of 18px.

The direction was right. 8px is genuinely cramped, and the roomier tree has held up well as a Positron characteristic.

## The overshoot

18px is about 2px more than the change needed. The reason it's worth correcting rather than living with is that indent is the one dimension that gets multiplied: the per-level step is paid once for every level of depth, but the panel doesn't get any wider to pay for it.

The evidence in #2688 was all Explorer screenshots, and the Explorer is shallow — three to five levels in ordinary use, where 18px is comfortable. Trees that nest deeper spend a much larger share of a fixed-width sidebar on empty space before the label starts, and at 18px that adds up faster than it should.

This surfaced while looking at indentation complaints in the Data Connections panel, which nests considerably deeper than the Explorer. The bulk of that problem is structural and is being tracked separately; this issue is only about the workbench-wide default being 2px too generous on its own terms.

## The change

Set the default for `workbench.tree.indent` to **16px**.

That is still double upstream's 8px, so it preserves the intent of #2688 — Positron's trees stay noticeably roomier than VS Code's — while trimming the step that every level pays.

## Scope and impact

- Affects every tree in the workbench: Explorer, Search, Debug, SCM, Testing, and any view built on the workbench tree.
- Anyone who has set `workbench.tree.indent` explicitly is unaffected; only the default moves.
- The setting is read live, so the change takes effect without a window reload.
- Nothing in the codebase asserts the old default. The only other references are `explorerViewer.ts`, which reads the setting at runtime, and `settingsSync.test.ts`, which uses an unrelated value as test data.

The change is a single line in the existing Positron block in `src/vs/platform/list/browser/listService.ts`, which already carries the commented-out upstream default for merge-conflict resolution.
