title: python: interpreter resolve loop when two symlinked paths have equal length
description:
When two configured Python interpreter paths point at the same interpreter through symlinks, and the two paths have the same character length, Positron resolves them in an endless alternating loop. Each pass spawns the interpreter. Example:

```
2026-08-19 16:00:59.153 [info] Resolved Python Environment /opt/python/default/bin/python
2026-08-19 16:00:59.211 [info] Resolved Python Environment /opt/python/3.11.13/bin/python
2026-08-19 16:00:59.265 [info] Resolved Python Environment /opt/python/default/bin/python
2026-08-19 16:00:59.323 [info] Resolved Python Environment /opt/python/3.11.13/bin/python
etc....
```

On my machine this runs at about 29 lines per second, with the extension host at about 15% CPU.

This is because two executables that resolve to the same interpreter are deduplicated by keeping the shorter path. The comparison that picks the winner treats the new environment and the existing one as an ordered pair and returns the first on a tie, so the new arrival therefore always wins a tie. This turns into an infinite loop.

The deduplication only runs for paths under the additional environment directories, which include the user-specified interpreter directories. That's why this appears in `/opt/python`, and not everywhere.

We should break the tie deterministically, for example by comparing the paths lexicographically when the lengths are equal. That alone stops the loop.

### Two related faults

These don't cause the reported symptom, but they're in the same code and they also make symlinked paths resolve more than necessary.

- The resolve cache is keyed on the wrong path: the cache is populated with the path that the locator returned, and read with the path that the caller asked about. When those differ, which is normal for an alias path, every lookup misses and spawns the interpreter again.
- A deduplicated path is never cached and never registered: when the check decides to keep the existing environment, it returns nothing. Only successful resolutions are cached, so the losing path stays uncacheable, and registration reports an invalid interpreter path. Returning the surviving environment would be more correct.

title: Data Connections: Support MySQL & MariaDB through ODBC
description:
Originally requested [here](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/discussions/14571#discussioncomment-17625902) by @jrosell

## Expected Outcome: 
1. Provide support for MySQL Driver through ODBC https://www.mysql.com/products/connector/
2. Determine if we can also support MariaDB through the same connector or if we should use the MariaDB connector instead https://mariadb.com/docs/connectors/mariadb-connector-odbc

## Notes
- Posit Pro Driver supports MYSQL https://docs.posit.co/pro-drivers/
- Claude assisted research: "MariaDB was forked from MySQL and maintains strong wire-protocol compatibility, so the standard MySQL ODBC driver (Connector/ODBC from Oracle/MySQL) generally works fine for connecting to MariaDB servers too."

title: Pre-configure Data Connections with available ODBC drivers
description:
> A customer is wondering why their configured ODBC drivers don't appear in the Connections pane in Positron, but do show up in RStudio? Reviewing this article: https://positron.posit.co/connections-pane.html It seems like maybe this is intended? 
> 
> Is there anyway to populate the Connections pane similarly between RStudio and Positron?

I believe Positron needs to respect `odbcinst.ini` and pre-provide connections from the available, configured ODBC Pro drivers, from the start rather than the user having to initiate a connection via the modal dialog.

Context: https://docs.posit.co/ide/server-pro/admin/data_connectivity/connectivity_using_odbc.html

Additionally, it would be nice to support Snippet files: https://docs.posit.co/ide/server-pro/admin/data_connectivity/snippet_files.html

> A Connection Snippet File is an R code snippet with additional metadata which is intended to initialize a connection. This file can be as simple as:
> 
> ```
> library(readr)
> data <- read_csv(readr_example("mtcars.csv"))
> ```
> 
> Once this file is saved under `/etc/rstudio/connections/` as `Motor Trend Cars.R`, RStudio Pro will make this connection as available under the Connection Pane.
> 
> The path is configurable through the `connections-path` environment variable and multiple connection files can be specified.

description:
### Summary

When a Python session is started from an **environment-modules** environment, positron-python probes the interpreter as the bare name `python` instead of the absolute path the module locator found. On any distro without a `python` on the session PATH (e.g. Rocky Linux 9 / EL9, which ship only `python3`), the probe fails with `command not found`, which:

1. makes `getInterpreterInformation()` return nothing, so `implementation` is `undefined`;
2. therefore disables the **bundled ipykernel** (`unsupported interpreter implementation: undefined`);
3. therefore falls through to `_installIpykernel`, whose sqlite3 guard probes with the same bare `python` and also fails;
4. surfacing to the user as **"The Python sqlite3 extension is required but not installed for interpreter: Python 3.12.10 (Module: Python 3.12.10 Module). Missing the system library for SQLite?"**

That message is misleading: sqlite3 is fine, the interpreter is fine, and no system library is missing. `import _sqlite3` succeeds in that environment when run directly.

### Evidence

From `Python Language Pack.log` in a Workbench session on Rocky 9 (interleaved, trimmed):

```
[ModuleEnvironmentLocator] Discovering Python from module environment: Python 3.12.10 Module
[ModuleEnvironmentLocator] Found Python at /root/scratch/python-env/bin/python3 from module environment "Python 3.12.10 Module"
pythonRuntimeDiscoverer: registering runtime for interpreter /root/scratch/python-env/bin/python3 with id 47f9961d24207ee6a5d24a01a6025097
createPythonSession: using module startup command: source "/etc/profile.d/modules.sh" && module load python/3.12.10
createPythonSession: kernelSpec argv: /root/scratch/python-env/bin/python3,.../positron_language_server.py,-f
createPythonSession: creating PythonRuntime
> "python" ".../positron-python/python_files/interpreterInfo.py"
[error] Failed to get interpreter information for 'python' [Error: Command failed: "python" ".../interpreterInfo.py"
/bin/sh: line 1: python: command not found
  code: 127
[info] Not using bundled ipykernel. Reason: unsupported interpreter implementation: undefined
> python -c "import ipykernel; print(ipykernel.__version__)"
> python -c "import _sqlite3"
```

Note the contrast: the locator resolves an **absolute** path, the kernelSpec argv uses the **absolute** path, and the module startup command is known and logged — but the probe uses a bare `python` and applies neither.

The probe originates at [`session.ts` `start()`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/extensions/positron-python/src/client/positron/session.ts#L532):

```ts
const interpreter = await this._interpreterService.getInterpreterDetails(this._pythonPath);
...
await this._setupIpykernel(interpreter, this.kernelSpec);
```

and the bundle is then disabled by the `implementation !== 'cpython'` gate in [`ipykernel.ts`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/extensions/positron-python/src/client/positron/ipykernel.ts#L110). I did not determine whether `_pythonPath` is itself bare or whether `getInterpreterDetails()` returns a bare-path environment — that needs instrumentation in a build.

### Why this is not only a Rocky problem

On Ubuntu the same bare `python` probe **succeeds**, because `/usr/bin/python` exists:

| | bare `python` on the session PATH | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ubuntu 24 | `/usr/bin/python` exists | probe succeeds, bundle used, session starts |
| Rocky 9 | only `python3` | `command not found`, bundle disabled, misleading sqlite3 error |

So on Ubuntu the bundled-ipykernel decision — including the architecture and `cpXY` wheel selection — is made from **a different interpreter than the module's**. It currently works by luck rather than by correctness, and would break the moment the two interpreters differ in version or architecture. Worth fixing on both platforms, not just to unblock EL9.

### Reproduction

1. `npm run pwb -- --os=rocky9 --workbench=daily --positron=daily`
2. `npx playwright test --project e2e-workbench --grep "Python - Create module environment"`

The R half of the same suite (`R - Create module environment`) passes, so this is specific to the Python path.

### Suggested direction

Probe the interpreter using the absolute path from the module locator, and/or apply the module startup command (`source /etc/profile.d/modules.sh && module load <module>`) that `createPythonSession` already has in hand, when running `interpreterInfo.py` and the sqlite3/ipykernel checks.

Independently: the sqlite3 guard's message should probably distinguish "could not run the interpreter" from "sqlite3 is missing", since the former currently reports as the latter.

### Environment

- Positron 2026.09.0-48 (Workbench 2026.08.0+187.pro5), `positron-rocky9:24.18.0`, arm64 local and x64 in CI
- Found by the new `@:workbench-rocky` e2e lane (#15472); reproduces in CI on x86_64 as well as locally on arm64

title: Environment Modules: Modules must be loaded before Python interpreter validation
description:
For a Python interpreter provided by an environment module (Lmod / Tcl "environment modules", `module load ...`), Positron aborts before the kernel ever starts with:

> The Python sqlite3 extension is required but not installed for interpreter: <name>. Missing the system library for SQLite?

The root cause is that the pre-launch validation probes (the ipykernel check and the sqlite3 check) run the interpreter **directly**, without the `module load ...` activation that Positron itself computes for the session. Because the module Python's runtime libraries (e.g. the `_sqlite3` shared library on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`) are only provided once its modules are loaded, `import sqlite3` fails, and the validation gate throws before the kernel is launched.

This contradicts the documented behavior that modules are "loaded before the interpreter is started" (https://positron.posit.co/environment-modules.html).

### Expected behavior

The interpreter validation probes (ipykernel check, sqlite3 check, and the interpreter-info probe) should execute the interpreter through the same environment-module activation that Positron computes for the session, so that a module-provided Python behaves the same during validation as it does at kernel start.

### Actual behavior

The probes invoke the bare interpreter path with only the standard Python-extension environment variables. The environment-module activation is never applied to them, so a module Python whose C extensions (like `_sqlite3`) come from `module load` fails the sqlite3 gate and the session is aborted.

### How Positron handles modules today (for context)

Positron has first-class environment-module support:

- At **discovery** time, `positron-environment-modules` computes a startup command of the form `source "<init-script>" && module load <mod1> && module load <mod2> ...` and stores it as `moduleMetadata.startupCommand` on the runtime metadata. Discovery probes (`which python`, `python --version`) correctly run **with** modules loaded.
- At **kernel launch**, Positron applies that startup command: `session.ts` sets `kernelSpec.startup_command = extraData.moduleMetadata.startupCommand`, and the supervisor (`KallichoreSession`) runs it in a login shell before spawning the interpreter. So the kernel-launch path **does** load the modules correctly.

The gap is only in the pre-launch validation probes, which do not use `startupCommand` at all.

### Root cause / code pointers

The validation gate runs in `start()` before the kernel is spawned:

- `extensions/positron-python/src/client/positron/session.ts`
  - `start()` -> `_setupIpykernel()` -> `_installIpykernel()`.
  - Inside `_installIpykernel()`:
    - ipykernel check: `this._installer.isProductVersionCompatible(Product.ipykernel, ...)` (~line 418)
    - sqlite3 check that throws the error: `this._installer.isInstalled(Product.sqlite3, interpreter)` (~line 427-432)
  - This runs before the kernel is launched with `startup_command` further down in `start()`, so the module activation is never applied to these checks.

- The probes ultimately spawn the interpreter directly:
  - `common/installer/productInstaller.ts` (`isInstalled` / `getProductSemVer`, module branch) -> `IPythonExecutionFactory.createActivatedEnvironment`.
  - `common/process/pythonEnvironment.ts` (`isModuleInstalled` runs `python -c "import sqlite3"`; `getModuleVersion` runs `python -c "import ipykernel; print(ipykernel.__version__)"`) via a direct `spawn(pythonPath, args)`.
  - The environment for these spawns comes from `interpreter/activation/service.ts` (`getActivatedEnvironmentVariables`), which only understands conda / venv / pyenv / pixi activation. It has **no** `module load` support; it just inherits the current process env or the `.env` custom vars. The precomputed `moduleMetadata.startupCommand` is never consulted here.

- A related bare probe: `extensions/positron-python/src/client/positron/ipykernel.ts` (`getIpykernelBundle` -> `getInterpreterInformation`) also spawns `interpreter.path` directly with no module activation.


### Suggested fix

Make the interpreter validation probes (ipykernel check, sqlite3 check, and the interpreter-info probe) run through the same module activation used at kernel launch, i.e. execute the interpreter under the computed `moduleMetadata.startupCommand` (login shell) rather than spawning the bare interpreter path. Equivalently, feed the module startup command into the activation-environment computation for module-typed interpreters so the probes and the kernel see the same environment.

### Notes

- Environment modules are Linux-only in Positron (macOS/Windows are explicitly unsupported), so this affects Linux HPC-style deployments.
- Related existing issue for the sqlite3 gate: posit-dev/positron#4698.

title: positron-commands skill: layout commands
description:
Part of #15343.

## Description

Give Assistant the layout commands: the reference file that documents the three named workbench layouts and when to pick each one.

## Commands

| Command ID | Agent-compatible in | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workbench.action.positronFourPaneDataScienceLayout` | #14969 | Done |
| `workbench.action.positronTwoPaneDataScienceLayout` | #14969 | Done |
| `workbench.action.positronNotebookLayout` | #14969 | Done |

See #15063 for the full command list and its current state.

## Notes

- All three are already agent-compatible, so this issue is documentation only.
- All three take no arguments, return no value, and have no preconditions. Each is a full layout swap rather than an incremental change, so they are mutually exclusive with each other but fine to follow with a focus command. The spike has usable prose for all three.
- The value here is the "when to use it" guidance, which the command metadata does not carry. Four-pane is the general-purpose default; two-pane is for comparing code against variables and plots side by side; notebook hides the console to give a single notebook more room.
- Metadata source: see the parent issue for the open question about generating reference content from `positron.ai.showAgentAllowedCommands` rather than hand-copying it.

title: Extension install fails with `Server returned 403` when an HTTP proxy denies the gallery host, even though the host is listed in `NO_PROXY` / `http.noProxy` (Positron Pro on Workbench)
description:
## System details:

#### Positron and OS details:

```
Positron Pro 2025.12.2 (build 5)
Code - OSS Version: 1.106.0
Posit Workbench 2026.01.0+392.pro5
OS: RHEL 9.6 (x86_64), standalone VM, Local Job Launcher
Session type: browser-based Positron Pro session (positron-server)
```

The behavior above was reported by the administrator of the affected deployment. We have not
reproduced it on a Posit-side test system; the files involved appear unchanged between the tag
matching this build and current `main`, but we have not verified a newer build empirically.

#### Session details:

Not interpreter-specific; occurs before any interpreter interaction, on a fresh session with no
extensions installed.

## Describe the issue:

In a Positron Pro session on Workbench, with `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` present in the environment
and a corporate proxy that returns **403** for the extension gallery host:

- Browsing and searching the extension gallery **works**.
- Installing any extension **fails immediately** with:

  ```
  Server returned 403
      at ExtensionGalleryServiceWithNoStorageService2.getManifest
      (installGalleryExtensions → checkAndGetCompatibleVersion → getManifest)
  ```

The gallery host is listed in `NO_PROXY`/`no_proxy` at the OS level, and `curl` from inside the same
session honors that and reaches the gallery host successfully. Adding `http.noProxy` for the same
host — both as an administrator-seeded default for all sessions and in individual user settings —
does not change the behavior. The failure is deterministic: it recurs after a Workbench restart and
in a brand-new session.


## Steps to reproduce the issue:

Two parts: what the administrator actually did in the affected deployment, and a self-contained
recipe we believe should reproduce it on a clean host. It is
written from the reported symptoms plus source reading, and the outcomes in it are predictions, not
observations.

### As reported in the affected deployment

1. Configure a self-hosted VS Code extensions gallery and point sessions at it with
   `EXTENSIONS_GALLERY` in `/etc/rstudio/launcher-env`.
2. Have all outbound traffic forced through a corporate proxy that returns 403 for that gallery
   host, with the proxy variables set system-wide and in the `rstudio-server` service environment,
   and the gallery host present in `NO_PROXY`/`no_proxy` at every layer.
3. Restart Workbench, open a fresh Positron Pro session, search the Extensions pane (returns
   results), then install an extension.

Reported result: install fails immediately with the `Server returned 403` / `getManifest` error.
Reported controls from the same host: `curl --noproxy '*'` to the gallery and asset URLs returns
200; the same `curl` forced through the proxy returns 403; a plain Node `https.get()` returns 200.
Adding `http.noProxy` for the gallery host changed nothing.

### Self-contained recipe (untested by us)

Needs one Linux host with Workbench + Positron Pro and outbound internet. Uses `open-vsx.org` as the
gallery so no private infrastructure is involved.

1. Install a forward proxy that denies the gallery host and allows everything else:

   ```bash
   sudo dnf install -y squid
   sudo tee /etc/squid/squid.conf >/dev/null <<'EOF'
   http_port 3128
   acl gallery dstdomain open-vsx.org
   http_access deny gallery
   http_access allow all
   EOF
   sudo systemctl enable --now squid
   ```

2. Confirm the two control paths, which should show 200 direct and 403 through the proxy:

   ```bash
   curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'direct:  %{http_code}\n' --noproxy '*' https://open-vsx.org/
   curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'proxied: %{http_code}\n' -x http://localhost:3128 https://open-vsx.org/
   ```

3. Attempt an install with the gallery host present in `no_proxy`:

   ```bash
   env HTTP_PROXY=http://localhost:3128 HTTPS_PROXY=http://localhost:3128 \
       NO_PROXY=open-vsx.org no_proxy=open-vsx.org \
     /usr/lib/rstudio-server/bin/positron-server/bundled/bin/positron-server \
       --install-extension redhat.vscode-yaml \
       --extensions-dir /tmp/repro-exts --user-data-dir /tmp/repro-udd --log trace
   ```

   Expected if this matches the reported behavior: the install fails carrying the proxy's 403,
   despite `no_proxy` covering the host.

4. Re-run the identical command with only `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` removed, keeping `no_proxy`.
   Expected: the install succeeds.

We chose the CLI form because `--install-extension` appears to construct the same
`RequestService('remote')` and `ExtensionGalleryServiceWithNoStorageService` as the in-session
install (`src/vs/server/node/remoteExtensionHostAgentCli.ts`), which would make it a smaller
reproducer than driving the UI — but that equivalence is also inferred from source rather than
tested, so the UI path in the reported-deployment section above is the authoritative symptom.

## Expected or desired behavior:

Hosts listed in `NO_PROXY`/`no_proxy` (and/or in `http.noProxy`) are not routed through the proxy by
the extension gallery request path — or, if that is not the intent, some supported way to exempt the
gallery host, and documentation stating that the bypass variables do not apply here. Today an
administrator whose proxy denies the gallery host appears to have no in-product configuration that
makes gallery installs work.

## Were there any error messages in the UI, Output panel, or Developer Tools console?

The UI error is the `Server returned 403` / `getManifest` message quoted above.

A `Server` output-channel trace (`Developer: Set Log Level…` → `Server` → `Trace`) has been
requested from the reporting administrator and is not yet captured.

## Observations that may be relevant

Offered as triage context, not as a conclusion. Items 1-4 are reported by the administrator of the
affected deployment; item 5 is our own reading of the source; items 6-7 are inferences from that
reading and are not confirmed by observation.

1. **Search works while install fails** — search results render normally in the same session in which
   the install fails, suggesting the query and the install may not take the same network path.
2. **The same URLs are reachable from the same host** — `curl --noproxy '*'` and a plain Node
   `https.get()` both returned 200 for the gallery and asset URLs; only the in-product install fails.
   Forcing the same `curl` through the proxy returned 403, so the 403 text is consistent with what
   the proxy returns for that host.
3. **The bypass variables are present and effective for other clients** — `env | grep -i proxy`
   inside the session shows the gallery host in `no_proxy`, and `curl` in that same session honors
   it.
4. **`http.noProxy` made no difference** at either settings layer tried (administrator-seeded
   defaults for all sessions, and individual user settings).
5. **Source reading we did while triaging, which may or may not be pertinent:**
   - `src/vs/platform/request/node/proxy.ts` — `getSystemProxyURI()` reads `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY`
     (and lowercase) and `getProxyAgent()` returns an agent whenever a proxy URL is found; we did not
     find a bypass-list check on this path.
   - `src/vs/platform/request/node/requestService.ts` — `configure()` reads `http.proxy`,
     `http.proxyStrictSSL`, and `http.proxyAuthorization`; we did not find a read of `http.noProxy`
     here.
   - `git grep -i no_proxy -- src/` returns a single hit, in
     `src/vs/platform/windows/electron-main/windowImpl.ts` (Electron main process). `http.noProxy`
     additionally appears in `src/vs/workbench/api/node/proxyResolver.ts`, which covers extension-host
     requests.
   - `src/vs/server/node/serverServices.ts` registers `ExtensionGalleryServiceWithNoStorageService`
     and a `RequestService('remote', …)` in the server container.
   - These files look the same at `main` as at the tag matching the affected build, so we do not
     expect a newer Positron to behave differently — though we would be glad to be wrong about that.
6. **The failure appears to involve two requests, not one.** Consistent with `getAsset` retrying
   against the fallback asset URI when the primary request fails, and with the gallery in use
   publishing an identical fallback URI. Worth knowing when reading a trace log so the pair is not
   misread as two separate attempts.
7. **`RequestService.request()` resolves the login shell environment and merges it over
   `process.env`.** The administrator's attempt to clear the proxy variables only in Workbench's
   session-launch configuration did not change the behavior; we have not confirmed which layer
   re-supplied them, and this merge is one candidate. Mentioning it because it may affect how you
   reproduce.

## Questions for triage

1. Is the extension gallery request path intended to honor `NO_PROXY`/`no_proxy` or `http.noProxy`?
   If not, is that documented anywhere we should be pointing administrators at?
2. Is there a supported way today for an administrator to exempt the gallery host from the proxy for
   Positron Pro sessions, short of removing the proxy variables from the whole machine?
3. Are VS Code (code-server) sessions on Workbench expected to behave the same way? **Untested** —
   the reporting administrator has only exercised Positron Pro sessions.

## Possibly related

- Upstream, appears to describe the same behavior in the same function, filed against VS Code Server:
  <https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/147595> (open, Backlog).
- Upstream feature request for a bypass setting: <https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/200464>
  (open, Backlog).
- Previous Positron issues in a similar class, all closed and all scoped to localhost rather than an
  arbitrary host, listed only for context:
  <https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/5481>,
  <https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/8426>,
  <https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/11270>.

## Impact

An enterprise deployment where all outbound traffic is forced through a corporate proxy that denies
internal hosts. With a self-hosted extension gallery on such a host, no user can install any
extension from the Extensions pane; the administrator's available options are all outside the
product (proxy allowlist change, or pre-installing extensions from `.vsix`). The extension gallery in
this case is housed in Posit Package Manager.

title: Positron Pro session quit from Workbench home page produces Error pods and Failed Jobs
description:
A normal user quit of a Positron Pro session from the Posit Workbench home page produces a session pod with status `Error` and a Kubernetes Job marked `Failed`. Quitting an RStudio Pro session from the same path on the same Workbench produces pod `Completed` / Job `Complete`. A normal exit should not produce Error pods or Failed Jobs.

## Impact

- Reported by at least two customers (one open support escalation, one direct meeting with a customer).
- Failed K8s Jobs are preventing nodes from being drained from the cluster, which is blocking a customer rollout to production Workbench.
- A customer is also seeing the same failure mode on **VS Code Pro** sessions, not only Positron Pro. Worth checking against the earlier Jupyter / VS Code graceful-exit parity work (rstudio/rstudio-pro#5317, Workbench 2024.09.0): either that fix did not fully land for VS Code at this customer's version, or there is a separate regression.

## Environment

- Posit Workbench 2026.01
- RHEL 8, Kubernetes launcher
- Customer reproduced side by side with `kubectl get pods | grep <user>`

## What `kubectl describe pod` shows on the Positron path

- Failing container: `pwb-supervisor`
- Exit Code: 143 (128 + SIGTERM)
- Reason: `Error`
- Restart Count: 0
- Session ran cleanly for 27 minutes; only went non-zero at termination.

The supervisor on the Positron path is not trapping the K8s termination signal back to a clean exit, where on the RStudio path it does.

## Related prior work

- Original RStudio supervisor fix: rstudio/rstudio#12594
- Follow-up: rstudio/rstudio-pro#4719
- Graceful-exit parity for Jupyter / VS Code: rstudio/rstudio-pro#5317 (Workbench 2024.09.0)
- Tightening for RStudio: rstudio/rstudio-pro#10167 (Workbench 2026.04.0)
- No equivalent Positron parity entry

Aaron notes the 2023 fix is only vaguely related to current behavior since IDE signal handling and home-page termination behavior have changed since then.

## Open question on where the fix lives

Possibly both, possibly one:

1. **Supervisor layer (rstudio-pro):** have `pwb-supervisor` trap SIGTERM and exit 0 for Positron sessions, the way it does for RStudio. The customer VS Code data point suggests this layer may not be fully fixed across IDEs either.
2. **Positron product layer (this repo):** provide an in-session quit command so users can exit cleanly without going through the home-page Terminate button that fires SIGTERM, and / or have Positron Pro handle SIGTERM gracefully so a clean exit propagates regardless of how the user quits.

## Artifacts

Customer has provided `kubectl describe pod` output and launcher logs (most directly relevant to the supervisor-layer investigation) in a support ticket (see [Slack](https://positpbc.slack.com/archives/C07NG5GJ2EA/p1779380150647879)).

title: positron-commands skill: diagnostics and help commands
description:
Part of #15343.

## Description

Give Assistant the diagnostic and help commands: showing startup diagnostics when an interpreter will not start or does not appear, rediscovering installed interpreters, and looking up a help topic for a function or symbol.

## Commands

| Command ID | Agent-compatible in | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `positron.startupDiagnostics.show` | #14969 | Done |
| `workbench.action.language.runtime.discoverAllRuntimes` | #14969 | Done |
| `positron.help.lookupHelpTopic` | #15140 | Done |

See #15063 for the full command list and its current state.

## Notes

- `lookupHelpTopic` takes an optional `topic` argument (#15140). A non-empty string shows that topic directly; omitting it, or passing an empty or non-string value, falls back to the input box. The reference file should say that leaving it out prompts the user, which is rarely what Assistant wants.
- `lookupHelpTopic` requires a running interpreter session for the language, and it picks the language from the active editor or the foreground session. The reference file needs to spell that out, since the model cannot tell from the ID whether it needs a session first.
- `discoverAllRuntimes` takes no arguments and returns nothing. It is the first thing to try when a user says an interpreter they just installed is missing, so the reference file should point at it before startup diagnostics.
- This area is about answering "why isn't my interpreter working", so the reference file should read as a sequence (run diagnostics, read the result, then act) rather than an unordered command list.
- Metadata source: see the parent issue for the open question about generating reference content from `positron.ai.showAgentAllowedCommands` rather than hand-copying it.

title: Assistant: detect Workbench managed Databricks credentials
description:
Claude-generated summary below. May need adjustments.

## Context

Follow-on to #8612. Databricks is now a first-class provider (PAT, OAuth U2M, OAuth M2M), but on Posit Workbench a user who already has Databricks managed credentials selected for their session still has to sign in again inside Positron. They shouldn't have to: Workbench already holds a working, auto-refreshing credential for that workspace.

[Workbench managed Databricks credentials](https://docs.posit.co/ide/server-pro/user/posit-workbench/managed-credentials/databricks.html) follow the [Databricks client unified authentication](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/auth/unified-auth) spec. In a session with a managed credential selected, Workbench sets:

- `DATABRICKS_HOST` -- the workspace host
- `DATABRICKS_CONFIG_FILE` -- path to a managed `.databrickscfg` holding a `workbench` profile with short-lived OAuth tokens

The tokens refresh automatically while the session stays alive, so we need to read them per request rather than capture one at sign-in.

## What we have today

- `DATABRICKS_HOST` already lands in the resolved catalog as `providers.databricks.databricks.host` (`ai-lib/packages/ai-config/src/connection-env.ts:83`), so the host comes for free in a Workbench session.
- On the credential side, only the PAT path is env-aware: `DATABRICKS_TOKEN` (`ai-lib/packages/ai-credentials/src/store-backend/providerEnvMappings.ts:80`). OAuth U2M/M2M grants live in `ai-lib/packages/ai-credentials/src/databricks-oauth.ts`.
- Nothing anywhere reads `DATABRICKS_CONFIG_FILE` or a `.databrickscfg` profile.
- Auth-method picker in Posit Assistant is `oauth-u2m | oauth-m2m | api-key` (`packages/standalone/src/client/components/auth/databricksAuthMethod.ts`); there's no managed/ambient option.

Closest precedent is Snowflake, where `snowflake.home` (from `SNOWFLAKE_HOME`) points credential discovery at Workbench's managed `connections.toml`. Databricks wants the same shape, with a config file plus profile name instead of a directory. The AWS SSO refresh work in #9652 is the precedent for keeping a short-lived credential fresh.

## User journey

1. User launches a Workbench session and selects Databricks managed credentials.
2. Positron starts. Databricks shows up as an available provider with no sign-in prompt, and the workspace host is already filled in from `DATABRICKS_HOST`.
3. Databricks models appear in the chat model picker.
4. The session runs past the lifetime of a single token; chat keeps working because the credential is re-read from the managed config file.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Databricks credential discovery reads `DATABRICKS_CONFIG_FILE` (falling back to `~/.databrickscfg`) and resolves the OAuth token from the `workbench` profile, honouring `DATABRICKS_CONFIG_PROFILE` when set.
2. The resolved connection carries enough non-secret detail (config file path, profile name) to show the user which credential is in play; the token itself is never written to `providers.json`.
3. In a Workbench session with a managed credential, the Databricks provider auto-configures: no PAT entry, no OAuth browser round-trip, no "Reload Window" (see #10831).
4. The token is re-read on each request (or on 401) rather than cached at sign-in, so automatic refresh mid-session is picked up.
5. Managed credentials take precedence over a stored PAT for the same workspace, with a clear indication of which one is being used.
6. Explicit user config still wins: a user who deliberately signs in with a PAT or OAuth isn't overridden by the ambient credential.
7. Graceful degradation: config file missing, profile absent, or token expired and unrefreshable falls back to the normal sign-in flow with a useful message, not a silent failure.

## Open questions

- Do managed credential tokens carry the scopes needed for `serving-endpoints` / AI Gateway model serving, or only for SQL warehouses and Unity Catalog? Needs testing against a real Workbench + Databricks setup (see #11707 for dev environment access).
- Should Desktop get the same treatment? Reading a local `~/.databrickscfg` profile is the same unified-auth spec and would cover users who already ran `databricks auth login`. Worth deciding whether that's in scope here or a separate issue.
- Does the host from `DATABRICKS_HOST` reliably resolve to the right chat endpoint for both `serving-endpoints` and AI Gateway deployments (the distinction from #13421)?
- Should this land in ai-lib as a credential source (so the TUI and standalone Assistant get it too), or only on the Positron path?

## Related

Assistant:

- #8612 -- parent: Support Databricks/Mosaic hosted LLMs
- #13421 -- closed: `serving-endpoints` vs AI Gateway base URL for Databricks
- #9652 -- closed: AWS SSO credential refresh flow, precedent for refreshing short-lived credentials
- #10179 -- closed: detect AWS credentials and register Bedrock automatically, precedent for ambient credential detection
- #11707 -- closed: dev environment with custom Workbench auth

Connections / Catalog Explorer (same managed credential, different consumer -- worth coordinating so we read it the same way):

- #11543 -- Epic: Pickup managed credentials for Catalog Explorer (lists Databricks)
- #14959 -- Databricks in Data Connections; AC 5 is the Workbench managed credentials case
- #14666 -- Detect Workbench managed Snowflake credentials (the pattern we're following, plus the "too many auth steps" feedback)
- #14776 -- Detect Workbench managed AWS credentials for Redshift
- #12105 -- Databricks credentials not persisted across sessions
- #13107 -- Databricks connections beyond PAT (hostname / HTTP path)

title: Assistant: complete Databricks provider support
description:
## Context

Follow-on to #8612. The Databricks provider shipped experimental in 2026.08 (#14898, posit-dev/assistant#1809, posit-dev/ai-lib#15) with personal access token (PAT) sign-in. Several authentication methods and credential-handling behaviors are still missing.

## Gaps

* Enable OAuth U2M on desktop - the code currently exists, but is not user accessible. We need a way to support multiple auth methods via the modal.

* Detect Workbench Managed Credentials, tracked in https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/15263

* Support `DATABRICKS_TOKEN` and `DATABRICKS_HOST` from the environment so an exported token signs the user in without manual entry.

* Fall back through ports 8020-8040 during OAuth sign-in, matching the Databricks CLI, so a second Positron window can sign in while the first holds 8020.

* Bind `::1` alongside `127.0.0.1` so the OAuth loopback redirect resolves on macOS.

* Discover the OAuth endpoints from `/oidc/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`, rejecting endpoints outside the workspace origin and falling back to the hardcoded `/oidc/v1/*` paths on any failure, so workspaces that front OAuth elsewhere sign in without regressing ones that work today.

* Refresh on a 401 from the model call, not just on the stored expiry, so a token revoked before it expires recovers without the user signing in again.

## Acceptance criteria

1. On desktop, a user can choose between OAuth and API Key in the provider dialog and sign in with either.
2. On server, Databricks authenticates from Workbench managed credentials without a manual token (#15263).
3. `DATABRICKS_TOKEN` and `DATABRICKS_HOST` in the environment configure the provider without manual entry.
4. Concurrent Positron windows can both complete OAuth sign-in.
5. A token revoked before expiry recovers on the next request, and the user is signed out only when the refresh grant is also dead.

## Related

- #8612 -- parent: Support Databricks/Mosaic hosted LLMs
- #15263 -- Workbench managed Databricks credentials
- #15257 -- [EPIC] 2026.09 AI Providers & Auth
- #13421 -- closed: `serving-endpoints` vs AI Gateway base URL

title: Create the positron-commands skill
description:
## Description

Depends on #15341 and #15342 for the plumbing that gets the skill to Assistant.

Ship a skill in Positron that teaches Posit Assistant which Positron commands exist, what arguments they take, and when to use each one.

Keep this to one skill with multiple reference files, not a skill per area. `SKILL.md` stays short and routes to the right file; the command IDs, arguments, return values, and preconditions live in the reference files, so the model loads only the area it needs.

## Shape

From the spike on [`feature/positron-platform-skills-spike`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/tree/feature/positron-platform-skills-spike):

- `skills/positron-commands/SKILL.md` -- how to call a command with the `positronCommand` tool, how to read a `disabled` or `not-found` failure, and an index pointing at the reference files
- `skills/positron-commands/references/*.md` -- one file per area
- `agentSkillDrift.vitest.ts` -- a test that fails when a command ID named in a reference file no longer exists in Positron

The commands themselves are being made agent-invokable in #15063. Each sub-issue below covers one area and links the PR that did the command work.

## Open question: getting command metadata into the reference files

This applies to every sub-issue, so deciding it once here is better than five times. How do we get a command's metadata into its reference file without hand-copying it?

Positron already has `positron.ai.showAgentAllowedCommands`, a command that dumps JSON for every command flagged `agentCompatible` (see `src/vs/workbench/contrib/positronAiFeatures/`). It has the IDs, descriptions, argument shapes, and preconditions, so it is a reasonable source. Options:

- generate the reference files from that JSON
- generate the mechanical parts, hand-write the prose around them
- hand-write everything and rely on the drift test to catch staleness

The spike hand-wrote its files, and its `references/ui.md` shows why the JSON alone is not enough. The pane focus commands have auto-generated descriptions ("Focus on Variables View") that say nothing about when to use them. Their single argument is reported as required even though every property inside it is optional, so a literal reading of the metadata sends the model down the wrong path. Whatever we choose needs room for hand-written guidance layered on the generated facts.

## AC

- [ ] `SKILL.md` with calling conventions, failure handling, and a reference file index
- [ ] Reference files covering the five areas in the sub-issues below
- [ ] A decision on generated vs hand-written metadata, written down somewhere durable
- [ ] Drift test covering every command ID the skill names

title: e2e: Revert bqplot pin once upstream publishes matching bqplot@>=0.6.1 JS package
description:
## Context

We pinned `bqplot` to `<0.13` in [posit-dev/qa-example-content/requirements.txt](https://github.com/posit-dev/qa-example-content/blob/main/requirements.txt) because `bqplot` Python 0.13.0/0.13.1 (released 2026-05-04 / 2026-05-07) bumped `__frontend_version__` to `^0.6.1`, but the corresponding `bqplot` JS package on npm is still at 0.6.0. Widget rendering fails with `Error: Script error for "bqplot"` because the CDN 404s on `bqplot@^0.6.1/dist/index.js`.

Original failure: run [25563686640](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/actions/runs/25563686640) (Windows e2e, `Verify bqplot Python widget`).

## How to verify upstream is fixed

Run all three checks. The pin can be removed when **all** pass.

1. **npm has a matching version published:**
   ```bash
   curl -s https://registry.npmjs.org/bqplot | jq '."dist-tags".latest'
   ```
   Expect `0.6.1` or higher.

2. **CDN serves the version specifier the latest Python package uses:**
   ```bash
   PY_VER=$(curl -s https://pypi.org/pypi/bqplot/json | jq -r .info.version)
   WHEEL=$(curl -s https://pypi.org/pypi/bqplot/$PY_VER/json | jq -r '.urls[] | select(.packagetype=="bdist_wheel") | .url')
   curl -sL "$WHEEL" -o /tmp/bqplot.whl
   FRONTEND=$(unzip -p /tmp/bqplot.whl bqplot/_version.py | grep -oE "'[^']+'" | tail -1)
   echo "Frontend version: $FRONTEND"
   curl -sI "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bqplot@$FRONTEND/dist/index.js" | head -1
   ```
   Expect `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`.

3. **End-to-end smoke:** Install latest `bqplot` in a fresh env, run the bqplot example from [test/e2e/tests/plots/plots.test.ts](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/test/e2e/tests/plots/plots.test.ts), confirm `.svg-figure` renders without the broken-image / "Click to show javascript error" placeholder.

## Action when fixed

- Remove the `bqplot` pin from `qa-example-content/requirements.txt`
- Re-run the Positron Windows e2e suite to confirm `Verify bqplot Python widget` passes
- Close this issue

## Upstream tracking

bqplot version-bump issue: https://github.com/bqplot/bqplot/issues (file if not already tracked)

title: Port the Workbench and remote SSH assistant sign-in e2e tests to the new provider modal
description:
## Describe the issue

Two e2e suites sign in to a model provider by driving the old "Configure Language Model Providers" dialog. Neither has an equivalent that goes through the new modal (the one behind the hidden `assistant.newProviderModal` setting).

| Suite | Providers | Tag |
|---|---|---|
| `test/e2e/tests/workbench/posit-assistant/posit-assistant-signin.test.ts` | anthropic, openai, posit-ai | `@:workbench` |
| `test/e2e/tests/remote-ssh/remote-ssh-assistant.test.ts` | anthropic | `@:remote-ssh` |

The desktop suite is already covered on both modals. #15109 added `posit-assistant-signin-new-modal.test.ts`, which mirrors `posit-assistant/posit-assistant-signin.test.ts` against the new modal. These two were left out because each needs setup the desktop suite doesn't, and each runs in its own CI job.

## Why this needs doing

When the new modal becomes the default, these two suites stop testing the path users take. They either fail outright, because their selectors belong to the old dialog, or they pass while exercising a dialog no user sees.

Both cover something the desktop suite can't:

- The Workbench suite runs against Posit Workbench, where the provider list, the credential store, and the network egress to the model all live in the container's server-side extension host.
- The remote SSH suite signs in on the client and chats against a remote host, so the same three things live on the remote machine. This is the class of gap that hid a missing `ai-config` module on the remote SSH server until a sign-in test ran there (#15306).

## What to do

Add a new-modal suite next to each existing one rather than converting them in place. While the setting is still off by default, both modals ship, so both need coverage. Once the new modal becomes the default, the old-modal versions can be deleted.

Follow the pattern in `posit-assistant-signin-new-modal.test.ts` and swap `app.workbench.modelProviderAuth` for `app.workbench.modelProviderModal`. The `ModelProviderModal` page object from #15109 exposes the same `loginModelProvider` / `logoutModelProvider` surface, and it reaches remote windows for free: `sshWorkbench` is a full `Workbench` built by `createWorkbenchFromPage`, so it picks up the new page object from the constructor.

Three things that are not copy-paste:

- **Turning the setting on inside the Workbench container.** Docker-based apps read settings from the container, not from the host file the `settings` fixture writes (see the comment on `copyUserSettingsToContainer` in `test/e2e/fixtures/test-setup/docker-utils.ts`). No test under `tests/workbench/` calls `settings.set` today. This needs either a new `test.use` option threaded through `dockerSettingsOverrides`, following how `enableFoundryAssistant` works, or a `docker cp` in `beforeAll` like the suite already does for `providers.json`.
- **The Workbench suite reloads the window in `beforeAll`**, to make the server pick up `providers.json` deterministically. The desktop new-modal suite had to stop reloading: on reload the extension host re-probes cloud metadata endpoints that are unreachable in the CI container, and the resulting DNS stall makes the modal's key validation abort on its fixed 5-second budget. Whether the Workbench container hits the same stall is unknown, and the reload there is not optional.
- **The Workbench `providers.json` setup is about 40 lines of `beforeAll` and `afterAll`.** Extract it into a shared helper rather than copying it into the new file.

## Notes on scoping

Doing both together is cheaper than splitting them. Verifying either one in CI means adding `@:workbench` and `@:remote-ssh` to the PR's tag line, which triggers two container builds plus two e2e lanes, and that is most of the cost either way.

Related: #14818, #14947

title: Consider a selection background tint for HC Dark lists (list.inactiveSelectionBackground is null in hcDark
description:
## Context

While fixing the invisible active console session tab in Dark High Contrast
(#15405), we noticed an asymmetry in the upstream list color defaults
(`src/vs/platform/theme/common/colors/listColors.ts`):

```ts
export const listInactiveSelectionBackground = registerColor('list.inactiveSelectionBackground',
	{ dark: '#37373D', light: '#E4E6F1', hcDark: null, hcLight: Color.fromHex('#0F4A85').transparent(0.1) },
```

HC Light gets a subtle 10% tint for inactive selection; HC Dark gets nothing.
Any component that (reasonably) uses list.inactiveSelectionBackground as a
selection cue is invisible in HC Dark unless it also implements the outline
convention. [#15405](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/15405) fixed the console session tabs with a contrastActiveBorder
outline, but the question of whether HC Dark should also get a background tint
was deferred to this issue (raised in review).

### Why this wasn't just fixed in [#15405](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/15405)
The null appears deliberate rather than an oversight:

It has been hcDark: null since before Positron forked (already null in our
2022-05-24 history import) and is unchanged upstream since.
It was left null in the very edit that introduced hcLight with a tint --
the hc -> hcDark/hcLight split touched this exact registration, so the
author chose null for HC Dark while giving HC Light a value.
HC Dark's design language conveys list state with outlines only
(contrastActiveBorder / list.focusOutline); HC Light was designed later
with a tint system layered on top of outlines.
Changing the default would also:

Affect every list/tree in the workbench for HC Dark users (explorer, search,
quick picks, ...), not one component -- it's a theme-wide design decision.
Require editing an upstream file (listColors.ts), a permanent
merge-conflict liability for something upstream arguably owns.

### Options
1. Do nothing -- keep the outline-only convention for HC Dark; components
must implement outlines (as [#15405](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/15405) does). Users who want a tint can set:

```json
"workbench.colorCustomizations": {
    "[Dark High Contrast]": {
        "list.inactiveSelectionBackground": "#ffffff1a"
    }
}
```

2. Propose the change upstream (microsoft/vscode) -- e.g.
hcDark: Color.white.transparent(0.1) to mirror HC Light -- and inherit it
through a future merge. Keeps us aligned and puts the accessibility design
question in front of the theme owners.

3. Positron-local override -- set the value in our fork. Fastest, but the
merge-liability and design-ownership concerns above apply.
Recommendation: decide with design/accessibility input; if we want the tint,
option 2 first.

description:
## Description

When setting up a Databricks connection via the Connections Pane, the entered credentials (e.g. host, HTTP path, token) are not saved between sessions. Each time a new session is started, the fields must be filled in again from scratch.

## Steps to reproduce

- Open the Connections Pane and create a new Databricks connection
- Enter credentials (host, HTTP path, auth token)
- Close and reopen Positron / start a new session
- Open the Connections Pane → credentials are gone

## Expected behavior
Credentials (or at least non-sensitive fields like host and HTTP path) should be pre-filled from the previous session.

=> ideally the credential information could also be stored in a safe way (e.g. keyring or similar).

Auth method used:PAT / OAuth U2M

title: "Configure Language Model Providers" does not hide disabled local providers
description:
`POSIT_AI_PROVIDERS_ENFORCED` marks a provider disabled via `providers.<id>.enabled: false`, and the provider dialog respects that for `anthropic` — the button disappears. With `lmstudio` and `ollama` disabled the same way, their buttons are still rendered.

Hiding appears to be intended behavior: #14817 specifies "Hide providers according to settings" for the built-in provider list. Flagging in case `lmstudio`/`ollama` are a deliberate carve-out.

Positron `2026.08.0` build `331` (VS Code `1.124.0`, commit `a3a370d418`).

## Reproduction

Launch Positron from a shell with:

```bash
export POSIT_AI_PROVIDERS_ENFORCED='{"providers":{"lmstudio":{"enabled":false},"ollama":{"enabled":false}}}'
```

Command Palette → `Positron Assistant: Configure Language Model Providers`.

- **Observed**: LM Studio and Ollama both still listed.
- **Expected**: neither offered, matching `anthropic` behavior.

For the contrast, swap the fragment for `{"providers":{"anthropic":{"enabled":false}}}` — the Anthropic button is reliably absent from the same dialog.

## Impact

Low if intentional. If not: an administrator disabling a local provider still sees it offered, and users can attempt to configure a provider that policy forbids. Both are unauthenticated local endpoints, so no credential is exposed — the concern is policy display, not access.

title: Add positron.ai.getAgentSkillRoots() so Positron can ship skill files to Assistant
description:
## Description

Add an extension API that tells Posit Assistant where Positron keeps the skill files it ships. Assistant calls it, scans those directories, and treats what it finds as trusted. Something like:

```ts
positron.ai.getAgentSkillRoots(): string[]
```

The Assistant half is #15341, the fourth skill source and the trust rules. The skill this API points at is #15343.

## The spike

Branch [`feature/positron-platform-skills-spike`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/tree/feature/positron-platform-skills-spike). It adds `getAgentSkillRoots()` to `positron.d.ts` and implements it in the extension host:

- `src/vs/workbench/api/common/positron/positronSkillRoots.ts` -- resolves the roots
- `src/vs/workbench/api/common/positron/extHostAiFeatures.ts` -- exposes them
- returns absolute paths, resolved from the app root

## Two things to settle

**Bundling.** The skill files live in `skills/` at the repo root. They need to end up in the packaged app so the path the API returns actually exists at runtime. This is probably just a matter of including the directory in the build, but confirm it in a real packaged build on each platform, not only in a dev build.

**Gating.** This is AI-facing, so it has to respect `ai.enabled`. Whether skill discovery is additionally gated on `assistant.experimentalFeatures` is an Assistant-side decision, tracked in #15341.

## AC

- [ ] `positron.ai.getAgentSkillRoots()` declared in `positron.d.ts` and implemented in the extension host
- [ ] Returns absolute paths that exist in a packaged build on macOS, Windows, and Linux
- [ ] `skills/` ships in the packaged app
- [ ] Additive, so an Assistant build that does not call it is unaffected
- [ ] Unit tests for path resolution

title: `inno_updater.exe` lost its Positron branding again in the 1.118.0 upstream merge
description:
The vendored `build/win32/inno_updater.exe` at HEAD contains no Positron strings at all:

```
$ strings build/win32/inno_updater.exe | grep -ci positron
0
$ strings build/win32/inno_updater.exe | grep -i "inno-updater"
vscode-inno-updater-.log
```

It still contains `Failed to install Visual Studio Code update.` and `Visual Studio Code is updating...`, which is what users see in the failure dialogs.

Tracing every commit that has touched the binary:

| Commit | Date | Change | Positron strings | Log filename |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `8ee7386a886` | 2025-05-14 | Rebrand inno_updater.exe (#7674) | 4 | `vscode-inno-updater-` |
| `195121d4158` | 2025-05-21 | Update to 1.100 from upstream (#7769) | **0** | `vscode-inno-updater-` |
| `c5e2f18c064` | 2025-10-09 | Merge 1.104 from upstream (#9867) | 0 | `vscode-inno-updater-` |
| `a3c249d6314` | 2025-12-10 | Update inno_updater.exe branding (#11005) | 6 | `positron-inno-updater-` |
| `7e601b51896` | 2026-04-30 | Merge upstream CodeOSS 1.111.0 (#12996) | 6 | `positron-inno-updater-` |
| `3ce43af3435` | 2026-05-28 | Merge upstream Code OSS 1.118.0 (#13572) | **0** | `vscode-inno-updater-` |

Three things worth pulling out of that table:

1. The branding has been lost twice, at #7769 and again at #13572. The first loss came **one week** after the rebrand that introduced it.
2. The first rebrand (#7674) never actually renamed the log file. It added Positron strings but left `vscode-inno-updater-*.log` in place, so the `positron-inno-updater-*.log` name only ever existed between 2025-12-10 and 2026-05-28.
3. The 1.111.0 merge (#12996) replaced the binary but kept the branding, so upstream merges do not clobber it automatically. #13572 is where it actually regressed.

The practical cost: when we ask users for `positron-inno-updater-*.log` they cannot find it, because the file is written as `vscode-inno-updater-*.log`. That happened on #10484, where the reporter said they could not find the Positron log and attached `vscode-inno-updater-1783393086.log` instead.

`build/win32/Cargo.toml` pins version 0.21.0, but no Rust sources are in the repo (upstream is https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-inno-updater), so the checked-in binary is the only artifact. The logs also show version drift in the field: 0.19.0 in a 2026-05-28 log, 0.21.0 in a 2026-06-18 log.

Work here:

1. Rebuild from upstream and restore Positron branding, including the log filename this time.
2. Add a merge guard so the next upstream merge cannot silently revert it a third time. A check on the binary's strings would be enough, and it is the only item here that prevents a repeat.
3. While rebuilding, add logging for the exact Win32 error code, the file that failed to rename, and ideally the locking process via the Restart Manager API. Today the updater logs `Failed to rename current to old` with no indication of who holds the handle, which is a real obstacle to diagnosing #10484.

Split out from the Windows auto-update investigation.

title: Data Connections: Add positronDataConnections.connect and executeQuery commands
description:
## Context

Part of the implementation plan in #14664 for cold-start Assistant awareness of data connections. Once Assistant can discover a profile via #14923's `getConnections` command, it needs a headless way to connect and to run queries against the result - both at the TypeScript layer, not by generating and executing R/Python code in a console session.

`IPositronDataConnectionsService.connect(profileId)` already does headless connect at the TypeScript layer: it resolves secrets via `getProfileWithSecrets` and calls `driver.connect(mechanismId, params)` as a structured RPC, never generated code text - so secrets never touch console history, the transcript, or the model. This supersedes the original plan of executing driver-generated `DBI::dbConnect(...)`/`sqlalchemy.create_engine(...)` code in the console.

There is currently no equivalent for running a query: `IDataConnectionHandle` only exposes schema-browsing methods (`getChildren`, `nodeGetChildren`, `nodePreview`, which returns `void` and opens the Data Explorer as a side effect) - nothing returns query results as data. This closes that gap, satisfying the design doc's requirement for "Assistant awareness at the TypeScript layer for: Connections, schema, metadata" (via `connect` + existing schema methods) and "SQL results" (via `executeQuery`).

## AC

### Connect

- New `positronDataConnections.connect` command takes `profileId`, calls `IPositronDataConnectionsService.connect(profileId)` directly, and returns `{ success: true, instanceId }` or `{ success: false, error }`.
- No code generation, secret-joining, console execution, or redaction logic - secrets never leave the service/secret-storage/driver boundary.
- If a live instance for the profile already exists, return it without reconnecting (existing `connect()` behavior).
- Binding a live object into the user's own R/Python console session as a scriptable variable (the original "connectInConsole" behavior) is out of scope here - split into a follow-up if still wanted.

### Query

- New `IDataConnectionHandle.executeQuery(sql: string): Promise<IDataConnectionQueryResult>` on the driver interface, implemented per-driver (sqlite/duckdb/postgres/redshift already hold a live DB client for schema queries - this is an incremental addition, not new infra per driver).
- `IDataConnectionQueryResult` is `{ success: true, columns: { name: string; type: string }[], rows: unknown[][], rowCount: number, truncated: boolean }` or `{ success: false, error: string }`. Cap returned rows (e.g. 100) and set `truncated` when the result exceeds the cap.
- New `positronDataConnections.executeQuery` command takes `instanceId` and `sql`, resolves the instance via `IPositronDataConnectionsService.getInstance(id)`, and calls `connectionHandle.executeQuery(sql)`.
- Query safety: when `isReadOnly()` is true for the instance, `executeQuery` rejects non-`SELECT` statements with a clear error before dispatching to the driver.
- Drivers that don't support arbitrary SQL (e.g. `pins`, which is REST-based) reject `executeQuery` with a clear "not supported" error rather than crashing.

## Testing

Vitest (stubbed `IPositronDataConnectionsService`/driver):

- `connect`: valid `instanceId` on success; no secret values in the return value; reconnect returns existing instance without calling `driver.connect()` again; failure surfaces the driver's error message.
- `executeQuery`: success shape with columns/rows; row cap enforced and `truncated` set correctly; read-only instance rejects a non-SELECT statement; unsupported driver rejects with a clear error; failure surfaces the driver's error message.

## Out of scope

- Full Assistant-driven validation (cold-start SQLite query, preferred-variant adherence, honest no-connections response, degradation with the flag off) - happens under #14693 once its `executeCommand` tool and curated command list exist.
- Legacy runtime-comm connections (sparklyr, odbc, `%connection_show`) - follow-up ticket.
- Rich schema context - tracked in #14658.

title: Assistant loads trusted skill files shipped by the platform
description:
## Description

Posit Assistant loads skills from four places today: the user's own directories, the workspace, installed plugins, and its own bundle. Positron needs one more. Positron ships skill files of its own, and Assistant has to find them, trust them, and let the model invoke them on its own -- no slash command from the user, no per-use approval prompt.

The Positron half is #15342, the extension API that reports where the skill files live. The skill Positron will ship is #15343.

## Work off `feature/platform-skill-discovery`

[`feature/platform-skill-discovery`](https://github.com/posit-dev/assistant/tree/feature/platform-skill-discovery) in posit-dev/assistant is the branch to build on. It is one commit on top of current `main`, so it already sits on the plugin and marketplace work from [posit-dev/assistant#1884](https://github.com/posit-dev/assistant/pull/1884).

There is an older branch, `positron-platform-skills-spike`. It was a very rough first pass, written before the plugin work landed, and the way it passed roots around has since been rejected (see below). Do not build on it. It is worth reading only as a record of the original exploration.

What the current branch does:

- Adds a fifth skill source, `platform`, for roots the host application reports. In Positron those come from `positron.ai.getAgentSkillRoots()`, read once per workspace.
- Scans each platform root one level deep, `<root>/<name>/SKILL.md`, the same rule as bundled skills. A root that is not on disk contributes nothing and is not an error, so a host that ships no skills needs no special handling.
- Orders discovery as `skills.paths`, then plugin roots, then platform roots, then bundled skills. The last three register without overwriting, so a user or project skill always wins a name collision.
- Lets the model invoke `platform` skills without a permission prompt, the same as bundled skills, since both ship with software the user installed. `isModelEligibleBuiltin()` is left as it stands and a parallel `isModelEligiblePlatform()` sits next to it, which `createSkillTool` ORs together. Two predicates rather than one merged one: a single policy name would have to be edited by anyone who later wants platform skills disabled by a setting, or given a different permission default, whereas two leave each source governable on its own. Plugin skills still prompt.
- Gives `platform` its own `<location>` label in the system prompt, so the model can tell the user a capability came from the IDE instead of presenting it as one of its own.
- Reclassifies a platform root that lies inside an open workspace root as `project`. That covers a development build whose application directory is a checkout: without the rule, Assistant would load instructions written by whoever authored that repository, with no prompt. Reclassifying rather than skipping keeps those skills usable once the user trusts the workspace.
- Contributes no roots when the running Positron lacks the API or the call throws, and logs why. There is deliberately no fallback to a guessed path.

## What changed from the spike

The spike passed platform roots through `SkillDiscoveryConfig`. The new branch makes them a `SkillRegistry` constructor argument instead.

One registry serves every conversation in a workspace, and `discoverSkills()` clears its map and rebuilds it. The config, by contrast, is assembled per conversation. So a root carried in the config is only as good as the conversation that supplied it: one conversation failing to fetch the roots would rebuild the map without those skills, and every other live conversation would lose them too. The plugin system hit exactly this, which is why plugin roots are registry state as well.

Platform roots are a constructor argument rather than a setter because they are a fact about the installed application, fixed for the registry's life. Plugin roots get a setter because they change while the app runs, as the user installs and enables plugins.

## Open question: does skill discovery need the `experimentalFeatures` gate?

`assistant.experimentalFeatures` (default off) decides whether the `positronCommand` tool is offered at all -- see `agentCommandsEnabled` in `packages/positron/src/tools/agentCommands.ts`, which is on `main`. The new branch gates platform skill discovery on nothing.

That leaves the two out of step. With the setting off, Positron's skills would load and tell the model about commands it has no tool to run. Pick one:

- Gate skill discovery on the same setting, so the skills and the tool ship together. The spike did this.
- Leave discovery ungated, and instead gate whether Positron reports any roots at all, or whether the command skill ships (#15342, #15343). Platform skills are a general mechanism, and tying it to a command-tool setting is a narrower fit than tying the skill to it.
- Drop the gate on the command tool, once we are ready to ship both.

The branch argues for the second, and its commit message carries the reasoning: platform skills are a general mechanism, and a skill about the variables pane would not need the command tool at all, so whether a setting should suppress a skill belongs with the skill that needs the tool. On that reading a gate would hook the roots -- either the host reports none, or the platform loop in `discoverSkills` is skipped -- rather than the directory scan or the permission predicates. `experimentalFeaturesEnabled` stays module-private in `agentCommands.ts` as a result. Recorded here as the branch's position, not as a settled decision; the AC below still wants one.

## AC

- [ ] Assistant discovers skills from the roots the host application reports
- [ ] A decision on whether skill discovery is gated on `assistant.experimentalFeatures`
- [ ] Those skills invoke without an approval prompt
- [ ] A platform root inside an open workspace root is trust-gated as workspace content
- [ ] The system prompt distinguishes platform skills from Assistant's own
- [ ] A host that reports no roots, and a Positron build without the API, both behave exactly as before

title: data explorer: date and time filters fail on file-backed data
description:
A filter on a date, datetime, time, or interval column cannot be applied to a file opened in the Data Explorer. The DuckDB backend builds the filter value into the WHERE clause without quotes, so DuckDB reads `2024-01-01` as arithmetic on three integers and refuses to bind the comparison.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a CSV that has an ISO date column, so that DuckDB types the column as DATE.
2. Add a row filter on that column, such as "is greater than 2024-01-01".
3. The filter doesn't apply.

title: data explorer: "contains" treats % and _ in the search term as wildcards for files
description:
The DuckDB backend builds the contains, starts_with, and ends_with filters as SQL `LIKE` patterns, with the search term inserted into the pattern unchanged. `%` and `_` in the term keep their `LIKE` meaning, so the filter matches rows the user didn't ask for. A search for `a_b` matches `axb`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a CSV that has a text column with values `a_b` and `axb`.
2. Add a "contains" filter with the term `a_b`.
3. Both rows match. Only the first row is correct.

This doesn't happen for kernel-backed data explorers.

title: R Pixi discovery: allow configuring the Pixi executable path
description:
## System details

- OS: NixOS 26.05 (x86_64)
- Positron package: 2026.08.1-2
- R: 4.5.3 from conda-forge via Pixi
- Pixi: 0.68.1, provided by the project's Nix devShell rather than installed globally
- `positron.r.interpreters.pixiDiscovery`: enabled

## Describe the issue

Pixi R interpreter discovery currently appears to require the `pixi`
executable to be available either on the Positron process `PATH` or in
one of Pixi's default installation locations, such as
`~/.pixi/bin/pixi` on Linux.

This causes initial discovery to fail when Pixi is supplied by an
external/project-local environment manager and is intentionally not
globally visible to the Positron process.

A concrete example is a Nix project where Pixi is provided by the
project's devShell:

```nix
devShells.x86_64-linux.default = pkgs.mkShell {
  packages = [ pkgs.pixi ];
};
````

In this setup, the Pixi version is pinned by the project's
`flake.lock`.

This seems like a follow-up to #3724: automatic Pixi R discovery itself
works correctly once Positron can locate the Pixi executable.

## Steps to reproduce

Create a fresh project. This public template is only used to keep the
reproduction short:

```bash
mkdir positron-pixi-repro
cd positron-pixi-repro

nix flake init \
  -t github:YONGHUNI/nix-data-science-templates/4b47d3f0caa0b5e2881fbabf5aff52dbe7b80d2b#r-pixi
```

Install the Pixi environment using the project's Nix devShell:

```bash
nix develop -c sh -c '
  pixi install
  pixi run R --version
'
```

This creates the R interpreter under:

```text
.pixi/envs/default/bin/R
```

Outside the devShell, Pixi is intentionally unavailable:

```bash
command -v pixi || echo "pixi not on PATH"
```

Output:

```text
pixi not on PATH
```

Now launch Positron normally from the desktop GUI and open this fresh
project.

With Pixi R discovery enabled, the Pixi R interpreter is not initially
discovered.

However, launching Positron from the devShell:

```bash
nix develop -c positron .
```

allows Positron to discover:

```text
R 4.5.3 (Pixi: default)
```

## Workaround and verification

On Linux, placing a small dispatcher at `~/.pixi/bin/pixi` works around
the issue. The dispatcher forwards Positron's Pixi calls into the
current project's Nix devShell:

```text
Positron
  -> ~/.pixi/bin/pixi
  -> nix develop <project> -c pixi ...
  -> project-pinned Pixi
```

With this shim in place, a completely fresh project is discovered
correctly when Positron is launched normally from the GUI.

Both discovery and environment activation work through the shim:

```bash
~/.pixi/bin/pixi info --json

~/.pixi/bin/pixi shell-hook \
  --manifest-path ./pixi.toml \
  --json
```

The resulting R session in Positron also uses the expected project-local
environment. For example:

```r
.libPaths()
```

returns the Pixi environment library under
`.pixi/envs/default/lib/R/library`, and BLAS/LAPACK and Pixi-installed R
packages are loaded from the same environment.

## Expected behavior

It would be useful if R Pixi discovery provided a supported way to
specify or locate the Pixi executable when it is not on the Positron
process `PATH` or in a default Pixi installation directory.

For comparison, the bundled Python extension exposes
`python.pixiToolPath`.

A similar configurable mechanism for R could be one possible solution,
although the implementation does not necessarily need to match the
Python setting.

The main requirement is simply to allow Pixi R discovery and activation
to use a Pixi executable supplied from a non-standard location.

## Additional context

I am **not** requesting that Positron automatically activate Nix
development shells.

Nix is just one reproducible example of the broader case where Pixi
exists and manages the project environment correctly, but its executable
is intentionally not globally available to the Positron process.

Once Positron can reach the Pixi executable, the existing Pixi R
discovery and `shell-hook` activation work correctly in my testing.

title: Footgun: Runtime session references go stale after an extension host restart
description:
When you get a runtime session from the session service and hold onto it, an extension host restart swaps that object for a new one with the same session ID but a fresh connection. Anything still holding the old object is now talking to a dead connection: calls fail and events stop arriving, causing confusing bugs.

This is easy to hit, because holding onto a session is the natural thing to do (consoles, notebooks, plots, help, and packages all do it), and nothing warns you the object has gone stale.

The root cause is that a session object mixes two things with different lifetimes: the session itself (ID, state, events), which lasts as long as the kernel, and its connection to the extension host, which dies on restart. Today a restart throws away the whole object even though the session is still alive.

We have tried patching this with reference-swapping and by storing IDs instead of objects, but neither is complete: some internal caches still hold stale objects, and nothing helps the many holders outside the service.

## Proposed solution

Keep one session object per session for the life of the kernel, and on a restart swap only its connection to the extension host, not the object.

With one object per session, every reference stays valid automatically and events keep flowing, with no changes required from callers. The reference-swapping and ID-indirection code can be removed.

The main work is moving ownership of the session object up into the session service, so it survives restarts instead of being recreated by the extension-host layer. As a companion change, a session with a dead connection should fail loudly with a clear "this session was replaced" error instead of silently doing nothing.

Concretely: the session object holds a swappable connection to the extension host rather than a fixed one, and a restart replaces just that connection.

The mouse turns into a hand, which is better than nothing, but that's it. There are some possibly related issues (e.g., #1769, #12975) but I don't think they're asking the same thing as I am. To be clear, this issue is not a bug report -- console links in Positron already work for me in that I can click them and something will happen -- but rather a feature request to make links even better.
