Chromium: Windows_NT x64 10.0.26200
Node.js: undefined
V8: undefined
OS: Windows
Editor: Positron Notebook Editor (.ipynb)


#### Session details:

python 3.13.10


## Describe the issue:
When a notebook cell's content is taller than the visible editor viewport, clicking inside the cell to place the cursor causes the view to immediately scroll to the top of that cell. This discards the current scroll position, so if you were viewing/editing content near the middle or end of a long cell, you're thrown back up to the start of the cell and have to scroll back down to find where you were.

## Steps to reproduce the issue:

1. Open a notebook (.ipynb) in the Positron Notebook Editor.
2. Create or open a code cell whose content is long enough to exceed the height of the visible editor area (taller than the monitor/viewport).
3. Scroll down within the cell so you're viewing content partway through or near the end of the cell.
4. Click anywhere inside the cell to place the cursor (e.g., at the end of a line near the bottom of the visible content).


## Expected or desired behavior:
Clicking to place the cursor should keep the clicked line in roughly the same on-screen position — the view should not re-scroll unless the clicked position was actually out of view.

## Were there any error messages in the UI, Output panel, or Developer Tools console?

No

Screen recording attached showing the behavior: cursor is positioned near the end of a tall cell, then clicking causes the view to jump to the top of the cell.

title: Quarto visual mode / source mode switching breaks equation block formatting and syntax highlighting
description: When switching between visual mode and source mode in a Quarto .qmd document, the editor reformats multi-line equation blocks ``` $$ equation $$ ``` into single-line form ``` $$equation$$ ``` , which causes two related bugs: Bug 1 — Cross-reference label malformation After a visual→source mode switch, a properly formatted numbered equation like: ``` $$ y_i = \alpha + \sum_{j=1}^{p} \beta_j x_{ij} + \varepsilon_i $$ {#eq-liner-model} ``` is reformatted into: ``` $$\text{equation}$$ {#eq-a-error-format} ``` The label {#eq-a-error-format} is placed on a new line with a leading space, making it unrecognizable to the Quarto cross-reference engine. Rendering the document produces: ``` Unable to resolve crossref @eq-a-error-format ``` Bug 2 — Lost syntax highlighting (gray background) A correctly formatted single-line numbered equation: ``` $$(\hat{\alpha}, \hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}) = \arg\min \left\{ \sum_{i=1}^{N} \left(y_i - \alpha - \sum_{j=1}^{p} \beta_j x_{ij}\right)^2 \right\} \quad \text{subject to} \quad \sum_{j=1}^{p} |\beta_j| \leq t$$ {#eq-lasso} ``` renders correctly and cross-references work, but the equation block itself is not wrapped in the usual gray background box. Moreover, any R code blocks that follow this equation also lose their gray background. Expected behavior: Switching between visual and source mode should preserve the original multi-line equation block structure. The {#eq-label} syntax should remain on the same line as the closing $$. All code blocks should consistently display the gray background regardless of preceding equation formatting. I have checked https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/discussions/8684#discussion-8640338. It seems to be related to the issue I am experiencing, but it looks like it has not been properly fixed yet. My Quarto version is 1.9.38 and my Positron version is 2026.07.0. Attachments:

title: Positron Notebooks: dispose orphaned overlay webviews when outputs are removed
description:
Overlay webviews (display plots, raw HTML) are not disposed when their backing outputs are removed. Clearing outputs, deleting a cell, or re-running a cell that changes output type leaves the webview alive in memory but invisible.

This is a pre-existing issue for display webviews (Plotly/Bokeh/HoloViews) and now also applies to raw HTML webviews added in the complex HTML output work.

## Proposed fix

Add a notebook model change listener in the preload service that compares live output IDs against cached webview IDs and disposes orphans. This requires:

- Exposing `textModel` and `onDidChangeModel` on `IPositronNotebookInstance`
- Listening to `NotebookCellsChangeType.Output`, `OutputItem`, and `ModelChange` events
- Reconciling display, raw HTML, and preload message caches uniformly
- Excluding widget webviews (they manage their own lifecycle via ipywidgets comm channels)

A working implementation existed on the original complex HTML branch (`_reconcileOutputWebviews`) and can be adapted.

## Impact

Each leaked webview is a small iframe process. Unlikely to be user-visible unless someone repeatedly clears/re-runs dozens of cells in a session.

## Context

Discovered during simplification of the complex HTML notebook output branch. Marked with a TODO in `positronWebviewPreloadsService.ts`. This is also a prerequisite for cell virtualization -- when cells are virtualized, the reconciliation system becomes the primary disposal mechanism.

title: python: interpreters can be deduplicated too aggressively
description:
I've noticed that if two different Python interpreters should show up on the list (because they're two different virtual environments, for example), but they both symlink to the same interpreter, only the one with the shortest path name is chosen. Example:

```
mkdir ~/all_my_venvs
mkdir ~/all_my_venvs/a
mkdir ~/all_my_venvs/bbb
cd ~/all_my_venvs/a
uv venv -p 3.12
cd ~/all_my_venvs/bbb
uv venv -p 3.12
```
On my computer, both `~/all_my_venvs/a/.venv/bin/python` and `~/all_my_venvs/bbb/.venv/bin/python` symlink to `~/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.12-macos-aarch64-none/bin/python3.12`.

Add to your settings
```
"python.interpreters.include": [
  "~/all_my_venvs/a/.venv/bin/python",
  "~/all_my_venvs/bbb/.venv/bin/python"
]
```

and open Positron. You'll see only `~/all_my_venvs/a/.venv/bin/python` show up.

The intent of the symlink deduplication is to protect against e.g. seeing all these in the list, since it's the same interpreter:
```
~/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.12-macos-aarch64-none/bin/python
~/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.12-macos-aarch64-none/bin/python3
~/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.12-macos-aarch64-none/bin/python3.12
```
or
```
~/all_my_venvs/a/.venv/bin/python
~/all_my_venvs/a/.venv/bin/python3
~/all_my_venvs/a/.venv/bin/python3.12
```
so maybe we should fix the symlink deduplication so it only looks in the same folder.

title: A DuckDB cannot be opened more than once in Data Connections
description:
If you set up two connections to the same DuckDB file, say, once using a tilde path: `~/Work/database-fixtures/example.duckdb` and once using a relative path: `../Work/database-fixtures/example.duckdb` You can only open one of them:

The DuckDB driver needs to be updated to share a worker role across multiple connections. This issue was discovered while validating that issue https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/14053 is actually fixed (it is). While it is not expected that people will do this a lot, it's bad that it doesn't work. It makes Data Connections seem broken.

title: Update ways to use PETE, post evaluation
description:
As part of our 30 days of code review experiments, we tried out using some automated testing evaluation:

https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/736971b1ee60a9325f1f4a71b6a9a3654f37e105/.github/actions/pr-test-checker/action.yml

At the end of the 30 days, we found that people agreed this prompting was very useful but wanted to make sure they have it locally during development and not only in CI. We have a local skill with the same prompting now ✅ but let's make two additional changes.

- Let's add awareness of the test-checker/PETE prompting to the `positron-pr-helper` skill, so when we are ready to make a PR, we evaluate test coverage, in much the way we check test tags.
- Let's keep the GH action but change it to run only via slash command and not automatically on every PR. We were evenly split on whether to make this change vs. make some changes to the PR comment (like, an exact tie in voting 😅) so let's try this approach and see how it plays out. I picked this one just for financial reasons 💸 but if we find we miss the automatic PR comments or, say, we observe a drift toward NOT adding appropriate tests without it, we can turn it back on.

title: Inline output: kernel picker disabled and Run Cell broken when jupyter: YAML key sets a custom kernelspec name
description:
## Describe the issue:

With `positron.quarto.inlineOutput.enabled: true`, opening a `.qmd` that
declares a **custom Jupyter kernel name** in its YAML header
(e.g. `jupyter: spectral-comparison-3.14`) leaves the kernel picker disabled
and "Run Cell" does nothing (there is red "x" below cell  and popup "Could not determine language for Quarto document. Ensure the document has code cells with a language specified.").

Does not reproduce when:
- `positron.quarto.inlineOutput.enabled: false` (cells run normally), or
- YAML uses `jupyter: python3` instead of a custom kernelspec name, or
- `jupyter:` key removed entirely.

Kernel is valid — `jupyter kernelspec list` shows
`spectral-comparison-3.14`; works fine in `.ipynb` and in `.qmd` without
inline output.

## Steps to reproduce the issue:

1. Enable inline output: set `positron.quarto.inlineOutput.enabled: true`.
2. Register custom kernel:

    ```bash
    python -m ipykernel install --user --name spectral-comparison-3.14
    ```

3. Create `test.qmd`:

    ```qmd
    ---
    title: "Python Test"
    format: html
    jupyter: spectral-comparison-3.14
    ---

    ```{python}
    x = 1
    print(x)
    ```
    ```

4. Open in Positron → kernel picker  doesnt do nothing,  "Run Cell" no outpuyt (only red x, when trying to run cell a popup "Could not determine language for Quarto document. Ensure the document has code cells with a language specified.").
5. Toggle `positron.quarto.inlineOutput.enabled: false` → picker + Run Cell work.
6. Re-enable inline output, change YAML to `jupyter: python3` → also works.

title: Python LSP logs SystemExit / "Unhandled exception in client_connected_cb" on every restart
description:
### Summary

During the investigation of #10016, I confirmed that the original `RuntimeError: Cannot close a running event loop` on Python LSP shutdown is resolved by #14435. However, the same `[asyncio] ERROR | Unhandled exception in client_connected_cb` log line still appears on every interpreter restart / LSP shutdown, now caused by a `SystemExit` raised from pygls's `lsp_exit` handler. It looks like a crash in the Python Kernel output even though the session continues to work, and it is very likely one of the alarming tracebacks that led users to report "the kernel crashed" in #10016.

Filing separately so the Python folks can weigh in on the right fix! 🐍 

### What the log shows now

On every restart, the Python Kernel output logs an ERROR-level traceback ending in:

```
[Python] [asyncio] ERROR | Unhandled exception in client_connected_cb
[Python] transport: <_SelectorSocketTransport closed fd=80>
[Python] Traceback (most recent call last):
[Python]   File ".../positron/positron_lsp.py", line 567, in start_tcp
[Python]     self._loop.run_until_complete(start_server())
[Python]   ...
[Python]   File ".../positron/positron_lsp.py", line 524, in lsp_connection
[Python]     await run_async(...)
[Python]   File ".../positron/_vendor/pygls/io_.py", line 167, in run_async
[Python]     protocol.handle_message(message)
[Python]   ...
[Python]   File ".../positron/_vendor/pygls/protocol/language_server.py", line 132, in lsp_exit
[Python]     sys.exit(returncode)
[Python] SystemExit: 0
```

(The traceback repeats once per restart.)

### Root cause

When the frontend sends the LSP `exit` notification during a restart, pygls's base `lsp_exit` handler calls `sys.exit(returncode)` (`_vendor/pygls/protocol/language_server.py:124` and `:132`). That is correct for a standalone LSP server process, but Positron runs the LSP on a thread inside the kernel process (`PositronLSPThread`, via `start_tcp` in `positron_lsp.py`). So `sys.exit()` raises `SystemExit` out of the connection callback (`client_connected_cb`), which asyncio surfaces as an unhandled exception and logs at ERROR.

`PositronLanguageServerProtocol` (`positron_lsp.py:436`) overrides `lsp_initialize` and `get_message_type` but not `lsp_exit`, so the base `sys.exit()` behavior runs unmodified.

Note that `returncode` is `0` (clean shutdown), the `SystemExit` does not actually terminate the kernel, and teardown still completes via the connection-close path (`lsp_connection` finally -> `_stop_serving` -> `serve_forever` returns -> `start_tcp` finally -> `_shutdown_server`). So this appears cosmetic, but it is logged as an ERROR with a full traceback on every restart and reads like a crash.

### Reproduction

1. Start a Python console.
2. Type a bit so the LSP has an active connection.
3. Restart the interpreter (or run _Developer: Restart Extension Host_).
4. Open the Python Kernel output channel and observe the `Unhandled exception in client_connected_cb` / `SystemExit: 0` traceback.

Observed on the 2026-07-21 daily build; the relevant code path is identical on current `main` (both include #14435).

### Questions for our resident Python experts

- Is the right fix to override `lsp_exit` in `PositronLanguageServerProtocol` so that, in the in-kernel threaded model, it runs any user EXIT handler and closes the writer but does not call `sys.exit()` (leaving teardown to the existing connection-close path)? Or is there a reason the base `sys.exit()` behavior is still wanted here?
- Should this be paired with a lifecycle regression test (start -> stop -> join thread) that also asserts no `SystemExit` / no unhandled-exception log on an `exit` notification? `test_positron_lsp.py` currently covers completions/patterns/signature help but nothing in the server start/stop/restart lifecycle.

### Context

- Part of the #10016 investigation (not a blocker for the other sub-problems).
- Original `RuntimeError: Cannot close a running event loop` was fixed by #14435; this is a distinct, remaining finding on the same shutdown path.

title: R: Integration with `mori`
description:
The [mori R package](https://shikokuchuo.net/mori/) allows two or more R sessions to share objects in memory. Since Positron supports multiple R sessions, we could give users affordances to help manage memory in their sessions using `mori`, if it is installed. For example:

- A decoration in the Variables pane indicates variables that are shared session data (by detecting the mori ALTREP type)
- A gesture in the Variables pane to share a variable with other R sessions
- A region in the memory usage meter to designated shared memory
- A facility to "clone" an R session, creating an independent R session but retaining all the data from the old session as shared data, without copying (good for long running work)

title: Add a Render button to the Quarto editor action bar
description:
The Quarto source editor's action bar has a Preview button, a render-on-save checkbox, and a Run All button, but no Render button. The existing alternatives for rendering are not amazing:

- `Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + K` clashes with VS Code's delete-line shortcut.
- **Command Palette > Quarto: Render Document** shifts focus to the terminal and then pops a modal asking for the output format. It's just slow enough that users lose their place / forget they triggered it.

## Proposed behavior

- Add a **Render** button to the Quarto editor action bar (alongside Preview).
- Render the document as a single operation, without stealing focus or requiring a per-run format prompt.
- Ideally offer a dropdown to pick which format(s) to render (e.g. HTML, PDF, DOCX), so the choice is made once rather than on every render.
- Consider supporting rendering a whole project file, not just the current document.

## Context

Requested in [discussion #14986](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/discussions/14986).

Related:
- #14513 - extension-contributable split buttons in the editor action bar (would let this be a Preview-style split button with format variants behind the chevron).
- #12891 - additional export/convert options for Quarto (`.qmd` -> other formats), completed. This request is about *rendering* in place from the action bar rather than converting the source file.

title: Preview `.rds` file contents in the Data Explorer from the file explorer
description:
Clicking a CSV or parquet file in the file explorer opens its contents directly in the Data Explorer. Clicking an `.rds` file instead only offers to load the object into the R session (the opener added in #9204). There's no way to preview the contents of an `.rds` file without loading it into a session first.

Request: let the Data Explorer render the contents of an `.rds` file when it's selected in the file explorer, matching the CSV/parquet experience.

## Context

The Data Explorer reads CSV/parquet via DuckDB, which doesn't support the RDS format (nor does Polars). Supporting a preview would likely require reading the file through another mechanism (e.g. the R session itself) before handing rows to the Data Explorer.

## Related

- #9204 - added the current `.rds` opener that loads the object into a variable (the existing behavior)
- #14414 - proposal to import an already-previewed CSV/parquet/XLSX into R/Python (the reverse direction)

## Source

Feedback discussion: https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/discussions/14988

DuckDB - con.sql(..) 3. Base R: data.frame/ tibble 4. polars.Dataframe ## Open questions 1. Can we pull the same logic of what is exposed in the variable explorer / Notebook Editor and expose it via a button in the console? 2. What happens when the connection is closed?

title: reticulate integration fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'positron_ipykernel'` for conda/mamba environments (works for venv)
description:
## System details:

#### Positron and OS details:

Positron Version: 2026.07.1 (user setup) build 5
Code - OSS Version: 1.118.0
Commit: d3cdd608df5afa3378c24c9a9c81b01fe1433a87
Date: 2026-07-08T19:52:09-06:00
Electron: 39.8.8
Chromium: 142.0.7444.265
Node.js: 22.22.1
V8: 14.2.231.22-electron.0
OS: Windows_NT x64 10.0.19045

#### Session details:

R 4.6.1, Python 3.10.12 (system), Python 3.12.13 (conda env)
Reticulate version 1.46.0
Quarto version 1.9.38

## Describe the issue:

Positron's reticulate integration fails to start the Python session for **conda/mamba environments**, exiting immediately with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'positron_ipykernel'`. The identical flow works for a **venv** on the same machine. This makes the managed "Python (reticulate)" console unusable with conda environments.

## Steps to reproduce the issue:

1. Create a fresh conda/mamba environment:
   ```bash
   mamba create -n testenv python=3.10
   ```
2. In Positron, open a .qmd file and run:
   ```{r}
   library(reticulate)
   use_condaenv("testenv", required = TRUE)
   repl_python()
   ```
3. Observe that the reticulate Python session fails to start.

For contrast, the same flow against a venv succeeds:
```{r}
# from a workspace containing a .venv created via `python -m venv .venv`
library(reticulate)
use_virtualenv(".venv", required = TRUE)
repl_python()   # starts normally
```

## Expected or desired behavior:
The "Python (reticulate)" console starts against the conda environment, the same way it does for a venv.

## Were there any error messages in the UI, Output panel, or Developer Tools console?

The session exits immediately (exit code 0) with:

```
Python (reticulate) failed to start up (exit code 0)
Reticulate initialization failed: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'positron_ipykernel'
Run `reticulate::py_last_error()` for details.
```

`reticulate::py_last_error()` R traceback:

```
── R Traceback ────────────────────────────────
     ▆
  1. └─.ps.rpc.reticulate_start_kernel(...)
  2.   ├─base::tryCatch(...)
  ...
 11.             └─reticulate::import("positron_ipykernel.positron_ipkernel")
 12.               └─reticulate:::py_module_import(module, convert = convert)

- Open the Developer Tools console by running the `Developer: Toggle Developer Tools` command from the Command Palette
- Open the relevant Output Channel logs by utilizing this guide: https://positron.posit.co/troubleshooting.html

## What I've already tried (all still fail for the conda env)

- Installed `ipykernel` into the conda env (`mamba install -n testenv ipykernel`) — no change; the missing module is `positron_ipykernel`, not `ipykernel`.
- Pinned `ipykernel<7` — no change.
- `use_condaenv("testenv", required = TRUE)` — the original failing path.
- `use_python("/home/<user>/miniforge3/envs/testenv/bin/python", required = TRUE)` — same failure. reticulate appears to still apply conda-style setup because the prefix contains a `conda-meta` folder.
- Confirmed the same machine/WSL works fine with a venv, so this is specifically conda-env vs venv rather than a filesystem/WSL issue (the venv is on `/mnt/d`, the conda env on the native Linux filesystem).

Workaround that does work: setting `positron.reticulate.enabled` to `never` (loses the managed console and Variables pane).

## Hypothesis (may be wrong)

Positron exposes `positron_ipykernel` by adding its bundled kernel directory to the interpreter's search path via `PYTHONPATH`. Conda environment activation seems to rebuild the process environment and drop that `PYTHONPATH` entry, so the bundled module is no longer importable for conda interpreters. venvs don't go through that activation step, so the entry survives — which would explain the venv-vs-conda difference.

title: python: New Folder flow lists uv last in the provider menu until Positron restarts
description:
## Describe the issue

Once Positron installs uv for you mid-session, the New Folder flow does not reorder its environment provider menu to account for the newly available provider. The menu keeps the pre-install order and appends uv to the end, so it reads `venv > conda > uv`. After a restart, the same menu shows `uv > venv > conda`, because the provider list is rebuilt at startup with uv available from the outset.

## Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Start Positron on a machine where uv is not installed.
2. Trigger the uv install flow (for example "Python: Install Python via uv", or the startup flow that offers a uv install when no Python is found) and let it install uv.
3. Open the New Folder flow and create a new Python project.
4. On the Python environment step, open the environment provider menu.
5. Note the order is venv > conda > uv.
6. Restart Positron, repeat steps 3-4, and note the order is now uv > venv > conda.

## Expected or desired behavior

The provider menu should present the same order regardless of when uv was installed. After a mid-session uv install, the New Folder flow should re-sort the provider list to match the post-restart order (uv > venv > conda) rather than appending uv to the end. The menu order should reflect the current state of the machine, not the state at the time Positron was launched.

## Related

- #13104 tracks allowing uv installation from the new project flow; this is the ordering side effect once uv can be installed.

title: Bedrock STS region falls back to us-east-1
description:
This came from a Workbench support issue #127667

Posit Assistant with Bedrock fails in a region-restricted VPC even when `authentication.aws.credentials` sets the AWS region. Setting a global `AWS_REGION` env var fixes it.

The Bedrock client gets the configured region, but the STS web-identity exchange that mints credentials first does not, so it targets `sts.us-east-1.amazonaws.com`. Where STS PrivateLink only covers the configured region, that call has no route and times out. The error surfaces during `ListFoundationModels`, so it looks like Bedrock is broken when STS is.

## Root cause

The auth extension reads the region but never passes it to the credential provider:

```ts
const region = awsConfig?.AWS_REGION ?? process.env.AWS_REGION ?? 'us-east-1';
const credentialProvider = fromNodeProviderChain(profile ? { profile } : {});
```
One theory: the auth extension activates on `onStartupFinished` and reads config once, possibly before the workspace-folder `settings.json` value is visible. The global env var would avoid this because the OS provides it at process launch.

title: Assistant: inconsistent code block formats when fixing Quarto documents
description:
## System details:

#### Positron and OS details:

Observed across multiple participants with various configurations in a workshop setting

#### Session details:

Quarto document with R code

## Describe the issue:

Discovered during a Positron workshop where most participants received executable R code blocks, but at least one participant received markdown blocks with fences for the same prompt.

When asking Positron Assistant to fix code in a Quarto document, responses inconsistently return either:
1. Plain R/Python code blocks (with play button to execute)
2. Quarto markdown code blocks with fences (no play button)

This inconsistency is confusing in workshop/teaching settings where multiple participants run the same steps but get different results (some with play-able R code blocks and some with non-play-able R code markdown blocks)

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/47d56888-fb02-4cd4-a3ab-81602ee1bb67)

## Steps to reproduce the issue:

1. Open a Quarto document with an error (e.g., https://github.com/posit-dev/positron-ai-workshop/blob/main/R.qmd)
2. Ask Assistant: "I have an error in my code, can you fix it?"
3. Observe the format of the returned code block

Some users receive plain R code that can be executed directly via the play button. Other users receive Quarto markdown blocks with fences that cannot be executed directly.

## Expected or desired behavior:

Responses should be consistent across users. When the user's intent is to run code in the console, Assistant should return executable code blocks rather than markdown.

- Should we enhance Quarto-related prompting to prefer outputting runnable R/Python code blocks in chat?
- Maybe a setting could provide flexibility for users who prefer markdown blocks in certain contexts?

## Workaround in the meantime

For individual code repos, project-level [custom instructions](https://positron.posit.co/assistant-chat-instructions.html) can be used to prefer runnable code blocks over markdown blocks.

title: Reuse cell editors across notebooks
description:
Currently, we cache the 3 most recently used notebook container DOM nodes. This improves the time to switch to a notebook after it was already opened, which is great.

The downside is it's still slow to open a notebook for the first time.

I experimented with another approach that worked well in my initial testing: To maintain a pool of cell editors and reuse them across notebooks.

This should give us really fast notebook load times, both for the first load and switching back to an open notebook. The only slow load should be the very first notebook.

title: Provide a way to preview and/or open a Python or R data frame from the editor
description:
Beta user feedback (https://github.com/posit-dev/positron-beta/discussions/113#discussioncomment-9147231):

> In RStudio, I like the feature where cntrl+click on the name of a data frame opens that object in the data viewer.

It is possible to open the Data Explorer from the Variables pane, and from the Console (via `View()` / `%view`). However, opening up a data object is such a common gesture that it would be helpful to support doing it from the editor pane, too. 

Note that <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> <kbd>Click</kbd> is already bound in Positron as "go to references", which is also a helpful gesture for data frames, so we probably shouldn't take that binding by default (unless the RStudio Keymap is enabled). 

Ideas:
- We could show a small preview on hover with a link that opens up the full Data Explorer, and/or
- We could create a command for this gesture with a default binding, and/or
- We could overload an existing command (e.g. F2)

title: R discovery rejects a Nix-built R because its R launcher is a compiled wrapper, not a shell script
description:
## System details: #### Positron and OS details: Positron 2026.06.0 (build 211) — commit d5f94f072b1083b8237930739cb6525c6e12e1da macOS 26.5.1 (25F80), Apple Silicon (arm64) #### Session details: R 4.5.3 (provided by Nix / nixpkgs; `R` on `PATH` is a compiled wrapper) ## Describe the issue: On Nix/nixpkgs, the `R` on `PATH` is a small **compiled** wrapper (`…-R-4.5.3-wrapper/bin/R` — a Mach-O binary that sets up env, then execs the real R). Positron's R discovery determines `R_HOME` by parsing the `R` launcher *as a shell script* (looking for `R_HOME_DIR=`). Because the Nix launcher is a binary, discovery logs **"Binary is not a shell script wrapping the executable"** and discards it as **"Invalid installation"** — even though `R RHOME` and `R --version` answer correctly. Every Nix-provided R is therefore undiscoverable, and adding it via `positron.r.customBinaries` hits the same validator and is rejected identically. The binary is a valid R launcher; it just isn't a shell script: ```console $ file "$(which R)" /nix/store/…-R-4.5.3-wrapper/bin/R: Mach-O 64-bit arm64 executable $ R RHOME /nix/store/…-R-4.5.3/lib/R $ R --version R version 4.5.3 (2026-03-11) -- "Reassured Reassurer" ``` (NB: this is **Nix the package manager** — distinct from the "*nix shell script" assumption stated in #10193 (comment). That comment is precisely the assumption that fails here.) ## Steps to reproduce the issue: 1. Provide R via Nix (`nix-shell -p R`, a flake devShell, or home-manager), so `which R` → `/nix/store/…-R--wrapper/bin/R`. 2. Launch Positron with that R on `PATH`. 3. Open the R interpreter picker — the Nix R is absent (only a non-Nix R, e.g. Homebrew, appears). ## Expected or desired behavior: An R whose `R RHOME` / `R --version` succeed should be usable even when the launcher is a compiled binary rather than a shell script. **Suggested fix:** when the launcher isn't a parseable shell script, fall back to querying the binary directly — `R RHOME` for the home, `R --version` for the version — instead of discarding the install. This would also let `customBinaries` / `override` accept such installs. **Workaround for other Nix users:** point `positron.r.customBinaries` at Nix's *inner* R (`$(R RHOME)/bin/R`), which *is* a shell script carrying `R_HOME_DIR=`. Caveat: `ark` dlopens `libR` and bypasses the Nix wrapper, so the wrapper-injected package library (`R_LIBS_SITE`) must also be exported into Positron's launch environment, or the R session starts with an empty library. ## Were there any error messages in the UI, Output panel, or Developer Tools console? UI: "No usable R installations" (Nix R silently filtered out). `Output → R Language Pack`:
Full discovery sequence — wrapper rejected via PATH and via customBinaries; Homebrew accepted for contrast ``` [info] Possibly found R on PATH: /nix/store/…-R-4.5.3-wrapper/bin/R. [info] Resolved R binary at /nix/store/…-R-4.5.3-wrapper/bin/R [info] Candidate R binary at /nix/store/…-R-4.5.3-wrapper/bin/R [info] Binary is not a shell script wrapping the executable: /nix/store/…-R-4.5.3-wrapper/bin/R [info] R binaries from 'positron.r.customBinaries' to discover: [ "/…/.direnv/R" # symlink -> the same -wrapper/bin/R ] [info] Ignoring R headquarters directory /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions because it does not exist. [info] Ignoring ad hoc R binary /usr/bin/R because it does not exist. … (all standard locations absent) … [info] Candidate R binary at /nix/store/…-R-4.5.3-wrapper/bin/R [info] Binary is not a shell script wrapping the executable: /nix/store/…-R-4.5.3-wrapper/bin/R [info] Candidate R binary at /opt/homebrew/Cellar/r/4.6.0_1/bin/R [info] R installation discovered: { "usable": true, "supported": true, "reasonDiscovered": [ "Found in a conventional location for symlinked R binaries" ], "reasonRejected": null, "binpath": "/opt/homebrew/Cellar/r/4.6.0_1/bin/R", "homepath": "/opt/homebrew/Cellar/r/4.6.0_1/lib/R", "version": "4.6.0", "arch": "arm64", "current": false, "orthogonal": true, "default": false } [info] Filtering out /nix/store/…-R-4.5.3-wrapper/bin/R, reason: Invalid installation. [warning] Some discovered R installations are unusable by Positron. [warning] Learn more about R discovery at https://positron.posit.co/r-installations ```

title: Asssitant: Speech-to-text
description:
In https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/7615 we decided to remove the voice chat button for now, but at some point it would be great for Assistant to support speech functionality.

### Implementation notes

We will have to [register a `SpeechProvider`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/7615).

It isn't documented, but I think the idea is:

1. Positron calls `SpeechProvider.provideSpeechToTextSession`.
2. The provider creates and returns a `SpeechToTextSession` object.
3. The `SpeechToTextSession` is currently only expected to do one thing: fire the `onDidChange` event.
4. The `SpeechToTextEvent` event has a status (started, recognizing, recognized, etc) and optional `text`. I assume the UI will respond based on the event's status.

#### Questions

* Since the speech API doesn't include any audio data, I assume that the provider will have to also listen to the microphone. Is there existing infrastructure for this in the codebase, Electron/browser APIs, or perhaps an npm package?
* Which AI providers have speech-to-text APIs and how do we integrate with them?
* How should the UI handle multiple AI providers offering speech-to-text APIs?

title: Assistant: need a way to get runtime session execution history
description:
In #8495, `ChatContext` was changed so that it no longer included `activeSession`, which is information about the current language session. Databot makes use of the execution history, which was previously available in `activeSession`. 

It would be useful to have a way to get the execution history, without using a `vscode.ChatRequest`, since Databot doesn't use that.

title: Provide an indicator that an operation uses a lot of tokens

title: Assistant: improve error messaging in chat when output tokens exceeded
description:
## Describe the issue:

From user feedback:

> When responses hit token limits, the Assistant fails mid-sentence with an opaque error message rather than a “limit reached” notification.

This makes it difficult for users to understand:
1. Why the response stopped abruptly
2. That the model successfully processed the request but ran out of output tokens
3. What action they should take (e.g., ask the model to continue, rephrase the question, etc.)

## Steps to reproduce the issue:

Speculative steps to reproduce based on the issue description:

1. Set `positron.assistant.maxOutputTokens` for a model to the lowest value 512 
2. With that model selected in chat, ask a question that requires a very long response (e.g., "Explain in detail every function in this large file" or "Write a comprehensive description of ABC")
3. Observe that the response cuts off mid-sentence with a generic error message

## Expected or desired behavior:

- Can we determine in advance that a response will exceed the output token limit based on the input and model parameters, and proactively warn the user before they submit the request?
- If not, when the response is truncated due to hitting the output token limit, ideas on what Assistant could do:
    - display a clear, user-friendly notification indicating the response was truncated (e.g., "Response truncated: output token limit reached")
	- ask the user to start a new chat and add any relevant context
	- ask the user to rephrase the question to be more specific or narrow in scope
	- ask the user to increase the `maxOutputTokens` setting for future requests

## Were there any error messages in the UI, Output panel, or Developer Tools console?

We'll need a repro to confirm, but based on the user report, the error message in chat is opaque and does not clearly indicate that the response was truncated due to hitting the output token limit.

title: Assistant: `inspectVariables` tool returns same information as in session context
description: ## System details: #### Positron and OS details: Positron Version: 2025.09.0 build 41 Code - OSS Version: 1.102.0 Commit: fd2186c301ecb6913b9614e22fe22c5423c6acdc Date: 2025-08-11T03:42:41.022Z Electron: 35.6.0 Chromium: 134.0.6998.205 Node.js: 22.15.1 V8: 13.4.114.21-electron.0 OS: Darwin arm64 24.6.0 #### Session details: Positron 3.11.12 ## Describe the issue: The `inspectVariables` tool provides the same information that's already included in the session context. ## Steps to reproduce the issue: 1. Open an R or Python console 2. In the console, run code that sets a variable to some value, like `x = 1`. 3. Set Log Level to Trace 4. In the chat panel, ask, "What variables are in my session? Use the `inspectVariables` tool." It will make a tool call using that tool. 6. In the Output panel, look at the Assistant logs. The first request will contain the following message: ``` { "role": "user", "content": [ { "type": "text", "text": "\nThe user has attached information about their interactive interpreter session below. This session is running alongside the conversation with you in the Positron IDE.\n\n\n{\n \"identifier\": \"python-553860d4\",\n \"language\": \"Python\",\n \"languageId\": \"python\",\n \"version\": \"3.13.3\",\n \"mode\": \"console\",\n \"executions\": [\n {\n \"input\": \"x = 1\",\n \"output\": \"\"\n }\n ]\n}\n\n[\n {\n \"access_key\": \"{\\\"type\\\":\\\"str\\\",\\\"data\\\":\\\"x\\\"}\",\n \"display_name\": \"x\",\n \"display_type\": \"int\",\n \"display_value\": \"1\",\n \"has_children\": false,\n \"has_viewer\": false,\n \"is_truncated\": false,\n \"kind\": \"number\",\n \"length\": 0,\n \"size\": 28,\n \"type_info\": \"int\",\n \"updated_time\": 1755723303059\n }\n]\n\n\n\n\n\n\nPositron version: 2025.09.0-41\n\n\n\nToday's date is: Wednesday, August 20, 2025 at 03:55:17 PM CDT\n\n" } ] } ``` The relevant part of the content looks like this when unescaped: ```json [ { "access_key": "{\"type\":\"str\",\"data\":\"x\"}", "display_name": "x", "display_type": "int", "display_value": "1", "has_children": false, "has_viewer": false, "is_truncated": false, "kind": "number", "length": 0, "size": 28, "type_info": "int", "updated_time": 1755723303059 } ] ``` Also in the log, it will show the result of the tool call, which has the same information: ``` { "role": "user", "content": [ { "type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "toolu_01DuPnfZgxcXoQBQQP12sGjC", "content": [ { "type": "text", "text": "[[{\"access_key\":\"{\\\"type\\\":\\\"str\\\",\\\"data\\\":\\\"x\\\"}\",\"display_name\":\"x\",\"display_type\":\"int\",\"display_value\":\"1\",\"has_children\":false,\"has_viewer\":false,\"is_truncated\":false,\"kind\":\"number\",\"length\":0,\"size\":28,\"type_info\":\"int\",\"updated_time\":1755723361347}]]" } ] } ] } ``` When unescaped, the text looks lik ethis: ```json [ [ { "access_key": "{\"type\":\"str\",\"data\":\"x\"}", "display_name": "x", "display_type": "int", "display_value": "1", "has_children": false, "has_viewer": false, "is_truncated": false, "kind": "number", "length": 0, "size": 28, "type_info": "int", "updated_time": 1755723361347 } ] ] ``` Since they contain the same information, I don't think the `inspectVariables` tool is helpful for the LLM -- but the LLM doesn't know ahead of time that the information is redundant, so it still sometimes calls the tool. This issue is worth thinking about in relation to #8992, where we're discussing simplifying the content included in the session context. I think we should decide what the purpose of the `inspectVariables` tool is. If it is just to provide the same information as the session context, then I don't think `inspectVariables` has a purpose. But if the session context is simplified, then perhaps the `inspectVariables` tool still could be useful, by providing more detailed information. But what information should that be?

title: Base URL env vars should not overwrite user-configured settings
description:
The `*_BASE_URL` environment variable sync in the authentication extension unconditionally overwrites the user's global setting on every activation. If a user sets a base URL env var in their environment and later manually configures a different base URL in settings, the env var wins every startup and the user's setting is lost.

## Affected providers

- Anthropic (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`)
- OpenAI (`OPENAI_BASE_URL`)
- Gemini (`GEMINI_BASE_URL`)

## Current behavior

In each `register*Provider` function in `extensions/authentication/src/extension.ts`, the env var is written to the global setting unconditionally:

```typescript
const envBaseUrl = process.env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL;
if (envBaseUrl) {
    await vscode.workspace
        .getConfiguration('authentication.anthropic')
        .update('baseUrl', envBaseUrl, vscode.ConfigurationTarget.Global);
}
```

## Discussion

Two separate questions need to be decided:

1. **Precedence** -- should user settings or env vars take priority at runtime?
2. **Persistence** -- regardless of precedence, should the env var overwrite the stored setting? Even if env var takes priority, it could be read at runtime without persisting, so the user's setting is preserved when the env var is later removed.

## Context

Raised during review of posit-dev/positron#12870 ([comment](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/12870#discussion_r3052368663)).

title: R test explorer: a test file's items go stale when its contents change outside the editor
description:
Split out from comments on https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/2929#issuecomment-3566945287 and https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/2638#issuecomment-3750972095. The file-level cases (a test file added / removed / renamed) are handled by #14492; this issue covers the remaining case where an existing file's contents change out of band. Pulling this out into its own issue, so it can soon receive a clean PR to close it.

When an R test file's contents change via a write that doesn't go through the Positron editor -- switching git branches, or an external tool / LLM agent editing the file -- the test explorer keeps showing the file's old test items. Editing and saving the file in Positron refreshes correctly; out-of-band changes do not.

Steps to reproduce

1. Open an R package using testthat; open the Testing view.
2. Pick a test file with a single test_that(); confirm its one item appears under the file in the tree.
3. Change the file's contents without editing it in Positron -- e.g. git switch to a branch where the file has a different set of tests, or have an external tool/agent add or remove a test_that().
4. Observe the tree.

The file's items should match the new on-disk contents: added tests appear, removed tests disappear, renamed descriptions update.

Currently, the items are stale -- a removed test lingers, an added test never shows -- until the file is edited and saved in the editor (or the window is reloaded).

Likely cause

`onDidChange` does fire and a re-parse runs, but `getMatchesForQuery` in `extensions/positron-r/src/testing/parser.ts` reads the file via `vscode.workspace.openTextDocument(uri).getText()`. That document cache returns stale content for a file changed outside the editor, so the re-parse sees the old text. Reading from disk (`vscode.workspace.fs.readFile`) should fix it -- and better matches what testthat actually runs.

title: Ext host test flake: positron API - runtime, register a runtime manager
description:
This test flakes pretty regularly.

```
  1 failing
  1) positron API - runtime
       register a runtime manager:
     Error: Timeout: runtimes should be registered after 20 seconds.
Did not pass accept function
      at poll (extensions/vscode-api-tests/src/utils.ts:176:10)
      at Context.<anonymous> (extensions/vscode-api-tests/src/singlefolder-tests/positron/runtime.test.ts:480:3)
```

Claude's analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

I dug through the registration/discovery flow. This is a startup race, and the `vscode-api-tests` harness makes it likely to lose.

### What the test depends on

When the test calls:

```ts
registerLanguageRuntimeManager('test', manager)
```

whether the manager's `discoverAllRuntimes()` ever runs depends on the ext-host flag `_runtimeDiscoveryComplete` at that instant.

**Reference:** `extHostLanguageRuntime.ts:1365`

```ts
if (this._runtimeDiscoveryComplete) {
    // flag already TRUE -> self-discover right now
    // (IIFE invokes the generator)
}

// flag FALSE -> just push to _runtimeManagers and HOPE
// the discovery enumeration pass iterates the list later
```

There are only two ways the test runtime gets registered:

### 1. Discovery already complete ✅

The flag is already `true` when the test registers.

The IIFE at line 1372 runs the generator immediately.

### 2. Discovery still in progress ✅

The flag is still `false`, the manager is stored in `_runtimeManagers`, and a later enumeration pass (`$discoverLanguageRuntimes`) walks the list and calls each manager's generator.

**Reference:** `extHostLanguageRuntime.ts:1054`

---

## Where it breaks: the warm-start fast path

There is a third path that sets the flag without performing any enumeration:

**Reference:** `extHostLanguageRuntime.ts:1088`

```ts
public $markRuntimeDiscoveryComplete(): void {
    this._runtimeDiscoveryComplete = true;
}
```

This is driven by the warm-start fast path in `RuntimeStartupService`, which is taken whenever no runtime manager requires a real discovery pass.

**Reference:** `runtimeStartup.ts:1033-1046`

```ts
if (plans.length === 0) {
    for (const manager of this._runtimeManagers) {
        manager.markDiscoveryComplete();
    }
}
```

In the `vscode-api-tests` harness there are no real Python/R interpreters or language packs, so `plans.length === 0` is effectively the normal path.

That makes the outcome a pure ordering race:

### Scenario A: Registration happens after discovery completes ✅

```
$markRuntimeDiscoveryComplete()
        ↓
_runtimeDiscoveryComplete = true
        ↓
registerLanguageRuntimeManager('test')
        ↓
IIFE runs immediately
        ↓
runtime registered
```

Result: **Pass**

### Scenario B: Registration happens before discovery completes ❌

```
registerLanguageRuntimeManager('test')
        ↓
_runtimeDiscoveryComplete = false
        ↓
manager added to _runtimeManagers
        ↓
$markRuntimeDiscoveryComplete()
        ↓
flag flips to true
        ↓
NO enumeration occurs
        ↓
test manager remains stranded forever
```

Result:

```ts
getRegisteredRuntimes() === []
```

Eventually the test fails with:

> "Did not pass accept function"

and times out after 20 seconds.

Because extension activation and runtime startup execute concurrently, CI timing determines which side wins.

Polling cannot recover from this state; once the manager is stranded, it is stranded permanently.

---

## Proposed Fix

The cleanest product fix is to close the gap in the warm-start path.

Instead of using a separate "mark complete" path that skips ext-host enumeration, route warm starts through the normal discovery mechanism while supplying the cache-satisfied languages in the skip set.

`discoverLanguageRuntimes()` already supports filtering via a skip set:

**Reference:** `extHostLanguageRuntime.ts:1156`

This preserves the warm-start optimization:

- Built-in Python/R managers remain skipped and do not rescan the filesystem.
- Newly registered managers (such as the test manager) still receive enumeration.
- `_runtimeDiscoveryComplete` is set normally at the end of discovery.

Conceptually:

```ts
// current
manager.markDiscoveryComplete();

// proposed
manager.discoverAllRuntimes(disabled, allCachedLanguageIds);
```

### Why not enumerate everything during `markDiscoveryComplete()`?

A blanket "enumerate all `_runtimeManagers`" fix would be incorrect.

The ext-host side cannot distinguish:

- managers already satisfied by cached discovery results
- newly registered managers that still need discovery

As a result, built-in runtime managers could be rediscovered unnecessarily, defeating the warm-start optimization.

The skip-set approach preserves the optimization while eliminating the race.

---

## Suggested Follow-up

I can implement the skip-set fix and add a regression test that exercises this sequence:

1. Register a runtime manager while discovery is still incomplete.
2. Trigger the warm-start completion path.
3. Verify the newly registered manager is still discovered and registered.

That should reliably cover the race condition currently causing the intermittent API test failures.

Would be good to have @jmcphers give his 2 cents!

#14356 adds a main AI switch for AI features in positron `ai.enabled`, which Notebooks features listen to as well.

However, there are multiple Notebooks settings to turn on in order to enable the various Notebooks AI features. This makes discovery of Notebooks AI features difficult, and also hard to keep track of whether the right Notebooks settings are configured properly.

title: Enhanced Environments Management pane
description:
Building off of #1369.

Package and environments management with renv and venv are similar in motion to version control -- make some changes, see the effects, commit (snapshot or freeze) them. Similar to the Git Pane in RStudio, or the Git extension in VS Code, a `renv` or `venv` pane would make package snapshots  and environments management more in the forefront and easier for users to adopt and thoughtfully manage their environments.  

Having the repository source clearly identified as well (options("repos") or index-url from pip.conf) would go a long way in preventing surprises when packages are being installed from unexpected repositories.  

One could even envision a close integration with Package Manager and ability to browse repo snapshots from the IDE.

title: ark: Support indentation of vertically aligned arguments
description:
A common R code formatting convention is to vertically align function arguments. In RStudio, this behavior is called "Vertically align arguments in auto-indent" (Code -> Editing). 

We should support this convention in Positron to make it easier for people to format their code nicely, and to make it easier to transition from RStudio.

Currently our auto-indent rules are declarative:

https://github.com/rstudio/positron/blob/main/extensions/positron-r/language-configuration.json#L37-L47

Note however that LSPs can supply as-you-type formatters, which might allow us to adopt more complex or contextual behavior. 

https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.17/specification/#textDocument_onTypeFormatting

title: Assistant: refactor state storage
description:
## Background

There has been friction around updating Assistant, especially when provider IDs and auth state changes are made. Some of the workarounds have been:

- Log out & back into a provider, e.g., https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/discussions/11340
- Clear Assistant State, i.e., https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/10346

However, this requires the user to take manual steps to get unstuck and also involves some additional issue/discussion intake effort to direct users to a resolution.

Some of the reasons for this issue in the past:

- provider ID for a provider changed, and that means the user needs to manually specify the new provider ID and log in again
    - in #10866, we will be removing provider IDs from settings so that even if those change, the user will be unaffected
- github copilot auth mechanism changed, requiring the user to log out and back in
- crucially, we store a bunch of info in the secret storage that can become outdated due to changes in auth and settings, which the user can't easily clear

## For investigation

- what info is currently stored in the hard-to-access secret storage that is unnecessary to store there?
    - can we store just auth creds in secret storage and move everything else out
- can we store that info in user settings instead?
- is there any info that does not need to be stored at all?
- how can we migrate users smoothly from the existing storage method to this new storage method?
- with the new storage mechanism, what will be the new user experience if we make changes to auth/other Assistant state?
    - can we make the experience so smooth that the user does not need to take any manual actions?
- on upgrade of positron, can we avoid the log out and back in steps when auth changes occurs?
- how can we avoid issues with Assistant when positron upgrades?

title: Add e2e tests for Azure Foundry
description:
## Overview

Add e2e test coverage for the Azure (msFoundry) provider to support calling it GA. Currently, workbench managed credentials are covered ✅, but two additional auth paths need tests before branching.

## Background

The existing Azure sign-in test uses the model router (`selectModel('model-router')`). Per discussion with Sharon and Melissa, that coverage alone isn't sufficient confidence for a GA label — we need coverage of the other supported auth methods.

## Tasks

- [x] **API key + model router (desktop)**
  - Add a test that configures the Azure provider via API key and uses the model router
  - Run against desktop (not workbench — the workbench env is set up for managed creds)
  - API key (`Microsoft Azure Foundry API Key (East2TestAI)`) and base URL are in the **Positron** 1Password vault

- [x] **`positron.assistant.models.overrides.msFoundry` setting (workbench)**

title: GitHub Copilot provider not detected without deprecated `positron.assistant.enable` `true`
description:
In Positron 2026.06.0 build 211, GitHub Copilot is no longer detected as a model provider and GitHub inline completions stop working when the deprecated `"positron.assistant.enable": true` setting is absent in the user settings JSON.

The release notes state this setting is deprecated in favor of `assistant.enabled` (and that the older Positron Assistant will be removed in the next release). However, with only `assistant.enabled: true` set, GitHub Copilot does not work. Re-adding `"positron.assistant.enable": true` to user settings and restarting Positron restores both Copilot provider detection and inline completions.

This suggests GitHub Copilot integration is still coupled to the deprecated Positron Assistant rather than the new Posit Assistant, which breaks Copilot for users who follow the documented migration path.

### Reproduce

1. In user `settings.json`, set `"assistant.enabled": true` and remove/omit `"positron.assistant.enable"`.
2. Restart Positron.
3. Observe that GitHub Copilot is not listed as a provider and inline completions do not appear.
4. Add the following back to user settings:

   ```json
   "positron.assistant.enable": true
   ```

5. Restart Positron — GitHub Copilot provider detection and inline completions work again.

### Expected behavior

GitHub Copilot provider detection and inline completions should work without requiring the deprecated ` "positron.assistant.enable": true`.

### Environment

- Positron Version: 2026.06.0 build 211
- OS: macOS

### Additional context

The Copilot Chat output log shows successful authentication, chat activation, and `[fetchCompletions]` HTTP 200 responses once `positron.assistant.enable` is present.

title: Migrate notebook LLM features to the headless service
description:
Notebook LLM features (ghost cell suggestions today, more in the future) currently route requests through the assistant extension via `vscode.lm`. They should use the headless LLM service (#13728) directly.

## Goals

- **Workbench-owned model selection** -- users can choose and pin models from the workbench, not hidden behind extension internals
- **Unified credentials** -- no separate credential resolution path for notebook features
- **Lower latency** -- simpler call path without extension-host round-trip overhead
- **Foundation for future features** -- any notebook feature that needs LLM output (ghost cells, visualizations, quick actions, etc.) should use the same service

## Context

Ghost cell suggestions are the first consumer to migrate. This issue tracks the broader direction: all notebook LLM features should flow through the headless service rather than `vscode.lm`.

## Follow-ups

- [ ] Headless service reads `ai.models.*` (core model overrides, per #13814 / #14394) and applies them to the model listing, replacing the bridge `/models` call for the applicable providers (e.g. Custom Provider, Foundry). Discussion: https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/13730#discussion_r3423680317

title: Add a headless LLM streaming service to the workbench
description:
Positron needs a workbench-owned service that can stream LLM responses with built-in model selection, credential management, and provider enumeration.

## Goals

- **Model selection** -- callers express intent (fast/cheap tier, pattern match, or exact model ID) and the service resolves it against available providers
- **Model enumeration** -- a stable list of available models for picker UIs, updated on auth changes
- **Credential management** -- resolved from Positron's registered authentication providers, not duplicated per consumer
- **Multi-provider** -- works with Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Bedrock, and other providers via a shared registry
- **Simpler architecture** -- avoids routing through the extension host, reducing latency and coupling

## Context

Today, workbench features that want LLM output must go through the assistant extension. This leaves model selection opaque to the workbench and duplicates credential logic across consumers. A first-party service provides a single integration point for any workbench feature that needs LLM output, with explicit control over which model is used and how credentials are resolved.

title: Positron Assistant `executeCode` tool changes result structure depending on whether something is explicitly printed
description: ## System details: #### Positron and OS details: Positron Version: 2025.06.0 (Universal) build 28 Code - OSS Version: 1.99.0 Commit: 710d34a61ec4506c6bc9956516d0167e8a6a73e6 Date: 2025-05-05T03:33:25.846Z Electron: 34.3.2 Chromium: 132.0.6834.210 Node.js: 20.18.3 V8: 13.2.152.41-electron.0 OS: Darwin arm64 24.4.0 #### Interpreter details: R 4.4.2 ## Describe the issue: The result object returned from `executeCode` differs based on whether the code explicitly prints output. For example, if it runs: ```R 1:3 ``` It puts the text in `result`: ```json {"result":"[1] 1 2 3"} ``` If it runs a `print()` command, it puts the text in `outputText`: ```R print(4:6) ``` ```json {"outputText":"[1] 4 5 6\n"} ``` The interesting thing is that if it runs both the first code without the explicit print, and then the second code with the explicit print, the data structure ends up with all of the content in `outputText`: ```R 1:3 print(4:6) ``` ```json {"outputText":"[1] 1 2 3\n[1] 4 5 6\n"} ``` In most cases, this difference doesn't matter, since the LLM will figure out how to interpret the result. In my case, I am invoking the tool and then looking at the result before sending it to the LLM, so a consistent format would be helpful. To me, I think it makes sense to always put the text in `outputText`. ## Steps to reproduce the issue: In the Positron Assistant chat, you can ask it to provide the exact output it receives from running the tool. For example, you can give it this request: ```` Give me the exact JSON output you receive from running the following with the `executeCode` tool: ``` 1:3 ``` ````

title: Assistant: remember last used model per provider in chat
description:
## Summary
When switching between language model providers in chat, the system should remember and restore the last used model for each provider, rather than always defaulting to the preferred model from configuration or the first available model.

## Current Behaviour as of https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/9799
Currently, when a user switches between providers, the chat input always selects:
1. Preferred model from configuration (if set and available)
2. Default model for the provider
3. First available model as fallback

This means if a user manually selects a specific model (e.g., GPT-4) for Provider A, then switches to Provider B and back to Provider A, they lose their previous model selection and must manually select GPT-4 again, if GPT-4 is not the preferred or default model for the provider.

## Proposed Behaviour

1. **Remember the last manually selected model for each provider**
2. **Restore that model when switching back to the provider** (if still available)
3. **Fall back to current logic** only when no previous selection exists or the model is no longer available

Look for a link to this issue in `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chatInputPart.ts` once #9799 is merged, for some additional TODO comments.

## Notes

- not everyone is switching between multiple providers regularly in a chat conversation, so it may not be likely for users to hit this particular issue
- good to note if we have tests that switch between providers

title: Assistant: tools that are added conditionally may cost more tokens
description:
## System details:

#### Positron and OS details:

Positron Version: 2025.09.0 build 41
Code - OSS Version: 1.102.0
Commit: fd2186c301ecb6913b9614e22fe22c5423c6acdc
Date: 2025-08-11T03:42:41.022Z
Electron: 35.6.0
Chromium: 134.0.6998.205
Node.js: 22.15.1
V8: 13.4.114.21-electron.0
OS: Darwin arm64 24.5.0

#### Session details:

Claude 4 Sonnet

## Describe the issue:

I'm filing this here so that we can revisit it in the future when we have good evals in place.

Some tools are added and removed based on the current state of things in Positron. For example:

- The `inspectVariables` tool is added only if the R/Python session has any variables
- The `documentEdit` tool is added only if no text is selected
- The `selectionEdit` tool is added only if text is selected

https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/6c45e8c66215551479af65dd8d6b9c0578f2d190/extensions/positron-assistant/src/participants.ts#L266-L310

When the set of tools changes, this will result in a cache miss (because tools are listed first in the conversation), which will cost more tokens and increase response latency. 

If the user starts with an empty R session, and then runs some code that creates some variables, then this will result in a cache miss. Or if they select text, that will also result in a cache miss.

I can think of a couple reasons why it could make sense to add tools conditionally:

1. It reduces cost and increase speed by reducing the number of input tokens to the LLM
2. It improves the LLM's behavior

Now that we're using caching, (1) is no longer true, and in most cases it is more token-efficient to not adjust the set of tools sent to the LLM. I think it's an open question whether (2) is true. When we have a good set of evals, we can test it. If it turns out that adding/removing these tools doesn't improve performance, then I think we should just keep the tools there all the time.

## Describe the issue:

Participants such as `@shiny` can access tools registered by the Positron Assistant extension, including tools that are filtered out in certain chat modes.

For example, the edit file tool is not available in Ask mode in Positron Assistant, but when using `@shiny`, files can be edited in Ask mode. This can lead to confusion about the distinction between chat modes, as Ask is typically only for questions and code generation, not the editing of files (which is only expected in Edit/Agent modes).

## Steps to reproduce the issue:

1. In Ask mode, ask Positron Assistant to make edits to files
2. Positron Assistant will not edit files, but may provide code suggestions that can be applied to files
3. In Ask mode, use `@shiny` as part of the prompt, and ask Shiny Assistant to make edits to files
4. Shiny Assistant will edit files, but this can be unexpected in Ask mode

## Expected or desired behavior:

Possible directions to go in:

### Find a way to unregister tools, so that participants are unable to use filtered out tools

We apply tool filtering for Positron Assistant in participants.ts, but participants contributed via extensions such as Shiny Assistant won't have this filtering applied. We would need to de-register or otherwise properly remove tools that we don't want participants to use.

- related to https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/8290

### Clarify that participants may be able to use tools beyond the chat mode

Participants are only available in Ask mode (can we change this?) and participants may expect to make their own decisions about which tools to make available? If this is the case, maybe we can better document the difference between Ask/Edit/Agent with Positron Assistant, vs. Ask mode with chat participants which have separate tool filtering.

title: Deleting messages from Positron Assistant history sometimes does not actually delete them
description: ## System details: #### Positron and OS details: Positron Version: 2025.06.0 (Universal) build 39 Code - OSS Version: 1.99.0 Commit: 55dad0b8cac13849ee986eb3f46c75cfcaa599e0 Date: 2025-05-07T03:32:13.732Z Electron: 34.3.2 Chromium: 132.0.6834.210 Node.js: 20.18.3 V8: 13.2.152.41-electron.0 OS: Darwin arm64 24.4.0 ## Describe the issue: Deleting a message from the Positron Assistant history sometimes does not actually delete it; that message will be present in the `ChatContext.history` for future requests. This can cause problems because usually when the user deletes a message, there's a reason for it. For example, the question might have been misworded and led the LLM down a bad path. If that message (and the LLM's response) remains in the message history, then the LLM may keep trying to go down that path. ## Steps to reproduce the issue: 1. Close any active R or Python console sessions (they get included as context, which is just a distraction here). 2. Start a new chat by clicking the + button. 3. Type "Hello" and press Enter. The LLM will respond with a short message. 4. Type "Provide the exact content of every message I've sent to you." and press Enter. The LLM will respond by listing three messages: One with "Hello", one with a JSON object representing the console state, and the current message that you just sent. 5. Delete those messages by clicking on the X in the upper right of each. 6. Type "Provide the exact content of every message I've sent to you." and press Enter. After this last message, the LLM will respond with something like the following: > You've sent me the following messages: > > 1. Your first message was simply: "Hello" > 2. Your second message was: `{"console":{"language":"","version":"","executions":[]},"plots":{"hasPlots":false},"variables":[]}` > 3. Your third message was another JSON object with the same content: `{"console":{"language":"","version":"","executions":[]},"plots":{"hasPlots":false},"variables":[]}` > > Your current message asking me to provide the exact content of every message you've sent to me. (This was with Claude 3.7 Sonnet v1) It should not include the "Hello" message, and it should not include one of the console state messages. At least, I think it should not include past console states; only the present one. Including past states seems like too much information to me.

title: Assistant switching between AI models: remaining in the same chat can cause conflicts between models
description: ## System details: #### Positron and OS details: Positron Version: 2025.06.0 (Universal) build 39 Code - OSS Version: 1.99.0 Commit: 55dad0b8cac13849ee986eb3f46c75cfcaa599e0 Date: 2025-05-08T03:32:55.440Z Electron: 34.3.2 Chromium: 132.0.6834.210 Node.js: 20.18.3 V8: 13.2.152.41-electron.0 OS: Darwin arm64 24.4.0 #### Interpreter details: Python 3.13.0 ## Describe the issue: When user switches between AI models, conflicts can emerge. Additionally, user is able to switch models "on the fly", while answer to previous prompt is still being loaded. In AI tools in general, switching between models often triggers the creation of a new chat instead of remaining in the same one (e.g., Gemini, ChatGPT). This might be considered good practice to prevent models from having conflicts with each other. ## Steps to reproduce the issue: In addition to being able to switch models "on the fly", while answer to prompt is still being provided, the main issue to be observed here is the **conflict between models after switching**, due to the presence of previous context provided by the other model. 1. Select a **Gemini** model. Ask `tell me which model you are`. Assistant responds `I am a large language model, trained by Google.` 2. Select **Claude** (Anthropic) model. Ask `tell me which model you are`. Assistant responds `I apologize for my previous incorrect response. I am Claude, an AI assistant created by Anthropic. I aim to be direct and honest about my identity. I apologize for the earlier confusion where I incorrectly stated I was created by Google.` 3. Select **Gemini** model. Ask `tell me which model you are`. Assistant responds `I am Claude, an AI assistant created by Anthropic.` Assistant will keep answering that, despite the model being Gemini. This might be happening because Gemini assistant is catching the previous context in the same chat and not wanting to "lie to the user". ## Expected or desired behavior: Although this might seem like a small issue, there are other issues that may occur due to conflicts between models. This is just an example of behavior that demonstrates the conflict. In general, expectation would be that, when user selects a new model, new chat should be created, as it occurs in Gemini, ChatGPT, and other AI tools. ## Screenshot

title: Assistant: add test to check if AI-related features are enabled/disabled
description:
## Background

`positron.assistant.enable` is the setting that should gate whether any Positron Assistant-related AI functionality should be enabled or not. When it is set to `false`, features like the chat pane, Console Actions, inline chat, completions and Positron Notebooks AI-related features should **not** be present.

There have been a couple instances where AI-related UI has been present despite the underlying Assistant functionality being disabled. So it appeared that AI features were enabled by default, though even if the user interacted with those components, connecting to providers and making chat requests would not be possible as those parts were gated by the enablement flag.

See https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/11229 for a bit more context.

## Goals

- Ensure that all AI-related features are always dependent on `positron.assistant.enable`, and are disabled/hidden appropriately.
- Ensure that code merged does not introduce AI features/UI to Positron if the user has not yet opted in (by setting `positron.assistant.enable` to true). If the user has not enabled Assistant via the setting, no AI features/UI should be present.

## Possible Solution

One way to achieve this is to add a test which fails if AI-related features appear to be available despite `positron.assistant.enable` being set to false.

> Add a test that checks that various AI-related features are not present when `positron.assistant.enable = false`? This is the approach taken by upstream with their equivalent setting `chat.disableAIFeatures`: https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/test/smoke/src/areas/chat/chat.test.ts 

 _Originally posted by @sharon-wang in [#11229](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/11229#issuecomment-3712277502)_

We may also want to add a bit of dev documentation/AI-related implementation checklist to ensure that features depend on `positron.assistant.enable` being set to true.

title: Auth: support OpenAI's Plus/Pro accounts
description:
### Discussed in https://github.com/posit-dev/assistant-feedback/discussions/30 Moving to this repo as an issue as the authentication support needs to be added to Positron Authentication extension.
Originally posted by **huangjiang89** June 9, 2026 Hi Posit team — thank you for the continued work on Posit Assistant and Positron I understand that Posit Assistant currently focuses on Posit AI subscriptions and BYOK/API-key based providers, including OpenAI-compatible custom endpoints. That model makes sense for enterprise, team, and API-first workflows. I would like to ask whether the team would consider an additional provider/authentication option for individual local users: **A Codex/OpenAI account-based provider**, similar in spirit to how Codex clients and IDE integrations can use an authenticated ChatGPT/Codex account rather than requiring a raw OpenAI API key. ### Motivation OpenAI/ChatGPT already has a very large individual-user base. Public reports have put ChatGPT at hundreds of millions of weekly active users — for example, Sam Altman said ChatGPT had reached 800 million weekly active users in 2025. Many of these users are individual developers, data scientists, students, and researchers who already pay for ChatGPT/Codex access but may not have separate OpenAI API billing configured. For local IDE usage, it would be helpful if Posit Assistant could support an official account-based authentication path where available, instead of requiring users to set up a separate API key. This could make Posit Assistant more approachable for individual users while keeping the existing Posit AI subscription, BYOK, and custom-provider workflows intact. ### Existing precedent This does not seem to be only a theoretical request. OpenAI has described the Codex app-server architecture as a JSON-RPC protocol and long-lived process that hosts Codex core threads. The same architecture is used to integrate Codex clients through an app server / harness model. This makes account-authenticated local IDE-style Codex integrations different from ordinary `/v1/chat/completions` or `/v1/responses` API-key based providers. There are also existing examples and community interest around this direction. For example, Codex clients and IDE integrations such as VS Code, JetBrains IDEs, Xcode, the Codex desktop app, and the Codex CLI use a Codex-style client/server integration model. In the broader ecosystem, projects such as opencode openclaw have also had requests or plugins exploring OpenAI/Codex account-based authentication for personal development use. ### Possible direction https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs/app-server

title: R: Manually runnable hyperlinks can be pasted in the wrong console when multiple are active
description:
Follow up to https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/7313

With the following reprex:
- Start R console 1
- Start R console 2
- Run `cli::cli_alert("{.run revdepcheck::cloud_summary()}")` in R console 2 and click the hyperlink.
- The pasted code will incorrectly end up in R console 1.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/74cc62b3-d3ef-4f3b-89e0-ce1a284c66e4

This is due to our call to `positron.window.getConsoleForLanguage()` here:
https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/6af5bd88e7ff43e833efd238a6a9bc077800059a/extensions/positron-r/src/hyperlink.ts#L51

It chooses the wrong console due to how `$getSessionIdForLanguage()` works, which just chooses the first session id that matches the language id.

`$getSessionIdForLanguage()` was introduced in https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/7313, but that was to restore the original pre-multi-session-world behavior, since adding multi-session support accidentally broke the feature entirely.

This issue is about further enhancing `$getSessionIdForLanguage()` to correctly support multi-session, which means that `$getSessionIdForLanguage()` will need to switch from:

"choose the first session id that matches the language id"

to:

"choose the most recently active (and still alive) session id that matches the language id"

We may need some additional helper to query the most recently active session id for a language, I'm not sure yet.

description:
## Describe the issue:

This issue came up because when trying to install a package via python's Conda, the package was not found. This is because the package in question `cowsay` is not published there. This is confusing as I expected it to be.

I thought there was a bug with the Conda implementation. I had to research the appropriate `conda` commands just to verify the situation. Sure enough, it's not installed. Oh yeah, that's when I remembered why I use `pyfiglet` for testing with Conda instead.

It would be nice if the quick pick had a selection that let me open the search results in the browser. Assuming, this were possible it would allow the user to further troubleshoot the issue -- either a typo in the search, a misunderstanding of what is published in the repository, or some combination of factors.

Something "out of band" would be nice.

1. Try to install `cowsay`

Ideally, we could provide some additional affordance for the user to troubleshoot the issue, e.g. performing the search in the browser.

If a user has gotten to this point, they generally are motivated so anything to demonstrate that the lookup is working (even if returning no results) would go a long way.
