title: Reconnecting to a long-idle Workbench session after an Extension Host restart fails with `createSession` HTTP 401 (Kallichore rejects a stale bearer token); the session is unrecoverable
description:
## System details:

#### Positron and OS details:

- Positron 2026.04.1 build 10 (SHA `5dfc9242`), running on Posit Workbench 2026.04.0+526.pro2 (server / remote mode)
- Kallichore (Positron Kernel Supervisor) 0.1.64
- Ubuntu 22.04 on GKE; Helm chart `rstudio-workbench-0.10.15`; 2 HA rserver replicas; launcher namespace `workbench-prod`
- Home directories and `/var/lib/rstudio-server` on NFS, so `~/.positron-server` (where the supervisor's `workspaceState` lives) persists across session pods

#### Session details:

- R 4.4.3 and R 4.5.3 (reproduces on both)

## Describe the issue:

When a user returns to an **already-running** Positron-on-Workbench session after an extended idle period (>~10 minutes; reproduced at ~23 minutes), the R kernel fails to come back with:

```
R 4.4.3 failed to start.
HTTP 401
  at t.KCApi.createSession (...)
```

The session is unrecoverable from inside Positron: the only way out is to quit (losing all in-memory R state) and start a new session. New Positron sessions and RStudio Pro sessions in the same deployment are **not** affected — only an already-running, idle Positron session that has to reconnect.

The 401 is a Kallichore bearer-token rejection. The same single, long-lived `kcserver` instance serves the session for hours; it never restarts and its token never rotates. The failure begins only **after** an Extension Host restart (an `ERR_IPC_CHANNEL_CLOSED` crash storm) that follows the long-idle reconnect. On that restart the supervisor reconnects to the still-running `kcserver`, the unauthenticated reconnect/status check succeeds, and then the first authenticated call (`createSession` -> `new_session`) is rejected with 401.

Our leading hypothesis is that the supervisor reloads a **stale/invalid bearer token from persisted state** on the reconnect path and presents it to the running server instead of the live token. This came from support case 129704.

## Steps to reproduce the issue:

1. On Posit Workbench (server / remote mode), start a Positron session with an R interpreter and let the R kernel come up normally.
2. Leave the session idle long enough for the browser <-> server WebSocket to drop (>~10 min; ~23 min in our repro). rserver records the hung reconnect, e.g. `post: 1382.936s`.
3. Return to the session. The reconnect triggers an Extension Host restart (`ERR_IPC_CHANNEL_CLOSED`, host relaunches with new PIDs).
4. The supervisor reconnects to the existing Kallichore server and then attempts to (re)create the kernel session.

Observed: `Failed to create session '<id>': HTTP 401` at `KCApi.createSession`. The session cannot recover in place.

## Expected or desired behavior:

On Extension Host restart / reconnect, the supervisor should authenticate to the running Kallichore server with the **live** bearer token (in server mode, re-read the authoritative connection file rather than fall back to a persisted token), so `createSession` succeeds and the session reconnects cleanly. Failing that, the failure should be recoverable in-session (refresh the token and retry) rather than forcing the user to quit and lose R state, and the surfaced error should be clearer than an opaque `HTTP 401`.

## Were there any error messages in the UI, Output panel, or Developer Tools console?

Yes. The customer captured the Kernel Supervisor pane, the positron-server log from inside the session pod, and both rserver replica logs. Timeline (all UTC, 2026-06-08):

- `14:15:39` — rserver logs the hung reconnect WebSocket (`post: 1382.936s`, ~23 min idle).
- `14:15:44 – 14:15:46` — Kallichore (`kcserver`) logs, repeatedly: `[WARN] Rejecting request; invalid Bearer token '[BEARER_351395]' supplied` paired with `channels_upgrade: token validation failed for session r-67ff1a43`.
- `14:16:34` — Extension Host processes restart en masse with `ERR_IPC_CHANNEL_CLOSED`.
- `14:16:43` — `new_session("r-8ac592d3")` followed immediately by another `Rejecting request; invalid Bearer token '[BEARER_351395]'` (same token).
- `14:18:18` — Kernel Supervisor pane: `Connected to previously established supervisor` / `Kallichore 0.1.64 server reconnected with 1 sessions` (the unauthenticated status check succeeds), then `Creating session r-37c93df2`.
- `14:18:20` — `Failed to create session 'r-37c93df2': HTTP 401`, stack terminating in `t.KCApi.createSession`.

## Mechanism / where we think the bug is

The "reconnect succeeds, then the first authenticated call 401s" sequence is explained by Kallichore's auth model: `validate_token()` gates `new_session` and `channels_upgrade` but **not** `server_status`. So a stale token passes the reconnect status check and fails on the first state-changing call (`createSession` -> `new_session`). Verified in `posit-dev/kallichore` `crates/kcserver/src/server.rs` @ `db7d370`:

- `validate_token()` — https://github.com/posit-dev/kallichore/blob/db7d3707fa3835b5e70697592cced8812931c735/crates/kcserver/src/server.rs#L1077
- `new_session` gates on it (call at L1380) — https://github.com/posit-dev/kallichore/blob/db7d3707fa3835b5e70697592cced8812931c735/crates/kcserver/src/server.rs#L1366-L1380
- `channels_upgrade` gates on it (call at L1624) — https://github.com/posit-dev/kallichore/blob/db7d3707fa3835b5e70697592cced8812931c735/crates/kcserver/src/server.rs#L1616-L1624
- `server_status` does **not** (no `validate_token` in its body) — https://github.com/posit-dev/kallichore/blob/db7d3707fa3835b5e70697592cced8812931c735/crates/kcserver/src/server.rs#L2065

On the supervisor side, the bearer token is persisted in VS Code `workspaceState` and reloaded on reconnect. Verified in `extensions/positron-supervisor/src/` @ `ffb7c18`:

- `KallichoreServerState.bearer_token` — https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/ffb7c189f0eb3102726467290703b0d549a6ff40/extensions/positron-supervisor/src/ServerState.ts#L27
- `start()` prefers the authoritative connection file (`POSITRON_SUPERVISOR_CONNECTION_FILE`, fresh disk read) but falls back to `loadServerState()` (workspaceState) when that path does not short-circuit — https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/ffb7c189f0eb3102726467290703b0d549a6ff40/extensions/positron-supervisor/src/KallichoreAdapterApi.ts#L246-L308
- `saveServerState()` -> `workspaceState.update(...)` — https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/ffb7c189f0eb3102726467290703b0d549a6ff40/extensions/positron-supervisor/src/KallichoreAdapterApi.ts#L755
- `loadServerState()` -> `workspaceState.get(...)` — https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/ffb7c189f0eb3102726467290703b0d549a6ff40/extensions/positron-supervisor/src/KallichoreAdapterApi.ts#L763-L764

In remote/server mode `workspaceState` is persisted under `~/.positron-server` on the NFS home, so a bearer token from a **prior** Kallichore instance can linger there across session pods and be reloaded on the post-crash reconnect, mismatching the token the currently-running `kcserver` enforces. An in-memory token desync on Extension Host relaunch (the relaunched host reloads/re-derives the token incorrectly and never re-reads the connection file) fits the same symptom and is the alternate. Either way it is a supervisor token-lifecycle defect on the reconnect path, not a customer misconfiguration.

## Evidence status (what is proven vs. inferred)

To be precise about what the capture does and does not establish:

- **Solid:** the user-visible failure is `createSession` -> `HTTP 401` for session `r-37c93df2` (Kernel Supervisor pane).
- **Solid, source-confirmed:** the Kallichore auth model above, which explains the reconnect-succeeds-then-401 sequence.
- **Real, but a different session:** the `invalid Bearer token` rejections in hand are logged against sibling sessions in the same pod/window (`channels_upgrade` for `r-67ff1a43`; `new_session` for `r-8ac592d3`), showing the failure mode is live here — but they are not the same session ID as the 401.
- **Gap:** the two session-pod capture files come from different pods/sessions (disjoint session IDs, different `kcserver` start times, a second user present), so we do **not** yet have a single same-session, same-pod trace where the session that throws the 401 is the one Kallichore logs rejecting the token. This is a strong inference (front half: the 401; back half: a real token rejection), not a single demonstrated chain.

Also ruled out for this 401: HA (PostgreSQL + matched secure-cookie key), OIDC/Entra login, and an unrelated `invalid_grant` flood (`rstudio/rstudio-pro#10922`) — the rserver replica logs show no real auth-401 in the incident window, so this is purely intra-pod (supervisor <-> Kallichore).

## What would pinpoint it (capture requested in parallel)

We have asked the customer for one more capture, all from the **single session pod that throws the 401**, collected before the session is quit (the pod auto-cleans on quit):

1. The Kernel Supervisor pane output (the 401).
2. The supervisor's Kallichore server log and connection file from that pod — `~/.positron-server/positron-supervisor-*.log` (where the `invalid Bearer token` line is written) and `~/.positron-server/positron-supervisor-*.json` (the live `bearer_token`).
3. The broader positron-server session log from that pod (the `ERR_IPC_CHANNEL_CLOSED` extension-host context).

That gets the matched same-session trace and lets us compare the rejected token against the live connection-file token to locate the stale source (persisted `workspaceState` vs. in-memory). We will add it to this issue as a comment when it arrives.

## Related issues

- `posit-dev/kallichore#4` — "Validate bearer token when creating websocket connection." The validation behind the `channels_upgrade: token validation failed` line.
- `posit-dev/positron#12476` — "Session terminated instead of reconnecting after extension host restart on Windows." Different symptom/OS, same problem family (supervisor reconnect after ext-host restart).
- `posit-dev/positron#6725` (closed) — "Multisession console: additional console cannot reconnect after 'Restart extension host'." Adjacent reconnect-after-ext-host-restart failure.
- `posit-dev/positron#8000` (closed) — supervisor create->connect timeout; different failure mode, same area.

No existing issue covers this exact symptom (supervisor presenting a stale bearer token that Kallichore rejects on reconnect, surfacing as a `createSession` 401 with no in-session recovery).

title: Assistant: simplify copilot completions language filtering settings
description:
## Background

We have two settings that both gate inline completions for Copilot with the same `{ [languageId]: boolean }` shape:

- `github.copilot.enable` — default `{ "*": true, "plaintext": false, "markdown": false, "scminput": false }`
- `positron.assistant.inlineCompletions.enable` — default `{ "*": true }`

Let's review how we read these settings in the `positron-copilot-chat` extension, as it affects Copilot NES and regular ghost text completions. We might have some inconsistencies here that we can clean up, as we roll back to stock Copilot, and we can simplify to just the `github.copilot.enable` setting.

I'm not sure if the `github.copilot.enable` setting was introduced before or after the `positron.assistant.inlineCompletions.enable` setting, but it seems like we probably want to just have the one github copilot one.

## Proposal

Remove `positron.assistant.inlineCompletions.enable` and use `github.copilot.enable` as the only setting controlling this. Copilot is the only provider using this setting currently, and Posit AI NES has its own `nextEditSuggestions.enable` (see #13541) and isn't affected.

Something like:

- Update [positronAssistantService.areCompletionsEnabled](../src/vs/workbench/contrib/positronAssistant/browser/positronAssistantService.ts) and the patched files in `positron-copilot-chat` (`documentFilter.ts`, `inlineCompletionProvider.ts`, `completions-core/.../config.ts`) to read `github.copilot.enable`.
- Update the "Toggle Inline Completions" command in [positron-assistant/extension.ts](../extensions/positron-assistant/src/extension.ts) to write to `github.copilot.enable`.
- Drop the `positron.assistant.inlineCompletions.enable` contribution from `positron-assistant/package.json` and the localized description.
- Migrate any existing `positron.assistant.inlineCompletions.enable` values into `github.copilot.enable`.


## Notes

- check if Workbench admins are setting this `positron.assistant.inlineCompletions.enable` and if we need to support backwards-compat/migration

title: Unable to launch Positron as non-admin user on Azure Virtual Desktop with FSLogix profiles
description:
## System details:

#### Positron and OS details:

Positron Version: 2026.07.0 (system setup) build 365
Code - OSS Version: 1.118.0
Commit: a0ebe4c3e2d2a9fd747f06ba0394d40ebfcb1dab
Date: 2026-07-02T10:53:06-07:00
Electron: 39.8.8
Chromium: 142.0.7444.265
Node.js: 22.22.1
V8: 14.2.231.22-electron.0
OS: Windows_NT x64 10.0.26100

OS more importantly: Windows 11 Enterprise Multi-Session (Azure Virtual Desktop, FSLogix profile containers)


### Steps to reproduce

1. Deploy Positron system-wide on an AVD host with FSLogix profile containers
2. Log in as a non-admin user
3. Launch Positron

### Observed behaviour

Positron fails immediately on startup with no GUI appearing. Console output:

```powershell
PS C:\WINDOWS\system32> & "C:\R\Positron\Positron.exe"
[main 2026-07-09T11:37:27.281Z] [PolicyConfiguration] No admin policy service provided
[main 2026-07-09T11:37:27.320Z] Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, mkdir 'c:\Users\5580\.positron\extensions'
[main 2026-07-09T11:37:27.369Z] FileOperationError: Unable to write file 'c:\Users\5580\AppData\Roaming\Positron\User\globalStorage\storage.json' (EntryNotFound (FileSystemError): File to move/copy does not exist)
    at FileService.writeFile (file:///C:/R/Positron/resources/app/out/main.js:56908:17)
    at async FileStorage.doSave (file:///C:/R/Positron/resources/app/out/main.js:21852:11) {
  fileOperationResult: 1,
  options: { atomic: { postfix: '.vsctmp' } }
}
```

### Root cause

The failure originates in Electron's `os_crypt` component, which calls DPAPI during early initialisation to encrypt its local state. DPAPI requires `%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Protect\<SID>` to exist and be initialised. Under FSLogix-managed AVD profiles, this path is missing or present as a broken reparse point with a zero timestamp (`1-1-1601`), causing DPAPI to return `0x3` (`ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND`).

This can be confirmed independently of Positron via PowerShell as the affected user:

```powershell
Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Security
$null = [System.Security.Cryptography.ProtectedData]::Protect(
    [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes("test"),
    $null,
    [System.Security.Cryptography.DataProtectionScope]::CurrentUser
)
# Returns: Exception: "Het systeem kan het opgegeven pad niet vinden." (path not found, 0x3)
```

Because `os_crypt` fails before the Electron `app` object is initialised, the error handler itself crashes, producing the misleading `application not set` message. The subsequent `ENOENT mkdir` error is a secondary crash artifact, not the root cause.

Launching as an admin user works correctly, as admin profiles have a functioning `Microsoft\Protect` path.

### Relation to RStudio issue

This is the same failure mode as rstudio/rstudio#16552, where RStudio Desktop also fails to launch for non-admin users on Windows multi-session/VDI hosts from version 2025.09.x onward. Both applications share the same Electron base and exhibit identical behaviour. The RStudio issue confirmed that reverting to an older build (2025.05.1) resolves the problem, suggesting a regression was introduced in Electron or in how `os_crypt` is called in more recent builds.

See especially comment <https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/16552#issuecomment-4382506333> on this, from an RStudio employee.

### Workaround

Launch Positron via `runas` with an admin account:

```powershell
C:\Windows\System32\runas.exe /user:DOMAIN\adminaccount "C:\path\to\Positron.exe"
```

### Expected behaviour

Positron should launch normally for non-admin users in FSLogix-managed AVD environments, or failing that, present a meaningful error message indicating the DPAPI initialisation failure.

title: Assistant: migrate provider enablement settings from Positron Assistant
description:
Summary

- [ ] Let's migrate the `positron.assistant.provider.<PROVIDER>.enable` settings to `assistant.provider.<PROVIDER>.enabled` <-- with a D!
- [ ] Update positron.posit.co docs to reflect the new settings
- [ ] Update pos.it/assistant-docs to reflect the new settings
- [ ] Update Workbench docs re: the new settings

The reader at `positronAssistantService.ts` already accepts `assistant.provider.<vendor>.enabled` and falls back to the legacy `positron.assistant.provider.<vendor>.enable`, so the read-side work for the 9 positron-assistant keys is mostly done, but we will want to change to the auth extension version of the settings.

We will need to migrate the existing settings to the new one though, and think about how to migrate user settings vs admin-enforced settings.

### Current State in Auth

The Authentication extension already declares two enablement keys, both in the `assistant.provider.*` namespace, both tagged experimental:

- `assistant.provider.googleVertex.enabled`
- `assistant.provider.deepseek.enabled`

9 keys below from `positron-assistant`:

- `positron.assistant.provider.anthropic.enable`
- `positron.assistant.provider.githubCopilot.enable`
- `positron.assistant.provider.amazonBedrock.enable`
- `positron.assistant.provider.snowflakeCortex.enable`
- `positron.assistant.provider.msFoundry.enable`
- `positron.assistant.provider.openAI.enable`
- `positron.assistant.provider.customProvider.enable`
- `positron.assistant.provider.positAI.enable`
- `positron.assistant.provider.google.enable`

Move every enablement key under the `authentication.` namespace in the Auth extension. The existing two `assistant.provider.*` keys get renamed in place.

Migrate `positron.assistant.provider.<vendor>.enable` → `authentication.<vendor>.enabled`

Setting | Action
-- | --
authentication.anthropic.enabled | Declare in Auth
authentication.github.enabled | Declare in AuthgithubCopilot -> github
authentication.aws.enabled | Declare in AuthamazonBedrock -> aws (matches the actual credential, AWS)
authentication.snowflake.enabled | Declare in AuthsnowflakeCortex -> snowflake
authentication.msFoundry.enabled | Declare in Auth
authentication.openAI.enabled | Declare in Auth
authentication.customProvider.enabled | Declare in Auth
authentication.positAI.enabled | Declare in Auth
authentication.gemini.enabled | Declare in Authgoogle -> gemini (the product is Gemini Code Assist; "google" collides with googleCloud and is ambiguous). Note: this is a coordinated rename -- the auth-provider ID in code is literally 'google' (GEMINI_AUTH_PROVIDER_ID and settingName: 'google' in providerSources.ts). The setting rename only makes sense if we also rename those.
authentication.googleCloud.enabled | Rename from assistant.provider.googleVertex.enabledgoogleVertex -> googleCloud (matches the auth ID google-cloud; "Google Cloud" reads better than "Vertex" since the credential is GCP-wide)
authentication.deepseek.enabled | Rename from assistant.provider.deepseek.enabled

Related
- https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/13354

title: Headless LM service: resolve credentials via a pull model (remove AUTH_PROVIDER_MAP duplication)
description:
Follow-up to #13730. Part of #13729. Depends on #13730 and [assistant#1427](https://github.com/posit-dev/assistant/pull/1427) merging first.

This is an architectural refactor with no user-facing behavior change.

## Problem

The headless LM service keeps two copies of the same provider knowledge in sync. The renderer maintains `AUTH_PROVIDER_MAP` -- a hand-written mapping of auth provider IDs to bridge provider IDs and credential types -- which duplicates the `PROVIDER_MAP` that `ai-provider-bridge` already exports. They are kept aligned only by a unit test, and that test compares against whatever bridge version happens to be installed, so it only catches drift at dependency-bump time, never when the bridge changes upstream. A brand-new bridge provider is not caught at all.

The duplication exists because credentials are resolved in the renderer and *pushed* across IPC to the shared process on every model-discovery and stream request, so the renderer has to know provider-to-auth mappings that otherwise belong entirely to the bridge. This is a regression from the assistant extension's design, which had no duplication (single process, imported `PROVIDER_MAP` directly, pulled credentials on demand).

## Solution

Invert the credential flow from a push model to a pull model that mirrors the assistant extension:

- The shared process imports `PROVIDER_MAP` from the bridge directly and becomes the single owner of provider knowledge.
- When it needs a credential it *pulls* it from the renderer via a thin credential channel ("give me a token for auth provider X of type Y"). The renderer answers from `IAuthenticationService` without knowing about bridge providers.
- `AUTH_PROVIDER_MAP` and its sync test are deleted; the renderer no longer transmits credentials in its model/stream calls.

Net: a deletion overall, a deeper module boundary, and behavior identical to today.

## Modules (tests for both deep modules)

- **Deep module 1 -- renderer credential server.** A small renderer-registered IPC service: `getCredentials(authProviderId, credentialType) -> IpcCredentials | undefined`. Owns the `IAuthenticationService.getSessions()` call + the token-shape transform (apikey / oauth / aws-credentials) currently in `_resolveCredentials`. Test with a fake `IAuthenticationService`.
- **Deep module 2 -- shared-process credential adapter.** Maps a bridge `providerId` to `{ authProviderId, credentialType }` via the bridge's `PROVIDER_MAP`, then pulls the token from the renderer channel. Concentrates all provider-mapping knowledge in the shared process; eliminates `AUTH_PROVIDER_MAP`. Test with a fake channel client.
- **Supporting (deletion/wiring).** `AbstractPositronLMService` loses `AUTH_PROVIDER_MAP`, `_resolveCredentials`, `_resolveAllCredentials`, `_findAuthEntryForProvider`; keeps the model cache and `onDidChangeSessions`-driven refresh (cache invalidation stays renderer-driven). `IpcGetModelsArgs`/`IpcStreamTextArgs` drop their `credentials` field.

## Reverse-direction IPC

The credential channel is registered by the renderer and consumed by the shared process -- the reverse of the usual direction. Prior art: `IExtensionRecommendationNotificationService` (renderer registers via `sharedProcessService.registerChannel`, shared process consumes via a client routed to the active window with `ActiveWindowManager` + `StaticRouter`); `ProxyChannel.fromService`/`toService` for transparent proxying.

- **Desktop** (renderer <-> shared process): implemented here; well precedented.
- **Web/remote** (browser <-> remote agent): the reverse channel here is less precedented and needs a short spike. If not cleanly supported, web/remote may keep the push model temporarily, gating `AUTH_PROVIDER_MAP` deletion on both deployments. The desktop refactor does not block on this.

## Out of scope

- Provider registration / display names / priority consolidation (tracked separately in the ai-provider-bridge single-source-of-truth issue).
- Auth provider registration in `extensions/authentication/` (irreducible for new credentials).
- Any change to the public `IPositronLMService` interface.

## Why this is safe as a follow-up

The IPC protocol and the hardcoded map are fully internal (both ends ship in the same build, no external compatibility), and the migration is mechanical deletion/delegation -- no lock-in, no compounding cost. Token rotation is preserved (credentials pulled fresh per request).

title: Migrate Positron notebook editor modals to the new PositronModalDialogReactRenderer API
description:
## Summary

The Positron notebook editor has three custom React modal dialogs still built on the older `PositronModalReactRenderer` (custom overlay div). Migrate them to the newer `PositronModalDialogReactRenderer`, which is backed by the native HTML `<dialog>` element + `showModal()`.

## Background

`PositronModalDialogReactRenderer` (`src/vs/base/browser/positronModalDialogReactRenderer.tsx`) was added in #13336 (May 2026). Because it uses a native `<dialog>`, the browser handles the focus trap, Escape-to-close, backdrop dimming, and top-layer stacking, instead of the manual event/overlay handling in the old renderer. It pairs with the `PositronDynamicModalDialog` component; the Data Connections feature is the reference implementation (e.g. `configureDataConnection.tsx`).

## Scope -- modals to migrate

| Modal | Current component + renderer | Files |
|---|---|---|
| Assistant Panel | `PositronModalDialog` + `PositronModalReactRenderer` | `AskAssistantAction.tsx:85,112`, `AssistantPanel/AssistantPanel.tsx` |
| Visualize DataFrame | `PositronModalDialog` + `PositronModalReactRenderer` | `contrib/visualize/visualizeModalDialog.tsx:104,112,278` |
| Ghost Cell Info | `OKModalDialog` + `PositronModalReactRenderer` | `contrib/ghostCell/GhostCellInfoModalDialog.tsx:81` |

For each: swap `PositronModalReactRenderer` -> `PositronModalDialogReactRenderer`, move the dialog body onto `PositronDynamicModalDialog` (or the appropriate new-renderer component), and verify focus/Escape/backdrop behavior.

## Out of scope

These notebook-editor surfaces use VS Code's built-in services, not custom React modals, and should stay as-is:
- Pending-Edits confirmation (`IDialogService.prompt`, `AssistantPanel.tsx`)
- Ghost-cell-disabled and new-editor notification toasts (`INotificationService.prompt`)
- Save-As (`IFileDialogService`, `PositronNotebookEditorInput.ts`)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All three modals render via `PositronModalDialogReactRenderer`
- [ ] No remaining references to `PositronModalReactRenderer` in the notebook editor
- [ ] Focus trap, Escape-to-close, and backdrop behavior verified for each
- [ ] Existing behavior (sizing, multi-step navigation in Visualize, click-outside) preserved

## References

- New API: `src/vs/base/browser/positronModalDialogReactRenderer.tsx`
- Reference usage: `src/vs/workbench/contrib/positronDataConnections/browser/dialogs/`
- Introduced in #13336

title: packages pane: updating a Python package can silently break the environment
description:
The Packages pane offers per-package **Update** buttons and an **Update All** action. For Python, the pip and some uv workflows don't check whether the new version(s) are compatible with the rest of the installed packages, so an update can leave the environment broken with no error surfaced in the pane.

This is a common "dependency hell" problem in Python and we'd probably lose credibility with experienced Python developers if this happened without guardrails to protect against it.

1. Single update: the Update button runs `<python> -m pip install --upgrade <name>==<picked>`. The explicit pin forces past other installed packages' version bounds.
2. Update All: runs `pip list --outdated` then a single `pip install --upgrade <names>`. Bulk resolution is less likely to conflict than the pinned single update but still ignores constraints of packages not in the outdated set.

The uv environment workflow (`uv pip install --upgrade`) behaves the same. Note that the uv *project* workflow (`uv add` / `uv sync --upgrade`) and conda resolve the full graph and are not affected.

## Steps to reproduce

### prerequisite: a demo package

This is most severely a problem when a package in your environment has a version ceiling on the package you want to install/update. Set one up like this:

```
# Set up workspace
rm -rf ~/test_break
mkdir ~/test_break
cd ~/test_break
uv venv

# Set up demo package
mkdir -p demo/positron_update_demo
echo 'from setuptools import setup
setup(
    name="positron-update-demo",
    version="1.0.0",
    packages=["positron_update_demo"],
    install_requires=["werkzeug<3"],
)' > demo/setup.py
echo 'from werkzeug.urls import url_quote' > demo/positron_update_demo/__init__.py

# Install demo package and a compatible version of its dependency
uv pip install ./demo werkzeug==2.0.3
```

### SIngle update issue

1. Open `~/test_break` in Positron
2. In the Console, `import positron_update_demo` should work
3. In the packages pane, Update button on 'werkzeug' -> pick latest (like 3.1.8). In the logs I see no warning.
4. Click 'Restart Session' button that pops up
5. Try `import positron_update_demo` again in the Console, get an ImportError

### Update All issue

1. Re-run the prerequisite code above so that `werkzeug` is back at 2.0.3
2. Open `~/test_break` in Positron
3. In the Console, `import positron_update_demo` should work
4. In the packages pane, Update All button. In the logs I see no warning.
5. Click 'Restart Session' button that pops up
6. Try `import positron_update_demo` again in the Console, get an ImportError

## Expected

- The Update button on a package should only exist if it's possible to update a sufficient set of packages such that the environment is still consistent
- If the Update button would end up updating multiple packages, a confirmation dialog should appear
- The Update All button should also always result in a consistent environment

I know it might be tricky to figure out whether an environment will be consistent before the update, but IMO it's important since the transaction is tough to revert. If we can't figure out a way to do this, we should disable the Update button for Python packages.

title: packages pane: update version picker can list versions incompatible with the environment
description:
Installing or updating packages in the Packages Pane opens a version picker populated by `searchPyPIVersions`, which returns the entire PyPI `versions` array for the package, unfiltered by the environment's Python version, platform, or yank status. A user on an older interpreter can pick a version that requires a newer Python.

For pip/uv this fails the install (`ERROR: ... requires a different Python`) rather than corrupting the environment, so severity is low, but it's a confusing dead end: the pane offers a version it cannot install.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a Python 3.9 environment
2. Packages pane > Install package > numpy > 2.4.6
3. Installation errors out

## Expected

The picker should list only versions installable in the active environment (respect `Requires-Python`, platform, and yank status)

title: Support Watch Pane (and Debug Console) for R notebook debugging
description:
Follow-up to https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/12104

We now support debugging R cells in notebook, but we had to postpone support for the Watch Pane (and Debug Console by the same token, which uses Evaluate requests with `context` set to "repl") as it was a little more tricky to implement.

Watch Pane evaluations come in via Jupyter's Control socket, the one that handles ShutDown and Interrupt requests for the kernel. Although these Evaluate requests arrive in principle at a time when the R console is idle, in practice they arrive asynchronously and the console might already be evaluating the next expression.

To solve this without race conditions and/or unsafe concurrent R evaluations, we need an atomic way to query the console for idleness and evaluate an expression from the Jupyter DAP handler.

title: Plots "Open in new window" shows broken styling in Firefox on Workbench
description: When using "Open in new window" from the Plots pane in Firefox on Positron Pro, the auxiliary window displays incorrectly. Text labels reading "Go to File", "Open Settings", and "Find in Files" appear overlaid on top of the plot content, along with broken icons. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Launch a Positron Pro session from Workbench in Firefox (consistently reproducible on https://workbench.posit.it/) 2. Create a plot 3. Click "Open in new window" from the Plots pane action bar 4. Observe the auxiliary window ## Expected behavior The plot should display cleanly in the new window without any overlay or placeholder text. ## Actual behavior The auxiliary window shows: - Text labels and broken icons - The plot renders underneath this unwanted content, but is cut off ## System details - Posit Workbench 2026.01.0+392.pro5 - Positron Pro 2025.12.2 build 5 - Browser: Firefox - Works correctly in Chrome on the same environment ## Additional context **Dev environment behavior:** In local development environments, both Firefox and Chrome show a similar issue with the placeholder text overlay. This appears to be a separate (though possibly related) problem from the production Firefox-specific issue. **Initial investigation:** The issue may be related to how CSS stylesheets are cloned to auxiliary windows. The placeholder text is normally hidden by CSS rules. The auxiliary window opens with an empty URL (Firefox uses `''` instead of `about:blank`), which could affect how relative stylesheet URLs resolve. Related files examined: - `src/vs/workbench/services/auxiliaryWindow/browser/auxiliaryWindowService.ts` - `src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/editor/media/editorgroupview.css`

title: Create a test runner build of Positron
description:
When you develop an extension, you can write extension-level tests:
https://code.visualstudio.com/api/working-with-extensions/testing-extension

The experience is pretty good! Either in CI or locally, when you run these tests, a special build of VS Code gets downloaded and then it runs your tests. You can actually see the tests execute in front of you locally in this special build, which is honestly _very_ entertaining and fun. 😅 

Right now when folks create an extension either solely for Positron or with some features that work in Positron, there is no good way to write extension-level tests that exercise anything specific to Positron, because we don't have an equivalent build for Positron. We could create one, or figure out how to adapt the testing strategy to a local regular build of Positron.

I think the best option folks have now is to mock out Positron-specific functionality.

title: api github all downloads in assets ?
description:
Hi,

This isn't a Positron issue, but rather a feature request regarding your release publishing process.

We use the GitHub API (https://api.github.com/repos/posit-dev/positron/releases/latest) to detect new versions of hundreds of applications.

Usually, we detect updates and download the installers directly from the URLs listed in the assets section of the release. However, for Positron, only the source code archives are included in the assets. The actual download URLs are only available in the release body, which makes them difficult to extract reliably.

Would it be possible to include the platform-specific binaries (Windows, macOS, Linux, etc.) in the release assets in the future? 

Regards

title: Gate Positron's AI features on single setting
description:
Provide a way to disable all Positron-provided AI features through a single setting.

It could be the `assistant.enabled` setting. Note that features like NES, AI features in Positron Notebooks, etc. can only work if the user opts into Posit Assistant chat as well. Though this setting is owned by Posit Assistant, other positron extensions can check for the setting as needed. It's likely most intuitive for users that `assistant.enabled` enables/disables all Positron AI features, rather than it only controlling the Posit Assistant chat interface.

We could also introduce a new setting that gates all the AI features like `ai.enabled` that is owned by Positron, if we think Positron itself should own the setting and all the AI features can be enabled/disabled independently of each other.

title: python: extension sometimes uses the wrong active interpreter
description:
For the positron-python extension, there are a few ways to get the active interpreter path:

- The API: `PythonExtension.api().environments.getActiveEnvironmentPath()`
- Internal service: `InterpreterService.getActiveInterpreter()`

These are used dozens of times each in our codebase, not to mention in extensions like pyrefly ([example](https://github.com/facebook/pyrefly/blob/c3190f7672bf9c80559104005bbf2f5ab25468cc/lsp/src/extension.ts#L77)).

We've noticed that sometimes these fail to return the correct interpreter. (A reprex is to start multiple Python sessions at once and change to the second one outside of a workspace.) This can mean that Assistant tools fail, like the "install packages" tool installing to the wrong environment ([example](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/11154#discussion_r2629559341)), or that extensions like pyrefly don't know when an interpreter changed and don't update their diagnostics (this probably was the original cause of https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/6936).

@samclark2015 pointed out this could have been due to commenting this out: https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/6e2641a491a8f716b7312738e1c5d429cade5f72/extensions/positron-python/src/client/common/interpreterPathService.ts#L114

We still don't want to permanently update the user config each time someone clicks on a different session, so we'll have to find a different way to make this work.

title: Last Executed Time - Improve cell visibility tracking for more responsive UI updates
description: ## Description Related to https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/11573 Currently, notebook cell visibility is checked via polling rather than being event-driven in the `CodeCellStatusFooter` component. This means when a cell scrolls into view, the relative execution time of a cell is not re-rendered immediately, but instead gets re-rendered on the next polling interval. For example, if a cell with execution time "2 mins ago" is scrolled out of view for several minutes and then scrolled back into view, the footer will still show "2 mins ago" until the next 60-second interval tick occurs. This isn't great since users expect the time to update immediately when they scroll back to the cell. The current pieces that allow checking for visible cells are: - `cell.isInViewport()` which uses `MIN_CELL_VISIBILITY_RATIO` (visibility threshold): method that checks if >= 50% of cell is visible - `onDidScrollCellsContainer` **Features that rely on cell visibility** 1. Cell Footer - `CodeCellStatusFooter`: Checks `cell.isInViewport()` on interval tick before re-rendering relative time 2. Assistant Follow Action - `handleAssistantCellModification()`: Checks `cell.isInViewport()` to decide whether to highlight in place or scroll to cell 3. Assistant Follow Action - `cell.reveal()`: Checks `isInViewport()` before deciding to scroll 4. Webview Mount (`useWebviewMount.ts`) - Subscribes to `onDidScrollCellsContainer` to reposition webviews As a solution to the cell footer polling problem, we may want to add an observable `isVisible` property to each cell. title: PDF viewer blocked by CSP in Workbench browser sessions: frame-src source missing trailing slash
description:
### Summary

When a PDF is opened in Positron running inside a Posit Workbench browser session (or any other deployment where `vscode.env.asExternalUri()` returns a path-routed URL), the embedded PDF.js iframe is blocked by the webview's Content Security Policy. The browser console shows:

```
Framing 'https://<host>/s/<session-id>/p/<viewer-id>/viewer?file=…&theme=1'
violates the following Content Security Policy directive:
"frame-src https://<host>/s/<session-id>/p/<viewer-id> http://localhost:* http://127.0.0.1:*".
The request has been blocked.
```

(Note the `frame-src` source has no trailing slash; the iframe URL is a sub-path of that source.)

The bug is specific to remote/path-routed deployments. **Desktop Positron is unaffected** because there `asExternalUri` returns a `localhost:<port>` URI that is already covered by the wildcard `http://localhost:* http://127.0.0.1:*` sources also present in the directive.

### Reproduction

1. Sign in to a Workbench browser session (Positron `2026.03.0` or later — anything with `extensions/positron-pdf-server` shipped).
2. Open any PDF file in the editor.
3. Observe: the PDF viewer pane shows "content is blocked" or a blank/error frame.
4. Open browser DevTools → Console; the CSP violation above is logged.

Workaround: right-click the PDF tab → "Open Externally" — opens the PDF in a new browser tab via the same proxied port (works because the new tab is not subject to the parent webview's CSP).

### Expected behavior

The PDF iframe loads normally inside the webview, as it does in desktop Positron and as documented for the integrated PDF viewer.

### Actual behavior

The iframe is blocked by CSP because the `frame-src` source has no trailing slash, which per [CSP3 §6.7.2.7 path-matching rules](https://www.w3.org/TR/CSP3/#match-url-to-source-expression) requires the URL to match the source's path **exactly** — sub-paths are rejected. The viewer URL is a sub-path of the allowed source, so it is rejected.

### Root cause

File: `extensions/positron-pdf-server/src/pdfViewerWebview.ts`, lines 51-74 (current `main` HEAD `ff19e435b0`; identical at every release tag from `2026.03.0-73` through current).

```typescript
// Get the CSP source for the webview and the server URL.
const cspSource = webview.cspSource;
let serverUrl = await httpServer.getExternalUrl();

// Remove trailing slash if present.
if (serverUrl.endsWith('/')) {
    serverUrl = serverUrl.slice(0, -1);
}

// Build CSP allowing localhost iframes with full PDF.js viewer resources.
const csp = [
    `default-src 'none'`,
    `style-src ${cspSource} 'unsafe-inline' ${serverUrl} http://localhost:* http://127.0.0.1:*`,
    `script-src ${cspSource} 'nonce-${nonce}' ${serverUrl} http://localhost:* http://127.0.0.1:* 'unsafe-eval'`,
    `frame-src ${serverUrl} http://localhost:* http://127.0.0.1:*`,
    `img-src ${cspSource} data: ${serverUrl} http://localhost:* http://127.0.0.1:*`,
    `font-src ${cspSource} data: ${serverUrl} http://localhost:* http://127.0.0.1:*`,
    `worker-src ${cspSource} blob: ${serverUrl} http://localhost:* http://127.0.0.1:*`,
    `connect-src ${serverUrl} http://localhost:* http://127.0.0.1:*`
].join('; ');

// Build viewer URL - use custom wrapper that sets theme preference.
const pdfUrl = `${serverUrl}/pdf/${pdfId}`;
const theme = getPdfJsTheme();
const viewerUrl = `${serverUrl}/viewer?file=${encodeURIComponent(pdfUrl)}&theme=${theme}`;
```

The strip-trailing-slash on lines 54-57 yields a `serverUrl` like `https://<host>/s/<sid>/p/<vid>` (no trailing `/`). On line 64 that bare URL is emitted as a `frame-src` source. Per CSP3, a source whose path is non-empty and does **not** end with `/` matches only the exact path — so the iframe at `${serverUrl}/viewer?…` (a sub-path) is rejected.

This is also a regression of an established pattern in the same repo. `src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostWebview.ts:81-94` does the *opposite* — it explicitly **appends** `/` to the source URL with the comment _"Always treat the location as a directory so that we allow all content under it"_:

```typescript
public get cspSource(): string {
    const extensionLocation = this.#extension.extensionLocation;
    if (extensionLocation.scheme === Schemas.https || extensionLocation.scheme === Schemas.http) {
        let extensionCspRule = extensionLocation.toString();
        if (!extensionCspRule.endsWith('/')) {
            // Always treat the location as a directory so that we allow all content under it
            extensionCspRule += '/';
        }
        return extensionCspRule + ' ' + webviewGenericCspSource;
    }
    return webviewGenericCspSource;
}
```

The PDF extension should follow that same idiom.

### Proposed fix

#### Option A (preferred) — invert the strip into an append

In `extensions/positron-pdf-server/src/pdfViewerWebview.ts`, replace lines 54-57:

```diff
-	// Remove trailing slash if present.
-	if (serverUrl.endsWith('/')) {
-		serverUrl = serverUrl.slice(0, -1);
-	}
+	// Ensure trailing slash so frame-src/script-src/etc. match all sub-paths under serverUrl.
+	// Per CSP3 §6.7.2.7, a path component without a trailing slash requires an exact match.
+	if (!serverUrl.endsWith('/')) {
+		serverUrl += '/';
+	}
```

…and adjust the URL construction on lines 72-74 to not double up the slash:

```diff
-	// Build viewer URL - use custom wrapper that sets theme preference.
-	const pdfUrl = `${serverUrl}/pdf/${pdfId}`;
-	const theme = getPdfJsTheme();
-	const viewerUrl = `${serverUrl}/viewer?file=${encodeURIComponent(pdfUrl)}&theme=${theme}`;
+	// Build viewer URL - use custom wrapper that sets theme preference.
+	const pdfUrl = `${serverUrl}pdf/${pdfId}`;
+	const theme = getPdfJsTheme();
+	const viewerUrl = `${serverUrl}viewer?file=${encodeURIComponent(pdfUrl)}&theme=${theme}`;
```

This matches the pattern in `extHostWebview.ts` and fixes the bug for **all seven** directives that use `${serverUrl}` (`style-src`, `script-src`, `frame-src`, `img-src`, `font-src`, `worker-src`, `connect-src`). Currently only `frame-src` manifests the bug because the iframe is the only resource loaded at a sub-path, but a symmetric fix is the safer change.

#### Option B — keep the strip; emit `${serverUrl}/` at every source position

Keep lines 54-57 as-is, then in lines 60-67 change every bare `${serverUrl}` to `${serverUrl}/`:

```diff
 const csp = [
 	`default-src 'none'`,
-	`style-src ${cspSource} 'unsafe-inline' ${serverUrl} http://localhost:* http://127.0.0.1:*`,
-	`script-src ${cspSource} 'nonce-${nonce}' ${serverUrl} http://localhost:* http://127.0.0.1:* 'unsafe-eval'`,
-	`frame-src ${serverUrl} http://localhost:* http://127.0.0.1:*`,
-	`img-src ${cspSource} data: ${serverUrl} http://localhost:* http://127.0.0.1:*`,
-	`font-src ${cspSource} data: ${serverUrl} http://localhost:* http://127.0.0.1:*`,
-	`worker-src ${cspSource} blob: ${serverUrl} http://localhost:* http://127.0.0.1:*`,
-	`connect-src ${serverUrl} http://localhost:* http://127.0.0.1:*`
+	`style-src ${cspSource} 'unsafe-inline' ${serverUrl}/ http://localhost:* http://127.0.0.1:*`,
+	`script-src ${cspSource} 'nonce-${nonce}' ${serverUrl}/ http://localhost:* http://127.0.0.1:* 'unsafe-eval'`,
+	`frame-src ${serverUrl}/ http://localhost:* http://127.0.0.1:*`,
+	`img-src ${cspSource} data: ${serverUrl}/ http://localhost:* http://127.0.0.1:*`,
+	`font-src ${cspSource} data: ${serverUrl}/ http://localhost:* http://127.0.0.1:*`,
+	`worker-src ${cspSource} blob: ${serverUrl}/ http://localhost:* http://127.0.0.1:*`,
+	`connect-src ${serverUrl}/ http://localhost:* http://127.0.0.1:*`
 ].join('; ');
```

This is a smaller diff but leaves the awkward strip-then-re-add pattern.

**Option A is cleaner and more idiomatic** — it normalizes once at the source and matches what `extHostWebview.ts` already does.

### Affected version range

The bug-introducing commit is `add2f699f8` (PR #11761, 2026-02-09, original PDF viewer feature). It is contained in **74 release tags** spanning `2026.03.0-73` (earliest) through `2026.06.0-47` (current latest at time of writing) plus all `main`-branch builds. **Every Positron release that ships the PDF viewer is affected.**

### Test gap

The existing E2E coverage (`test/e2e/tests/pdf/pdf.test.ts`, added in PR #12781 and extended in PR #13078) runs against a Positron server bound to `localhost:<port>` (see `test/e2e/infra/playwrightBrowser.ts`). In that mode `vscode.env.asExternalUri()` returns a `http://localhost:<port>/…` URL whose host-port-only origin is already permitted by the `http://localhost:* http://127.0.0.1:*` wildcards in every directive — the bug is **masked**.

A regression-catching E2E should run under a path-routed `asExternalUri` configuration (e.g. via a code-server-style proxy in front of Positron Server, or by mocking `asExternalUri` to return an `https://example.com/p/abcd/` shape) and assert that no CSP violation is logged when a PDF is opened. Tagging the test `@:web` alone is not sufficient — the test infrastructure also needs path-routing.

### Other extensions audited (cross-extension sweep)

I grep'd `extensions/` for the same anti-pattern (trailing-slash strip + bare `${variable}` in a CSP source-list). Result:

| Extension | File | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `positron-pdf-server` | `src/pdfViewerWebview.ts:55-57,64` | **BUG** (subject of this issue) |
| `simple-browser` | `src/simpleBrowserView.ts:132` | Safe — uses `frame-src *;` (wildcard) |
| `media-preview` (video, audio, image) | `src/{video,audio,image}Preview/*.ts` | Safe — uses `${cspSource}` (the webview API, which auto-appends `/`) |
| `mermaid-chat-features` | `src/{editorManager,chatOutputRenderer}.ts` | Safe — uses `${webview.cspSource}` |
| `markdown-language-features` | `src/preview/{previewManager,documentRenderer}.ts` | Safe — uses webview cspSource and `default-src 'none'` |
| `positron-run-app` | `src/api.ts:118-120,790-792` | Safe — strips slash, but uses URL as a `Map` key, not in CSP |
| `positron-r` | `src/kernel-spec.ts:453` | Safe — strips slash for a CLI argument, not CSP |
| `positron-catalog-explorer` | `src/catalogs/unityCatalogClient.ts:276`, `src/fs/dbfs.ts:155` | Safe — strips slash for DBFS / Unity Catalog REST URL normalization, not CSP |

Only `positron-pdf-server` combines both the trailing-slash strip **and** a bare path-routed source in a CSP directive that is later used as a sub-path prefix. **No other extension has the same bug.**

### Customer impact

This is a regression of basic PDF-viewing in Positron when used via Posit Workbench (the supported remote-IDE deployment shape). Reproduces deterministically and across multiple browsers (confirmed Chrome and Edge). Affects every user of Positron-on-Workbench since the PDF viewer was added.

---

### Suggested labels

`bug`, `area: core`, `area: pdf-viewer`, `support`, plus whichever team-owner label applies.

### Cross-reference

- Internal ref: IDEESC-709
- No existing Positron issue or PR addresses this; verified via search of `posit-dev/positron` for `frame-src trailing slash`, `PDF viewer CSP`, `positron-pdf-server`.

## System details:

#### Positron and OS details:

Positron Version: 2026.05.0 build 13
Code - OSS Version: 1.109.2
Commit: 841ee7342bac43cf1e3b670afeb90c3d7c01b75c

Node.js: 22.21.1
V8: 14.2.231.22-electron.0
OS: Darwin arm64 25.4.0

#### Session details:

R 4.5.2 (2025-10-31)

## Describe the issue:

Elsewhere in Positron (and many other editors), after you Ctrl+F and search for a word, clicking enter moves to the next instance of the search result.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/795f602c-6870-44c3-ad5c-d26b20c68970

In the help pane, this doesn't work. You have to click on the down arrow, which I find frustrating. In the video below, I try clicking Enter first, but it doesn't work (hence you can't see anything happening), then clicking on the down arrow finds the next instance.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7ca25078-3389-4e3d-8163-b1d89c9ef9f8

## Steps to reproduce the issue:

<!-- For example, are you using a Jupyter notebook, R script, Quarto document, etc? -->

1. Open help for `plot()` with `?plot`
2. Search for the word "title"
3. Click enter to try to get to the next instance

title: Resolve problems around how keyboard shortcuts are surfaced in "Keyboard Shortcuts" UI
description:
In #7252 I ended up pretty confused and misinformed about how some keyboard shortcuts work, because we have two categories of problems:

## Keybindings hardcoded in a React component are not surfaced in the UI

The OP in #7252 said they accessed the console history using <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>R</kbd>. If you try to find out what that keybinding does as a user, you do not see it at all:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/186867de-ffa8-4180-99a8-bd8daaa277ec)

This is because we don't contribute this in a "normal" VS Code way, but in this component for the Console:

https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/64988dfaeaa5de9219cb777569c2e8631aefbe0e/src/vs/workbench/contrib/positronConsole/browser/components/consoleInput.tsx#L488

Can we get keybindings that we create in this way to show up in the keybindings UI, or otherwise help people know what they are doing? Should we move these out of the console component into `positronConsoleActions.ts`?

## Keybindings that we have turned off still leak into the UI

Another commenter in #7252 said they use <kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>Up</kbd> to access the console history. If you try to find out what that keybinding does, I see this:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/635a0302-011f-48e6-8775-4cd9d3516186)

The command `interactive.history.focus` comes from upstream's interactive window:

https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/aab7765f7cb336dbfdef8f820997bce03b61f9f5/src/vs/workbench/contrib/interactive/browser/interactive.contribution.ts#L793

We have disabled the interactive window in Positron. You can't run this command from the command palette (good!) but the keyboard shortcuts are leaking through still into this UI (bad!).

Between both of these, I sure ended up wrong and confused about what was happening! 😬

title: Quarto inline output: code-cell run buttons detach and drift along the viewport when scrolling
description:
## Describe the bug

In `.qmd` documents with `positron.quarto.inlineOutput.enabled` turned on, the per-cell run buttons that appear at the top-right of code chunks intermittently detach from their anchor and "stick" to the viewport, drifting across the screen as I scroll the document. Once it happens, the orphaned buttons remain visible over unrelated content and do not return to their correct position on their own.

This appears to be a stale decoration / editor-widget rendering issue rather than a logic bug: the buttons keep working, they are just drawn in the wrong place.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a `.qmd` file with one or more executable code chunks.
2. Ensure `positron.quarto.inlineOutput.enabled` is `true`.
3. Edit / run cells and scroll up and down through the document for a while.
4. Observe that, after some interaction, the top-right cell run buttons separate from their chunk and float along the viewport while scrolling.

(It is intermittent, but recurs regularly during normal editing.)

## Expected behavior

The run buttons stay anchored to their code chunk and scroll with the document content.

## Actual behavior

The run buttons detach and move independently of the chunk they belong to, overlaying other content until the editor is refreshed.

## Workaround

`View: Split Editor` to open the document in a new editor group, then close the original (glitched) pane. This forces a fresh editor-widget instance and clears the artifact. `Developer: Reload Window` also works but is much heavier (it restarts the front end, extensions, language packs, and tears down integrated terminal processes).

## What does not resolve it

- `"editor.codeLens": false` (globally or scoped to `[quarto]`) has no effect — these buttons are not CodeLens.
- Closing and reopening the file in the **same** editor group does not help (the pooled editor widget appears to be reused).
- Toggling the sidebar/panel, editor zoom, and tab switching do not reliably clear it.
- Disabling `positron.quarto.inlineOutput.enabled` removes the buttons, but also removes inline output, which I want to keep.

## Proposed solutions

**1. Fix the rendering bug.** Ensure the cell run-button affordances are re-anchored (or their decoration layer invalidated) on scroll/layout so they cannot become detached from their chunk. The fact that creating a fresh editor-widget instance (Split Editor + close original) fixes it suggests the stale state lives on the reused editor widget's overlay/decoration layer.

**2. Add a separate setting to toggle the run buttons independently of inline output.** Right now the cell run buttons are bound to `positron.quarto.inlineOutput.enabled`, so the only way to hide them is to lose inline output entirely. Please decouple them into their own setting (e.g. `positron.quarto.cellExecutionButtons.enabled` or similar) so that users can keep inline output enabled while hiding the buttons and running cells purely via the keyboard (`Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Enter` for the current cell, `Ctrl/Cmd+Enter` for the current line). This would also serve as a clean mitigation for the bug above.

## System details

```
Version: Positron Version: 2026.06.0 (system setup) build 211
Code - OSS Version: 1.111.0
Commit: d5f94f072b1083b8237930739cb6525c6e12e1da
Date: 2026-05-28T01:04:13+02:00
Commit: 39.6.0
Date: 142.0.7444.265
Electron: 22.22.0
ElectronBuildId: 14.2.231.22-electron.0
Chromium: Windows_NT x64 10.0.26200
Node.js: undefined
V8: undefined
OS: undefined
```

## Additional notes

Inline output for `.qmd` recently moved out of preview in 2026.06, so this may be a recent regression in the new inline-output cell UI. Happy to provide a screenshot/recording of the detached buttons if useful.

title: Migrate incidental-notebook E2E tests to the Positron notebook editor
description:
In #14062 I am making the Positron notebook editor the default for `.ipynb` files! 🎉  Several E2E tests open notebooks only as a vehicle for testing some other feature, and they drive the notebook through the legacy `Notebooks` page object (`app.workbench.notebooks`, e.g. the `a.kernel-label` kernel selector). Once the new editor became the default, those selectors no longer exist and the tests timed out.

To keep CI green in #14062, these suites were pinned back to the legacy editor with `test.use({ useLegacyNotebookEditor: true })` (the worker option now lives in the base e2e setup). That is a stopgap only. It means these features are still being exercised against the legacy editor, not against the new default that users will actually have.

### Goal

Migrate these tests to the new editor via the `PositronNotebooks` page object (`app.workbench.notebooksPositron`) and remove the `useLegacyNotebookEditor: true` pin from each, so they exercise the default editor. We don't _have_ to do this during 2026.07 but we shouldn't wait too long.

### Files pinned to legacy in #14062

- [x] `test/e2e/tests/autocomplete/autocomplete-notebook-console.test.ts`
- [x] `test/e2e/tests/data-explorer/data-explorer-python-pandas.test.ts`
- [x] `test/e2e/tests/help/f1.test.ts`
- [x] `test/e2e/tests/new-folder-flow/new-folder-flow-jupyter.test.ts` (uses a raw `a.kernel-label` locator, not the page object)
- [x] `test/e2e/tests/plots/matplotlib-interact.test.ts`
- [x] `test/e2e/tests/variables/variables-notebook.test.ts`
- [x] `test/e2e/tests/welcome/welcome.test.ts`
- [x] `test/e2e/tests/notebook/notebook-working-directory.test.ts` (lives in the legacy `notebook/` regression suite; decide whether to migrate in place or add a Positron-editor equivalent, and confirm `notebook.workingDirectory` behaves the same on the new editor)

### Notes for whoever picks this up

- The kernel API differs: the legacy page object uses `selectInterpreter()` / `expectKernelToBe()` against `a.kernel-label`; `PositronNotebooks` exposes a `kernel` helper instead.
- Output assertions differ: legacy `runAllCells()` / `assertCellOutput(regex, index)` vs. `notebooksPositron.runCodeAtIndex()` / `expectOutputAtIndex(index, lines)`.
- The dedicated `notebook/` suite (notebook-create, notebook-debug, notebook-large-*, notebook-raises-exception) should stay on the legacy editor; it is the legacy-editor regression suite and is paired with the `notebooks-positron/` suite for the new editor. This issue is only about the tests above that use notebooks incidentally.

### Acceptance criteria

- Each file above runs against the Positron notebook editor (default settings) with the `useLegacyNotebookEditor` pin removed.
- The `notebook/` legacy regression suite is unaffected.

title: `positron.quarto.inlineOutput.enabled` prevents the "Python (reticulate)" interpreter from launching, causing knitr+reticulate Quarto chunks to hang indefinitely (0% CPU)
description:
## System details:

#### Positron and OS details:

Version: Positron Version: 2026.06.1 (user setup) build 6
Code - OSS Version: 1.111.0
Commit: 63f0568b148d4d18b7a3194286686d6fb970bed3

Electron: 22.22.0
ElectronBuildId: 14.2.231.22-electron.0
Chromium: Windows_NT x64 10.0.19045
Node.js: undefined
V8: undefined
OS: Ubuntu on WSL2

#### Session details:

- Quarto version: 1.9.38
- R version: 4.6.1
- Python version: 3.10.12 (venv: tcrio)
- reticulate version: reticulate_1.46.0
- Document engine: `knitr` (not `jupyter`)

## Describe the issue:

In a Quarto document with `engine: knitr` where Python chunks run via `reticulate` (i.e. an R session driving an embedded Python interpreter, not a native Jupyter kernel), enabling `positron.quarto.inlineOutput.enabled` prevents Positron from starting the "Python (reticulate)" interpreter it normally launches alongside the R interpreter. Without that interpreter, chunk execution hangs indefinitely — the busy/spinner indicator never resolves, and the process shows 0% CPU, indicating it's blocked rather than computing.

## Steps to reproduce the issue:

### Observed behavior across setting combinations

| `inlineOutput.enabled` | `console.showNotebookConsoles` | "Python (reticulate)" interpreter launches? | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| false | false/true | Yes | Document executes fully and normally (no inline output rendering, output goes to console as usual) |
| true | false | **No** | Hangs indefinitely on the *first* Python chunk that produces any output (even a bare `import` + `print`), 0% CPU |
| true | true | **No** | Improves — no longer hangs on the first chunk — but still hangs on a later chunk that does more substantial work (a `for` loop calling several operations that each report progress via `tqdm`), 0% CPU |

### Steps to reproduce
1. Create a `.qmd` with `engine: knitr`, an R setup chunk calling `reticulate::use_virtualenv(...)`, and at least one Python chunk that prints output.
2. Set `positron.quarto.inlineOutput.enabled: true`.
3. Execute the document top to bottom.
4. Observe: the "Python (reticulate)" interpreter does not appear in the interpreter list, and the first chunk with output hangs indefinitely at 0% CPU.
5. Optionally set `console.showNotebookConsoles: true` as well — the first chunk now succeeds, but execution still hangs on a later chunk with heavier output (e.g. one driving `tqdm` progress bars across multiple iterations).


## Expected or desired behavior:
The "Python (reticulate)" interpreter should launch and chunks should execute and render inline, same as when `inlineOutput.enabled` is false (minus the inline rendering).

### Additional notes
- Disabling `positron.quarto.inlineOutput.enabled` entirely is a reliable workaround — the document runs correctly end-to-end in that state.
- The correlation between "Python (reticulate)" interpreter absence and the hang was consistent across both `inlineOutput=true` states tested.

## Were there any error messages in the UI, Output panel, or Developer Tools console?
No

title: Quarto inline output: Share single interpreter session and console among multiple Quarto documents
description: One of the major differences between Quarto inline output in Positron and the similar feature in RStudio is that in Positron, every Quarto document receives its own interpreter session and, optionally, console. This design is an improvement over RStudio's in many ways. In particular: - It better matches the render-time behavior. - It prevents documents from polluting each others' state. - It increases reproducibility by ensuring that each document is more self-contained. - It resolves ambiguities around working directories (each document gets a session started in its working directory). - It is symmetric with the behavior of all other notebook-like things in Positron and in the larger notebook community (e.g. Jupyter notebooks do not share sessions) However, there are some tradeoffs to this approach. Among them: - It doesn't match what happens when inline output is disabled -- without inline output, all Quarto cells are run in a shared console. - It can be confusing for users coming from RStudio, who expect shared state. - Having a console around as a scratch pad is also useful (you can turn this on for Quarto documents, technically, but you still get one per document). - When working with large data or resource constraints, starting multiple sessions can be expensive. One customer noted: > I typically have multiple notebooks open at the same time with some big datasets shared between them - but with separate sessions, each notebook holds its own copy, which has significant memory and performance implications. Proposal for feedback: Decouple the "session per document" feature from the "inline output" feature, such that you can choose the combination appropriate to your work.

## System details:

Describe the bug
I am trying to connect to a remote Linux server via SSH using Positron, but the connection fails because the remote extension host server for this specific version seems to be missing from the download servers.

To Reproduce

Install Positron version 2026.05.2-3 on the local machine.

The remote server binary should be downloaded successfully and the SSH connection should be established.

title: Python runtime discovery hangs and fails to find uv-installed Python on fresh Windows install
description:
In getting Positron running on a fresh Windows (parallels) install I ran into some issues working with Python. 

1. **Hang with no Python installed**: Opening Positron on a fresh Windows machine with no Python causes it to hang on Python discovery. No error message is shown to the user.

2. **uv-installed Python not found**: After installing Python via `uv` (which does not add `python.exe` to PATH), Positron fails to discover it. The runtime discoverer tries `python -c "import sys;print(sys.executable)"` which fails with exit code 9009, then hits repeated autoselection timeouts.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Fresh Windows install with no Python
2. Install Positron (release build)
3. Open Positron -- hangs on Python discovery, no user-facing error
4. Install `uv`, then run `uv python install`
5. Reopen Positron -- repeated "Autoselection timeout" errors, Python not discovered

## Error messages

From the Python Language Pack output:

```
[error] Command failed: python -c "import sys;print(sys.executable)"
Python was not found; run without arguments to install from the Microsoft Store, or disable
this shortcut from Settings > Apps > Advanced app settings > App execution aliases.

code: 9009, killed: false, signal: null,
cmd: 'python -c "import sys;print(sys.executable)"'

[error] Autoselection timeout out, this is likely a issue with how consumer called
execution factory API. Using default python to execute.
```

## Expected behavior

- If no Python is installed, Positron should complete discovery gracefully and let the user use non-Python features (not hang).
- If Python is installed via `uv`, Positron should discover it even if `python.exe` is not on PATH.

## Codebase context

- `pythonExecutionFactory.ts:69-71`: 50s autoselection timeout when no Python path is configured
- `executable.ts:27`: 15s timeout per `python -c "import sys;print(sys.executable)"` call
- `windowsKnownPathsLocator.ts:80-89`: UV directory search exists (implemented via #6701) but may not work when `python.exe` is not on PATH
- `discoverer.ts:51`: `triggerRefresh()` with no graceful handling for zero interpreters

## System details

```Positron Version: 2026.03.0 (system setup) build 212
Code - OSS Version: 1.108.0
Commit: f3aae65e0a1a11d39226cd884520f49301daef82

title: R: Extended LSP requests for object at cursor
description:
_Originally posted by @lionel- in [#2974](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/2974#issuecomment-2102575695)_:

> Relatedly, I've been thinking for a while about porting a feature I created in Emacs and used all the time as a data analyst. This feature has two parts:
> 
> 
> 
> - Detect relevant object at cursor. For instance, `foo$bar$q<>ux` gives you `foo$bar$qux`, `foo$bar<>$qux` gives you `foo$bar`, and `f<>oo$bar$qux` gives you `foo`. This would be provided via an extended LSP request.
> 
> 
> 
> - Provide various exploration commands for the object at cursor: `print()`, `summary()`, `str()`, `lobstr::sxp()`, etc. These exploration commands should be user-configurable (simple list of strings with some kind of symbol representing where the input goes). And `View()` could be one of the default actions.
> 
> 
> 
> The commands could each be an assist but I'd worry about cluttering the assist menu and making it harder to use as we add new kinds of assists in the future. So we could have a single assist for "Actions at point" that opens up a quickpick menu. It'd be great to implement frecency (thanks for the notion @DavisVaughan!) sorting of these commands.
> 
> 
> 
> This should also be its own command to make it quicker to use (no need to open the assist menu). Making it an assist is good for discoverability though. And there should also be a command to directly run an action. The command would take an action string as argument. This could be bound to Cmd+Click with `View(%%)` as action for instance.

title: Defer rendering notebook cell editor widgets
description:
Currently, all notebook cell editor widgets are mounted in their `useEffect`s which run before the notebook is first painted.

Could we defer rendering editor widgets, and instead start with a placeholder (that looks like an editor) or a more obvious "loading" indicator?

This would improve the time to first paint when opening a notebook for the first time and when switching to a notebook whose DOM node isn't cached.

title: Defer notebook output parsing
description:
I profiled notebook rendering and found that outputs are parsed during first render, and are one of the slower parts of rendering.

Can we defer output parsing?

title: Epic: Notebook editor performance improvements
description: Using this to group known issues related to the performance of the Positron notebook editor.

title: Decouple Positron notebook editor from VS Code kernel abstraction
description:
The Positron notebook editor routes cell execution through VS Code's `INotebookKernel` / `INotebookKernelService` via `RuntimeNotebookKernel`. We took this approach to get early support for notebooks in Positron, and to make the VS Code notebook editor fully functional as we get our new editor ready.

Now that Positron notebook editor is stable, this indirection isn't necessary and only adds merge conflict surface and duplicates session management logic already present in `QuartoKernelManager`.

title: Only render notebook cell editor widgets in the viewport
description:
In #14264 we found that simply reusing cell editor widgets across notebooks did not improve render time enough to drop the notebook render cache.

However, in notebooks with ~20 or more cells it is still slow to load the notebook for the first time and inefficient to hold all cell editor widgets in memory.

Could we explore only rendering cell editor widgets in (or new) the viewport? This could open up a can of worms around scrolling, height tracking, etc, so we'd need to first profile and decide whether this is worth pursuing. I would also rather try to address the other issues in the performance epic first.

title: Move headless LM service node layer + IPC protocol to vs/platform/positronLM
description:
The shared-process entry point imports the headless LM service's node implementation and IPC protocol from `vs/workbench`, which crosses the layer boundary (the shared-process / electron-utility layer must not depend on `vs/workbench`).

`src/vs/code/electron-utility/sharedProcess/sharedProcessMain.ts` (lines ~152-155):

```ts
// eslint-disable-next-line local/code-import-patterns -- LM service will move to vs/platform in a follow-up
import { PositronLMNode, PositronLMChannel } from '../../../workbench/services/positronLM/node/positronLMService.js';
// eslint-disable-next-line local/code-import-patterns
import { POSITRON_LM_CHANNEL_NAME } from '../../../workbench/services/positronLM/common/positronLMService.js';
```

The cross-layer import is currently suppressed with `local/code-import-patterns` disables.

### Fix

Move the shared-process-facing pieces to `vs/platform/positronLM/`:

- `node/positronLMService.ts` (`PositronLMNode`, `PositronLMChannel`)
- the IPC channel name + IPC types from `common/positronLMService.ts` that the node layer and shared process require

Leave the workbench-only pieces (`browser/` service, model picker, `*.contribution.ts`) in `vs/workbench/services/positronLM/`. Update imports and remove the two `eslint-disable` lines.

Introduced by #13730; intentionally deferred there to keep that PR scoped to introducing the service.

title: Provide a way to close a notebook console without shutting down the notebook session
description: ## System details: #### Positron and OS details: ``` Positron Version: 2026.04.0 build 180 Code - OSS Version: 1.109.2 Commit: d02b28a902a289e1e5a972734f6dec3f87000ecf Date: 2026-03-19T07:38:24.313Z Electron: 39.3.0 Chromium: 142.0.7444.265 Node.js: 22.21.1 V8: 14.2.231.22-electron.0 OS: Darwin arm64 25.3.0 ``` #### Session details: ## Describe the issue: Notebook consoles can be _opened_ with a gesture, but not _closed_ with a gesture -- once opened, closing them will shut down the entire notebook session. This is asymmetric and also reduces the usefulness of the notebook consoles a scratchpad that can be opened and closed at will. ## Steps to reproduce the issue: 1. title: Positron/Runtime API: Group/namespace execution metadata
description: Right now, the `execute_request` field we send to kernels contains a bag of key-value pairs that any extension (or Positron itself) can add. These can include figure width/height information from Quarto and editor information from Positron: And/or code location info: It's convenient to have all of these fields at the top level, but some grouping and namespacing would be helpful: - It would allow us to know the provenance of each field, possibly for display in the UI (e.g. if the figure width/height came from Quarto we could use that instead of assuming Quarto on the `ark` side) - It would prevent conflicts, collisions, and/or unintentional overrides for metadata fields that have the same name but contributed from different places (only a theoretical concern today) - It would provide stronger type guarantees for deserialization There are a few ways we could approach this, including separating Positron's built-in fields (e.g. `code_location`) from others, adding an `ark` key, adding a `quarto` key, etc. Some good discussion from @DavisVaughan & @lionel- in the related Ark PR: https://github.com/posit-dev/ark/pull/1119#discussion_r2955580539 https://github.com/posit-dev/ark/pull/1119#discussion_r2955656420

title: Direct line of communication between extensions and their kernels
description:
Historically we used custom LSP messages for communication between an extension and the kernel. However this has downsides:

1. Since we implemented support for multiple sessions, the LSP sessions are now closed when the console session goes in the background. This makes the LSP unreliable as a line of communication.

2. In future language packs, a kernel might not have an embedded LSP.

This suggests we'd be better off using Jupyter infrastructure for this. We're currently lacking major pieces of infrastructure:

- [x] **Unmanaged comms.** Currently all comms are mapped to a Positron client, i.e. an instance that lives in the main process and whose messages are handled/propagated by the core. We have some workarounds to let the core know it should be ignoring some clients (https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/pull/2892) but we're still missing a way to tell the core to ignore message types. Ideally we'd never go through the core at all. For a direct line of communication, extensions should be able to create and handle their own private message types without any oversight.

- [ ] **Async comm messages.** Currently all comm messages are sequential. For a direct line of communication, they shouldn't _have_ to be queued along with things like Execute Request. There should be a way to fire and handle them immediately. See https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/7447.

- [ ] **Requests from backend to frontend.** Currently only the UI comm is allowed to do such requests, via StdIn. We should generalise the mechanism with replies sent via Control: https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/2061

- [x] **Notifications from frontend to backend.** Not as important as requests because you can always notify with a request, but would be nice for API consistency and symmetry: https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/7448.

## Describe the issue:

### Summary
Currently, `positron.runtime.executeCode` supports an observer that receives error messages when code execution fails, but it doesn’t return standard output when the code completes successfully. This makes it difficult for extensions or clients to capture the printed output of executed code directly.

### Motivation / Problem
At present, the only way to access printed output is by writing to a temporary file and reading it back. This workaround is cumbersome and introduces unnecessary I/O overhead and potential race conditions. For example, an extension that runs snippets to produce lightweight feedback or inline results must handle file writes, file cleanup, and synchronization — all of which could be avoided if `executeCode` exposed stdout.

### Proposed Solution
Extend the observer interface to include a callback or event for standard output. For example:
```ts
positron.runtime.executeCode(code, ..., {
  onOutput: (text) => { /* handle printed output */ },
  onError: (err) => { /* handle errors */ },
  onComplete: () => { /* handle completion */ },
  ...
});
```


This would parallel the existing error reporting mechanism and make it much easier to build extensions that need to capture or display output dynamically.

### Benefits

- Enables extensions to display code output inline without temp files.
- Reduces file system operations and improves performance.
- Aligns with common patterns in REPL- or notebook-style APIs (e.g., Jupyter, Node.js child_process).
- Simplifies extension development and debugging.

### Alternatives Considered
Using temporary files works, but it is an ugly and brittle solution compared to an API-level event.
